Chan Master Jinnangfu Jingshan Daguan Tanying was a native of Qiantang. His clan name was Qiu. He received full ordination at Longxing Temple.
His spiritual presence was majestic and imposing. He had extensively mastered both Buddhist and secular classics. Having traveled to various monastic seats, he first visited...
Dayang Ming’an asked, “Regarding the ‘partial and correct,’ ‘ruler and minister’ established by the Master of Dongshan—what matter does this clarify?
He replied, “The state of affairs before one’s parents were born. [Dayang] asked, “How does one realize this? He replied, “At midnight it is perfectly bright; at dawn, nothing is revealed.
Master [Dayang] was perplexed and went to Shimen, where he took up the previous dialogue, saying, “I do not yet understand what you mean, Master. He replied, “I do not say it is not so.”
"However, my mouth is narrow; I have not finished speaking even though my mouth is full. He asked, "What is the matter before one's parents were born? He replied, "A brick from the latrine.
He asked, "What is 'midnight is perfectly bright, yet at dawn it is not revealed'?

He replied, "A cat sleeping beneath a peony flower. The Master’s doubts grew deeper. One day, he thought: "Stonehead’s taking up administrative duties was originally delusion; even his realization of the principle..."
Fenwu asked him. Baizhang said, "Do you consider these words to be medicine or sickness? Fenwu replied, "They are words of medicine.

Baizhang scolded him, saying, "If you still take sickness for medicine, how can you know the intent of the Patriarch’s transcendence? Upon hearing this, the Master was suddenly enlightened and exclaimed, "How should one apply this?
Baizhang said, "If speech does not leave the old nest, how can one escape the entanglements? The Master sighed and said, "Just now—"
To engage with the mere words and phrases is to fall into the realm of conceptual thought; these are all gates of death and are by no means the path of life.

He then bowed twice and took his leave. Initially, he resided at Lufeng on Mount Shu; subsequently, he moved to Yingsheng, Yinjing, Xuedou, and Jinnshan. [There,] he ascended the hall to address the assembly.
[The Master] raised [the case]: "The body is the Bodhi tree; the mind is like a bright mirror stand. At all times diligently wipe it clean;
do not let it gather dust. He also said: "Furthermore, the Bodhi tree originally has no tree; the bright mirror is likewise not a stand. Originally there is not a single thing;
what need is there to wipe away dust? The Master said: "These two venerable elders are sleeping on the same bed yet each dreams of their own things. 'Go, drink tea.'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "In other quarters, the hook is curved and the bait is fragrant; they swarm together like bees clustering around a queen.
Here at Sheng’s place, the hook is straight and there is no bait at all—it is like pressing a gourd underwater. Raising his staff and making the gesture of fishing, he said:
"To catch fish in deep water, one must trust in fate; never before have I offered wine to the River God. He threw down the staff and descended from the seat.

[The Master] ascended the hall. He raised [the following case]: Once, while Master Changsha Cen and Yangshan were admiring the moon, Yangshan said, "Everyone possesses this very thing, yet they simply cannot make use of it.
Changsha said, "That is exactly where you need help; let me borrow it for you. Yangshan asked, "How would you, my junior uncle, use it?
Changsha kicked Yangshan down. Yangshan said, "He is just like a great tiger! The Master said, "Yangshan..."
Mount [Shishuang] calls a tiger a "great beast. Because the Holy Path resembles a mad dog. Ascending the hall, he said:

"The gate of this mountain monk is unique; I have already altered the tracks of all other quarters. To extract Mañjuśrī’s wedge from his eye, I instruct Samantabhadra to cease chewing the iron in his mouth.
I urge you to loosen the hand that grips the slithering snake, and I shall hew away for you the hitching stake for the donkey. If you pause to fix your intent and attempt to deliberate..."

He shouted, saying: "Squeeze! Squeeze! Examine! Ascending the hall, he said: "From the Deer Park at the beginning, until the Bahudā River at the end—within these two intervals, not a single word was ever spoken.
The Master said: "The World-Honored One only knew how a sacred tortoise drags its tail;

later people failed to realize they were merely watching a hare and guarding a stump. Ascending the hall, he said: "Traveling ten thousand miles on a long road, one goes away and does not return. This person speaks in vain."
His heart was already ashen. If one passes before the Gate of the Sages from the perspective of causes, one must understand that even upon encountering spring, one will return again.
A monk asked, "What is the person who goes forth? He replied, "Once returned to within the green peaks, he does not emerge from the white clouds.
The monk asked, "What is the person who returns? He replied, "Since wandering the purple thoroughfares, who would be willing to hide in the green mountains? [The monk] asked, "As for..."
"What is 'seizing the person but not seizing the environment'? He said: "At home there is no longer any hope of returning; by the roadside stands empty the sign for longing for one's hometown.
"What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? He said: "The vast ocean is made to dry up to its very bottom;
the green mountains are ground down until they become dust. "What is 'seizing both person and environment'? He said: "Heaven and earth themselves are yet empty."
"The sun and moon of the Qin dynasty; the mountains and rivers do not see the sovereign and ministers of Han. [The Master] asked: "How is it that both the person and the environment are not usurped?
[The Master] said: "The oriole warbles through a thousand forests; flowers fill the earth. A traveler roams for three months; the grasses encroach upon the heavens. [The Master] asked:

"What is the house style of the Master? [The Master] said: "Reaching out one's hand, one cannot see one's own palm. [The Master] asked: "If a guest from the Immortal Tuo should suddenly arrive, what then?"
[The Master] said, "Facing each other across a thousand li. [The student] asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? [The Master] said, "Linji.
[The student] said, "If that is so, then you are the son of Guyin. [The Master] said, "Deshan. [The student] asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?
[The Master] said, "Into the womb of a donkey or the belly of a horse. [The student] said, "What is the proof of this? [The Master] said, "Plant such a cause; reap such a fruit."
"This is the fruit. Question: "Linji would shout as soon as someone entered the gate; Deshan would strike with a staff as soon as someone entered the gate.
I do not know how you, Master, guide people. He said: "Lingyun saw the peach blossoms. [The questioner] asked: "Is this not where you, Master, guide people?"
[The Master] said: "Zhaozhou’s response regarding the cypress tree. [Question: "What is the long Dharmakāya? [Answer: "My staff is six feet long. [Question: "What is the short Dharmakāya? [Answer:
"A counting-stick is three inches short. [Question: "If that is so, then the Dharmakāya has two forms?
[Answer: "There is still more—squareness and roundness. [Question: "Regarding Mazu Daoshi’s single shout, Baizhang was [stunned] for three days."
"Deaf in the ears. What was his meaning? [The Master] said, "Throughout my life, I have never once shouted at anyone; thus, for my entire life, I have been deaf in my ears.

[The questioner] asked, "How do you understand this? He replied, "Lately, my eyes have also grown dim. Li Gongduan-yuan, the Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince, once lodged within the Inner Garden and sought instruction from him day and night.
Consequently, when high officials came seeking medicinal cures for their ailments, he would provide them with instructions according to their circumstances, leading them all to realization.
He entered [the state of realization], and his eloquence was unimpeded. Wen Kanggong, Wang Xianggong, and other eminent scholars all served him with the etiquette due to a teacher.

His words were recorded as the *Dengmen ji* (Collection of Entering the Gate). On the eve of the New Year in the fourth year of the Jiayou era, he sent a servant with a letter to part from the Academician Dao Jingchun in Yangzhou.
He wrote: "I am to depart tomorrow morning; take good care of yourself. When Dao opened the seal, he was struck with astonishment.
He immediately dispatched an official to ride with a letter to inform him. As the boat was about to reach the shore, the Master joyfully ascended the seat.

He recounted the origins of his renunciation and expressed his gratitude to those who had assisted him, instructing them to advance in their practice. He then appointed the Prior, Master Xian, to succeed him.

After descending from the seat and finishing the reading of the letter from Scholar Li, the assembly escorted him to the abbot’s quarters. There, he sat cross-legged and passed away. The fifth year of the Yuan [era].
On that day, his worldly age was seventy-five and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇerakalpa) was fifty-three.
A monk asked Chan Master Faxian of Zhuyuan in Jingnan Prefecture: "All phenomena return to the One; to what does the One return?"

[The Master] said: "The water is deep; its bottom cannot be seen. [The student] asked: "How does one find a place to moor? [The Master] said: "One must be a person who practices from the very foundation.

[The student] asked: "What is the Way? [The Master] said: "A crossroads where paths intersect. [The student] asked: "What is it like to be a person on the Way? [The Master] said: "People often do not recognize one another."
When Chan Master Dacheng Zun of Tangzhou was attending Master Cizhao, he once asked, "What is the meaning of the ancients' request for fire?
Cizhao replied, "Let it go out. Zun asked, "What is it like after it has gone out? Cizhao said, "The first of the third month; the eleventh.

Zun said, "If that is so, then it is a fine occasion. Cizhao asked, "What principle do you perceive here? Zun said, "Today I am quite exhausted. Cizhao then struck him. Master [Zun]—*Record of the Sayings of Master Dacheng Zun of Tangzhou*.
He immediately attained great enlightenment. He spoke in verse: "How joyful is the occasion of seeking fire! The subtle function of concealing the point is rarely guessed by others.
If you wish to understand my Master’s direct intent, When the red furnace fire is spent, do not add more wood."
Chan Master Tianyi Yihuai of Tianyi Monastery in Shaoxing Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Xuedou Mingjue Chongxian (the tenth generation of Qingyuan and the fourth of Yunmen).
He was born into the Chen family of Leqing, Yongjia, and his family had been fishermen for generations.

He was born as the result of karma. His mother dreamed that a star fell upon her house and she subsequently conceived. At the time of his birth, there were many auspicious signs. When he was a child, he sat at the stern of a boat;
his father caught a fish and gave it to the master to skewer. The master could not bear to do so and secretly threw it into the river.

His father grew angry and whipped him, yet the master remained as calm as ever. Later, he traveled to the capital and became a novice monk under the Jingde Temple. During the Tiānshèng era, he underwent the scriptural examination.
He attained realization. He himself claimed that this was what had been recorded in the *Lotus Sūtra*. Afterward, he went to visit Shan of Jinnian and Xing of Ye County;
he attained a slight degree of accord with them. Later, he arrived in Gusu and paid his respects to Mingjue at Cuifeng. Cuifeng asked, "What is your name? He replied, "Yihuai."
[The Master] asked, "Why not name him Huaiyi (Embracing Righteousness)? He replied, "I obtained it at that time. [The Master] asked, "Who gave you this name?

He replied, "It has been ten years since I received the precepts. [The Master] said, "How many pairs of straw sandals have you worn out on your travels? He replied, "Master, please do not deceive people.
[The Master] said, "I too am without measure; you too are without measure. What do you say to this? The Teacher was silent.

Feng struck him, saying, "You empty-talking, deceptive fellow! Get out! Later, when entering the room, Feng said, "It is not so, nor is it not so; both 'so' and 'not so' are not acceptable. As the Master hesitated, Feng struck him out again. This happened several times. Subsequently, he served as the head of the water supply; while drawing water, his carrying pole broke, and he suddenly attained enlightenment. He then composed a verse of renunciation: The old master’s staff has been broken; The cold ashes have long since turned to dust. The thousand-year-old dragon has shed its scales; The jade rabbit has leaped into the void. The moon in the sky is bright and clear; The spring in the valley flows deep and wide. The myriad phenomena are all as they were;

The ten directions are naturally vast and open. I bow my head to the ancient Buddha; The world is filled with the fragrance of the Dharma. He then submitted this to Feng. Feng read it and said, "This is indeed the work of a true man. He subsequently appointed him as the head cook. One day, while washing rice, he suddenly realized that the rice was already cooked. He threw down the rice paddle and shouted, "What a pity! What a pity! Feng heard this and came to see him. The Master said, "The rice is already cooked. Feng asked, "Who will eat it? The Master replied, "Only those who have eyes can see. Feng said, "If you had spoken thus before, I would have beaten you to death. The Master said, "If you had beaten me then, I would have died for nothing. Feng said, "Now that you have spoken thus, I shall beat you. The Master said, "Strike, strike! Feng struck him three times and left. The Master laughed and said, "Today I have finally met the old fellow. From then on, he became known as the "Laughing Monk" (Hanshan).

His reputation spread throughout the realm, and he eventually passed away at the age of seventy-four. His remains were enshrined in a stupa at Mount Xuefeng. His disciples built a temple there, which was named Hanshan Temple. To this day, it remains a place of pilgrimage. The Master’s dharma heirs numbered over a hundred. Among them, the most prominent were: Chan Master Wuxue, Chan Master Changqing, Chan Master Yunmen, and Chan Master Dongshan. Their teachings flourished widely, and their influence extended to later generations. Thus, the lineage of the Baizhang school was firmly established. The Master’s life and deeds are recorded in the *Jingde Chuandeng Lu* and other historical records. His legacy continues to inspire practitioners of the Way.
The verse on the pivot says: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Standing alone with one foot atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak, He snatches the bright pearl from the jaws of the black dragon.
With a single word, he exposes Vimalakīrti’s hidden depths. Upon hearing this, Fengwen struck the desk and praised it as excellent.

Later, he sat in the seat of enlightenment (the patriarchal hall) for seven times, and his transformation spread throughout the land. Those who succeeded to his Dharma were all like dragons and elephants. Ascending the hall, he raised [the following] case: Fayan said:
While preaching the Dharma to the people on the Imperial Street at Shengyuan Pavilion, the Master said: "Do you all know?

On the night of the third watch, the Buddha of Chongshou Temple laughed aloud once while performing a ritual self-sacrifice upon the temple roof. The Vajra at the main gate shouted, 'What are you laughing at?
I laugh because throughout this vast and boundless universe, people merely waste their years and pass their time in a daze, devoid of virtue and wisdom."
Do not practice. This waste of food and clothing will suddenly land you with Old Man Yama; a disaster, a disaster! Ascending the hall, he said:
"The withered mulberry tree knows the wind from heaven; the sea water knows the cold of heaven. The place where the Golden-Colored Dhūta perceives is not true;
he stays in Mount Kukkuṭapāda to keep watch over his robes and bowl. The three thousand great parables and eight hundred minor parables are much like mud."
Washing away the soil of inner delusion over forty-nine years and more than three hundred and sixty assemblies, even the kingdom of Magadha still leaves something to be desired.
Though Deshan and Linji were indeed great men, how can they compare to the King of Kaśmīra, who severed them in two with a single stroke of his sword?
"If there were someone today whose nostrils reach the heavens, where would this mountain monk’s life be?

After a long silence, he said: "Peace was originally brought about by the generals; yet we do not permit the generals to witness that peace. He ascended the hall and said: "Last night the cold frost was piercing;
the Yellow River froze solid. The iron ox of Shanzhou broke its back. Everyone says that Nüwa melted stones to patch the heavens."
"But alas, there is a single opening in the northwest. Now, if I were to fill it up for him, I fear that people throughout the great earth would have no place to breathe.

For now, I shall leave this one aperture so that the people of the great earth may breathe through it. *Chan* (Investigate). Ascending the hall, he said: "Empty clarity illuminates itself; there is no need to exert mental effort.
When those of superior capacity see this, it is like a meal of ghosts and spirits. When those of middling or inferior capacity attain it, their wild minds are suddenly stilled."
[Pause. Furthermore, there is one person whom you must absolutely avoid mentioning. Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Light penetrates the sun and moon;

brightness and darkness cannot contain it. Wisdom transcends the holy and the ordinary; the worthy and the foolish do not pass through it. Therefore it is said: 'It is not found by lowering the head in thought.
[After a long silence,] he asked: 'What is it? Ascending the hall, [he said: 'On the summit of Mount Sumeru, the golden bell is not struck. Before the Pippala Rock...'

There is no assembly of people. This mountain monk rides backward upon the Buddha hall; everyone puts on their straw sandals backward. In the morning they roam Mount Tandi; in the evening they arrive at Mount Luofu.
As for the staff and the needle-case, take them up yourself. A monk asked, "The heavens cannot cover him, and the earth cannot support him.

I wonder, who is this person? The Master said, "Dig the ground deep and bury him. The monk said, "Will this person receive peace? The Master said, "He will not receive it. The monk said, "Why not? The Master said, "Because he has already been buried."
“Even when you push it away, there is still nothing. He said, “It is like adding mud on top of the earth. Question: “Does a great practitioner of the Way still possess cause and effect?
He said: “I have only heard of people becoming ghosts; I have never seen a crane become an immortal. Question: “How about the ancients then? He said: [Silence].
Furthermore, recall the previous dialogue. [The Master] asked: "What is the device of the ancient Buddhas? He replied: "Attained. [The Master] asked:
"How was it before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? He replied: "The Yangtze River has no sixth month. [The Master] said: "And after he saw him? He replied:
"Spring comes once every year. In the meditation hall, he questioned a monk: "A handless man can box; a tongueless man can speak. Suddenly—"
However, a person without hands strikes a person without a tongue; what can a person without a tongue say? He also said:

"The soul of Shu cries out through the night; the quail and the *diāo* bird wail all night long. The Gate of Perfect Penetration stands wide open; for what reason is there a barrier between clouds and mud?
In his later years, he lived at Shanshan Hermitage in Chiyang due to illness. His disciple Zhicai, who was residing at Foyue Monastery in Linping, welcomed him back.
The attendant Sōjō had not yet returned. The Master urged him to hurry back. When Sōjō reached the temple gate, the Master had already written a verse for the assembly and was reclining on his bed.
Sōjō asked, "The egg-shaped stupa is now complete; what is the ultimate matter? The Master raised his fist and showed it to him, then pushed his pillow aside and passed away peacefully.
The verse said: "The red sun shines upon Fusang; Cold clouds veil Mount Hua. Three watches have passed."

Iron Encircling Mountains. He snapped the horns of the Azure Dragon. His lifespan was seventy-two years; he spent forty-six summer retreats. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the plain to the east of the monastery.
The Master once established one hundred questions to test scholars; two are recorded here.

Furthermore, he compiled the causes and conditions of the awakening of venerable masters of antiquity and the present, titled the *Tongming Ji* (Collection of Penetrating Clarity), which circulated widely in the world. During the Chongning era, he was posthumously honored with the title "Vibrant" (*Zhen*).
The Great Master [Zongmi] cited the discourse of Chan Master Xiansheng of Mount Junshan in Yuezhou, who said: "The Great Square has no exterior; it encompasses the ten voids.

The Ultimate Principle does not take form; it perfectly fuses the three temporal dimensions. Transcending names and appearances, its wondrous essence is fully manifest, standing far beyond past and present."
The true mechanism is uniquely revealed. Grasping the dragon pearl, one reflects all things; things flow with radiance.
Casting the precious sword, one sweeps through the void; the void and the sky finally reach their end. If held fast, Makhadeva shuts his room and Vimalakīrti silences his words;
if let go, Shide shakes his head and Hanshan claps his hands. But tell me, whose realm is this? He picks up his staff, strikes once, and says:
"At the moment of blinking an eye or raising an eyebrow, rely on you to look closely.
During the Qingli era, Huijin, the kitchen steward of Shuiyue Monastery on Mount Dongting in Pingjiang Prefecture, went to Mingzhou to rely upon Mingjue.
Upon hearing the story of lifting Mount Sumeru, he silently attained a realization. One day, wishing to go and inquire after him, he encountered him in the palace courtyard.
Juexian asked, "What is your name? He replied, "Huijin. Juexian said, "Who bestowed this gold upon you? He replied, "I shall go to the abbot’s quarters shortly to express my gratitude.
Juexian said, "What about right now? He replied, "In this place, even Master Juexian cannot exist. Juexian then desisted. Thereupon, the assembly...

He was highly esteemed by those he encountered. He was appointed to oversee the Xiangji (Fragrant Accumulation) Monastery. Later, when it was time for him to take his leave, Sengjue composed a verse to see him off, saying:

"A light boat on the wild waters, sailing at will through diverging streams; The autumn light is inexhaustible—who else would strive to capture it? Gripping pine branches as oars, one has not yet reached the point of breaking willow twigs."
Parting gifts—how could they ever suffice? The surging waves of a hundred rivers flow on in empty vastness.
On another day, he again sent a verse, saying: "The old monk’s withered vine is divided into many parts; At the ends of the earth, there is no companion, yet the Way remains.
Reflecting on the events of the Longshuo era, The lofty spirit of carrying stones is not easily discussed. (These two verses and the letter were inscribed upon the "Water-Moon" [stone]).
Chan Master Yunju Xiaoshun of Nankang Commandery, successor to Chan Master Dongshan Xiaocong (the words regarding his entry into the Way are found in the *Xu deng lu*), ascended the hall and said:
"To hear mention of the two words 'Buddha-dharma' is already to defile one's ears and eyes. Before you have even stepped through the gate of Yunju, look well beneath your own heels."
"Thirty blows! Although it is thus, he still exerts himself to the utmost for the sake of the assembly. He ascended the hall and said: "Jiashan addressed the assembly, saying:
'Apprehend the old monk at the tips of the hundred grasses; recognize the Sage in the midst of the bustling marketplace.

Yunju, however, is not like this: the wife rocks the shuttle with a *ya-ya* sound; the child plays with his mouth, making a *guo-guo* noise. He ascended the hall and said: "In various quarters, there are those who play..."

Grasping the snake’s head, pulling the tiger’s tail, leaping across the great ocean, and concealing one’s body amidst the edges of a sword—here at Yunju, we wash our feet in hot water on a freezing day, sleep with our socks off at night, and fashion our own straw sandals at dawn. Then, the wind blows and the fence collapses.
He called for laborers to split bamboo and bind [the coffin] upright.

Chan Master Fachang Yiyu of Longxing Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Beichan Zhixian, was a native of Gaoting in Linzhang. His clan was the Lin family; he renounced worldly life in his youth.

He was from the Jia family and received ordination at Chongfu Monastery in Jun County. Possessing great ambition, he traveled to various regions after receiving full precepts, becoming renowned within the monastic community.
Zen Master Fushan Yuan once pointed him out to others, saying, "This is a model for those who study while traveling. He then took his leave of Yuan.
He visited the abbot of Bājiā Hermitage and also visited various renowned masters such as Yuántōng and Xìnghuà (the records of their dialogues are found in the *Sēngbǎozhuàn*).

He remained at Běichán for the longest period; there, the dynamic interplay between master and disciple reached its peak excellence for the time. Later, he went to the West Mountain region, where the Shuānglǐng area was secluded and profound.
He stayed there for three years before finally accepting the invitation from Fǎchāng. Entering the hall, he said: "If you withdraw a thousand steps..."
"Chic! If you were to sprout a bud right where you stand, I would hide my body while revealing my shadow.
If you were to pick up pebbles from a spring pond, I would scatter bright pearls.
It would become such that water could not splash it and wind could not enter, like a solid iron hammer without a hole. Now tell me, does Fachang have any way to benefit others? Thereupon—
It is said: "A sharp blade may cut the flesh and the wound will still heal; but words that wound a person leave resentment that does not fade.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring mountains are green, the spring waters are lush. A single dream of the Southern Ko. At dawn, I take up my staff and stride out through the pine gate.
Everywhere, the peach blossoms are fragrant and rich. This brings to mind the old Master Lingyun of days past—after thirty years, there was nowhere to be found. Like...
Now everyone vies with one another to pluck the willow blossoms; red fragrance fills the ground, yet no one sweeps it up.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "If I hold it up, you immediately call this 'first illumination, then function.
If I set it down, you immediately call this 'first function, then illumination. If I cast it away, you immediately call this 'illumination and function simultaneous. Suddenly—"
He held it up but did not let go. Where would you go to speculate?

Even if you were to understand it with such clarity and decisiveness, if you encountered Linji or Deshan, your forehead would still strike the ground. But tell me, what excellence does he possess? After a long silence:

He said: "Having once crossed the great ocean, one no longer boasts of water; except for Sumeru, there is no mountain. Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: "The earth is covered in vast snow;
though spring arrives, it remains as cold as ever. To speak of Chan or speak of the Way is easy; to become a Buddha or a Patriarch is difficult.
Fachang said: "The earth is covered in vast snow; yet when spring arrives, it is no longer cold. In the end, becoming a Buddha is easy—it is rather speaking of Chan that is difficult."
Zen is difficult. When people hear such talk, they give a cold laugh from the bridge of their noses and say, "What is so difficult?
Reaching India in the morning and returning to Tang China in the evening; clouds rising on the southern mountain and rain falling on the northern mountain;
licorice is sweet and Huangbo is bitter; fish enter the deep abyss and birds nest in high trees. They pick up their staffs, [claiming to see] the eyes of Bodhidharma, and then set them down.
"A pearl! Śākyamuni’s nostrils! If this were Chan, even a foul-mouthed old woman from a village of three households could explain it.
But as for becoming a Buddha—that remains to be seen. Now tell me, what after all is Chan? He then said, "It is such that sweat breaks out on one's forehead.
He ascended the hall [and said]: "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, the stages and positions of the Three Vehicles, liberation, and the Dharma-body—"
This is the leftover rice of beggars. When the Patriarch came from the West, he pointed directly to the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature one becomes a Buddha;
this is precisely the kind of food used for sacrifices to spirits and ghosts. If you were to see it, it would be like entering a region infested with *gū* poison;
do not even look at it, for if you look, calamity will arise. Here at Fachang, there is a different kind of food, which we have never brought forth in the ordinary course of things. Today—

Having no other choice, he intended to provide offerings for all those present. He said, "In the future, when you travel to various regions and enjoy abundant provisions, you must remember the offerings made by Fachang today.
He then drew a circle, threw down his staff, and descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "At midnight, who has snatched away the black hen? The stone woman has been pointlessly subjected to this scrutiny. By the decree of the Empty King, a swift search is ordered;

the Mind-only immediately becomes the commander-in-chief of the army. Yunmen leads the long march of the Mui-shan ranks, arraying the banners of the five positions and deploying the spears and crossbows of the three mysteries.
Yaoshan wields the blade, Qingyuan carries the axe, and Shigong bends the bow."
Heoshan beats the drum: the battle lines are arrayed at Snowy Ridge like a long serpent; the troops are stationed at Huangbo like soaring tigers.

The wooden horse is cooked with its fur on; the clay ox is boiled with its horns intact. Rewards are distributed to the three armies; the host is gratified. They cut through the entanglements and issue the proclamations.
They cross the sea and raise dust; they traverse the mountains and scatter earth. They strike the dark gate and clear the narrow paths. How many common folk suffer such hardship! None.
The oceans of peripheral lands vie with one another in their bustle; among the sages and ordinary folk of the three realms, there is no place to be found.

No place to be found—do you still not know? Last night the clouds withdrew and the heavens were vast; as before, it cried out at the high tree, accompanied by the moon. Ascending the hall, he said: "When idle, I simply sit like this.
Clapping my hands, who can join in the response? Turning my head, I suddenly see the Winnowing Basket Star; the Water-Moon Guanyin knows how to push the millstone."
[The Master] clapped his hands once and said, "Do you understand? Though the eighty-year-old elder has white hair, look closely and you will not see the features of an old man.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Today, Fachang opens the furnace for the winter retreat. Not a single wandering monk is here;

there are only eighteen eminent practitioners sitting in meditation around the fire with their mouths sealed. This is not because our rules are strict or difficult, but simply to spare you all from further talk."

A fall! Even if one’s mouth were like a scale-weight, one would still not escape being exposed by the lantern. Not realizing that the Way is beyond merit and achievement, you recklessly cultivate causes and realize fruits.
[The Master] shouts: "If you can but turn the light back for a single thought-moment, you will certainly be liberated from the shackles of the Three Vehicles."

Chan Master Huanglong Nan arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "Seizing the clouds and grasping the waves, they are as numerous as hemp seeds; once the coppery eyes are struck, they immediately blossom.
Aside from the head and horns of the Yellow Dragon, everything else is nothing but a red-spotted snake. This is the small monastery of Fachang.
The road is distant and the mountains remote; the scenery is desolate and sparse. Rarely do travelers venture here, yet I dare say that Master Huanglong has deigned to grace us with his presence.
This not only adds luster to the springs and rocks, but also brings joy to both humans and devas.

Yet, as clouds move and rain falls from ancient times to the present, it remains a pity that in the smelting furnaces there are still many pieces of dull iron, while at the gate of the skilled physician, those who are ill continue to seek healing.
Indeed. To cure an illness, one must seek a divine medicine; to dissolve stubbornness, one must rely on a golden hammer. Here at Fachang, there are several teachers who are like "stump-rooted" trees.
Those who are ill have their disease deep in the vital organs; those who are stubborn have their obstinacy entered into the very marrow of their bones.
Had it not been for the arrival of the old man Huanglong, they would all have lived in vain and died in vain. He picks up his staff and says: "Do you understand? Grinding flour..."
"Though he eats the wheat of other lands, when he sings, he is still a man of the Imperial Capital. A monk asked, "What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished?
The Master said, "Then you must polish it. The monk said, "I do not know how to apply myself to this. What is the starting point? The Master said, "Where is the mirror?
The monk then drew a circle. The Master struck him and said, "This lacquer bucket! You do not even recognize a common brick! [Question] Two... (text fragment)

"What is it like when the dragons struggle for the pearl? He said, "Fachang makes a small exit and meets with a great encounter. [The Master] said, "If suddenly the torrential stream overflows and the mountain peaks topple, what then?
The Master struck him. On a winter night, while eating fruit with Senior Seat Huigan, the Master picked up an orange and said, "How does this flavor compare to that of Huanglong?
He said, "One must taste it further before one can know. The Master said, "This is to test people."
"At the point of ultimate truth, one knows the sound as soon as the mouth opens. He said, "The Chan masters of this degenerate age are mostly empty and seldom substantial.
Again, picking up a bag, he asked, "How do you taste this? [The monk] said, "It must be the Master himself who can do so. [Baizhang] said, "A single bag is already beyond what can be managed.
[The monk] said, "To yield to others is not to be a fool. Once, while drinking soup on New Year's Eve, he sighed, saying, "In the past, at dawn..."
[The guest] asked, "In the past, at Beichan, they celebrated the New Year by roasting a white ox from the open fields. What arrangements have you made for this year’s New Year celebration, Master?
The Master said, "The snow covers the mountains in white; the spring wind presses against the door, cold. [The guest] asked, "What will the assembly eat?
The Master said, "Do not disdain its plainness and lack of flavor; one full meal can dispel the hunger of ten thousand kalpas. [The guest] asked, "I wonder, who is it that eats this?"
He set aside his discourse and said, "You shameless fellow! You do not even know where you have come from. When Chief Seat Zhe arrived, the Master said, "The mountain is deep and the road is far;
why trouble yourself to visit? Zhe replied, "Within the Way of benevolence and righteousness, this is not considered an extra burden.
The Master asked, "What have you brought with you? Zhe crossed his hands and stepped forward. The Master said, "Is it only this? Or is there something else? Zhe unfolded his sitting mat. The Master—
[The Master] said, "In the beginning there was a slight discrepancy; in the end, he could not hit the mark. Zhe said, "Please allow me to attend to my own business.
[The Master] asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "Yunju. [The Master] asked, "How is it at the summit of that peak? He replied, "Many people harbor doubts about it.
The Master struck his staff on the ground and said, "How does Hongjue’s nostrils compare to this? He replied, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated. [The Master] said, "This monk..."
He did not even recognize the *huatou*. [Zhaozhou] asked, "What does the Master ask? [Cuiyan] said, "I am asking you about the nostrils of Hongjue.
[Zhaozhou] said, "And yet you say you do not recognize the *huatou*. [Cuiyan] said, "It is no mistake for me to be a disciple of Cuiyan.

One day, Zhaozhou asked, "I wish to hear one or two instances of the Master’s usual instructions and opportunities for awakening within the meditation hall. [Cuiyan] said, "Drawing the horizontal bone from within the dark; clearly..."
Zhongzuo was sitting with his tongue out. "How about you? he asked. Zhongzuo replied, "Master, you are originally a descendant of the Yunmen lineage;
why do you cite an anecdote from the Dongshan tradition? The Master then kicked out a shoe, and Zhongzuo ceased speaking.
When Chan Master Haitang Xin arrived and sat down, the Master said, "Lately, the Dharma assemblies have become truly flourishing. Haitang replied, "Every household contemplates Avalokiteśvara."
[The Master] asked, "Is there still a 'man-eating lion'? [The monk] said, "In a forge, dull iron is still plentiful. [The Master] asked, "I have heard that in your quarters there is the 'fist-talk.
Is this true? [The monk] said, "Do not broadcast family scandals abroad. The Master picked up a hoe and asked, "How does this of mine compare?
[The monk] said, "The real does not conceal the false. [The Master] asked, "Within the realm of birth and death, which one would you employ? [The monk] said, "..."

"There is no need for the labor of hanging up a stone mirror; when dawn comes, the rooster will crow of itself. [The Master] said, "If you seek a person like this, it will be as far off as a donkey's year.
When Xu Gong Xi of the Longtu was still a commoner, he associated with the Master, engaging in the joyful pursuit of the Dharma.

On the day before his passing, the Master composed a verse and left it to him, saying: "This year I am seventy-seven; if I were to go out, I would have to choose an auspicious day. Last night I consulted the tortoise shell—"
Brother Ji of Mingzhou reported this news. Upon reading the verse, Xu was struck with awe and invited Chan Master Lingyuan Qing to go together with him.

At that time, the Master was sitting in his quarters; he instructed the administrators regarding the affairs of the monastery, saying, "I have resided on this mountain for twenty-three years, protecting and cherishing the communal property, attending to it myself at all times.
Now I am departing. You all must apply yourselves with vigor. Having finished speaking, he raised his staff.
He said, "Now tell me, to whom shall this be entrusted? Xu and Lingyuan both held their breath in anticipation.
He then cast aside his staff, lay down upon his bed, rested his head upon his arm, and passed away.
Chan Master Guangyin Zheyao of Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The King occupies the precious throne; Hu and Han share the same customs.
The five knots are untied, the three poisons are shattered, and the Buddha Hall stands upside down. I do not ask you about the phrase for 'concealing the body,' but tell me:

how do you express the single word that transcends it? He held up his staff and said: "The spring wind opens the bamboo door; the night rain drips upon the heart of the flower. He ascended the hall again.
The Way of the ancients was simply this: I fear that if one’s mind as a monk is not resolved, then even if one’s mind as a monk is resolved, one has still lost out to the monk.

Furthermore, what is the "resolved mind" of you venerable seniors? After a long silence, he said: "The fisherman sleeps soundly; the spring pool is vast. The white heron does not fly; the boat drifts of its own accord.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He replied, "East of Chang’an, west of Luo."
Yangxi said, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "The Fuzhou olive is pointed at both ends. A questioner asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?
He replied, "Hiding in crags and dwelling by ravines. The questioner asked, "How is it after he appeared in the world? He replied, "The mountains in front and the mountains behind."
Chan Master Zhengjue Benyi,
the first generation patriarch of Zhikai in Dongjing and dharma heir of Chan Master Kaixian Shengxian (the preface is found in the *Xu deng lu*), ascended the hall and said:
"I recall that when I was seven years old, I obtained a Dharma gate at a village school. It transcends emotion and is free from views; it is most wondrous and most profound.
Since it first permeated my spirit more than sixty years ago, I have kept it within me. Today I shall bring it forth to announce it universally to the great assembly.
If you wish to transmit and uphold it, you should listen attentively. He then said: "The plowing of the fields on the cold plain is finished; The calf is led as one carries firewood upon his back."
Return. This night’s single brazier fire, the clothing upon the bodies of the whole family. All you practitioners of Zen:
when meeting people, do not speak of this mistakenly. Entering the hall: Observe within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the vast primordial void;
every person has feet—to walk, they walk; to stay, they stay—not dependent on another. Each individual has a mouth—to open it, they open it; to close it, they close it...

It is complete. How could it rely on any external power? At this very moment, it is neither past nor present; it is neither principle nor phenomenon; it is neither ordinary nor holy; it is neither delusion nor enlightenment.
It encompasses all lands of the *sahasra-lokadhātu* and enshrouds the two polarities of heaven and earth. The Tathāgatas of the three periods cannot analyze it;
the great patriarchs of the various schools cannot proclaim it. Even Deshan and Linji, with their staffs and shouts, would not dare to employ them.

Proceed. Śāriputra and Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra possess wisdom and eloquence; there is no gate through which one may fathom them. Nevertheless, even so, when arriving here, you must have sinews within your eyes.
If there are no sinews in the eyes, one is the same as one born blind from heaven.

Furthermore, there must be blood beneath the skin; only then can one know pain and know itchiness. If one does not know pain and itchiness, how is one any different from earth or wood? Even if you possess eyes and sinews, and know...
To know pain as itchiness is precisely when one should beat straw sandals and travel on foot. If you go to various places, do not let them break the staff used for universal pilgrimage by Luopu.
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'Receiving beings and benefiting life is most exquisite. But an outsider's grandson is ultimately unworthy;
his own descendants will surely come, and their application will be perfectly suited. Do you all understand, monks? It is like vegetables."
The garden wall has collapsed; it shall be rebuilt once the weather clears. The fences of the guest quarters have been pierced by rain; they shall be repaired after the downpour.

When the buildings leak, they are mended as best as possible. All the descendants, great and small, are full of refined elegance. Ascending the hall, he raised an example, citing Master Xian: "Chilly! Chilly! The fire in the earthen stove is warm.
Sitting idly upon the *pútán*, one says that Kāśyapa was not right and speaks of Bodhidharma’s groundlessness. This and that—necessarily..."
Generally speaking, the Master called to the assembly, saying: "Where was it that Kāśyapa was not right? Where did Bodhidharma act without cause?
If you can examine this thoroughly, those two elders will be left looking quite foolish.
If you cannot examine it, do not say thirty years from now that you were not deceived by others. A monk asked, "What is the Way? He replied, "The dragon’s roar in the golden [clouds]."
Ding. "The tiger roars in the *dantian*. He asked, "What is it to be one among those on the Way? He replied, "Exhaling the old and inhaling the new.

He asked, "How far apart are the Way and those on the Way? He replied, "A skeleton crane atop a precipice; its flavor soars to heaven, yet it feeds on the rice of the common people. Question: [The text ends here.]
"What is the Buddha? He replied, "Rising in the east and sinking in the west. "What is the Way? He replied, "Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down.
"What is the Dharma? He replied, "You ask and I answer. "What is Chan? He replied, "Neither square nor round. He asked again.
"If one goes thus, what then? He said, "A person of keen intelligence is hard to find.
This was Chan Master Jingxuan Dayang Ming'an, the tenth generation descendant of Qingyuan (the sixth generation of Dongshan), and a successor in the lineage of [Chan Master] Daoyuan.
Chan Master Qingpou of Xingyang in Yingzhou was a man of unknown origins. He once served as the garden head for Dayang.
While he was planting melons, Dayang asked, "When will the sweet melons be ripe? He replied, "They are already overripe right now. Dayang said, "Pick out the sweet ones and bring them here.
He replied, "For whom would they be eaten? Dayang said, "For those who do not enter the garden. He asked, "I wonder, who are those who do not enter the garden?"
"Will you eat it back? He replied, "Do you recognize him? Yang said, "Even though I do not recognize him, I cannot help but give it to him.
Yang laughed and departed. While staying at Xingyang, he ascended the hall and said: "The Great Way from the West is in principle beyond all negations."
To strike the vital point within a phrase is entirely to deviate from the subtle intent. To stop where one has not yet reached the end is to bring shame upon the ancestors;

how much more so to speak at length—what benefit would that bring? Nevertheless, as it is said, "Matters are never absolute. For now, let us open a single thread of the path within the gate of proclaiming the Teaching, and let everyone deliberate together.
A monk stepped forward and asked: "When Sāgara emerges from the sea, heaven and earth tremble; face-to-face, he presents himself directly."
“What is the matter? He said, “The Golden-Winged Bird King presides over the universe; who among them is the one who emerges? He asked, “If one suddenly encounters the moment of emerging, what then?
He said, “Like the hawk snatching the pigeon, you do not realize it; only when verified before the skull does one know the truth.
He said, “In that case, I shall fold my hands at my chest and step back three paces. He said, “The Seat of Mount Sumeru.”
"Release the little turtle; do not wait until you suffer the mark of a painted forehead once more. A monk asked, "Where have all the sages of the past gone?
He replied, "The moon shines upon a thousand rivers in stillness; a single lamp glows at the bottom of the sea. Minister Zheng Jinbu asked, "When will you open the hall for teaching, Master?
He replied, "Without passing through the kalpas of the *asaṃkhyeya*; before the birth of sun and moon."
When Chan Master Ru of Luofu in Huizhou arrived at Dayang, Dayang asked, "Where are you from, Senior Monk?
He replied, "Yizhou. Dayang said, "How far is it from here? He replied, "Five thousand li. Dayang said, "As you have come this way, have you ever trodden upon it?
He replied, "I have not trodden upon it. Dayang said, "Do you know how to fly through the air? He replied, "I do not know how to fly through the air. Dayang said, "Then how did you get here?"
[Yangshan] arrived there and said, "At every step, one is not lost to the directions; throughout the entire body, there is no place for discrimination.
[Yunyan] replied, "The Sage’s mind cannot be apprehended; how could samādhi manifest a name? Yangshan said, "So it is! So it is!
You should believe that this is the total manifestation of the fundamental essence, where principle and phenomena are non-dual. Guard and maintain this well yourself."
Furthermore, a monk asked Chan Master Jianming Jichong of Fuzhou, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
He replied, "This question is not in vain. The monk asked, "What is the realm of Dongchan? He replied, "The water of samādhi has never left its old shore;
how would the red dust of the world dare descend upon the waves?"
A monk asked Chan Master Baima Guichun of Xiangyang Prefecture, "What is it like when a tortoise hides its six limbs?
He replied, "An arrow and bow inside a cloth bag. He asked, "What is the great purport of the Buddha-dharma? He replied, "A good dog wearing a collar."
Chan Master Shencheng of Fuyan in Tanzhou was once visited by a Chief Minister (whose surname has been lost). The Minister asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master pointed to the cypress tree at the edge of the courtyard and showed it to him. He did this three times. The Chief Minister attained realization and composed a verse, saying:
"Emerging and disappearing amidst floating clouds, filling the vast void; From the beginning, the true form has never possessed a single speck of dust. Layer upon layer..."
When asked about the meaning of the Westward Transmission, he simply pointed to a single cypress tree in front of the courtyard.
Zen Master Yiqing of Touzi in Shuzhou was a native of Qingshe. His clan name was Li (the *Xudeng lu* states it was Wang, which is incorrect).

At only seven years of age, he was exceptionally gifted. He went to Miaoxiang Temple to leave the household life, passed the scriptural examination to receive ordination, and studied the *Śataśāstra*. Before long, he sighed:
He said, "The path of the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* is so remote; what benefit is there in exhausting oneself? Thereupon, he entered Luoyang and spent five years studying the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

His understanding of its meaning was like stringing together pearls. Once, while reading the verses of the Bodhisattvas of the Forest of Trees (*Vana-vyūha*), he reached the passage on the "intrinsic nature of the mind" (*citta-svabhāva*) and suddenly realized:
"The Dharma transcends words; how can it be expounded? He immediately abandoned his seat among the followers of the school. At that time, Chan Master Yuanjian resided at Huisheng Rock.
One night, he dreamed that he was keeping a handsome, blue hawk; this was an auspicious omen. When the Master arrived, Yuanjian received him with due ceremony and invited him to stay for three years.

One day, Yuanjian asked, "When an outsider questioned the Buddha, he did not ask about words, nor did he ask about wordlessness. The World-Honored One remained silent for a long time—how do you understand this?
As the Master was about to respond, Yuanjian covered his mouth. At that moment, the Master attained clear awakening and prostrated himself. Yuanjian said:
"Have you wondrously awakened to the profound mechanism? He replied, "Even if there were, it must be spat out.
At that time, Attendant Zī was standing by the side and said, "Today Master Qing Huayan has recovered from his illness with a good sweat. The Master looked back and said, "Shut your dog’s mouth!
If you chatter further, I shall immediately vomit [your words]. He served him diligently for another three years, then took his leave. Master Jian bestowed upon him the robes and sandals of Dayang.

He sent a verse with it, saying: "Mount Sumeru stands in the vast void; The sun and moon revolve as its attendants. The myriad peaks gradually lean upon one another, While the white clouds undergo their transformations.
The wind rises through the thickets of Shaolin; The bamboo blinds of Caoxi are rolled up. The golden phoenix roosts in the dragon’s nest; How could the imperial moss be crushed by a carriage wheel?
He further recommended the Chan Master Yiyuan Tongxiu. When the Master arrived at Qixian, he had no questions to ask.
He did nothing but indulge in sleep. An attendant reported to Xiu, "There is a monk in the hall who sleeps every day; we should apply the monastic regulations. Xiu asked, "Who is it?
The attendant replied, "It is the Senior Monk Yiqing. Xiu said, "Not yet; wait until I have investigated the matter. Xiu then took up his staff and entered the hall.
Seeing the Master sleeping soundly, he struck the meditation platform and rebuked him, saying, "There is no idle food here for you, Senior Monk!"
[The monk] ate and went to sleep. The Master said, "Wait, what do you intend for me to do? [The monk] said, "Why not go practice Chan?

[The Master] said, "Fine food is not fit for a person already full to eat. [The monk] said, "But there are many who are unwilling to accept your seat. [The Master] said, "I shall wait until they are willing."
"What can he possibly do? [Fengxue] asked. [Wuzu] replied, "Whom have you, Venerable, ever met? He said, "Fushan. [Fengxue] remarked, "No wonder he is so stubborn and unruly.
Thereupon, they shook hands and laughed together, then returned to the abbot’s quarters. From this point on, his reputation for the Way became widespread.

In the sixth year of the Xining era, he arrived at Longshu, where both monastics and laypeople welcomed him to reside at Baiyun. Subsequently, he moved to Touzi, thereby fulfilling the legacy of Chan Master Ciji.
Record of the Ascending to the Hall. He called to the assembly, saying: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a phoenix soaring to the clouds, leaving no trace behind;
or a ram with its horns caught in a tree, from where can one seek its tracks? A golden dragon does not dwell in the cold pool; how could a jade hare nestle within the shadow of the moon?
Should host and guest be established, they must shake their heads beyond the world of Vipaśyin. Thus he spoke these words of question and answer.

"Chen! He then raised his voice from the side of the dark path as a chant. "If you can do this, you are still only halfway there. Look even more intently; there is no need for us to meet. Ascending the hall, he said:
"When the Dharma-gate is raised, both ordinary beings and sages leave no trace. When the gates of the multi-storied pavilion open, one meets another at a separate door.
Even if one attains awakening upon rolling up the curtain, how can one avoid being a bystander? Meeting spring blossoms amidst peach trees only increases the burden on one's eyes."
"Illness. Thus the ancients said: "The path that goes upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages.

"Virtuous ones," [the Master continued], "since it is not transmitted, why did the Iron Ox gallop across to the land of Silla? He then shouted, "Those who attain it must know the secret alarm in the dark!
A monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? He replied: "Before the time of Vipaśyin Buddha..."
[The Master] drew an arrow and shot it so that it pierced through two layers of mountains. He asked, "What is the matter that has been transmitted?

[The monk] said, "It is entirely because of the moon over Huai that the spring of Yingyang can be illuminated. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then you have entered the water and seen the long man [the Dragon King].

[The monk] said, "I only know that the jade of Jing is extraordinary; how could I discern the heart of the King of Chu? The monk bowed. The Master struck him with his whisk and said again, "There is more to ask."
Is this so? If not, both sides will suffer. On the first day of the fifth month in the fifth year of the Yuanfeng era, at midnight, he took up his brush and wrote this verse:
"Presiding over two monasteries, there is nothing to assist the Way. Take care, all you people; there is no need to seek further."
He cast down his writing brush and passed away in stillness. His body was cremated, from which many sacred relics were obtained, including five-colored *śarīra*.

In an intercalary month, these were enshrined together with his remains in a stupa at Sanfeng Hermitage to the north of the temple. He was fifty-one years of age and thirty-seven years since his ordination.
