Ascending the hall, he said: "In the heavens there is no Maitreya; on the earth there is no Maitreya. Smash through the Great..."
"Empty space—how can one seek it and not find it? He lowered one foot and said, "Where have the great assembly gone?
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the gate of the Patriarchs, no person passes; it is a precipice deeper than a pit of ten thousand fathoms. To lower the hand cannot be done in vain;
let the green moss grow upon the hall. Ascending the hall, he said: "If one speaks of the Dharma as an offering..."
"Great assembly, you cannot avoid the falling out of your eyebrows and whiskers.

If you say that providing worldly offerings to the great assembly leads to entering hell like a shot arrow—setting aside these two paths, tell me, what is Baoning’s extraordinary teaching today? A three-inch tongue has no place to use;
a pair of empty hands do not form a fist. Ascending the hall, he said: "The mechanism of 'biting the bullet' is still dull."
The point facing forward is not yet intimate; Nanda’s ten faces and ten eyes stir. The formless numinous light eclipses the sun’s orb.
*Du!* Ascending the hall, he raised his staff and said: “Gong, Shang, Jue, Zhi, Yu; Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth.”

He struck the desk once and said, "The good and bad fortune of this hexagram will be discerned after three days; wait and see. Ascending the hall, he said, "Look, look! This mountain monk is going to the Hell of Plucked Tongues.
He pulled his tongue with his hand and cried out, "A-ya! A-ya! Ascending the hall, he said, "That which belonged to the ancients is used by the people of today;
that which belongs to the people of today was practiced by the ancients. There is no front or back between past and present; how many people have there been throughout all time?"
"Know! Jā-mi. Nineteen and twenty-nine meet, yet they do not reach out their hands.
He ascended the hall, drew a circle with both hands, split it open, pressed his knees together, and said: "The whole lump cannot be split; three people share only two.
There is truly no flavor to be found. Who can swallow this? If you can swallow it, then so be it. If you cannot swallow it, do not be confused."
[He] acted. Ascending the hall, he said: "Having hands and feet, yet no front or back; even those with clear eyes cannot see it.
Heaven rotates to the left, earth turns to the right. He struck his knee and said: "A gust of west wind comes, and two or three leaves fall. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The wind whistles through the branches, the rain breaks the clods of earth. At dawn, upon the pillow, the song of the oriole shatters. The frogs and earthworms all cry out at once. Miaode.
None of them would dare to do so. None of them would dare. Three would form a cluster; four would make a troop.

Deeply hidden and elegantly poised, drifting and soaring, they would travel north, south, east, and west, gathering pear blossoms and plum blossoms until they had a string for themselves and a string for another.
Again, at the invitation of Baoning, he ascended the hall. He clapped his hands three times, pointed to his mouth, shook his hand three times, and then descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it. To speak of it is to give rise to horns. Great assembly, the horns have grown!
Is it a cow? Is it a horse? Ascending the hall, he said: "Unoutflowed and truly pure—how could there be anything further within this?"
[He] allowed for other things. He shouted, saying: "A fine man is unwilling to act; he must insist on lying in excrement. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"Coming thus, it overturns the ravines and topples the mountains. Going thus, it fills the ditches and blocks the valleys. To do neither of these—wrong! wrong! Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"Swallowing up heaven and earth, the great earth opens its mouth. Where can one breathe out? Yongjia stayed for one night at Caoxi. Upon arriving...
Even now, you have not yet had a glimpse of it. Ascending the hall, he said: "Ten eyes look; ten fingers point. One is not accomplished; two are not right. Do you understand?
Before the cold hawk has even raised its head, the swift falcon has already soared into the clouds. A monk asked: "In years past, those beyond the clouds all understood;
today, on this very stage, please lend us a brief look. The Master said: "This mountain monk loves anger and does not love joy. The monk said: "A brand-new [turn of events]."
"Sun and moon; the heavens and earth stand apart. He said, "It is as if we have never met. Question: "What is the Buddha? He said:
"The one near the fire is scorched first. Question: "What is the Way? He said: "Sinking into the mud, there are thorns. Question: "What is one who walks upon the Way? He said: [The same as above].
He said, "By all means, do not step on it. Question: "At Vulture Peak they pointed to the moon; at Caoxi they spoke of the moon. I do not know how it is under Baoning.
He said, "Ha! Question: "The former masters said: 'The cold wind withers the fallen leaves; one still rejoices that an old friend has returned.'"
“May I ask who this old friend is? He replied, “The Master of Yangqi passed away long ago.
He said, “At such a time as this, who else could be a true connoisseur? He replied, “The blind village elder nods his head in the dark.
A monk asked, “What is the realm of Baoning? He replied, “The main mountain peak stands upside down. He asked, “What is it like for one within that realm? He replied, “The nose.”
The hole was missing half its side. Question: "What is the Buddha? He said: "One does not perceive the stench of one's own excrement. Question:
"How is it when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water? He said: "Half in shadow, half in light. Question: "And after it has emerged? He said: "Scattered and dispersed."
Chan Master Muzhe Zhenru of Daopei in Tanzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Cuiyan Zhenke.
He was a native of Linchuan and belonged to the Wen clan. Before reaching the age of ten, he paid respects to Vinaya Master Yuanjue of Yong’an in Jianchang;
upon passing his examination of the monastic precepts, he received full ordination. He was upright, simple, and possessed great discernment, dedicating himself to upholding the Dharma.

This was his resolve. Cuiyan, while among the assembly, said: "The Master has been my companion for nearly twenty years; though we live together, I have always honored him with the etiquette due to a teacher.
Cuiyan said to others: "Thirty years hence, this worthy son will surely perform great Buddhist works. After Cuiyan passed away, he was interred in a stupa on West Mountain.
The Master observed a period of mourning for three years, after which he departed to rely upon Huangbo. While traveling through the region of Xiang, he encountered Lord Xie.

The Master Zhishou resided at Tan. Admiring his reputation, the [officials of] Yuelu Mountain welcomed him with formal ceremonies; it was only after several days that he finally accepted. He subsequently moved to Huiguang and later to Miao.
In the first year of the Shaosheng era, he was summoned by imperial decree via the postal service and granted an audience in the Yanhe Hall.

His responses were deemed satisfactory, and he was bestowed with purple robes and the title Zhenru. Shortly thereafter, he was appointed to the Great Xiangguo Temple. Entering the hall, he said: "The ancients said: 'One Śākyamuni...'"
"Two, harmony, and three Buddhas—what else are these but *wande-chou* (empty-headed fools)? Hui-guang does not think so; he says:
'One Śākyamuni, two harmonies, and three Buddhas—all are but *wande-chou*. Do you all know where Hui-guang has landed?
If you do, I grant that you possess iron eyes and copper pupils. If you do not, do not say that it is merely a matter of a few..."
Having braved the perils of wind and waves, my small boat once roamed the Five Lakes. Ascending the hall, he said: "There is no need to think in order to know;
there is no need to deliberate in order to understand. The price of rice in Luling is high; the radishes in Zhenzhou are large. Ascending the hall, he said: "A-la-la!"
"What is this? Reflecting back upon Pòzào Duò, as soon as the staff struck him, he finally realized he had failed me.
With his staff, he struck the incense table once and said, "Duò! Duò! Ascending the hall, he said: "The ten directions gather together;

each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting the Buddha; with an empty mind, one returns having passed the imperial examination. Under Huìguāng’s gate, there is direct transcendence and elevation.
Without passing through the formal stages of the examinations, once you have all arrived here, the winds and clouds are spread across the earth and your fangs and claws are fully formed;
you merely lack the thunderous roar to burn off your tails. Now, for your sakes, I shall strike the sudden thunder.

(He struck the meditation seat with his staff and descended from the seat. A monk asked: "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat upon the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas; why did he not [attain Buddhahood]?"

[The Master] attained the Buddha-way. [A monk] said, "It kills people with suffering. [The Master] asked, "How was it before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? [The Master] said, "The hairs on one's body stand on end.
[The monk] asked, "How was it after he saw him? [The Master] said, "Sweat breaks out on the forehead.

[The monk] asked, "What is the one phrase of the separate transmission outside the teachings? [The Master] said, "It cannot be translated. From the time the Master took his seat until the end, in his private quarters he asked nothing other than this.
The scholar asked about the story of washing the alms bowl. "How do you understand it, Venerable Sir? The monk prepared to respond, whereupon the Master placed his hand upon him and said, "Rest.

On the eighth day of the tenth month in the second year, he spoke a verse to bid farewell to the assembly without any illness. After a long while, he passed away into stillness. The verse says: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
Last night at the third watch, wind and thunder suddenly arose; the clouds dispersed across the vast sky, and the moon sank behind the eastern stream.

During the cremation, relics as large as beans and pecks were found; his eyes, teeth, and fingernails remained uncorrupted. His disciples divided the remains and erected stupas in the capitals of Jing and Tan.

Chan Master Chengxi Yingyue of Shaozhou, a successor of Chan Master Juehai Zanyuan of Jiangshan, was a native of the Dai family from Yihuang in Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "In our school there are no words or phrases;
to labor in search of a path is but toil. The ready-made public case is already manifold; how could one bear to further involve oneself in it?"

He opens the gateway; meeting face-to-face, he directly raises the essential point. What need is there for the bitter suffering of *pāṭha*? *Tu!* Chan Master Faxia of Xuedou in Mingzhou was asked by a monk:
"The person who brings up the matter does not ask about the meaning of the Westward Journey;

I beg the Master to use skillful means to point out the deluded state. The Master said: "A thunderclap passes over one's head, yet one still sleeps. The monk said: "Thank you, Master, for answering my question. The Master said: "Once more—"
Three times he opened his mouth to ask who it was, saying, "How can it be that this student has not yet prostrated? [The Master] said, "Stop being so dull-witted.
This was Chan Master Zhìyuán of Qiónglóng in Píngjiāng Fǔ, a successor of Chan Master Chāoxìn of Dìnghuì Háyìn.
He was a native of that same prefecture; his clan was the Shěn family. Before reaching the age of twenty, he relied upon Néngrén.

Tangqing shaved his head and studied the teachings of the Tiantai school. He was entrusted with the translation of Sanskrit texts and visited the chambers of Chan Master Ganlu Fu and Baoning Zhenjing, where he first attained initial enlightenment.
Later, he relied upon Haiyin; one day, while drawing water and washing his robes, he suddenly achieved great awakening.

His correspondence with the Imperial Seal was as if joined by a tally; he remained in attendance for two intercalary years. He subsequently led the assembly at Kaisheng in Hezhou, then moved to Qingshan, and later to Qionglong.
Entering the hall, he said: "In the late spring of the third month, the flowers are in full crimson bloom. Their fragrance attracts a swarm of bees in disarray.
They know only to recklessly compete for the harvest, unaware that the creative forces of the past have long been empty. [End of Section]
In the Hall: "When blessings arrive, I do not speak of Chan; with nothing to do, I sleep the day away. If someone asks about the meaning of the Patriarch, I strike them two or three times.
The assembly, tell me: why is it so? Because it is improper to disturb the mountain monk’s sleep. The Master’s nature was straightforward and sincere;

even with servants, he would sit together with them in his room, which contained nothing but a rush-cushion and a paper curtain. Whenever anyone requested instruction, [he would respond in this manner].

Regarding the "words for the assembly," the Master replied: "You seek words for ascending the hall; I shall now repeat them for you once more. Do not seek within the phrases; herein, nothing at all is permitted.

In the fifth month of the year Jiachen of the Xuanhua era (1124), when Chan Master Yuanwu was traveling for proselytization and arrived at Suchou, he went to the mountain [to visit the Master], where he burned incense and paid his respects.
On the middle day of the waxing moon, he said to his disciples: "I shall depart shortly; my life-limit has reached its end."
He bathed, sat upright, and passed away. His body was cremated, and innumerable relics of five colors were produced. His remains were gathered and a stūpa was erected in the northwest corner.
He was sixty-nine years old in secular age and fifty-two years in monastic seniority.
Jiatai Pule Lu, Scroll Four, Phonetic Explanations: Jū (居) is pronounced as jū;
Ū (鄔) is pronounced as wǔ; Huáng (肓) is pronounced as huāng; Cān (參) is pronounced as sēn.
Xǔ (兕): initial *xǔ*, final *-i*. Bèn (窆): initial *bǎo*, final *-iàn*. Chǐ (褫): phonetic transcription *chǐ*. Bó (駮): initial *bù*, final *-jiǎo*. Shè (舍) is the same as shě (捨).
Tóng (穜): phonetic transcription *tóng*. Xiǎn (陝): phonetic transcription *shǎn*. Wén (閿): phonetic transcription *wén*;
originally written as wú (閺). Chōu (瘳): phonetic transcription *chōu*. Liáo (廖): phonetic transcription *liù*.

Xùn (pronounced with the rhyme *rùn* and the initial *qì*) Qiào (pronounced *qiào*) Lù (pronounced *lù*) Sù (pronounced *sù*) Ōu (pronounced *qū*) Ná (pronounced *nà*) Zào (pronounced with the rhyme *cái* and *xiào*) Yǎo (pronounced *yǎo*) Tiǎo (pronounced *diào*) Cōu (pronounced *chū* and *shuò*)
*Jiatai Pudeng Lu*, Volume Five,
Compiled by the Monk (臣) Seng Zhengshou of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture.
The Twelfth Generation of Qingyuan (The Sixth Generation of Yunmen).
Chan Master Datong Shanben of Fayun Monastery in Dongjing was a successor of Chan Master Huilin Yuanzhao Zongben.
His clan name was Dong; he was a descendant of Dong Zhongshu of the Han dynasty.
His grandfather, Qi, and his father, Wen, both served as officials in Ying, so he subsequently became a native of Ying. His mother had no children, so she prayed to the White-Robed Bodhisattva.

He finally found his teacher. Upon reaching adulthood, he read extensively across all categories of literature; nevertheless, he maintained a life of pure cultivation and had no intention of holding office.
In the eighth year of the Jiayou era, he and his younger brother Shansi went to the Jizang Monastery in the capital, where they were selected for ordination through the examination of the scriptures.

There, he studied the *Vinaya*. He traveled east to Gusu, where he paid homage to Yuanzhao at Ruiwang Monastery. Yuanzhao took special notice of him, and thus [Fahai] attained a profound realization of the fundamental principle. After five years, his understanding grew even further.

He ascended to the subtle and profound depths. He illuminated the essentials for Master Yiyuan Tongxiu (at that time, Xiuxiu was residing at Louxian). When the Master arrived, he further exhausted the essential points [of the teaching].
In the seventh year of the Yuanfeng era, he crossed the Huai River and stayed at Taishouyan for a long time. He subsequently left to reside at Shuanglin and was later transferred to Jingci.
Soon thereafter, by imperial decree, he was moved to reside at Fayun. Entering the hall, after a long silence, he said: "Just like this, stop; do not trouble others."
The Elder of Vīraśaṅkha: the staff and the shout fly back and forth, leaving Deshan and Linji at a loss. To "tie up half" and "break three"—I do not want you to try to understand it through words.
How do you speak that single phrase which does not touch the ordinary? If you have not yet been able to distinguish black from white, do not recklessly ply your needle and chisel.
[He] descends from the hall. Above, one sees no heaven; below, one sees no earth. It fills and obstructs all of space. There is none.
He remained in seclusion. To act as a ruler by breaking through with clarity would not hit the mark. "Just go look at the turtle-nosed one on the South Mountain.
He threw down his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "All phenomena within the three realms, whether existent or non-existent, cannot serve as metaphors for the Buddha.
This is the place where the Old Barbarian has never been able to be named or delineated. Today, without sparing my eyebrows, I shall attempt to bring it up for you all."
After a long silence, he took up his staff, struck the ground once, and said: "The sound of the ice on the few-foot staff has just struck the earth;
with the momentum of a coiled dragon, it is about to soar into the void. Up in the sky: "Monks have no concerns; they truly enjoy leisure. When weary, they brew tea;

when cold comes, they turn toward the fire. They laugh and roam among the groves, forgetting their cares beyond the mundane world. Wielding the handle of the pine-tree as they engage in pure conversation, they accompany the mist and clouds."

[The Master] dismissed the assembly. With heaven as his canopy and earth as his mat, who is right and who is wrong? Thirty years from now, if someone asks about the matter of the ultimate limit, simply say to them:
"Drawing the bow after the thief has fled. Ascending the hall, he said: "Words cannot unfold the reality; speech does not meet the occasion."
He tramples the great ocean underfoot and kicks over Mount Sumeru, leaving the old man Dongshan with no place to hide his body.
Why do you all not go and rescue him? If you cannot rescue him, I, Shuanglin, shall rescue him for you! Thereupon, he let out a shout.
[The Master] descended from his seat. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the rewards for labor during the three months of summer retreat;

what is the matter from now on? [The Master] said, "Gao shaves his head; Jing washes his bowl. The monk said, "Thank you for the teacher’s instruction. [The Master] said, "A drop of water is difficult to digest.

Another asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? [The Master] said, "You have come on foot pilgrimage; what do you hope to achieve? The monk said, "I, your disciple, do not understand."
He said, "Wait for a donkey’s year. Question: "The spring mountains layer upon layer of chaotic green; the spring waters ripple with empty azure. I wonder, what realm is this?
He said, "If you want to speak, what difficulty is there? [The questioner] said, "I request it at once. He said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; little rain, much wind. Question:
"The mind of *nirvāṇa* is easy to understand, but the wisdom of differentiation is difficult to distinguish. What is the wisdom of differentiation?"
[The Master] said, "The lantern swallows the dew-pillar. [A monk] said, "I, a student, do not yet understand. [The Master] said, "The Buddha Hall emerges from the triple gate.
On the day of opening the hall, a monk asked, "The precious stupa is fundamentally without seams; how can one point this out to people? [The Master] said, "Mist and clouds arise behind its face;

stars and moon circle its eaves and rafters. [The monk] asked, "What is it like for those within the stupa? [The Master] said, "Throughout the day they have no concern with the affairs of the mundane world. Long...
He divined his lifespan as three years in the White Clouds Village. Later, having received imperial permission to return home, he built a hermitage at Longshan on West Lake (now known as Chongde).
On the day of Jiazi in the twelfth month of the third year of the Daguan era, he held up three fingers and said to those around him, "There are only three days left."

When the appointed time arrived, he indeed passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. Extraordinary birds circled and sang in the courtyard. By imperial decree, his entire body was enshrined in a stupa in the north.
He was posthumously titled Yuan-ding (Perfectly Settled), and the stupa was named Ding-guang (Light of Stability). He was seventy-five years old and had been a monk for forty-seven years.

Chan Master Shouyi Faben of Benjue Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture ascended the hall. Holding up his whisk, he said, "The Buddhas of the three periods and the Patriarchs of the six generations are all here.
Do you see them? If you do not see them, it is because you are not equal to the task.
He then spoke the Dharma, saying, "There is no duality, nor is there a division; there is no distinction, nor is there a discontinuity. Do you hear this? You are still not awake.
"Awake! At that very moment, he departed for the world of Fragrant Accumulation above. [The Master] struck the whisk and said, "Step back!
Step back! You have already collided with your own eyes! Ascending the hall, he said: "An ancient said: 'Buddha is like a clenched fist; the Way is like an open hand.'"
He then joined his palms and said, "What is this like? If you can say it, I will grant that you are a person who has finished their business.

If you cannot say it, do not pretend there is no doubt. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you do not understand the Way when you look at things before your eyes, how can you know the path when you move your feet?
Even if you bump into things in a village of three households, it is still somewhat better; but as for the Buddha-dharma and the Way of Chan, [it is another matter]."
"Set it aside; it does not apply at all to his own station. Why is this so? One must not speak falsely before a true person.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "Subduing the barbarians and defeating the invaders—this is a merit that covers a generation.
But as for the four seas being tranquil and clear, would you still have any use for this? After a long silence, he said, "General Li has a glorious reputation."
He was there; not attaining the rank of Marquis was also a form of leisure. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
He replied, "Carrying water, selling it at the riverhead. The monk said, "What is the intent of this? He replied, "Deceiving the Hu and mocking the Han. The monk said, "Laboring without merit.
He replied, "For nine years no one recognized him; with a single shoe, he returned to the void himself. The monk asked, "What is the mystery within the phrase?"
[The Master] said: "Riding an elephant on Mount Kunlun, pulled by a lotus fiber. [The student] asked: "What is the mystery within the essence?

[The Master] said: "A reflection sinks into the cold pond; the moon is in the sky. [The student] asked: "What is the mystery within the mystery? [The Master] said: "Sleeping with a sword at one's side upon the long couch.
[The student] asked: "Is there anything further beyond this? [The Master] said: "Put it down."
A monk asked Chan Master Ning of Nanchan in Wuxi, Changzhou: "Does a newborn infant possess the six consciousnesses?

The Master said: "As the water rises, the boat floats higher. The monk asked: "How would you appraise the price of rice in Luling? The Master said: "The confession comes from the prisoner's own mouth."
Chan Master Miaoyin Xiaotong of Shifosi in Shaoxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Cold as the moon in an autumn pond, mindless, it merges with the Great Void.
The mountains are high and the flowing water is swift; where can the wandering fish find rest? A monk asked, "What is the Sudden Teaching?
He replied, "The moon sets in the cold pond. The monk asked, "What is the Gradual Teaching? He replied, "Clouds arise in the azure sky. The monk asked again, "..."
"How can it be neither gradual nor sudden? He replied, "An eighty-year-old grandmother does not speak of being married.
Chan Master Shou'en of Dizang in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said, "The ancient sages said:
'One who preaches the Dharma should preach according to the Dharma. Today, I shall preach according to the Dharma for the sake of the great assembly. Thereupon, he lowered one foot and said, "One."

[He] was subjected to all manner of disparagement and denigration. Entering the hall for formal instruction, he remained silent for a long while and then said: "In this single realm, who can reach it? It is serene and utterly free from a speck of dust.
Let not the celestial flowers be scattered in disarray; I am no one who merely understands emptiness. He further said: "The woodcutter goes down the steep mountain ridges barefoot."
The laughing old fisherman shivers on the cold creek. Shouldering the mountain scenery across the marketplace, he passes through the door of every house to reach Chang’an.
A monk asked, “What is the Buddha? He replied, “Sleeping during the day is of no benefit. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of this? He replied, “Rising early is very long.
[The monk] asked, “Where does a person who does not cultivate good or evil end up? He replied, “Step by step.”

[The Master] snapped his fingers and said, "Thank you for the teacher’s instruction. [The student] replied, "I turn my head back and call upon Avalokiteśvara. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
[The Master] said, "The wind blows dust all over one's face."
A monk asked Zen Master Zhijue Fahui of Mount Jinshan in Zhenjiang Prefecture: "Does a great practitioner of the Way still fall within the realm of cause and effect?
The Master replied: "When a poison-darting bird enters the water, all the fish die; where a venomous dragon passes, no grass grows."
Chan Master Foyun Foguo Weibai, Dharma heir of Chan Master Fayun Yuancong Faxiu,
first resided at Guishan in Si and subsequently moved to Fayun at Tangquan. In the first year of the Jianzhong Jinggu era,
he presented thirty fascicles of the *Zongmen Xudeng Lu* (Continued Lamp Record of the Zen School), which he had compiled, to the throne.

He advanced to present his report, which accorded with the Imperial Will. He respectfully received the Imperially composed Preface and was further commanded to include it in the Tripitaka for circulation throughout the realm.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If Li Lou had held intent, the white waves would have been in vain as they surged to the heavens; if the *wangxiang* had no mind,"
A bright pearl suddenly appeared in his palm. He drew a circle with his hand and called to the assembly, saying, "Do you see it?

After a long silence, he said, "If you look, there is a chance. He ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, showed it to the assembly, saying, "I have held this monastery for over seventy days and have never once moved this staff.
Now, I cannot help but manifest a small measure of spiritual power as an offering."

The Master then planted his staff upright, descended from the seat, and ascended the hall. "Those of the past have already passed; those of the future need not be reckoned. As for the matter of the present:
today is the fifteenth day of the first month. The bright moon is perfectly full. Strike the drum and let everyone come to look!
People of the assembly, there is no doubt that you can look, but ultimately, what do you call 'the moon'? Do not seek it in the heavens."
He searched for it within the water. A monk asked, "Using the eye of the mind to observe the external forms of the body—what is this 'eye of the mind'?
He replied, "The red sun shines upon Fusang. The monk asked, "What are the external forms outside the mind? He replied, "White clouds seal Mount Hua."
Chan Master Jingchun of Xianyan in Wenzhou first resided at Zhi Guang and was subsequently promoted to Huguo Jiangxin.

A monk asked, "Without manifesting the marks of Buddha-dharma, you respond according to worldly conventions; please, Master, speak quickly. He replied, "When encountering Yao and Shun, there are rites and music;
when meeting Jie and Zhou, there are shields and spears. The monk said, "That is not where I was asking. He replied, "A living tiger or rhinoceros is captured."
"Death fears the blind turtle. A monk asked, "Regarding the staff of Deshan and the shout of Linji—how do you, Master, apply them?
The Master said, "I am tired today, old monk. The monk then shouted. The Master said, "In fact, it is you who are flustered."
Chan Master Shoune of Guangjiao in Ningguo Prefecture was a senior disciple of Yuanzhao; the world called him "Uncle Ne.
A monk asked, "What is the phrase that has existed eternally throughout antiquity and the present? He replied, "An iron ox lies across the seashore.
The monk asked, "What is the true eye of a patch-robed monk? He replied, "Not a needle can pierce it."
Zen Master Huiyuan Qingman of Yuanfeng in Wei Prefecture, a successor of Zen Master Wenhui Chongyuan of Tianpo, ascended the hall and said: "The Old Barbarian took seven steps after birth;
when the morning star appeared, he spoke again of awakening. To catch him with his loot and evidence—this is groundless. Thirty blows of the iron staff will suffice."

[The Master] spoke with leniency. He suddenly raised his staff and said, "How much should the Patriarch have deserved? Do you wish to know? From ancient times until now, offenses against the Dharma have filled the heavens;
they are entirely brought about by you all. On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said, "I recall in the past when I lived in the mountains and lacked food.

I have a verse which I shall present to the assembly: 'When hungry, I eat the leaves of pines and cypresses; when thirsty, I drink the spring water from the mountain stream. Having finished gazing at the green bamboo, I sit in silence.'"
"Sleeping freely with one's robes on. Great assembly, there is more; let Shan-huai speak for you: This year’s year is last year’s year.
Ascending the hall, he gave a shout and said: "It is not the Way, it is not Zen. Whenever the third or fifth night comes, the bright moon is perfectly full.
*Chan*! Ascending the hall, he said: "This is a matter upon the edge of a sword; it requires a man who stands upon the edge of a sword to begin."
It is so. There are those who seek profit and fame, acting as teachers to gods and humans while hanging up the head of a sheep to sell dog meat.
They ruin the beginners among the later generations and diminish the great statutes of the ancient sages. When you people hear of such matters, do you not feel a chill in your hearts?
Because they thus mislead and confuse sentient beings, they fall into the Avīci Hell. Alas! Alas! To take pleasure for a single lifetime, one undergoes ten thousand [aeons of suffering].
"The calamities of kalpas ago—what urgency is there in death? Come here, you son of the Śākyas! He shouted, "A deaf man merely tilting his ear!
Then he descended from the seat. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "The sky is cold and the earth is freezing. The monk asked, "What is the Way? He replied, [the same].
[The Master] did not speak. [The monk] asked, "Why do you not speak? He said, "Speaking is but a mundane name. A question was asked:
"What is the matter that is fully manifest? He said, "Autumn winds stir with spring breezes. A Dharma Master asked, "Regarding Vimalakīrti’s silence—what was his intention?
The Master extended his hand and said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "That too is difficult. Whenever the Master saw [a student], he would...

The monk said, "Buddha-dharma and worldly dharma are like flowers in the sky seen by one with cataracts. Another monk asked, "What is it like when the cataracts have cleared and the flowers have vanished?
He replied, "I take it you are quick-witted."
A monk asked Chan Master Dinghui Faben of Qingzhou, "When ancients reached this point, why did they fold their hands and surrender?
The Master said, "It was only fitting that it should be so. The monk asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "Sleeping at night and walking during the day."
Chan Master Zhenzhao Zongze of Hongji Monastery in Zhending Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Guangzhao Yingfu of Changlu, ascended the hall and said:
"Lately, my body and mind have become dull and rigid, much like a single slab of iron. Within, there is no clever or subtle wit; without, there is no flowery ornamentation or elegant prose. Who..."

It can be forged into a needle for Yanzhou; it makes one laugh to death that the axle-pins of the Qin dynasty were so coarse. Its four corners touch the ground; in ten thousand matters, there is no mind.
Although it cannot be seen through, in the end it cannot be smashed. Why is this? Have you not heard it said: "In general, fine things are not durable;
colorful clouds easily disperse, and lapis lazuli is brittle"? Ascending the hall, he said: "Though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a speck."
"Obstruction! Now that the gold dust has been removed, where is the eye? If it is like this, you have not yet emerged from the thicket of thorns;

to seek realization at the tip of the staff or to take responsibility upon being struck by a shout is to remain right within the Golden Peak's nest. Ascending the hall, he said: "Beyond the pavilion, the colors of the Purple Gold Mountain are exquisite;
before the gate, the sound of the nectar-water is cold. Beneath the shade of the ancient locust tree, amidst the clear breeze, let us try for a moment—"
Pointing again at everyone, he held up his staff and said, "Do you see it? Striking the incense table, he asked, "Do you hear it?
Leaning the staff against the wall, he said, "If the eyes and ears are unobstructed, the sound of water will be heard everywhere; the mountain colors will naturally drift on.
A monk asked, "What is the realm of Shangyuan (the Lantern Festival)? He replied, "The lanterns are large for the large, small for the small. The monk said, "As for that cart..."
"Where does a horse go when it comes and goes? What kind of matter has it accomplished? He said, "How can it compare to this mountain monk sleeping until dawn?
Question: "What is it like when the six gates have not yet ceased? He said, "Incense is burned inside the nostrils. The student said, "I do not understand. He said, "A drum is beaten inside the ears.
Question: "What is the merit of meritless merit? He said, "The clay ox does not move its feet; Heaven..."
[The monk] buried it in a wasteland. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then your effort has not been in vain.
[The monk] replied, "Even with such vast and great supernatural powers, one cannot avoid receiving his severe blows."
Chan Master Jueyin Daorong of Xuedou in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of that commandery.
A monk asked, "What is it like when Hanshan meets Shide? He replied, "Raising an eyebrow, flashing a lightning bolt. The monk said, "Is there anything further? He replied, "[There is]."
He opened his mouth and emitted rays of light, saying: "What is the path that leads upward? He replied: "Seven, six, eight.

Chan Master Huiri Guangdeng Zhijue of Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of that region. His clan name was Mei. He had long frequented the seats of various masters but had not yet attained realization.
Later, he attained awakening under Guangzhao; shortly thereafter, he returned to his hometown and began teaching the Dharma at Huiri, subsequently moving to Cheng.

At Nanfeng Peak. Entering the hall, he remained silent for a long while, then said: "Rest! Rest! Rest! All in vain, drifting aimlessly. The fishing rod remains firmly in hand; the fish is cold and will not swallow the bait.

He let out a shout and descended from the seat. On an autumn day in the Ding-si year of the Xiangxing era, when the sun was nearly setting, he called his attendant monk and ordered him to assemble the congregation.
He recounted their past inquiries and exhorting them to discern the matter of their own selves, he took up his brush and wrote: "Nan..."
To the north there is not an inch of shadow; east and west, he is cut off from his four neighbors. A single breath of news from his native land; the morning wind blows away the lingering clouds.
He set down his brush and passed away.
[This is the entry for] Master Jie of Zisheng, a successor in the Dharma lineage.
Chan Master Wenyou Huikong Yuanjue Dazhi was a native of Jinjiang County in Quanzhou. His clan name was Chen.

By the age of several years, he could memorize a thousand words a day. During the Xining era, his elder brother Hao submitted a memorial to the throne whose remarks offended the imperial administration; consequently, the authorities launched a desperate manhunt for him.
His elder brother, Dun, retired to Mount Luofu. Later, [Jie] relied upon Master Si Yong of Zishou Monastery to shave his head and don the robes (Jie was the Dharma-transmitting disciple of Yong).

He consequently went there to attend upon him. When Yong gave instructions within the meditation hall, Jie failed to understand them at all. One day, Yong asked Jie, "The ancients pointed toward the place where eyes open and close to demonstrate the secret function;
is this truly so? Jie rebuked him, saying, "You fellow who trails behind the donkey and the horse—what use is there in that?"
He raised his staff and chased him away. The Master attained great enlightenment. Jie laughed and said, "This dullard" (other remarks have not been seen).
Jingzhong Fanyan Shouzuo was a Dharma heir of Chan Master Guangdeng Weizhan of Zhaoti in Xijing; he was born into the Wang family of Changshi and followed [the monastic life] at the age of seven.

He entered the monastic order at Jingyan Monastery. Possessing extraordinary talent, he could grasp a text upon a single reading without needing to look at it again. At the age of fourteen, he received full ordination. He traveled extensively to seek out the gates of Chan, finding his spiritual resonance with Master Jingzhong.

Later, he went to the capital to attend upon Chan Master Bai of Foguo Monastery. Upon being summoned for an audience, the Emperor bestowed upon him the title Guangdeng (Extensive Lamp) and granted him purple robes.

Since he first appeared in the world at Zhaoti Monastery, he has successively moved to many great temples. On the day of his formal opening of the hall (*kaitang*), he held up the incense and offered this prayer:
The ceremony concluded. He again held up the incense and said: "This one offering of incense was obtained twenty years ago on the banks of the Ruoye River at Mount Yunmen;

its roots were not planted by grafting. Today, I burn it within this burner as an offering to the Venerable Head Seat Master Yan of Jingzhong Monastery in Yuezhou, so that the iron tree may sprout branches and its fragrance be inexhaustible. Thereupon, he proceeded to...
Taking his seat, the Head Monk struck the gavel and said, "In this Dharma assembly of dragons and elephants, you should contemplate the primary meaning.
The Master struck the meditation seat and laughed heartily, saying, "What a fine 'primary meaning'! It has just been struck into two pieces by the Shaolin Chan Master’s single blow.
Is there anyone here now who can receive it? (The question and answer follow). He spoke again: "Holding up the flower was already an error; the smile..."
Deviation and error ensued. Four times seven were transmitted in vain, like echoes resounding through valleys; two or three pointed falsely, like moonlight scattering across a stream.

Five branches split wildly, and a thousand twigs protruded crosswise. To point at a deer and call it a horse, to mistake a bow for a snake—first the mind was deluded regarding its resting, then the marrow was lost in confusion.
Upon the platform of Huangmei, the Southern and Northern schools opened; at the bank of Caoxi, waves surged to the east and west. From that time forth...

Waves surge in competition; paths and lanes branch out in confusion. Signposts line the roads in abundance, yet no one cuts them off. Following the current, one drifts ever further away; who can understand how to return to the source?
When the staff and the shout are applied according to the occasion, ten thousand miles of white clouds arise—leaving even the Yellow-headed One tongue-tied and the Blue-eyed One speechless.
Even such an understanding remains but talk for the journey; when observed by those with clear eyes, it is but a single scene of failure.
A source of laughter. Nevertheless, today, for the sake of the nation, I open the hall. Within this second gate of meaning, I shall test everyone by drawing a single thread through it.
Raising his whisk, he said: "Do you all understand? A stone woman dances the song of longevity."
A wooden man sings a song of Great Peace. Ascending the hall, he said: "Enduring the spring breeze as a hundred birds cry out, the peach blossoms secretly enter the Wuling Brook.
When Master Xie turns his oars and returns late, he is not like the people of Qin who remained forever lost.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Biased? Not biased. Correct? Not correct. That matter has never been comparable to anything else. Amidst the wind and rain filling the heavens, one’s very bones and hair stand on end."
"Cold! Why must you enter the *nāga-samādhi* again? [The Master] struck his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "The six sense-objects are not evil;
they are identical to perfect enlightenment. On horseback, who is this fair-faced youth of noble family? Piercing flowers and breaking willows, his kerchief hangs down from the corner of his cap.
Last night, he was drunk at the Bright Moon Tower; calling for dice, he lost his golden mansion. With falcon on arm and hound in hand, will he return or not? O..."
With white eyebrows and pearly teeth, his anger is powerless. How many people can truly know this mind? One with yellow hair and blue eyes is not someone I recognize.
*Lara-lari*. (Claps hands once. Descends from the seat. Ascending the hall: A straight hook catches the *gong-jing* fish; a curved hook catches fish and turtles.
The ancients exerted too much effort for very little gain. Today, Chengtian casts a massive net into...
In the vast blue ocean, fish and dragons make no distinctions; when a great net is cast across the vast wilderness, how can their heads and horns be differentiated?
But tell me, is there anyone among them who has passed through the net? After a long silence, he said: "Ordinarily, there is no need to raise your head or horns;
the day when wind and clouds meet will surely come. A monk asked: "The patriarchs have transmitted this to one another without interruption; in truth, whom do you now succeed?"
A person said, "The waters of the Ruo River are swift; Mount Qinwang is high. [The Master] said, "In those days, I attained a verse of distinct clarity;

today, I have no private intention but wish to proclaim it. He said, "When the frost is high, hawks and falcons are swift; raising their wings, they fly beyond Silla. [Someone] asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
He said, "Autumn winds scatter yellow leaves; distant peaks see white clouds return. He said, "I do this specifically for the sake of those who flow [in the stream]."
[The Master] said, "It is pervasive. [A monk] asked, "Right now, how would you express it? The monk gave a shout; the Master struck him. [Another] asked, "What is the realm of the *jātī* (monastery)?
He replied, "Pavement flowers are spread like gold upon the ground; the courtyard trees are emerald, piercing the void.

[The monk] asked, "Who is the person within this realm? He replied, "Sometimes they open their azure eyes; nowhere can one find the Yellow-Headed One (*Huangtou*). [Another] asked, "Regarding the retreat to Jingzhou—"
At the ancestral seat, he again ascended the Dharma hall at Danqiao. [A monk] asked, "What is the Venerable Immovable One?

He replied, "The floating cup comes from the Chu marsh; the flying staff passes through Qiantang. [The monk] said, "Is this not the Venerable Immovable One? He replied, "But you must still tie your straw sandals tight.
At the beginning of the Jianyan era, he passed away at Nan’an in Danghu, which is now called Nanta.
Chan Master Dajue Zujing Faying of Daimei, in Qingyuan Prefecture, was a successor of Chan Master Jiushao Jianshao. He was a native of Ning County in the commandery; his clan was Zhang.

Having renounced Confucian studies, he took the scriptural examinations and became a monk. He practiced lecturing at Yanqing Temple. Whenever those studying the doctrinal teachings were stumped by veteran masters, he would [immediately provide the answer].
The Master Qie was eloquent in debate and was held in high esteem by the assembly. Suddenly, he remarked, "Names and forms are circuitous and indirect;

how could they be what I take as my primary principle? He then changed his robes and went to Nine Peaks (Jiufeng). Seeing that he possessed great potential, Jiufeng spoke with him as if he had long been at the seat of practice and probed him with piercing questions.

The Master grasped the essential meaning, and from then on he gained renown. He traveled to the capitals of Chang'an and Luoyang, where monastics and laypeople alike vied to welcome him wherever he went.

The Chief Judge Zhong Yuan, having encountered [the Master] through the Way, grew increasingly respectful over time. He petitioned for the bestowal of purple robes and the Master’s formal name, and commanded him to reside at Baima Monastery in Xiangyang.
After more than two years, he retired and returned east. The Prefectural Governor welcomed him to fill the Dharma seat at Damei, where his influence flourished throughout the regions of Ou and Yue.
In the first year of the Xuanhua era, an imperial edict was issued requiring all monks and nuns to become "virtuous scholars" (deshi), despite...
The presiding officials held a council, yet not a single word could turn the Emperor’s mind. The Master then composed a commentary on the *Laozi* with a free hand and presented it.
Upon reading it, the Emperor said to his attendants, "The commentary on the *Daodejing* submitted by Fa-ying is concise in expression and profound in principle."
"Since this has never existed in antiquity, it should be granted entry into the Daoist Canon for circulation. Furthermore, please grant me the ceremonial cap, sash, altar, and edict accordingly.

Those of the world who did not understand the Master’s intent often regarded him as a sycophant. In the autumn of the following year, an imperial decree was issued to restore the status of monks and nuns throughout the empire;
yet the Master alone remained steadfast in his resolve. At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, he rose at dawn wearing a birch-bark cap and a crane-feather cloak.

Holding the ivory tally and wearing vermilion-soled shoes, he had the drum beaten to assemble the multitude. Ascending the seat, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The fragrance of orchids lingers in the spring valley; chrysanthemums flourish by the autumn fence.
All things must undergo their cycles of flourishing and withering according to their own seasons. In the past, monks and nuns were disparaged while the Way was exclusively served;

later, the Way and its flatterers were suppressed, and monks and nuns were restored. But tell me, assembly, how were the forms and appearances of these monks and nuns restored? He then took up his crown and showed it to them.
The assembly said, "My crown has always been like the full moon; though my hair is capped, I have not become an immortal.

This morning, casting it down without obstruction, I release divine light that pierces the azure heavens. Having said this, he cast it away, immediately changed into monastic robes, and holding up a crane-feather cloak, he said:
The Tathāgata once traded for a fur robe; for many years he felt ashamed wearing this crane-feather cloak.
Return to me the garments of a manly tamer of men; you should know that these items are not suitable for him. He cast it aside. Holding up his official tablet (xiàngjiǎn), he said:

"I loathed the Zen board for no reason at all; who would have thought it would be deceived by this official tablet? Why today do I suddenly set it down? An old man in retirement throughout the heavens."
The Immortal Official threw it down. Holding up his vermilion shoes, he said: "Dharma brought one pair back with him; from this day forth, descendants shall walk barefoot.

Borrowing these vermilion shoes to replace the hemp sandals—do not say that the times are difficult and hinder one's efforts. When seeking to transform into a Peng bird, failing to meet its opportunity, one remains no more than a Kun.
To paint a tiger and fail to complete it results in something resembling a dog. He threw them down. Holding his staff crosswise, he said: "Today, my staff..."
He transformed into a dragon and split Mount Hua into tens of millions of layers. Then, leaning on his shoulder, he said: "Take care, O True Sage-Lord with the Buddha-mind;
may you well employ the virtue of Yao to revitalize my school. He then sat upright, closed his eyes, and passed away at over eighty years of age.
His *Kanzheng lu* (Record of Carving and Correcting) and his commentary on the *Yijing* (Book of Changes) circulate in the world.
Chan Master Danxia Zichun of Dengzhou was a successor of Chan Master Tiaokai of Fuyong at Tianning (the twelfth generation of Qingyuan and eighth generation of Dongshan).
He was a native of Jianmen and belonged to the Jia clan. Having left home to become a monk at a young age, he entered the monastic life at Dajian Temple.
He became a monk in his early twenties. Initially, he studied under Chan Master Fang of Yuquan; next, he sought instruction at the quarters of Zhenru of Dayue;

and finally, he attained thorough realization under Furong. He ascended the hall and said: "Within heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a single treasure, hidden within the mountain of form.
Dharma Master Zhao spoke thus, but he only knew how to point to tracks and discuss traces; he was simply unable to—"
He brought this forth for people. Today, Danxia tears asunder the universe and shatters the mountain of form;
he brings it forth for all of you. Let those with eyes discern it! He struck the ground once with his staff and said: "Do you see?

The egret standing in the snow is not of the same color; the bright moon among the reeds is not like him. Ascending the hall, he said: "The precious moon flows with radiance; the clear pool spreads its reflection."

The reflection has no intention of soaking the moon; the moon has no intention of dividing its light to illuminate the water. When both water and moon are forgotten, only then can it be called "severance.
Therefore it is said: "The matter of ascending to heaven must be cast away; the matter of being fully perfected must be discarded."
If you can cast yourself to the ground with a golden sound and not look back—if you can do this, only then do you understand how to walk among those of different species.
Do you all understand this point thoroughly? After a long silence, he said: "Constantly walking without lifting his feet from the human path, wearing fur and horns, he mingles with the dust and mud.
Ascending the hall, he cited: "Deshan addressed the assembly, saying: 'In my school, there are no words or phrases.'"

"In reality, there is not a single dharma for others. When Deshan speaks thus, it can be said that he only knows how to seek people while entering the grass, yet fails to realize his entire body is covered in mud and water.
Upon careful observation, he possesses only a single eye. If it were Danxia, it would not be so:
"In my school, there are words and phrases that a golden blade cannot cut open; the profound and wondrous principle is the Jade Maiden..."
Conceiving in the night. Ascending the hall, he said: "Stately at midday, it is still half-deficient; Silent at the third watch, it is not yet full. The six gates have never known its warmth;
Coming and going, it is always before the bright moon. Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Beiyuan asked Qingfeng about Luopu’s saying, "Entering a wasteland, one does not discriminate;
one simply picks up whatever grass comes to hand. Beiyuan asked, "Why not say, 'I act'? (He then added, "Why not say, 'I act'? as a challenge.)
"What is this 'grass plucked at hand'? Feng made a gesture of picking something up. The Master said, "It is indeed so, yet it is simply that he has not yet been able to eat the grass.
Furthermore, when the lay practitioner Gan-zhi was receiving guests, a monk said, "It is no easy matter for you, practitioner, to receive guests."
Zhi said, "It is like feeding a donkey or feeding a horse. Ming'an said, "I know that the practitioner always travels this path.
The Master added separately, "Next year, I will buy a *zhidu* robe for the practitioner. A monk asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
He replied, "The golden chrysanthemums have just bloomed; bees vie to gather their pollen. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him? He replied, "The stalks wither."
When the flowers wither, there is nothing left to rely upon. In the spring of the Jihai year of the Xuanhua era, he passed away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the south of Mount Hong.
Chan Master Mudu Facheng of Jingyin in Dongjing was a native of Chongde, Jiaxing (details regarding his life are not yet fully known).
He ascended the hall and said: "The lantern suddenly bursts into laughter; how is it that even the pillar is pregnant? At daybreak, it gives birth to white..."

The eldest daughter has wandered off until now and still has not returned. This wretched person—come back soon! For whom will the yellow chrysanthemums and green bamboos be planted morning and evening?
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "For nine years, Bodhidharma offered but this one phrase, which remains even unto this day."
Various directions have been led astray. If you wish not to be led astray, Mount Xiangshan shall raise it once more for all of you:
Great Dragon Mountain is high, Little Dragon Mountain is low, and Mount Xiangshan stands in the middle, perfectly suited and appropriate. Having raised it thus, will you then not be free from error?
After a long silence, he said: "The Bear Ear Mountains have ceased their dreams; The Snowy Courtyard need no longer speak of the Spring at Shaolin."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "On the solitary peak, at its very summit, the numinous pine soars ten thousand fathoms high. Across the rivers and lakes of ten thousand leagues, the bright moon radiates its brilliance across the azure void.
At this very moment, the wild crane has no place to set its feet; where can the wandering fish hide its form?
If your eyes flicker for even an instant, you are already a hundred thousand eight thousand miles away. In the space of a single deliberation, home and kin are blocked from view. At Xiangshan now—"
"The sun has already risen; you have opened your eyes and urinated on your bed. You all must not speak of dreams within a dream. Ascending the hall, he said:

"The source from which one returns is non-dual, yet the expedient means are manifold. If you simply understand the nature of the source to which one returns, why worry about the gates of expedient means?"
Do you all wish to understand the source of returning to the origin? Take a pillar and use it as a wooden ladle; bystanders may not agree, but let them do as they please.
Do you wish to understand the gate of skillful means? Take a wooden ladle and use it as a pillar; it is equally suitable for propping up heaven and supporting the earth.
But tell me, how would you express the single phrase that does not fall into the gate of skillful means? After thirty years have passed, do not...
A teaching given in error. Entering the hall, [the Master] said: "Only when one knows there is that which transcends Buddhas and Patriarchs does one have the right to speak.

All you Zen practitioners, tell me: what is that which transcends Buddhas and Patriarchs? There was once a man’s son whose six sense-faculties were incomplete and whose seven consciousnesses were not whole;
he was not an icchantika, yet he lacked the Buddha-nature. Whenever he encountered a Buddha, he killed the Buddha; whenever he encountered a Patriarch, he killed the Patriarch."
The Patriarch: "Heaven cannot contain him; hell has no gate to admit him. Do you all recognize this person?
After a long silence, he said: "Face-to-face, yet not a seer; sleeping much, full of drowsy talk."
Chan Master Yuanyi of Zhaoti in Dengzhou was the son of the Xie family of Tongsan in Tongchuan.
In the fourth year of the Daguan era, he went forth to reside at Zhaoti, where he presided over ten different monasteries in total. Ascending the hall, he said: "The ten directions gather together;

each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting the Buddha; with an empty mind, one returns having attained the highest degree. "Great assembly, as for hearing, seeing, sensing, and knowing—"

There has never been an interval [between them]. How can you explain the principle of the "emptiness of mind"? Is it that because you see yet do not see, and hear yet do not hear, the mind is empty? No, that is wrong.
Is it that by forgetting contrivances and ceasing discursive thoughts, all phenomena are simultaneously discarded, such that the mind is empty? No, that is also wrong.
To dissolve that which enables one to enter the profound mystery, and to obliterate nature and characteristics so as to return to the Dharma-realm—is this because the mind is empty?
No, it is a mistake. It cannot be thus; it cannot be otherwise; it cannot be both thus and otherwise.
I do not know what ultimately happens—do you understand? After a long silence, he said: "If truly there is nothing to be done, yet there is nothing that is not done. Heaven.
The hall of hell constantly follows one. A three-foot staff stirs the Yellow River; the eight-armed Nezha peers with cold eyes.
Infinite fish and dragons all flee in haste; he seizes a three-legged tortoise that follows the river. He strips off its shell and drives it with an iron awl.
The omens of good and ill are already distinguished by their radiance. I ask the white-haired old man of the eastern village: "When good and ill have not yet manifested as omens, what is there to do?
Rest, rest, rest! From antiquity to the present, spring follows autumn; the bright sun passes its time according to its own measure.
What more could one find lacking in elegance? *Du!* [A clap of the hands]. Ascending the hall: Today is the first day of the fourth month. The eyes of the patch-robed monk are like—
Lacquer. Looking at the pillar and the lantern, a clap of thunder rolls across the level ground;
startled, Vajra emerges from his door. At midnight in a desolate village, he loses his way; at dawn, he returns to the gate. Dust fills his eyes, ears, and nose. "O Assembly!
Just as Vajra’s eyes blaze through the four worlds, why has he lost his way? Do you understand? Because—"
Pitying the beauty of the wind and moon, I have forgotten the spring in my old garden. Ascending the hall: The bright moon hangs in the sky; the clear pool has no reflection.
Where the Purple Microcosm turns, the setting sun shines; when the colorful phoenix returns, the heavens are about to dawn. Beyond the clouds in the azure void, the stone bamboo shoots span the air;
amidst the waves of the green water, the clay ox rides the billows. The pregnant jade hare passes the western peak at dawn, cradling her young.
The Golden Cock roosts on the eastern ridge at night. At this moment of clarity, one finally knows that outside the "Night-Bright" curtain, there is a distinct family tradition.
Within the Hall of the Empty King, both sages and ordinary beings leave no trace. But tell me, what is the matter outside the Night-Bright curtain?
Do you understand? It happens just as the autumn wind enters the door; whose house is it where a single stroke of the pestle falls? Ascending the hall, he said:
Case: Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying, "The entire earth is scooped up and made as small as a grain of millet;

it is tossed before you. You lacquer buckets do not understand! I beat the drum and invite everyone to look! Great assembly, when Xuefeng speaks in this manner, is there still a place for him to manifest himself?
If you say there is, why is the great trichiliocosm contained within a single grain? If [you say]...
"The Way is non-existent. Who is it that beats the drum and invites all to look? If you can understand this, there is no need for further elaboration.
If not, listen to this verse: Shaking the heavens and earth with every step, Who knows the Southern Dipper as it faces North?
The golden crow hastens toward the Western Mountain at dusk; At dawn, it flies through the Fusan tree in the dead of night. A monk asked: "The ancients..."

The Way. In a place far removed and utterly devoid of people, they gather their heads together and lift it up. Since it is a place far removed and utterly devoid of people, who is it that lifts it up together?
He said: "The green mountains and the white clouds. [The Master] asked: "As for these green mountains and white clouds, do they know there is something, or not?
He said: "If they knew there was, then there would be people. [The Master] asked: "I wonder, what kind of person provides the witness? He said: "White..."
"Clouds and green mountains. [The monk] said, "Is this not the Master’s way of dealing with people? He replied, "Do not mistake it. A question was asked:
"How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? He replied, "The spirit frowns. [The monk] said, "And after it has been polished?
He replied, "The Persian snaps his fingers. [The monk] asked, "Why is it so? He replied, "Good things do not leave the door. The seventh month of Ding-si, Xiang-er (1137).
On the twenty-fifth day, he took up his brush and wrote a verse. He then sat peacefully in stillness.
After the cremation, his relics were collected and enshrined on Mount Shoushan at Xueshe. He was eighty-five years old.
Chan Master Tianning Dayong Qi Lian of Chang’an ascended the hall and said: “The principle of pure emptiness is where Buddhas and Patriarchs alike return;
ultimately there is no self, for the holy and the ordinary are one body. Such is the principle. But as for the myriad phenomena arrayed before our eyes—how are they?
When even a speck of dust is absent from the boundaries, those who possess eyes do not need to peer from the side. Official channels do not admit a needle, yet private passages allow it to pass.”
As for the carriage and horses: if you reach such a state of emergence, only then can you utilize them according to circumstances and grasp them with the hand of faith;

wondrous responses will be without hindrance. On the mysterious path facing the wind, the golden needle and brocade seams are such that the stitches do not show; at the jade palace and jeweled steps, [the same applies].
The jeweled curtain has not yet been rolled up; it is precisely at this moment. Tell me, whose realm is this? At the ancient ferry, the autumn wind blows chill and whistling;
red reeds and marsh grass fill the bends of the river.
A monk asked Master Jici of Meishan in Tongchuan Prefecture, "What is the matter of the Dharma-body?
He replied, "Withered wood sprouts flowers, yet it does not offend the spring. The monk asked, "What is the matter beyond the Dharma-body? He replied, "The stone woman does not paint her eyebrows."
Chan Master Zizhao of Jingyin in Tokyo was a native of Qingzhou. His clan name was Wang.

In his youth, he gained the recognition of Sima Guang through his Confucian studies and remained in Sima’s entourage for over ten years. He pursued noble ideals and had no interest in fame or official rank.
One day, he shaved his head and followed Fuyong. His practice was meticulous and precise, and his realization was transcendent. In the fourth year of the Chongning era, he emerged [from seclusion].
He resided in the Mahāyāna.
When Emperor Huizong heard of his reputation, he issued an imperial decree for him to dwell at Jingyin Monastery. Entering the hall, the Master said:

"The Patriarch came from the West specifically to proclaim this matter. Since then, people have been unwilling to comprehend it fully; instead, they have sought it outwardly, casting themselves into the waters of the red sands."
Seeking the pearl, one travels to Mount Jing to search for jade; yet one fails to realize that those who enter through the gate do not see the treasures of their own home.

To mistake the shadows for the head—is this not a great error? Only when the teachings of the Zen school are fully realized does one find that the essence is quiescent and without dependence, and that divergent thoughts do not arise.

There is no interval between past and present; the myriad phenomena of the universe are the family style encountered at every turn. Though the bird-path is vast and empty, it does not hinder one’s ability to raise [the voice of the Dharma].
A step. The golden rooster announces the dawn; the vermilion phoenix soars aloft. The blossoms open upon the jade trees;
fruit forms upon the withered branches. Only beneath the Gate of the Sun does every day mark the three autumns; before the Hall of the Bright Moon, every moment marks the nine summers.

Do you wish to understand? A shadowless tree hangs over the moon in the cold stream; the ocean tide flows east while the Dipper shifts west. Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Do you still..."
Do you understand? Even the Buddha does not believe it; even the Patriarchs do not believe it.
This very self is still an enemy—how much less can one find anything else to believe in? Great assembly, tell me: why do they not believe? Not believing! Not believing!
"I do not see the Way. Do not take matters lightly; one must observe them over a long period.

A monk asked, "Since you have ascended the lion throne this day, I request a single phrase from the Master to settle heaven and earth. The Master said, "Great drought reaching to the heavens, yet three feet of rain;
startling thunder on level ground. The monk said, "I knew that you had long harbored a treasure within your bag; today, I borrow it briefly to look upon it in the arena."
He said: "A wooden horse tramples open the road beyond the clouds; a clay ox plows the fields within the sea. He continued:
"If this very message is already known now, why need one ask further about the sky within the cave? He added: "Rest immediately before you even reach Tongguan. Question: [What is it?]
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? He replied, "When there is a question, it does not meet the head; herein there is no path for speech.

The student said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master to point it out again. He replied, "If one could open their mouth beyond the empty kalpa, even a stone person would know how to knit their eyebrows."
Chan Master Fuzhou Puxian Shanshou was asked by a monk: "What is 'the partial within the central'? He replied: "The dragon roars after the first watch;
the tiger howls before the fifth watch. The monk asked: "What is 'the central within the partial'? He replied: "Light smoke veils the bright moon;
thin mist locks the cold crags. The monk asked: "What is 'coming from the central'? He replied: "How could the withered pine ever grow old? The flower..."

[The Master] said: "The blossoms are open, yet the buds have not yet sprouted. He asked: "What is 'reaching within the simultaneous' (jiānzhōng zhì)? [The Master] replied: "The sound of the monkey’s cry cannot be distinguished;

the call of the crane is difficult to clarify. He asked: "What is 'arriving within the simultaneous' (jiānzhōng dào)? [The Master] replied: "Clearing the path beyond the clouds; shedding oneself before the bright moon."
Chan Master Faldeng of Lumeng in Xiangyang Prefecture was a native of Huayang in Chengdu. His clan name was Liu. In his youth, he relied upon Daci Baofan to become a monk;
he studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* under him and grasped its essential points. Later, he left to visit Furong Daokai. Upon meeting Kai, the Master asked:
"What is one's own self before the empty kalpa? At these words, the traces of the Master’s mind vanished. [The questioner] proceeded with composure and said:
"A single phrase, numinous and clear, transcends all phenomena; it stands far beyond the Three Vehicles and requires no cultivation. Yunrong patted him and certified his realization.
Later, he opened the Deer Gate of the Dharma. Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly, saying: "The sound of the spring beneath one's ears; the mountain colors before one's eyes;
raindrops on the eaves; yellow chrysanthemums by the fence. The new geese cry out in harmony toward the southern clouds; the leaves of the autumnal trees fall, their red filling the ground.
Pointing it out thus, everything is clear and distinct. A person of true substance must immediately realize it. Nevertheless—"
It is so. Yet this still falls within the realm of sound and form. How would you speak a phrase that does not fall into sound and form?
Do you understand? "The pillar and the lantern constantly converse; at night, they turn and reveal the great void. A monk asked:
In the Western Heavens, they use a wax figure as proof [of having completed the summer retreat]. I wonder what proof Lumen uses? He said: "When the rain comes, the mountain colors darken;
when the clouds emerge from the cave, it is bright. Question: "When the void and the profound are unassailable and the light of the precious mirror is cold, what then?
He said: "Dig deep and bury it. Question: "What is one who wanders freely beyond the mundane world? He said: "His entire body..."
[His body] was crimson and putrefied; it could not be supported.
Chan Master Tianning Xipu of the Western Capital was a native of Xiping in Cai. His clan name was Song. He left his parents at the age of seven.
Master Kaiyuan succeeded Ping. In the sixth year of the Xining era, he passed the monastic examinations, shaved his head, and received full ordination.

Initially, he traveled among centers of Buddhist study, where he investigated the teachings until reaching their profound depths; his disciples took him as their master. One day, he ceased lecturing and wandered beyond the conventional world for nearly twenty years.
At first, he received his formal recognition at Fuyong. He then established himself at Fantian and Ning, followed by moving to Shaoshan, Guanyin, and Danxia.
There, he ascended the hall and said: "Lately at Shaoshan, there has been no trace of anything. Hearing sounds with the eyes and tasting flavors with the nose;
sometimes one awakens all the way until dawn, neither remaining on the bed nor falling to the ground. Great assembly, tell me: where is it? All.
If a person can produce a turning word upon this, not only will they save Shaoshan, but they will also not have brought shame upon their travels.
If this is not yet so, then: "The waves surge high at the third level and the fish transforms into a dragon; yet the deluded man still scoops out the water from his night pond.
Ascending the hall, he raised his staff and said: "All is a seamless unity, without interior or exterior; above and below are harmoniously blended and level. To call this 'pure'—"

Regarding the Dharma-body, he held his staff horizontally across [his chest] and said: "The zelkova staff of Tiantai and the ten-thousand-year rattan of Nanyue—call this the Complete Retribution Body.
He struck the staff once and said: "Striking the void produces sound; striking wood makes no noise.
Call this the Thousand Myriad Transformation Bodies. Then, leaning against the staff, he said: "Three names, one essence—this is the family style of the Dharma Master. He leaned back upon it.
In the empty hall, the views and understandings of worldly people do not accord with this at all. How shall we deliberate? [The Master] throws down his staff and says:
"It startles the wooden cock to crow at the dead of night; it can cause the straw dog to bark at the break of dawn. A monk asked: "What is the Lord?"

[The Master] said: "In the universe there is no second sun; in heaven and earth there is but one person. [The Disciple] asked: "What is the minister? [The Master] said: "Virtue clearly manifests the transformation of the sovereign;

the Way accords with the mechanisms of things' nature. [The Disciple] asked: "How does the minister turn toward the sovereign? [The Master] said: "With a sincere heart, he returns to the sun of Shun."
"Exhausting one's loyalty to repay the Heaven of Yao. He asked, "What is 'the ruler looking at the subject'? He replied, "The dark pupils are fixed and do not blink;

the wondrous body reflects what comes from the side. He asked, "What is 'the union of ruler and subject'? He replied, "The curtains and seals separate the noble from the lowly, yet the secret correspondence passes through unimpeded.
On the fourth day of the ninth month in the fifth year of the Zhenghe era, he suddenly summoned his attendants and ordered that his paper bag be divided into two parts.
Four [offerings]: one each for the Sangha, the novices, the permanent property, and the ferry transport.
Having finished, he spoke again: "Dana has a public case (gong'an) that from of old has been knocked down and raised up; today it is shown universally to all people. Tell me, what is this thing?
He looked left and right and asked, 'Do you understand? They said, 'We do not understand. The Master said, 'How magnificent! This great man does not understand even at the very end.'"
He then lay down on his right side and passed away. He was fifty-nine years old; he had spent thirty-nine summer retreats.

Chan Master Leshan Chanti Weizhao of Longxing Prefecture, whose courtesy name was Jianzhi, was a native of Yang’an. His clan was Li. From childhood, he was exceptionally transcendent and loathed the vulgarities of the world.
One day, while studying the text that reads, "By nature, people are close to one another; by habit, they become far apart," he suddenly exclaimed:

"Ordinary people and sages are fundamentally of one essence; it is only through habitual conditioning that they appear as distinct. Having realized this, he left his home and went to Chengdu, where he studied under Master Qingtai of Luyuan.

At the age of nineteen, he shaved his head, received the precepts, and ascended to full ordination. Qingtai once ordered him to listen to the *Awakening of Faith*, but the Master would simply return to his room and lie down.
When Qingtai questioned him about this, the Master replied, "Since it is called 'Right Faith in the Mahayana,' how could it be something attained through mere words?"
Nengliao then traveled with an open mind to visit Rongping at Dahong. Once, while sitting in the gallery at night, he was suddenly buffeted by a violent wind and snow.
Hearing the watchmen calling out as they patrolled for thieves, he followed them until he obtained something; he then took his leave. During the Daguan era, [he...]
Furong encountered difficulties. The Master intended to head toward the Yi River from the Three Wu regions, but his servant lost the way. The Master raised his staff and struck him;
the servant suddenly attained great awakening and exclaimed with joy, "Is this place not Mount Ao?

Upon reaching the Yi River, Furong looked at him and said with delight, "Those who will propagate my school must surely number several like you. He then remained there, personally tilling the land by the lake for many years. His wisdom...

He attained realization and took charge of Lingzhao Temple. During the Renyin year of the Xuanhua era, the Third Patriarch [Zhaozhou] was summoned by imperial decree to serve as the Abbot of Yuan Tong, but he declined and returned to reside at Letan.

Entering the hall, he said: "The ancient Buddhas said: 'When I first attained perfect enlightenment, I clearly saw that all sentient beings throughout the great earth had already attained perfect enlightenment.
Later, they also said: 'Profound, firm, remote, and distant; no one [can reach it].'"
"Can you reach it? [He] descended from his seat. He said: "You fellows who have lost sight of your own awareness are like fine dragon-heads with snake-tails.
Then he ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the past have already entered nirvana; you people should not dwell on them with longing remembrance.
The Buddhas of the future have not yet appeared in the world; you people must not indulge in idle conceptualization. Right now, at this very moment—who are you?"
"Enter. He ascended the hall and said: "Bo Yi was narrow-minded; Liu Xiahui was disrespectful. The gentleman does not follow either of these paths.
When neither of the two extremes is established and the Middle Way is not settled, what then? Taking up his staff, he said: 'The embroidered mandarin ducks are finished—look at them as you will.'"
I do not pass on the golden needle to others. Entering the hall: Under the Gate of the Great Sun, the sublime song rises ever higher;

before the Hall of the Bright Moon, those who truly understand are few. Unable to avoid it, I shall let my boat drift across the river islets and raise my oars upon the clear waves, singing of the auspicious years of Yao.

In *Heqingpingle* (Harmonious Peaceful Joy): "To report it thus is to universally request that you take it up. In the space of a single deliberation, white clouds stretch ten thousand miles. Entering the hall, he said:
"Fundamentally unborn, now likewise without extinction—this is the pattern of that which cannot die.
Arising right where it is, extinguishing wherever it goes—this is the model for living life. A man of great character must directly abide in this state."
The stream of birth and death lies within a forest of thorns; bowing, rising, bending, and stretching—whatever is applied according to the occasion, one is able to act thus.
The great gate of liberation, the Samādhi Adorned with Immeasurable Expedient Means, is suddenly and completely opened.
