Master Zhen of Yuelin, of Qingyuan Prefecture, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Tanzhen of Emperor Yong’s Monastery, ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, there ought to be thirty blows of the staff for the sake of reprimand.
But Yuelin is not like this. At the assembly on Vulture Peak, the World-Honored One held up a flower."
Master Ye smiled. At such a moment as this, he should have been given thirty blows of the staff.
Why? Because in such a time of great peace, one needlessly raises weapons of war. He commands people to blow the Great Dharma Conch and beat the Great Dharma Drum;

when he takes a step, golden lotuses bloom beneath his feet, and when he sits upright, his precious throne stands majestic. Brahma leads him from the front, surrounded by swirling incense and flowers, while the Emperor...
Śākyamuni followed after them; dragon-elephants crowded together, causing descendants in later generations to imitate one another in succession.
In groups of three or two, they all claimed to possess extraordinary style and bearing. Through kalpa after kalpa, through toil and wandering, they were unwilling to return home to sit in peace.

Their flapping lips and wagging tongues were like bells, chimes, reed organs, and flutes; their brandishing arms and pointing at their chests were more numerous than rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds. Furthermore—

Displaying their prowess by roaming the mountains and playing in the waters, parting the weeds to gaze at the wind—speaking before others until the rocks nod their heads and celestial flowers fly down to the ground—they too deserve thirty blows.
But tell me, when rewarding them for their summer retreat, how should one bestow the prize? After a long silence, he said:
"When the myriad treasures have achieved their work, what thickness or thinness is there? When the price of a thousand-jin weight is set, it naturally rises or falls."
Chan Master Guanzhen of Huating Guan Yin Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Weizhan of Zhaoti Guangdeng: A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?

As an infant, he entered a temple and upon seeing a Buddha statue, his joy moved his brows and eyelashes; everyone marveled at this. At the age of eleven, he relied upon Qingjun of Shengguo Temple.

as he stood in attendance, Danxia struck him with his palm and said, "I thought you knew. The Master bowed joyfully. The following day...
On a certain day, Dayxia ascended the hall and said: "The sun shines upon the solitary peak’s emerald hue; the moon descends upon the mountain stream’s barrier.

The profound and wondrous secret of the Patriarchs—do not seek to settle it within a single inch of the mind. He then descended from his seat. The Master stepped directly forward and said, "Today you have ascended the seat;
you shall no longer be able to deceive me. Dayxia said, "Try to cite my discourse from today's ascent of the seat for me. After a long silence, the Master remained silent. Dayxia said, "I thought..."

"You have glimpsed it. The Master then departed. Later, he traveled to Mount Wutai and then to the capital. Floating down the Bian River, he arrived at Changlu and paid his respects to Chan Master Zu Zhao.

A single word resonated with him, and the Master appointed him as his attendant. After more than a year, he was assigned a seat alongside the Master. In the third year of the Xuanhe era, Zu Zhao retired from the monastery due to illness.
In the autumn of the fourth year, Chen Gongzhang, the Commissioner for Military Affairs, invited the Master to succeed him on the throne. Monks flocked there in great numbers.
The assembly in the hall numbered seventeen hundred. At the end of the Jianyan era, he traveled from Yizhen to Mount Potalaka in Siming, and subsequently to Tianfeng Peak in Danqiu.
He accepted an invitation from Xianggu in Min. At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, by imperial decree, he resided at Yuwang Temple;

he followed [the invitation] to Longxiang in Wenzhou, where he transmitted the Chan teachings while residing in the Vinaya quarters. He then moved to Jingshan and the newly established Chongxian Temple. [The Emperor] said:
The Hall Master said: "Under my late teacher’s single hall, I exhausted all my skills; I could not find a single opening through which to speak.
Is there now anyone such a person—a man who is so free and easy yet has not reached the bottom? If there is none, you shall wear the iron bit and carry the saddle."
Each person attains what is appropriate for them. Entering the hall: Salt is invariably salty; vinegar is invariably sour. Everyone knows this flavor.
Why, then, is such a person called one who merely "cuts reeds and mows grass"? Do you still not know where his own footing remains unsteady?
If one does not travel the noble path, how can one ascend the highest barrier? Entering the hall: For a long time I have kept silent regarding this essential point. It has not...
"Hurry up and speak! Old Śākyamuni intends to dally and show off his wares, but alas, even before leaving the womb he was seen through by others.
But tell me, what was it that was seen through? He could not deceive Xuefeng. He ascended the hall and said:
"Climb to the peak of the solitary mountain and cross the bridge of solitude; walk straight ahead just like this. Even so, it is still a matter of people’s feet being high or low."
Regarding this matter: if you see through it thoroughly, without leaving your door your body pervades the ten directions; without entering the gate you are always within the house.
If this is not yet so, take advantage of the coolness to go out and gather some firewood. Ascending the hall, he said: "The sky breaks at dawn with thick white frost;
still, the realm has not yet been distinguished. Upon stepping out the door there is nothing to discern; the flowers and birds are silent and unheard. At such a time as this, what do you do?"
This emptiness does not fall into a fixed position; one must strike it to ignite the flames of the frozen river.

Do not let it remain stagnant and frozen, never to thaw. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you can utter the first phrase, you will not be deceived by this staff. Even recognizing the staff is still a matter of being on the path.

It is attained. There is only one place where you find it spontaneously without seeking. Tell me, what is that one place? After a long silence, he said:

"The thief’s own body has already been exposed. He ascended the hall and said: "Only when the white mold forms on the lips does one first enter the gate; only when the entire body is scorched and raw does one [attain it]."
Only then does one know the matter within the gate; yet one must further know that which does not go out through the gate. He said again, "What do you call the gate?
A monk asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time turn the Great Dharma Wheel within the flames—is this truly so, or not?"
The Master laughed loudly and said, "I, however, have my doubts. [The monk] asked, "Why, Reverend, do you have doubts? He replied, "Wild flowers fill the path with fragrance;
the secluded birds know nothing of spring. [The monk] asked, "If one does not fall into the traces of wind and color, is it permitted to turn back?"

[The Master] said, "The actions of a stone person do not match [ordinary] merit. A monk asked, "What is the matter beyond this? The Master said, "The wonder lies before a single bubble; how could it admit the eyes of a thousand sages? The monk bowed. The Master said, "I fear it is not quite like that. In the ninth month of the twenty-first year, on the *renzi* day, Empress Dowager Cining visited the temple and commanded him to open the hall for the formal sermon (*kaidō*). She raised the curtain to listen to the Dharma. She bestowed upon him a gold-embroidered robe, silver silk, and other gifts.

At the end of the month, he manifested illness. On the first day of the tenth month, the Empress Dowager dispatched an imperial messenger to summon a physician to attend to him. He followed [the summons].

He adjusted his robes and sat cross-legged, passing away. His remains were kept in the shrine for seven days. The Empress Dowager sent down incense and bestowed gold to provide offerings for the funeral rites.
He was enshrined in a stupa at the Peach Blossom Grove to the west of the monastery. He was sixty-four years old and had been a monk for forty-five years.
In the autumn of the twenty-third year [of the Shaoxing era], he was posthumously granted the title Wukong. His stupa was named Jingzhao.
Chan Master Hongzhi Zhengjue of Tiantong, in Qingyuan Prefecture, was a native of Xichuan in Xi.

His clan was Li. His mother dreamed that a monk from Mount Wutai untied a ring and placed it upon her right arm; she then became pregnant. She subsequently observed the precepts of fasting and purification. When the Master was born...

His right arm rose prominently in a ring-like shape. At the age of seven, he could recite a thousand words daily. His grandfather was Ji, and his father, Zongdao, had long studied under Chan Master Fotuo Xun.
Xun once pointed to the Master and said to his father, "This boy’s spiritual resonance is exceptionally superior;
he is no one of the mundane dust. If he leaves the household life, he will surely become a vessel for the Dharma. At eleven, he received the tonsure from Jingming Benzong.

In his fourteenth year, having observed the full precepts, he crossed the river to Luo. He spent the summer retreat at Shaoshi and arrived at Xiangshan in the autumn to pay his respects to Chan Master Kumu Cheng.
Having tasted a drop of the flavor of the Dharma, he immediately proceeded to Danxia. Danxia asked, "What is one's own self prior to the empty kalpa?
He replied, "A frog at the bottom of the well swallows the moon; at the third watch, one does not borrow the night-bright curtain. Danxia said:
"Not yet. Speak further. The Master hesitated. Xiang struck him with a whisk and said, "And you say it is 'not borrowed'?
At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened and prostrated himself. Xiang said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? He replied, "Today I have lost my money and incurred this punishment.
Xiang said, "I have no leisure to beat you; go for now" (the Master was twenty-three years old at the time). When Xiang took charge of Dahong, the Master served as the attendant for correspondence.
Record: In the third year of the Xuanhua era, he was appointed as the head of the assembly; several people had already received the Dharma from him.

In the fourth year, while passing through Yuan Tong, Zhenxie was newly residing at Changlu and sent a monk to invite him there. As the assembly came out to welcome him, they saw that his robes and sandals were worn and tattered, and they offered to change them for him.
Zhenxie instructed his attendant to provide him with new shoes, but the Master declined, saying, "Did I come here for shoes? The assembly [was moved by this].
Heavenly beings heard this and were moved to sincere submission; they earnestly requested him to preach the Dharma. He occupied the seat of the First Seat for six years.
He then went forth to reside at Puzhao in Sishui, followed by successively filling the positions at Taiping, Yuan Tong, and Nengren, as well as Changlu and Tiantong.

At Tiantong, the monastic dwellings were cramped and dilapidated; upon the Master’s arrival, he renovated them entirely. Monks vied with one another to join him, numbering more than ten thousand. Ascending the hall, he said: "The yellow curtains hang down."
It is difficult to transmit a family letter. A purple silk curtain is drawn shut; true pearls are scattered in the dark.
At such a time, where sight and hearing cannot reach and words and explanations fall short, how can one pass along this news? Returning from a dream, the night colors are faintly turning to dawn;
with a smile, he points to the family tradition—a spring in full bloom. Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind cannot perceive it; the mouth cannot speak it."

Consider this: you must simply step back and take up the burden; by all means, avoid confronting the taboo head-on. When the wind and moon are cold and clear at the ancient ferry crossing, the night boat turns its prow upon the crystal ground.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the empty eon there is a true principle; before a sound is uttered, ask about your own person."
A destitute new livelihood; a pure and white ancestral style. Clearly manifest beyond the Three Vehicles, vast and empty within the Single Seal.

Yet coming to act among the heterodox classes, ten thousand streams naturally flow toward the east. Ascending the hall, he said: "It is easy to clarify the essence within a phrase, but difficult to discern the essence within the essence itself.
After a long silence, he said: "Do you understand? The frosty rooster has not yet announced the dawn in the home forest; it remains dimly hidden..."
A traveler crosses the Snowy Mountains. Entering the hall, he said: "Today is the anniversary of the birth of Śākyamuni Buddha.
Changlu does not understand how to preach Chan; I shall simply provide a model for you all. Suppose he were still in the womb of Māyā—what would that be like?
With his whisk, he drew this symbol (a circle with a dot inside) and said: "It is just like bathing the golden body with pure water."
At that time, what was it like? Again, he drew this [circle with water] symbol and said:

"Just consider his walking seven steps, looking around in the four directions, pointing to heaven and pointing to earth, attaining enlightenment and preaching the Dharma, his supernatural powers and transformations, his wisdom and eloquence, his forty-nine years and over three hundred assemblies, speaking of blue and describing yellow, pointing east and drawing west—what was it like at the moment he entered parinirvāṇa?"
"How is it? he asked, thereby exhausting this ⊕-sign. He spoke again: "If one is a monk who possesses the eye, they will surely grant their approval;
if not, one must pass through each and every stage before it is attained. A monk asked: "What is the person who goes forward? He replied: [The text ends here].

White clouds vanish into the ravines; green ridges lean high against the void. [The Master] asked: "What is the person who returns? He replied: "With a head full of white hair, he leaves the mountain valleys;
at midnight, he pierces the clouds to enter the marketplace. He asked: "What is the person who neither comes nor goes? He replied:
"The stone woman calls back the dream of the three realms; the wooden man sits, cutting off the mechanisms of the six gates. [The Master] asked: "One..."
"Before the silk is even attached, what then? He said, "The boatman and his companion row side by side. He asked, "What is the matter within it?
He said, "A swift blade or a sharp axe cannot cut into it. Question: "When the mouth of the cloth bag is opened, what then?

He said, "It is left entirely to you to fill the ditches and block the ravines. Question: "Regarding the principle of pure emptiness, when one ultimately has no body, what then? He said, "The Pattern."
The traces of color have not yet appeared; at this juncture, news is difficult to convey. It is said: "A single step secretly shifts beyond the thousand sages;
letting go of the entire body, the kalpa-jar is empty. He asked: "When birth accords with the father, the whole body is without any lack of illumination. It is said: "Since the principle is thus..."
"How is it with the matter? He said, "The events of Tonghua have just been clearly revealed; what harm is there in responding to the capacities of the ten directions?
He asked, "If that is so, then every dust mote manifests the original body. He said, "It penetrates all forms and transcends all minds.
He asked, "What about 'according to principle and according to fact'? He said, "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not beat it to death. No [words].
He took the basket and carried it back home, saying: "Entering the market, one can let out a long啸; returning home, one puts on the short shirt.
He said: "The wooden man sings atop the ridge; the stone woman dances by the stream. Since the Master took up residence as abbot, he received offerings without greed and gave alms without weariness.
The harvest failed that year, and food was scarce. He exhausted his own resources as well as the surplus from supporting the community, thereby saving tens of thousands of lives.
He regularly refrained from eating after noon. In the ninth month of the *dingchou* year of the Shaoxing era, he paid his respects to the local officials and donors;

subsequently, he visited Master Zhao Lingwen of Yue and took leave of him. On the seventh day of the tenth month, he returned to the mountain. At the hour of *chen* or *si* on the following day, he bathed and changed his robes.

Dressed in his robes, he sat upright and addressed the assembly. Looking toward his attendant monk, he requested a brush and wrote a letter to leave for Master Dahui of the Yuzhuang Monastery, requesting him to preside over his funeral affairs.
He then inscribed a verse, saying: "A dream, an illusion, a flower in the sky; sixty-seven years have passed. The white birds vanish into the mist;

the autumn waters join the heavens. Having cast down his brush, he passed away. His coffin remained for seven days, his countenance appearing as if alive, while his nails and hair gradually grew longer. [The remains were] enshrined...
His entire remains were enshrined in a stupa at Donggok. He had fifty-three years of monastic seniority (*śrāmaṇera*).

The hair and teeth he left behind during his lifetime were strung together like beads, with some strands of hair threaded through them; even to this day, those who seek them with sincere hearts will surely obtain them.
In the spring of the Wuyin year, he was posthumously honored with the title Hongji, and his stupa was named Myogwang.
Chan Master Huizhao Qingyu of Dahuang Monastery in Suizhou ascended the hall and said: "To take one step forward is to tread upon the water and grass of the sovereign;
to take one step back is to trample upon the ancestral fields and gardens. To neither advance nor retreat is to stand right in the midst of the waters of death.
Is there any path for emerging from this state? The evening whistles are sparse and the pine needles are short; the spring breeze drifts and ripples."
The willow threads are long. Entering the hall, he raised the following case: "The Boatman instructed Jia Shan, saying: 'You must ensure there are no traces where you hide your body;
do not hide your body where there are no traces. For thirty years I was at Yaoshan, and I clarified nothing but this matter.
Why is it that people nowadays act so recklessly? At times, the vermilion mountain has no colorful phoenix; the precious palace does not retain its crown. Sometimes...
"Han! Sometimes one is deluded; how could I know this while on the road?

Master Wuru of Zhizhou Tizheng Monastery ascended the hall and said: "Strolling at ease in the wondrously luminous home of ultimate reality, A step taken, the body shifts, pointing toward the setting clouds.
Countless white clouds remain unseen; At night, riding the bright moon, one emerges from the reeds."
Chan Master Faxuan of Jixiang Monastery in Taipingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Facheng of the "Withered Tree" of Mount Jiao, ascended the hall and said:

"Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations—Deshan’s staff was still dull, and Linji’s shout was yet late. As for the news prior to the seven Buddhas, what need is there to wait when we meet?"
He raised his eyebrows once more. "O worthy ones, if you engage in idle deliberation, you fall directly into the ranks of the icchantikas;
if you attempt to understand this through the lens of Buddhist doctrine, that is merely a groundless fabrication. Now, you must directly strike open the single aperture above."
Severing the tongues of a thousand sages and bringing forth the treasures of one's own house—only then does one possess the "nose" of a patch-robed monk.
Were it otherwise, one would be chewing frost and ice with a full mouth; meeting people, to whom could one speak? A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
He replied, "A long drought has brought no sweet rain; the rice stalks in the fields are withered. The monk asked, "What is the intent of this? He replied, "[The same as before]."
This year the price of rice is high; it is easy to obtain, so do not disdain its coarseness.
Master Guicun of Tianfeng Monastery in Taizhou ascended the hall, struck once with his staff, and called to the assembly, saying:
"The eighty-four thousand Dharma gates have been flung open with eight characters. Do you see them? A golden phoenix perches at night."
The Shadowless Tree: The peaks have just emerged when sea clouds obscure them. Entering the Hall: A single word from Tianfeng is given directly at all times;
do not let it hang upon your chest, but you must take it to heart and remember it.
Chan Master Shouchang of Huguo Temple in Taizhou ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he struck it and said: "The beginning of the thirty-six decennia;
the source of the seventy-two seasonal signs. It is the time when ten thousand bows welcome the harmonious breath, and the Eastern Emperor issues the decree of creation and growth.
Truly, heaven displays auspicious radiance and earth abounds in solemn blessings. A fine, light rain washes away the cold."
Emptiness. The faint spring light envelops the colors of the wilds. One might say that blessings have arrived in accordance with the season; there is no celebration more fitting.
All people throughout the great earth add another year to their lives. I dare ask you all: tell me, how many years does that one person have? After a long silence:
It is said: "The thousand-year-old child has a countenance like jade; the ten-thousand-year-old youth has hair as fine as silk.
Chan Master Danxia Puyue first resided at Baoying in Ruzhou and subsequently moved to Danxia.
Entering the hall, he said: "Before the time of Vipaśyin Buddha, who could discern the truth? After the time of Dīpaṃkara, who was a true connoisseur? Even if..."
To accept it from the other side inevitably splits it into two parts; even if one proceeds on this side, it would still not be entirely complete.
This is because when [Śāriputra] remained silent at Vaiśālī, the celestial mechanism was already leaked; even if one were to shut the room at Mahāgama, [the truth would still be revealed].
In the end, the seams must surely fray and fall apart. Do not say that the body reveals the eternal truth; it is simply pure clarity, free from a single speck of defilement.
What need is there to speak of the shedding of skin? It naturally functions alone with solitary brilliance. Although this may seem fresh and new, it does not yet match the spirit of a true monk.
Only when the five eyes are opened simultaneously and the three mysteries are fully revealed will the line on the fishing pole naturally [extend].
One must not violate the waves. One must clearly understand the shifting of positions and the turning of faculties before one can comprehend entering the marketplace and extending a hand.
Therefore it is said: "Even if the teeth grow hair, do not let the eyes look back. To recognize [this] is like a chaotic swirl of empty flowers;
to speak of it is to have a divergent path of words. Since this is so, I dare ask you all: what is the single phrase that does not violate the blade's edge?
Furthermore, how can one speak of it? After a long silence, he said: "At midnight, the turtle’s eyes open wide; when dawn breaks, all phenomena are of one color.
In the spring of the third year of the Xuande era (1121), the Imperial Edict appointed the Nun of Dongjing, Master Jingzhi Hui Guang, as the Abbot of Miaohui.
Hui. Ascending the hall, he raised the story of Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman and said: "Zhaozhou’s tongue reaches to the heavens;
the old woman’s brow-light covers the earth. Having clearly exposed her upon his return, countless ordinary people have been struck blind."
Chan Master Qiyuan Qi of Qingyuan in Jizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Shimen Yuan Yi.
A native of Changle, he belonged to the Chen clan. At the age of twenty-eight, he took leave of his father and elder brother.
He left the household life under the guidance of Chan Master Yungai Zhi. He served as the attendant in the Head Seat’s quarters.

One day, after the Head Seat had finished presiding over the *bifu* (the incense-burning sermon), the student came before him and said, "I have privately heard what the Head Seat has taught, yet I do not understand its meaning.

I prostrate myself in hope that you will compassionately provide instruction. The Head Seat exhorted him earnestly, leading him to investigate this Dharma through the teachings of Wuzhuo. After more than two days, he attained realization and presented his understanding in verse.

He said, "There is no one more intimate than this in expounding the Dharma. Within a single mote of dust in the ocean of lands of the ten directions, if one can clearly realize the true principle herein, has a single person ever been seen upon the great earth?
The assembly was struck with awe. Because he attained liberation through these words, he traveled extensively to seek instruction from various masters.
Later, he arrived at Shimen, where he was deeply favored and accepted as a disciple. He went on to reside at Qingyuan for barely twelve years. On the day of his passing, [he said:]
He spoke a verse to the assembly, saying: "Last night at the third watch, I crossed the swift rapids; at the head of the rapids, clouds and mist were vast and black.
With a single staff as my only companion, I shattered the ten barriers and the myriad gates."
Chan Master Fanchong of Tianyi Monastery in Shaoxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The cold lamp in the dark chamber needs no oiling;
the bright moon in the void pierces the clouds and sky. If you wish to know that daily life is ever without interruption, a strange sprout emerges from within the blazing flames.
While preparing the robes for the Great Being Samantabhadra to perform the ritual of opening the light, the Master climbed the ladder, took up his brush, and looked at the assembly, saying: "Speak!"

Upon obtaining [the brush], he immediately took up the pen; the assembly had no response. The Master called to his attendant, saying, "Bring a ladder for this old monk to hold firmly," and then he marked it.
Thus, the Great Master Fútōng (her name has been lost), a nun of Mount Xiāngshān in Suīníng Prefecture, attained realization while reciting the Lotus Sūtra and went to see him.
Shimen said, "One cannot eat this in Chengdu; one cannot eat this in Suining. As he spoke, he struck him with his staff.
Tongsu suddenly attained enlightenment, saying, "Those who prosper do so of their own accord; those who decline do so of their own accord. Autumn dew and spring winds—how convenient they are!
Shimen shook out his sleeves and returned to the abbot’s quarters, while the nun also turned away and departed. From this point on, both monastics and laypeople followed him in great numbers.
Those who attained the Dharma were numerous.

On the occasion of the public assembly of Chan Master Zhenyi Huilan of Huayan Monastery in the Eastern Capital, successor to Chan Master Jingyin Zizhao, he said: "The Great Master Bodhidharma spent nine years..."

Facing the wall—before he had even opened his mouth, it was enough to leave people in a state of doubt. Yet, as soon as Master Shenguang took one look, [Bodhidharma’s] hands and feet fell into a frantic scramble, and he said:
"I have come to this land from the outset, to transmit the Dharma and save those lost in delusion. When the flower blooms, five petals unfold;
the fruiting will naturally follow. Had there been a man at that time with the power to illuminate past and present from behind the crown of his head...
He possesses the true eyes; in his hands he holds the tongs and hammer for severing empty space. As soon as he sees you, he seizes you by the chest.
Set aside for a moment the "five-petaled flower"—what is the Dharma you transmit?
As soon as you open your mouth, he overturns the meditation seat. Even if it were Bodhidharma himself with his full capacity, he would retreat three thousand miles.
[I] fear that beneath a thousand ages, [I] shall bring shame upon my descendants. Today, Huiyan—how could I remain idle?

Not only must I restore the collapsing order of the Dharma, but I must also clear the wrongs of all of you. He then took up his staff, held it horizontally across his chest, and called to the assembly:
"Where has Master Bodhidharma gone? He threw down the staff and descended from the seat. *Autumn Moon Festival Rain*
Descending from his seat, he ascends the hall and says: "Every household opens its door to await the beauty of the moon; yet who would have thought that wind and clouds would obscure the azure sky?
He strikes a circular gesture with his hand and says: "Fortunately, the news remains within this circle; perfectly still and unmoving, it illuminates the three thousand worlds.
Ascending the hall, he takes up his staff and says: "On the assembly at Vulture Peak, it was called 'holding the flower'; before the peak of Shao-shi, it was named 'attainment'."
The marrow. From antiquity, the virtuous of old could only look on from the sidelines; the patriarchs of the final age all stand with hands folded.
Today, at this Flower Garland [Assembly], one must not merely follow the waves and currents. One intends to point out the spring colors of the entire world before the ten-thousand-fathom peak.
Do you understand? "The skull has no consciousness of joy; the withered tree resounds with dragon-singing."
Master Ci, the Dharma heir of National Teacher Xi Pu of Tianning, ascended the hall at Xijing Xiongeri and said: "Prajñā is without cognition; it illuminates in response to conditions.
