he composed a verse to mock him, saying: "Alas, old Xingkong! You insist on feeding fish and turtles. Departing, you did not seek permission."
Xingqu merely went about telling people [of this]. The Master read the verse and said with a smile, "I shall wait for my elder brother to come and provide testimony.
He ordered that the announcement be made throughout the fourfold assembly. When the assembly had gathered, the Master expounded the essentials of the Dharma and further spoke this verse:

"To die while sitting or standing is not as good as water burial; First, it saves the need for firewood for cremation; Second, it avoids the opening of a grave. To cast off one's hands and depart is truly swift and unimpeded. Who is it that..."
He was one who understood the music. The Venerable Boatman’s lofty style has been difficult to emulate for a thousand years; few now sing his single strain of fisherman’s song.
He then sat cross-legged within the basin and drifted downstream with the tide. The assembly followed him all the way to the seashore, watching until their eyes nearly failed them.
The Master took out the stopper and bailed out the water before returning. The crowd pressed forward to observe, yet no water entered. He then resumed his journey with the current, singing:
The Boatman returned to his hometown in those days; where his traces vanished, his wondrousness was immeasurable. His true spirit was sent everywhere to those who could appreciate it;

he blew his iron flute crosswise to bring the performance to its conclusion. The sound of that flute was mournful; for a moment amidst the vast expanse, he was seen throwing the flute into the air and disappearing.
The multitude wailed in lamentation and worshipped his image. Three days later, he appeared sitting cross-legged upon the sand.

Upon his birth, both monastics and laypeople vied with one another to welcome him home. He remained for five days, after which he was cremated. The *śarīra* relics were as numerous as they could not be counted, each being as large as a soybean.
Two cranes circled in the air and only departed once the fire had been extinguished. The assembly enshrined the sacred *śarīra* bones and constructed a stupa at Qinglong.
His secular age was seventy-two, and his years since ordination (*varṣa*) were fifty-three.
Dao-long, the Head Seat (shouzuo) of Zhongshan in Yanzhou, was the son of the Dong family from Tonglu. He received full ordination at Zhongshan Temple.

Throughout his travels, he was esteemed and held in high regard by veteran monks wherever he went. In his later years, he arrived at Huanglong, where Si-xin invited him to serve as the head of the assembly (zuoyuan).

After Si-xin passed away, he returned to live in seclusion at Zhongshan. Admiring the world-transcending character of the venerable master Chen, he shut himself away behind closed doors and ceased all worldly affairs.
He would sell his yarn by the skein every day for his own livelihood, and no one recognized him. He always wore a single sock on one hand.
Whenever a Zen practitioner arrived, he would hold it up and show it to them, saying, "I have been wearing this sock for thirty years.
A temple monk once asked him in jest, "What is the samādhi of non-contention? The Master then gave him a slap.

The head seat Qimí of Yangzhou was a native of that very prefecture. Sīxīn called him a "thorough practitioner. Several Confucian scholars repeatedly invited him to visit famous mountains, but he would not comply.
Later, he manifested his passing at Gùshān in Tán. His miraculous traces were numerous.
His disciples once painted his portrait and requested a eulogy; for them, he wrote: "This fellow has a head of ash and a face of dust; ordinarily, he does not wish to reveal himself."
Manifested. Now, having been transcribed before people’s eyes, it is much like shooting an arrow into empty space. Alas! Alas! What a pity for the three feet of silk from the human world!
The person who dwells in the empty chamber, Zhìtōng, is the daughter of Fàn Xún of the Longtú. She was intelligent and wise from childhood; as she grew up, she became the wife of a high minister.
Su Song’s grandson, Ti, before long grew weary of worldly phenomena and returned home to seek tonsure. His father objected to this, so he instead pursued pure cultivation.

Upon studying the *Dharmadhātu-vipaśyanā*, he attained sudden enlightenment and composed two successive verses to express his realization. The first says: "In the vast expanse of dust and confusion, the essence is suchness;
Transverse and longitudinal, intermingling, they seal Vairocana. The entire wave is water, yet the wave is not water; The entire water..."
The waves and water are inherently distinct. Next he said: "Objects and self are fundamentally no different; the myriad phenomena are like reflections in a mirror.
Clearly they transcend both principal and attendant; with perfect clarity, they penetrate the True Principle. A single essence contains manifold dharmas, interlacing within the Indra’s Net.

In this place of infinite layers, movement and stillness are entirely pervasive. Later, when both his parents passed away, his elder brother Jian took up the post of Magistrate of Fening. Tong accompanied him.

Xing heard that the reputation of Sishin was great and went to pay him a visit. When Sishin saw him, he recognized what Xing had attained and asked, "When the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita sold his heart and liver, whom did he instruct in the study of Prajñā?
Xing replied, "If you have no mind, I shall also cease. Sishin asked again:
"Nourished by the same rain, yet the roots and sprouts differ. [The Master asked: "When there is neither sun nor shade, what grows upon the ground?
[Xuefeng] said, "A single flower with five petals. Later, [Xuefeng] asked, "In the twelve hours of the day, where do you establish yourself and sustain your life?
[Xuefeng] said, "Master, you had better save your eyebrows. Xuedou remarked, "This woman creates a chaotic sequence. [Xuefeng] bowed in acknowledgment, and Xuedou approved.
Thereupon, his reputation for the Way became widespread. Later, she became a nun with the name Yongjiu. She took up residence at Xizhu Monastery in Gusu.

Among the monastics and laypeople who sought instruction from her day and night, many attained the Way. Shortly thereafter, she passed away without illness, having written a verse and sitting in the lotus posture until her end.
The *Yumingxin lu* (Record of Illuminating the Mind) circulated in the world; Chan Master Fuguo wrote its preface, and both Lingyuan and Foyan composed verses in praise of it.
[He was] a Dharma successor of Chan Master Huanglong Lingyuan Weiqing.
Chan Master Huigu of Lingfeng at Zhencheng in Shu Prefecture was a native of Susong in that commandery. His clan name was Xiang.

In his youth, he passed the scriptural examinations and received full ordination. He first visited Lingyuan, who instructed him to contemplate the story of Shushan building a stupa. Suddenly, he attained realization.

Yuan found this difficult to reconcile, yet it was not without merit; thus he became known by this name. He went forth to reside at Zhensheng Monastery, and later moved to the two monasteries of Guangxiao and Jingguang.

Upon ascending the hall to see off the itinerant fundraisers from various regions, he said: "In Sanskrit, a *bhikṣu* is translated here as 'one who begs' (*qishi*). What does it mean to be one who begs?
Above, one begs the Dharma from all Buddhas to sustain the life of wisdom; below, one begs food from donors to sustain the physical body."

The physical body relies on alms for its sustenance; thus, through thousands of gates and ten thousand doors, one follows conditions among the noble and the humble, lowering one's own banners and canopies to increase the merit of others.
The Dharma-realm relies on the Dharma for the sustenance of the life of wisdom; thus, seated upon a simple three-mat mat, one enters a state of tranquil illumination and concentrated spirit.
Internally, one forgets the exertion of intellectual insight; externally, one extinguishes the root of great suffering. In an instant, one becomes eternally one with all beings.

Divided, yet it is indistinguishably of the same substance as the great void. Furthermore, there is another person who neither possesses great wisdom to ascend nor great compassion to descend and transform others;
they do not sit upright upon the dais, nor do they respond to the dualistic mechanisms of the two extremes. Among the common folk, even the ordinary cannot fathom them.
Among the sages, none can know it; throughout the ten directions, it cannot be gathered; across the three periods of time, it cannot be encompassed.
Tell me, then, what name may be given to it? A dragon emerges from its cave with rain in its mouth; a butterfly returns from amidst the flowers with fragrance upon its wings.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Gazing up at the Honored Countenance on Jingshan Peak, one realizes perfect penetration in silent immobility. Since Sudhana departed, there has been no news;
on the towers and terraces as the sun sets, a single flute plays in the wind. On the nineteenth day of the eighth month in the Bingchen year of the Shaoxing era, he passed into nirvana.
His stupa was enshrined on Mount Fang in Huangyan.
Chan Master Focin Cai of Shangfeng in Tanzhou was a native of Changxi in the Seven Fujians. His clan was Yao.

Having received the tonsure and full ordination in his youth, he traveled to study until he reached Dazhong, where he relied upon Chan Master Haiyin Long. An elderly master sat at the right side of his desk, perusing [the scriptures].

While reading the *Huayan Jinsi zi zhang* (The Golden Lion Chapter of the Avatamsaka), the Master looked aside and saw a lion at the tip of a single hair; within that, ten billion lions at the tips of hairs appeared all at once.

He was filled with doubt. Later, when Haiyin had finished answering the questions of his disciples, the Master threw down his staff and said, "When one realizes it, the tip of a hair swallows the vast ocean;
only then does one know that the sands of the universe are but a single mote of dust. The Master attained a sudden awakening and did not sleep for the entire night. Upon reaching...
Xiao spoke to the senior monk (lǎosù), who said, "I am not as capable as you. However, you should visit Donglin Zong; he will surely bring you to a full realization of the Great Matter.
When the Master arrived at Donglin, Zong had already passed away. He then relied upon Sīxīn for a long time. Later, he went to consult Língyuán at Huánglóng, remaining there for three years.
Língyuán constantly prodded him with matters of the "Ultimate," yet the Master found no point of rest or resolution. One day, while reading an ancient [text]...
Dongshan’s record is as clear and expansive as the open sky. He composed a verse saying: "Penetrating! Penetrating! The great ocean dries up, And empty space shatters.
In the four directions and eight corners, there is no obstruction; The myriad phenomena of the universe all manifest their secret essence.

Later, he shared the teaching seat with Zhencheng at the command of Emperor Shengfeng. He subsequently moved to Daolin Temple, before retiring to Min Province, where he resided at Dachen, Qianyuan, Lingshi, and Gushan.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Before Bodhidharma had come, the supreme treasure was harbored within; there was a pearl upon the topknot.
Since Bodhidharma came, Bian He had his feet cut off and Yang Zhu reached the end of his path. Whether he has come or not yet come, where can one find news of this?
Do you know? In the mere interval of a deliberation, I see you at a loss. Ascending the hall, he said: "A single dharma has form and encompasses all that moves and grows. A hundred..."
The mountain streams rush and compete to flow toward the sea; the lute of the Shao dynasty remains unstruck as the clouds and sky grow faint.
I imagine the old, ailing elder at Vaiśālī. When Vimalakīrti is ill, it is Shangfeng who is ill; when Shangfeng is ill, it is the staff that is ill;
when the staff is ill, it is the myriad phenomena of the universe that are ill; when the myriad phenomena are ill, then both the ordinary and the sage are ill. Do you all perceive this yet?
Is this the very place where the sickness arises? If you can awaken to it, the sentient and the insentient are of one body; everywhere is the same true Dharma-realm.
Should you not yet have reached this realization, the sweet melon is sweet to its stem, and the bitter gourd is bitter to its roots. During the Xiangsheng era...
He spoke a verse to bid farewell to the assembly and passed away in serene stillness.
Chan Master Tongzhao Defeng of Huanglong in Longxing Prefecture was a native of Jing’an in the commandery. His clan was Hu.
At birth, he possessed a thick, bushy brow. At the age of seventeen, he received the tonsure under Chan Master Jin of Shanglan and subsequently went to rely upon Lingyuan. Immediately—
He clarified the profound intent. At the beginning of the Xuande era, Prefect Xu Ren Dao of Jiangzhou invited him to reside at Tianning Temple. After three years, he moved to Huanglong.

In the sixth year, by imperial decree, he was appointed to preside over Tianning Temple in the capital. His Imperial Highness Uncle Zhonggong presented a memorial requesting that he be granted ceremonial robes and the Master’s title.
Upon ascending the hall, he cited the "Jiashan’s Realm" anecdote, saying: "Fayan merely had these words; they were truly nothing more than..."
It is clear that Old Man Jia-shan was lightly pressed by this monk until he was left with no place to stand, neither before nor behind.

Even if one does not interpret this as a "situational talk" (jing-hua), one cannot avoid still being halfway there. A monk asked, "The assembly of humans and devas gathers here; dragons and elephants meet in mutual inquiry.
As I, a student, have come forward, I request the Master to preach the Dharma. Jia-shan said, "A withered tree has no horizontal branches; when a bird comes, it finds no place to perch."
Zu Tanzhou Falun Yingduan Chan Master was a native of Nanchang. His clan name was Xu. In his youth, he relied upon Huiyue at Huadu Monastery;
having attained a shaven head, he received full ordination. He visited Chan Master Zhenjing Wen, but their karmic rapport did not harmonize. Upon arriving at Yunju, he encountered Lingyuan.
As he sat, he stirred the assembly with great fervor. The Master (Yuan) probed him for his core meaning; however, [the monk] prided himself on having "mysteriously entered" the various sutras.
Yuan once severely rebuked him, whereupon the monk cited the pivotal dialogues of Mazu and Baizhang, as well as the essential tenets of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, as his proof.
Yuan laughed and said, "Mazu and Baizhang were certainly mistaken, but the essential tenets of the *Avataṃsaka* have no connection whatsoever to this matter."
The Master was indignant and wished to depart elsewhere; he therefore requested leave. As he lifted the curtain, he suddenly attained great enlightenment, and sweat poured down his back.
When Fayan saw this, he said, "This man now knows good from evil. Mazu, Baizhang, Mañjuśrī, and Samantabhadra—how many times have they been brought to ruin by you!
From this point on, his reputation spread in all directions, and eminent scholars vied with one another to entreat him to appear in the world, yet he declined them all. Zhenghe.
At the end, Master Zhang Gongsheng urged Baizhang firmly to open the Dharma. Reluctantly, the Master finally complied.
Ascending the hall, he raised the dialogue concerning Dasuī’s "The kalpa-fire blazes forth" and said: "The six directions overturn and come crashing against my face."
For a moment, he donned coarse hempen cloth to mingle with the dust; letting the wind blow the fire was but a trivial matter. Thus, he drew in the wandering traveler who refused to turn back.
Whether it be ruined or unruined, whether one follows or does not follow—this is all in vain, for one merely uses what is heard and seen to force a needle through a cone.

The Three Hundred and Sixty Thousand Ponds of Lake Tai—the moon speaks from its heart upon the waves—to whom can it speak? A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? He replied, "Straw sandals."

"Carrying a bamboo staff, I run through the red dust. [The Master] asked: "What is the host within the guest? He replied: "Meeting the Patriarch at the crossroads. [The Master] asked: "What is the guest within the host? He replied:
"A golden whip for the imperial horse, mingling with the four classes of people. [The Master] asked: "What is the host within the host? He replied:
"Who would dare to lift their eyes and look upon the Golden Gate? [The Master] said: "I have already received the Master’s instruction on guest and host; what about that which is above?"
"What, then, is the essential vehicle (zōngshèng)? He replied: "Last night the frost wind scraped the earth with cold; an old ape wailed on the ridge above the waning moon.
Chan Master Shouzhuo Changling of Tianting Monastery in Dongjing was a native of Quannan. His clan name was Zhuang. He traveled to the capital to pursue his studies.

He received ordination by passing the scriptural examinations at Tianqing Temple. He then traveled to Sanqu to pay his respects to Chan Master Nanchan Ya, and subsequently relied upon Chan Master Dinghui Shi of Eastern Wu, through whom he mastered the profound mysteries of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
Hearing that Lingyuan was expounding the Dharma at Taiping and that his reputation for the Way resounded throughout the four quarters, he immediately went there to visit him.
Arriving during the night session, he happened to strike the core of the master’s teaching; he attained a sudden, profound realization and, with sincere devotion, entered the inner chamber. Lingyuan—
He refined [his disciples] with discerning wisdom and, for another ten years, enjoined them to observe silence. He took leave to visit Fojian, who ordered him to share his seat.
The Governor of Shu, Lord Sun Jie, invited him to expound the Dharma at Ganlu. Later, he moved to Tianning. Entering the hall, he said:
Among three thousand swordsmen, only Zhuang Zhou was permitted entry. Why could he not leap out? At the gate of a skilled physician, there are many patients;
why does he not require even a single prescription? Those who have already penetrated the barrier, please examine this further.
Ascending the hall, he said: "For example, the faculty of sight cannot see itself. The nature of the eye is inherently equal. When there is no 'equality,' then go thus. There is nothing."
The iron hammer of Kong [Zhao]: for the time being, let it rest. It is such that one may enter the forest without stirring the grass, or enter the water without disturbing the waves;

this too is a provisional expedient. If, however, the bamboo shoots within the fence emerge as sprouts outside the fence, and the flowers on the east side of the stream bloom red on the west side, then we shall wait until they have been thoroughly examined before striking.
A monk asked: "When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, why did the temple master..."
His eyebrows and beard fell out. [The Master] said, "A cat can climb a tree. [The monk] said, "Had I known it would be thus from the start, I would never have let it be so.
[The Master] said, "Save your eyebrows! [The monk] asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? [The Master] said, "When the heavens are parched with drought, one grieves for the people."
Question: "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Answer: "Not a hair’s breadth, not a speck of dust. Question: "How is it after he appeared in the world? Answer:

"Filling the ditches and blocking the ravines. Question: "What is the difference between his appearing and not appearing? Answer: "When people are level, they do not speak; when water is level, it does not flow.
On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month in the fifth year of the Xuanhua era, he suddenly manifested his passing into nirvana. On the day of his cremation:

The Emperor dispatched an imperial messenger to bestow incense. Holding a golden tray, he sought śarīra relics. When the burning of the incense was finished, there was a metallic clanging sound within the tray.
Upon inspection, several five-colored grains, each as large as a bean, were found. The messenger hurried back; when the Emperor saw them, he was greatly delighted.
This was circulated throughout the capital as a momentous event.
On the first day of the year, Chan Master Wuyin Zijing of Boshan in Xinzhou ascended the hall and said: "Harmonious breath arises from withered stumps;
cold clouds disperse across the distant outskirts. The wooden man divines an auspicious omen; at midnight, the tortoise-shell reveals its hexagrams. "O virtuous practitioners of Zen, the tortoise—"
The lines are revealed and the patterns are already manifest; one immediately perceives the twelve months of a year, each month being thus, and the twelve hours of a day, each hour being the same.
Reaching this point, it is truly like the yellowness of gold and the whiteness of white jade.
Since the beginning of the vast kalpas, it has never changed its color. Do you see it?
If you have not yet realized this, then for now let Zhang San follow the seasonal rhythms, and let Li Si’s hair turn white and gray.
Baizhang Yiqi of Longxing Prefecture was a native of Xinghua. He ascended the hall and said:
"When Kāśyapa Matanga entered the Han and Bodhidharma came to the Liang, the tracks were already laid out; thus, the descendants of later generations open their eyes only to lose their way.
If one is truly alert and awake, one will never pluck flowers from the sky or grasp the moon in the waves—do not labor your mind and strength in vain. After all..."
What is this? Today, this mountain monk has already raised a heap of bones from level ground. As you all walk along, each of you must look with full alertness.
Master Tanching of Guangxiao Monastery in Shaoyang entered the hall and said: "If one has killed one's father or mother, one repents before the Buddha."
To kill the Buddha and kill the patriarchs does not require repentance. Why does it not require repentance? Because it allows one’s enemies to attain liberation.
Chan Master Dezhou of Guangxiao Temple in Wenzhou was a native of Shangrao; his clan name was Qu.

He received the tonsure at Zunseng Monastery in Jingde and pursued the Way for many years. Later, he went to Lingyuan, where upon hearing the mention of the Shaolin wall-gazing, he attained sudden enlightenment.

He composed two verses to present them, and Yuan granted his permission. From then on, his fame spread throughout Jiang and Ze. He ascended the hall and said: "The entire body is manifest and majestic;
throughout the ten directions there is no obstruction. A thousand sages cannot transmit it; ten thousand spirits all revere it.
If you wish to deliberate upon it together, the moment you open your mouth, it shatters into a hundred pieces. But as for that which is before the opening of the mouth—how is it? *Du!* (A shout)"

Ascending the hall, he said: "Mutual accommodation or non-accommodation—when looked upon, there is nothing to be seen. Having penetrated the barrier of the Patriarchs, one tramples the path of humans and devas.
A-he-he! Whether you awaken or not, where do the falling flowers and flowing waters go?
On the thirteenth day of the ninth month in the Jiashu year of the Xiangxing era, he gathered the assembly, spoke this verse, and passed away.
Chan Master Daozhen of Huanglong Shangtang in Longxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Shanching.
He was a native of Jinling, belonging to the Zhao clan. In his youth, he relied upon Chan Master Jueyin Ying as a novice.
When Ying moved to Puzhao Temple in Si, it happened that the Imperial Consort Shu was selecting novices for ordination.

He traveled on. Having received full ordination, after some time he took his leave to visit Chan Master Danxia Chun. One day, while discussing the fundamental tenets of the Dongshan school, the Master presented this verse:
"Thick white clouds cover the ancient, cold cliffs; Strange herbs and numinous flowers are carried by the wondrous phoenix."

At midnight, when the sun was due to rise at noon, the Master was riding an ox with his back turned, wearing boots and a robe. Chūn admired him deeply. The Master, however, considered himself an obstacle and abandoned him to rely on Sōtō.
Upon their first meeting, they were in perfect accord. Every day, the Master would take the Tripitaka to read.

One night, hearing the drum for the evening session, he stepped out from the sutra hall; looking up, he saw the moon and attained great enlightenment. He hurried to the abbot’s quarters, where Sōtō saw him from afar.
He immediately granted him certification. Initially he resided at Caoshan; subsequently, he moved to Guangshou and Huanglong. He ascended the hall and said:
"I cite an ancient precedent to question you, *ācārya*. You must not interpret it as something of the past;

if you interpret it as something of the past, you lose the eye right before your face. I cite a present-day precedent to question you, *ācārya*. You must not interpret it as something of the present; if you..."
By convening this assembly, you have obstructed the original eye of the Ācārya.

Even if it were not lost and not obstructed—being neither ancient nor modern—it would still be a case of medicine and disease treating one another, a mere expedient teaching to stop a child’s crying. As for that single phrase of ultimate penetration, can you, Ācārya, speak it?
If you cannot, then wait until I am at Lohan Peak to discuss the true nature of reality (dharmatā) in depth; only then shall I speak to you.
Ascending the hall: When the eyes see forms, the ears are deaf; where the ears hear sounds, the eyes have no function.

This morning, unable to bear the call of the auspicious bird, the *yángméi* on the tree is as red as fire. Ascending the hall: The sound of thunder shakes the earth, yet within the room it is not heard;
the celestial drum roams the light, yet grasping it does not fill the hand. A person of keen intelligence understands this directly; why need one strike [the bell]?

He enters the glue-pot. If you further ask how many strands of tortoise hair there are, or how long a rabbit’s horn is, even if you were to cleave through the clouds and mountains with a single stroke of your hoe, I would still not speak to you.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The dark fellow sells charcoal, yet does not recognize the stars on the scale.
The madman doubts his head, imagining it to be in the mirror. Suddenly awakening, one finds it is neither crooked nor straight."
The mountains, rivers, and great earth have long since attained perfect enlightenment; yet the Old Man Śākyamuni has not yet possessed Buddha-nature. [He] ascended the hall and said:
"At Shaolin, he sat in cold silence, while his disciples each propounded divergent views—much like a group of blind men feeling an elephant. Shen Guang performed three prostrations."
It stands established according to its position. Dharma said, "You have attained my marrow. Yet this dark-faced Brahmin has not even touched the ground with his heels.
Ascending the hall, he said: A stone man asks a withered tree stump, "When will you bloom? The withered tree stump is angry at the stone man;
how can you talk so much nonsense? The stone man laughs aloud; the withered tree stump spits out strange blossoms. Red clouds shine forth.
Jade Elephant: White jade carved with golden sand. I ask the master of profound mystery: who is there that has not reached their home?
Chan Master Fayi of the Snow Nest at Wannian in Taizhou was the great-great-grandson of Li Gong Zunmian, the Prince of Xiangyang.
His family had resided for generations in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng. His mother dreamed of an elderly monk arriving before she gave birth to him. Master...
At the age of seventeen, he attempted to enter the Imperial Academy. His paternal great-uncle, who was serving in Huainan, wished to appoint him to office, but he did not accept.
He intended to leave his family to serve Chan Master Cijue Ze of Changlu, but his father would not permit it. His mother said, "This man must surely have been a śramaṇa in a previous life;
I pray you do not thwart his resolve. Not long after, Cijue passed away. In the first year of the Daguan era, he paid homage to Chan Master Tongzhao Yuan of Lingyan.
Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he relied upon [his teacher] for ten years, yet he remained bewildered and was unable to enter [the Dharma].

When Chan Master Yuanwu resided at Jiangshan, he saw him and said, "This one is a vessel for the Dharma. Yuanwu, having received an imperial decree, moved to Tianning in the capital; the Master attended him during this journey.
At the end of the Jingkang era, from Tianning to Shushan, as soon as a single word was spoken, the Great Dharma was suddenly clarified. In the seventh year of the Shaoxing era, Quanzhou...
Master Shoubao Wen, courtesy name Liu Gongyanxiu, was invited to reside at Juyuan Temple. Later, he moved through four successive major monasteries. Once ascending the hall, he said:
"The Dharma-eye of the patch-robed monk Shatters through the Iron Ring Mountains. The four directions and the eight facets— Their sharp corners are yet perfectly round."
The twin mallets thunder the Dharma drum; a single strike penetrates the profound barrier. Heaven and earth cannot contain it; it is left for later generations to behold.
Since heaven and earth cannot contain it, how shall later generations behold it? Do you wish to understand? When the gate opens, there is no contrivance;
the wind through the pines and cypresses aids the solitude. Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "This staff..."
Sometimes he manifests as a water-dwelling dragon, where clouds and mists stretch for ten thousand miles without ceasing.

Sometimes he manifests as a lion crouching on the ground, where the tracks of a hundred-year-old monster vanish. Sometimes mind and phenomena are both forgotten, and one stands alone as the illuminating essence.

Sometimes illumination and function occur simultaneously, with host and guest acting interchangeably. Pointing his staff at them, he said: "Under the Gate of Yanfu, none of these are of any use. For now—"
"Dao Yan, what do you usually use for seeking blessings? He planted his staff on the ground and gave a shout, then descended from the seat.
He ascended the hall and said: "Looking up, one does not see the sky; looking down, one does not see the earth. Before the ancient sword and the skull, the great ocean’s waves boil."
In the spring of the twenty-eighth year, he retired from his seat at Changlu and returned to the Guanyin Temple of Wannian on Mount Tiantai.

Scarcely ten days had passed when he suddenly manifested a slight illness. He instructed his disciples to prepare the coffin and nail it shut. On the fourth day of the third month, he wrote a verse, saying:
This year I am seventy-five; returning, I shall become the master of this hermitage. Be careful, Avalokiteśvara! A clay snake swallows a stone tiger.
Entering the shrine, he sat cross-legged and addressed the assembly, saying: "I cannot listen to the drowsy chatter of those coming from all quarters. He then personally locked the door.
After a short while, the administrators ordered a craftsman to open the shrine and feel inside; the flesh was still not cold. On the eighth day, he was interred in a stupa.
Behind the Kannon-in (Avalokiteśvara Hall), on the fifth day of the twelfth month, there was Zen Master Dongshan Huikong of Xuefeng in Fuzhou;
he was a native of that province, of the Chen clan. At fourteen, he shaved his head and became a monk.

He immediately traveled abroad, visiting all the venerable masters. Later, he attained realization at Caotang. In the *Guiyou* year of the *Shaoxing* era, he ascended the hall to open the Dharma at Xuefeng.
On the day he accepted the invitation, he said: "Those who are swift and clever act as soon as they are pointed to; those who are dull and ignorant cannot be moved even by being pushed or pulled.
When they act, everyone rejoices; when they do not move, everyone feels resentment. As for me, the mountain monk now—"
"Transform this dull stupidity into a swift departure! [He] snapped his fingers once and said: "That which previously could not be pushed out is now out;
that which previously would not dwell in the monastery now dwells there; that which previously despised the Buddha and would not act as one now acts as one;
that which previously despised the Dharma and was unwilling to speak it now speaks it. Whether it goes out or stays, whether it dwells or does not dwell—let it be for now."
Set that aside for now. I venture to ask the assembly: what kind of Buddha is it that you are practicing?
Is it Akṣobhya Buddha? Is it Dīpaṃkara Buddha? Is it Śākyamuni Buddha? Or is it Maitreya Buddha? Furthermore, what kind of Dharma are you expounding?
Is it the Fundamental Dharma? Is it the Dharma of Non-arising? Is it a worldly dharma? Or is it a supramundane dharma? Is there anyone among you who can explain this? If...
"If you can speak thus, this mountain monk’s work in the world is finished. If not, do not misrepresent it when meeting people. [The Master] gave a shout and descended from the seat.
He ascended the hall and said: "I cite Yunmen’s address to the assembly: 'Just this very thing brings misery upon people. The Master said:
'Yunmen usually possessed a majestic bearing like a king; yet to speak in such a way is much like a poor man who regrets having only one body.'"
[The questioner says: "Much! The Mountain Monk says: "I am not like that. This very thing is enough to kill one with joy. Why? Because when the heavy rain finally subsides, one sits inside the house;
yet when the karmic winds blow, one wanders again around the mountains. Even so, it is still like a beggar seeing a small profit.
Furthermore, regarding the phrase "without harming the principle of things," how would you say it? Ascending the hall, he said: "With one punch, I knock down Yellow Crane Tower;
with one kick, I overturn Parrot Isle. When there is spirit, I add more spirit;
where there is no elegance, I am elegant nonetheless. How magnificent! How magnificent! What joy! What joy! It is just like a nineteen-year-old crown prince."
Who cares for heaven? Who cares for earth? When the King of Mind does not stir falsely, the six realms are simultaneously penetrated.
Lay aside the three-foot sword; cease playing with the single bow. Freedom! Freedom! Happiness! Happiness! It is just like an eighty-year-old man serving as prime minister:
the winds blow in their proper season, the rains fall in their proper season, the five grains flourish, and the myriad people live in peace.
Holding up his staff, he said, "O Great Assembly! These two, together with this mountain monk’s staff, make one whole.
When a patch-robed monk arrives at the gate of Xuefeng, he simply knows how to follow the custom and eat the hammer; he may also get three coins to buy straw sandals.
He gave a shout, struck the ground with his staff, and descended from the seat. A monk asked, "Before the Master had seen Cudapanthaka, [what was it like?]"
"How is it? he asked. [The Master] replied, "There is one in Jiangnan. He asked again, "After seeing him, what then? [The Master] replied, "There is none in Jiangbei.
On the thirteenth day of the third month of the Wuyin year, he passed away at Dong’an. He was sixty-three years of age and forty-eight years since his ordination.
Chan Master Yetao Puchong of Yuwang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of this very region. Addressing the assembly, he raised the following case:
"The Monk of Baling said, 'It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. If it is neither the wind nor the banner, then where do you place it?
If there is anyone who can speak on behalf of the Patriarch, come forth and meet with Baling!"—thus spoke Master Xuedou.
The Way. "It is the wind that moves, it is the banner that moves. Since it is both wind and banner, where else could they be placed?
Someone came forward to give voice on behalf of Baling, saying, "I will come out and meet Xuedou. The Master said: "Neither wind nor banner—nowhere to place them;
being wind or banner—no place for attachment. The swift falcon soaring in the vast heavens loses its tracks; the golden-haired lion crouching on the ground likewise falls into confusion. Ah!
Hehe. Whether one awakens or not, it makes me recall Master Xie Sanlang all the more: "A single thread on a lone hook amidst the rain over the cold river.

Zen Master Liangshan Huan of Tanzhou, a Dharma successor of Zen Master Qingyuan Weixin, was asked by a monk: "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; we pray that you will grant us an instruction. He replied: "The sky..."
"In stillness, one knows not where the clouds have gone; the ground is so cold that the snow remains for a long time. The student said, "I do not yet understand these profound words.
I beg the Master to grant me further expedient means. He replied, "Behind one mountain range lies another person."
Chan Master Ximing of Zhengfa in Chengdu Prefecture was a native of Mianzhu, Han. In his early twenties, he received the tonsure and the full precepts under Chan Master Guang of Maci.
He traveled south to Jia Shan, where he relied upon Chan Master Xiaochun; through inquiry and study, he attained a profound realization.
Qiye left for Furuo Kai at Liangshan. Kai directed him to see Qingyuan. When the Master arrived at Qingyuan, one day Qingyuan entered the room and held up his fist to show him.
The Master attained realization; Qingyuan patted him on the back to certify his enlightenment. After more than a year, he returned to live in seclusion at his former residence.
The Prefect appointed Yanzuo to fill the vacancy; subsequently, he was transferred to Qucheng in Pengzhou. Upon the conclusion of the retreat, he ascended the hall and said:
"Leaves fall in profusion from the forest trees; heaven and earth announce the early autumn. This is clearly the meaning of the Western Patriarch; why need one seek it further?
If you can understand it thus, you will finally believe that the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is fundamentally level and easy, and that the Great Gate of Liberation has never been absent."
The pivotal key encompasses the universe and fills the void; its measure is inexhaustible and its wisdom unfathomable.

If one has not yet clarified this principle and does not penetrate its source, then even if one cultivates merit for a hundred kalpas and refines one’s conduct through a thousand lifetimes, it will be nothing but self-exhausting toil, with no connection whatsoever to the truth.
If, however, one deeply clarifies this principle and thoroughly penetrates its source, one will then know that whether in motion or stillness, all actions—
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, every action accords with the Way, and every thought returns to the source. As the Patriarch said: "Delusion gives rise to stillness and agitation;
awakening is devoid of like and dislike. Let gain and loss, right and wrong, be cast off all at once. If this is so, who is deluded and who is awakened?
Who is right and who is wrong? It is simply because these people have individually given rise to divergent views. They perceive the great as small; they cling to existence and cling to non-existence.
Their own spiritual brilliance shines alone, yet they refuse to accept it; the moon of mind is solitary and perfect, yet they themselves create opposition to it.

How is this different from abandoning one’s father within the home, or forgetting the pearl within one’s clothing? This causes thorns to form a forest upon the path to Bodhi, and [obstacles to arise] within the space of liberation.

The clouds of delusion obscure the sun. Today, by good fortune, this mountain monk encounters the *pravāraṇā* ceremony of the assembly, as the fundraising master returns to the mountain and various virtuous friends have come specifically to visit.
I cannot remain silent; thus, I shall offer some idle talk according to my capacity, bending it to suit these times and opening a small expedient.
You must all open your eyes and observe closely for yourselves. If you further hesitate or engage in discursive thought, [it will be too late]. White.
"Clouds ten thousand miles away. He then took up his staff and said, "If you can understand this, the assembly on Vulture Peak is solemnly present before your eyes.
If it is not yet so, wait until tomorrow morning for the transmission."
The Master Zu’an was a man of unknown origins. Having met with Qingyuan, he built a thatched hut among the peaks of Mount Heng and remained there for over thirty years, yet no one knew of him.
One day, moved by inspiration, he composed a verse: "A small cauldron boils vegetables while rice steams above;
The vegetables are cooked, the rice is fragrant, and people are hungry. Once this hunger-wound is healed, there is nothing more to do; Tomorrow morning, I shall paint a likeness as it is."
Miaor. Consequently, monastics braved the undergrowth to seek him out. The layman Zhang Wujin earnestly urged him to open a Dharma center, but he did not comply;
in the end, he passed away on this very mountain.

Chan Master Chengdu Fu Xingxiang Zhengjue Zongxian, a dharma successor of Chan Master Zhaojue Shaojue Chunbai, was a native of Feiwu in Tongchuan. His clan was the Wang family. In his youth, he pursued the civil service examination and achieved renown.
Once, while playing by scooping up mountain stream water during the day, he thought about it until nightfall; subsequently, he perceived the water as cold.

However, although his room was filled with them, he could not draw any water from them; yet the dusty world of sensory objects became empty of its own accord. He said, "The net of worldly existence has been torn asunder.
He went to rely upon Master Zhaojue for ordination and received the full precepts.

Later, while practicing alongside the assembly, Zhaojue one day asked the Master, "Standing atop the highest peak, walking on the bottom of the deepest sea—how do you understand this? At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
[The Master] said, "This is like nailing down one's heels. Jue picked up his whisk and asked, "What about this one?

The Master smiled and departed. He served [the Master] diligently for seven years. Later, he traveled south to the capital and passed through Huai and Xi. In his later years, he met Wuzu Yan Heshang at Haihui, where he went forth and asked:
"One who does not yet know the pivot of the gate finds it difficult to cross Zhaozhou’s bridge. Zhaozhou’s bridge—
He then did not ask, "What is the pivot? The Patriarch said, "You stay outside the door for now. The Master stepped forward, gave a kick, and withdrew.
The Patriarch said, "For all this time, it turns out there has been someone who knows the flavor of the tea and rice.
The next day, he entered the room. The Patriarch said, "Are you the monk from yesterday who asked those questions? I certainly knew you had seen [it]."

"Even though you have reached this place, you have simply not yet passed through the White Cloud Barrier. The Master said, "Take care," and then departed. At that time, Yuanwu was serving as his attendant;
the Master questioned him regarding the meaning of the White Cloud Barrier. Yuanwu said, "You must simply realize it directly. The Master smiled and said:
"It is not that I do not know; it is simply that I am not yet familiar with it. I shall wait until I see this old man and settle the matter with him.
The next day, Xuanshu went to Shucheng, while the Master and Wujing followed after him.
They happened to meet at Xinghua. Xuanshu asked the Master, "Do you remember where we met before? The Master replied, "I was attending to the fire. Xuanshu looked at Wujing and said, "This fellow..."

"Talkative! From that point on, their spiritual affinities were in perfect accord. Upon returning from his travels at Mount Lu, the Master told him of the words he had received: "Standing atop the highest peak, walking upon the bottom of the deepest sea.

The Patriarch said, "I once questioned my former teacher about this matter. My former teacher said, 'I once asked Venerable Yuan; Yuan said, "A cat has the merit of drinking blood; a tiger has [the power of devouring it]."'"* *Note: This passage refers to a famous kōan concerning the "blood-drinking cat" (māo yǒu chà xuè zhī gōng).

The dialogue between the Patriarch (Nanyue Huairang) and his teacher (Mazu Daoyi) regarding the former teacher's response to Mazu’s inquiry about the meaning of "standing atop the highest peak, walking upon the bottom of the deepest sea" is a classic example of the *kanhua* (contemplating the phrase) method in Chan Buddhism.*

The virtue of reviving the dead is something that cannot be attained unless one has fundamentally mastered the source from the outset. Having served his master for a long time, the Patriarch held him in deep affection.

Later, when he took his leave to return to the West, the Master gave him a small discourse (*xiao can*) and further sent him off with a verse, saying: "I have been away from my hometown for over forty years."
For a time, he forgot the Sichuan dialect. When the Chan practitioner returned to Chengdu, he was strictly advised to remember the Lu (Qin) dialect.

At that time, Jue was still in good health, and the Master again attended upon him. His reputation became widespread, and he subsequently went out to reside at Changsong, later moving to Baofu and Xinsiang.
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: Yangshan asked Zhongyi, "What is the meaning of Buddha-nature? [Zhongyi] said, "I shall give it to you."
"I shall give you a parable; then you will understand. Suppose there is a room with six windows, and inside there is a single monkey.
Outside, someone calls out, 'Singing-sing! and the monkey immediately responds. Thus, as all six people at the windows call out simultaneously, it responds to them all.
Yang bowed and then said, 'Just now, I received the Master's instruction, yet I have a point of doubt. [The Master] said:
"What doubts do you have? [The monk] said, "What about when a monkey is asleep?
Xingzhou seized him by the meditation seat and said, "A *xingxing* (a type of monkey)! Let me meet you. The Master said, "Do you all wish to see these two elders?
I shall also give you a parable. Zhongyi was very much like a goldsmith; Yangshan brought him a piece of gold."
"Come," he said, "let the goldsmith pay the price. The goldsmith likewise paid the full price in return. As they were about to complete the transaction, the seller added extra weight to the scales.
Although the goldsmith was inwardly pleased, he could not help but harbor a secret suspicion in his heart.
Why? "Unless this man is a spy, he must surely be a thief with stolen goods. He then descended from his seat. A monk asked: "The Buddhas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs—"
In total, one cannot get out of this circle. What is this circle? He said: "The rim of a well."
Chan Master Huirui Yuneng of Zhongyan in Meizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Daomeng Zuzun.
He was a native of that prefecture and belonged to the Lü clan. At the age of twenty-two, he...

While serving as a librarian for a wealthy household in a village, he happened to visit a mountain temple and saw a collection of Chan texts. Upon reading them, he felt as though he had attained some realization;

he immediately tore off his official cap and received full ordination. Carrying a single alms bowl, he traveled to various regions to seek instruction, first visiting Chan Master Baosheng Chengfu, whose approach was quite different from his own.
He then went to the Jinghu region to pay respects to Yong’an Xi, Zhenru Zhe, and Deshan Hui, through whom his level of attainment grew even higher. By the time...

Upon arriving at Daowei, Daowei asked, "Where is your home district, Senior Seat? The Master replied, "Western Sichuan. Daowei said, "I have heard that the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra manifests there; is this true?
The Master said, "Today I have been able to behold his compassionate countenance. Daowei said, "Where is the white elephant? The Master replied, "Its claws and tusks are already fully formed.
Daowei said, "Do you know how to turn around? The Master lifted his sitting cloth and circumambulated the meditation seat once.
[The monk] circled him. Guishan said, "This is not the principle. The Master stepped out.

One day, while Guishan was conducting a private interview with the assembly, he asked a monk, "After Huang Chao passed through, was there anyone who managed to recover his sword? The monk held up his fist. Guishan said, "A kitchen knife.
The monk said, "But it is still of inexhaustible use. Guishan shouted and sent him out. He then asked the Master, "After Huang Chao passed through, was there..."
"Is there anyone who can pick up this sword? The Master also raised his fist. Guishan said, "It is merely a kitchen knife.

The Master replied, "If you can kill someone, then stop. He then stepped forward and struck him across the chest. Guishan said, "For thirty years I have been riding horses; today I have been thrown by a donkey.
Later, he returned to Shu and established a hermitage at his former site, appearing before the fourfold assembly at their request.

He resided at Bao'en and other monasteries, wearying of worldly affairs. He thatched a hut at Laimu and remained there until his death, which was known as Huimujing. The Master’s reputation for the Way was prominent;
his practice and understanding were in accord, and he welcomed others with compassion and patience. Thus, he was revered by both scholar-officials and veteran monks.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Longji said: 'The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are but the awakening of the nature.'"
"The tree has neither delusion nor enlightenment; it simply requires realization today. The Master said, "If there is neither delusion nor enlightenment, what is there to realize?
He gave a shout (*dū*). Ascending the hall, he raised an example: One day, while Xuefeng was working together with the community to carry firewood, he saw a monk along the way.
He dropped down a piece of wood and said, "The entire Great Canon speaks only of this. Later, Zhenru Zhe said, "One..."
The Great Canon does not speak of this. Based on the words of these two venerable masters, are they the same or different?
I, this mountain monk, do not think so. [He] raises his whisk and says: "If you lift it up, it is 'Thus have I heard. If you let it go, it is 'Believing and accepting, one practices.
In the room, he asks the attendant Chongzhen: "What is your father and mother prior to the void kalpa?"
Zhēnlǐngwù said, "Venerable Master, please lower your voice. He then offered this *jiūjī* (penetrating the occasion) verse: "In the Myriad-Year Granary, I have suffered from hunger;
Dwelling within the great ocean, my thirst remains unquenched. At first, when seeking it, I could not find it;

Now, when trying to avoid it, I cannot escape it. The Master granted him approval (*yìnkě*). One day, while playing a game of chess with Huang, the Judicial Commissioner, Huang asked about several previous games.

Among these, not a single move is the same; yet whether one makes a thousand or ten thousand moves, it remains as it is. "What is that one move? The Master picked up a chess piece and showed it to him.
Huang stood there lost in thought. The Master said, "Have you not heard it said: 'Of the nineteen paths from before, how many people have been driven to distraction?
The Master presided over the monastery for more than thirty years. Whenever he preached the Dharma, he did not permit his words to be recorded. As he approached [his end]...

At the end, he composed a verse and passed away while sitting in the lotus posture. When his body was cremated, a violent wind suddenly arose; wherever the smoke reached, it rained down *śarīra* relics.
Both monastics and laypeople dug into the ground and obtained them all. His heart and tongue remained uncorrupted, and they enshrined them in a stupa at Huimù.
Chan Master Zongyin of Yunjing Baojue in Huai’an Army ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'If you recognize the bench, there is more than enough space around it.
They also said, 'If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different. I, this mountain monk, do not agree with either of these.
To recognize the bench—what kind of trivial household furniture is that? One day, after finishing his general discourse, the Master said:
"Do not disperse yet, my sons; listen further to this verse. He then said: "For forty-nine years, one great commotion;
For eighty-seven springs, this old man has played alone. Who is less, who is more? All alike are dreaming. Go back! Return!"
"The snow is heavy upon the plum branches. Having finished speaking, he descended from his seat. Supported by attendants, he took a few steps and then passed away with a sudden stillness.

Chan Master Shuchan Liaochang of Sushan in Fuzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Zhenji Congyue of Tushita, ascended the hall and said: "If you let go casually, even the Buddha’s hand cannot cover it."
Abiding. Gathering it up from the ground, the great earth is utterly free of even a speck of dust. I tell you: do not doubt or speculate. Everywhere, at every head, one sees Sudhana.
When clearly revealed beneath the mallet, it is as if one has attained the essential meaning; the eyes of infinite weary beings open of their own accord. A monk asked:
"What is Shushan’s phrase for helping people? He replied: "The jade ruler in his breast has not yet been lightly cast;
the golden mallet in his sleeve comes crashing down across the face.
Chan Master Huizhao of Doushuai in Longxing Prefecture was a native of the Guo clan from Nan’an. One day he ascended the hall and said: "Long’an..."

Below the mountain, the roads intersect in every direction; within the Tuṣita Palace, the pavilions are layered one upon another. Though it is not the celestial realm, it is no longer the domain of ordinary men.
Those who arrive find peace in their hearts and completely forget all discursive thoughts. The skillful practitioner does not shift his feet; the skillful enterer does not budge the double doors.
One can naturally laugh and stroll amidst the misty thickets; who cares about letting the years and months pass away in stillness? Since this is so:
Furthermore, tell me: is there still something beyond? After a long silence, he said: "Do not let it be pushed down by the rocks at the cliff’s edge;
break through the clouds below that obscure the sun. On the day of his formal opening of the hall, a monk asked: "What is the primary meaning of the ultimate truth? He replied: [Silence].
He struck him with the mallet and said, "What about the second gate of meaning? He replied, "The spring light remains within the curtains of a thousand homes;
in several gardens, the fresh beauty of the scenery has newly appeared."
Chan Master Bian of Dongshan in Junzhou, successor to Chan Master Guozhao of Fayan, ascended the hall and said: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing."
A sky-piercing hawk, a vast-heavens falcon—crossing neither fire nor water, passing neither through the furnace. An arrow released from the string has no path to return.
Even if you were to understand this to the full extent, you would still make the blue-eyed barbarian from the West laugh to his heart’s content.
Chan Master Huihai Yi of Tokyo ascended the hall and said: "The formless Tathāgata manifests his body;
he shatters the hosts of Māra’s armies, leaving not a speck of dust behind. Where the seven stars slant and reflect, the wind arises; the four seas return to their original master. O worthy ones!
At the assembly on Vulture Peak, Mahākāśyapa saw the Buddha hold up the flower; seizing the opportunity, he smiled. Subhūti..."

Hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, he deeply understood its meaning and intent; he wept with tears of sorrow. Now tell me: who is it that laughs? Who is it that laughs? Have you not heard the saying:
"Ten thousand streams flow crosswise, all toward the east; transcendent on eight sides, naturally lucid. On the battlefield, the courage of ten thousand men is shattered;
with a single arrow, two birds fall from the azure sky. Ascending the hall, he raised an instance: When Yangshan was sitting with Guishan...
Shan asked, "After the Master has passed away for a hundred years, if someone asks about the Dharma and the Way of the late teacher, how will you respond?
Miaoyan said, "One bowl of porridge, one bowl of rice. Yangshan said, "If someone ahead of you does not approve, what then?
Miaoyan said, "An adept monk. Yangshan then bowed. Miaoyan said, "When meeting people, do not misrepresent [the teaching]. The Master said, "From antiquity until now..."
How many people have offered these responses: "Dignified yet without awe; reverent yet without ritual form. Or they cross their staffs and hold up their fists.
If it were merely like this, how could one know the place where father and son reach mutual accord? Today, I, this mountain monk, also wish for all of you to know it together.
Do not distinguish between self and other; self and other are no different. A weary fish stays in the pond; the sick...
The bird perches upon the reeds; hesitating, it does not advance into the mud with its feet. How can one obtain a single scroll of the Master’s teachings?
Regarding the Dharma Master Bian of Western Shu, his clan and native place are lost to history. He became a bhikṣu in his youth and was versed in both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna.
When Fozhao retired from his duties, he resided at Jingde Temple. When the Master arrived there, he asked Fozhao, "The words of the Chan school are often unfounded; why is this so? Fozhao—
[Zhao] asked, "What sutras and treatises do you study? [The Master] replied, "I have a rough knowledge of various sutras and am somewhat proficient in the *Śata-dharma-śāstra*.
Zhao said, "As for yesterday’s rain and today’s sun—into what dharma are these included? The Master was bewildered.

Zhao raised his *yanghezi* (itching-comb) and struck him, saying, "Do not say that what is spoken by the Chan school lacks a foundation. The Master said indignantly, "Yesterday it rained; today it is sunny. [Zhao] finished.
"Under which category of dharmas is this ultimately subsumed? Zhao replied, "It is subsumed under the twenty-fourth category: the dharmas that are non-associated with the mind.

The Master was suddenly awakened; he immediately prostrated himself in thanks. Later, he returned to Shu, where he resided at a lecture hall. He instructed his disciples through the direct path, refusing to become mired in names and marks (*nāma-lakṣaṇa*).
Consequently, many followers departed. Thereupon, he recited a verse and ceased his lectures, saying: "The multitude sell flowers, while I alone sell pine."
The green of the colors is not as good as red; calculatedly, it will never harmonize with the times. Return, return to the midst of the verdant mists!

Thereupon, he lived in seclusion for twenty years. As both monastics and laypeople pursued him with longing, the Emperor issued a decree commanding him to expound the Dharma. He smiled and replied with a verse:
He sought seclusion on High Peak Mountain, but even there the mountain would not accommodate him. "It is better to return to Jinli and continue selling my green pines," he said.
The assembly prostrated themselves to repent their transgressions, and lecturers from the two Sichuan provinces vied with one another to rely upon him.
Chan Master Tianyou Dinyu of Yunyan in Longxing Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Leditang Wenzhun.
He was a native of Chengdu and belonged to the Zheng clan, whose family had been eminent scholars for generations.

Having twice participated in the imperial examination registry without success, he became deeply inspired by Danxia and shaved his head to receive full ordination. He then traveled across the Gorges...
He went down to pay his respects to renowned masters at various seats. Later, he arrived at Letan. At that time, Letan was just returning from Wuzhong with his assembly.
One day, as the assembly gathered for a general discourse, Letan said, "Everyone, you all are so earnestly seeking the Buddha-dharma from me, Elder Zhun.

He then tapped his knee and asked, "Do you understand? "It is like adding frost to snow," [Zhun replied]. Again, Letan tapped his knee and said, "If you do not understand, have you not seen the dry..."
Feng addressed the assembly, saying: "If you bring up one, you must not bring up two. To let pass one move is to fall into the second.

Upon hearing this, the Master attained a sudden and penetrating enlightenment. Feng confirmed his realization before the assembly, whereupon his reputation spread in all directions. He then traveled to the regions of Huai and Zhe.
Before long, he returned to Yuzhang and built a hut before the barrier at Letan, naming it Dianiu An (The Cow-herding Hut).
He subsequently left to reside at Yungai and later moved to Yuyan. Ascending the hall, he planted his staff in the ground and said, "Long rain without sun;
*zha*! The golden crow flies upon the corner of the bell tower. He struck once more and said, "Still inside the shell. Then he added, "Let the monks name it as they please."

Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Mazu’s single shout caused Baizhang to miss the mark. Linji, that little fellow, picked up a pair of tattered straw sandals from a heap of refuse and began shouting 'Hu-he!
Hu-he! at random. The Master let out a thunderous shout and asked: 'Can you call this shouting "Hu-he! Hu-he!"? Ascending the hall, he said:
'Xianggu’s skill with the rolling ball is exhausted; Xuansha’s art of chopping the wooden plaque is spent.'"
It is also exhausted. Do you still know? The fire-star enters the hem of the trousers; the matter arises from the family gate. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Three hundred, five hundred—copper heads and iron brows. The wooden flute is blown crosswise; who comes to join the beat? At that time, a monk stepped forward. The Master said:
This is also "drawing the bow after the thief has fled.
Chan Master Jiyao of Sanjiao in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "Molding clay to weigh a thousand *jin*; not even a fly alights on the scale-head.
Within this, there is a small matter that exhausts the capable ones of Lingnan. Is there anyone who can recommend [an answer]? Even if you were..."

The second month: On the day Zen Master Deqiong of Deshan in Changde Prefecture—successor to Zen Master Wenxuan Neng—accepted his invitation, he ascended the hall and said: "An adept does not use a net to catch [fish]."
Willingly remaining, he does not turn his head when called. Why does he go from east to west? [The Master] provides his own answer: "Look after five days.

Chan Master Foguo Keqin of Tiantong in Tokyo was a native of Pengzhou during the Chongning era. His clan name was Luo, and his family had followed the Confucian tradition for generations.

The Master possessed a prominent brow and a moon-like countenance; his physical features were extraordinary. From childhood, he could memorize a thousand words a day. Once, while wandering through Miaoji Temple, he encountered a monk.

Amidst the strains of pipes and songs, one is drunk and supported home. Such youthful affairs of elegance and charm— Only the beloved knows them alone.

Yet, viewed through the true eye, he is still but dregs of hemp and yeast-scum. One must know that throughout the four quarters and the zenith and nadir, there is no limit.

If one were to take unspeakably many *Buddhakṣetra* of Floating Banner Kings from oceans of fragrant waters and crush them into fine dust, manifesting infinite bodies within each particle to preach immeasurable Dharmas—this would still be merely teaching that accords with the capacities of beings, like looking into a hollow and inserting a wedge.

How much more so when employing the upward-pointing tongs and hammer as the furnace and bellows of the master; this is the entire realm of Deshan, where the staff exists but there is no place to strike.

Throughout the entire world, the golden-colored dhūta has his power of samādhi, yet there is no room for him to stand.

beneath the green pines, within the bright window—though the jade palace and pearl towers are not the match—wrapped in a patched robe with head covered, all matters cease. At this moment, even this mountain monk understands nothing. Truly.

The advisor said, "You still harbor afflictions. Upon hearing these words, the Master attained a realization.

When he returned to serve his Patriarch, whenever the Patriarch saw him and asked a question, he would immediately say, "I am not as good as you; you have understood it well yourself," or sometimes he would say, "I do not understand;

Later, while serving as the Guest Prefect at Haihui Monastery, he was reading the *Chuan Deng Lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp) one rainy night when he reached [the passage]:

Chan Master Nantang Yuanjing (later named Daoxing) of Daisui in Pengzhou was a native of Yushan in Langzhou.

He was the son of the great Confucian scholar Zhao Gong Yuezhong. At the age of ten, he fell gravely ill; his mother prayed for him and, moved by a miraculous dream, relinquished him to the monastic life.
The Master was a descendant of the lineage of the Chengjiao Daci Baosheng Monastery. In the third year of the Yuanyou era, he received full ordination after mastering the sutras.

Chan Master Wuzu Baizhang of Qizhou was a native of Huai’an. Initially, he relied upon the Fifth Patriarch, who instructed him to contemplate the kōan concerning the reason why Deshan did not answer a question during a small-scale sermon (xiaocan).
He had not yet attained realization. At that time, Yuanwu served as the seat-head (zuoyuan); the Master went to seek his instruction, and Yuanwu said:

Chan Master Daochu of Longhua in Qizhou was the son of the Ma clan. He served as Attendant to the Patriarch [Fayan] for many years.

During his tenure at Longhua, he ascended the hall and said: "When a rooster sees another, it fights; when a dog sees another, it bites. On the dais, they will surely end up goring one another to death."
"Facing the sun, why do you not get angry? He then descended from his seat. The Master’s wit and eloquence were sharp and swift;
his disciples did not know the depth of his realization. One day, he said to the assembly, "Yesterday I left the city; white clouds came and went through the void.
The pine wind clears the ears and eyes; it is truly superior to the human world. He called to the assembly and said, "This is the final word of my late teacher. After a short while—
He passed away suddenly.
