[The Master] asked, "Since you say you know the matters of the road, what flavor is there on the road? [The monk] said, "Do you not know? He asked again, "Have you ever traveled through Zhejiang?"
"No," [the Master] said. "Not yet. [The Patriarch] continued, "You have not yet attained awakening. From that time on, for five years, the Master was unable to respond.
One day, as the Patriarch ascended the hall, he looked at the assembly and said, "An eighty-year-old old man rolls a brocade ball," and then descended from his seat.

The Master joyfully stepped out from among the crowd and said, "Venerable Sir, please try rolling one yourself. The Patriarch made a gesture with his hand as if striking a war drum, speaking in the Shu dialect.
He sang the "Ba Song" of Mianzhou, saying: "On Mount Douzi, they beat the earthen drums; On Mount Yangping, they scatter white rain.
As the white rain falls, they take the dragon maidens; They weave silk, obtaining two zhang and five chi. Half belongs to Luojiang, and half belongs to Wuxu."

Upon hearing this, the Master attained great enlightenment. He covered the Patriarch’s mouth and said, “It is enough to sing only up to this point. The Patriarch laughed heartily and returned home. After the Patriarch entered nirvana, the Master returned to Shu.
The fourfold assembly requested him to open the Dharma at Wúwéi, where he later moved to Zhèngfǎ. Ascending the hall, he said:
“This great matter of cause and condition has been transmitted since the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kāśyapa smiled. The World-Honored One then said, ‘I have...’”
The Treasury of the Eye of the True Dharma was entrusted to Mahākāśyapa.

Thereafter, it has been passed down from lamp to lamp and transmitted from patriarch to patriarch until the present day, continuing unceasingly without falling into ruin. It has truly reached the point where flowers bloom everywhere;
therefore, it is called the "Wondrous Mind of Nirvāṇa," also termed the "Original Mind," the "Original Nature," the "Original Face," and the "Ultimate Truth."
The Truth. It is also called the *śakara* eye, and it is also called the Great Mahāprajñā. In a man, it is called "man"; in a woman, it is called "woman.
All of you, simply awaken for yourselves! All such things are merely idle words.
He then picked up his whisk and said: "To understand it is called Chan; not yet awakened, it is truly difficult—difficult, difficult. Before one's eyes, there is a barrier that must be..."
Mount Mi: Awakening is easy, easy, easy. To speak from the mouth of faith, there is nothing that is not so. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Who taught you to ask such a question? As the monk hesitated, the Master said, "Understood."

The head seat Yuanli was a native of the Seven Min Regions. He relied upon the Patriarch at Baiyun. Whenever he entered the room [for private instruction], the Patriarch would invariably say to him, "Monks, you must clearly distinguish between the black and the white.
Yuanli could not cease his doubts. One day, when the Patriarch ascended the hall, he cited the saying of Shoushan:
"The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it," and said, "Do you all wish to understand? Do not ask about the bride or the mother-in-law; avoid them."
Wearied by the journey, he arrived at Pāṭali. Encountering rice, he ate rice; encountering tea, he drank tea. Entering and exiting the same gate, they were like enemies from past lives.

Huìlì was as broad-minded as the sky, saying, "Today, the distinction between the monastic and the lay is clearly established. Two years later, the Patriarch moved his seat to the Patriarchal Mountain (Nanyue).

He was ordered to share his seat, but he did not accept it. After the Patriarch passed away, he immediately departed for elsewhere. During the Chongning era, he returned once more to the Fifth Patriarch’s monastery.
A monk greeted him and asked, “Where has the Fifth Patriarch gone after his parinirvāṇa? He replied, “Having eyes but no ears; sitting by the fire in the sixth month.

The monk asked, “What is the meaning of this? He said, “At home, poverty is still bearable; on the road, poverty is enough to kill one with grief. Or, someone asked about gold: [he replied,] “The golden wheel turns. (Note: The final phrase regarding "gold" appears to be an incomplete citation.)
The *Diamond Sūtra* says: "All wholesome dharmas. [A monk asked: "What are wholesome dharmas? [Linji] said: "Above is heaven; below is earth.
As for those sitting in the middle—if they are sitting, they sit; if they are standing, they stand. What do you call 'wholesome dharmas'? The monk had no reply. Linji struck him and then left.
Later, he passed away at Ruiyan in Siming.
Puyong Zhizang was a native of Gutian in Min. While traveling, he arrived at Wuzu’s monastery and entered the room with the assembly.

Wuzu brought up the story of the "Two Women and the Separated Souls" to question him. Zhizang attained a realization and presented this verse: "The two women merge into one daughter-in-law; The turning wheel is severed, impossible to reverse.
From the beginning, coming and going leave no trace; Travelers need not ask the road by which they came."

Whenever a monk from the local district came to visit, he would speak in the Min dialect, reciting in vernacular: "At the beginning of the letter, I instruct my mother-in-law to be diligent in her rest;
at the end of the letter, I instruct my mother-in-law not to doze off. Now tell me, what did he say in the middle? As soon as a monk attempted to respond, he would immediately push him out.
The elder Fashu had long relied upon the Fifth Patriarch, yet he had not yet attained realization.

One day he entered the patriarch’s quarters, and the Patriarch asked him, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion? He replied, "Fashu is not like that. The Patriarch pointed his finger and said:
"Abiding! Abiding! Huichao then asked, "If that is not so, what then? At these words, he attained enlightenment. Later, he went to the assembly of Chan Master Xuandu at Donglin.

Seeing that [Xuandu] had realized the principle of the "plain and real," one day [Huichao] held up a flower, walked once around Xuandu’s meditation seat, and with his back turned, thrust it into the incense burner, saying, "Master, tell me: what is the meaning of this? Xuandu looked at him repeatedly.
He offered several responses, none of which were accepted. After two months had passed, he finally questioned Huichu, instructing him to try explaining it.
Huichu said, "I simply took some flowers and stuck them in the incense burner; you yourself were suspicious—what else was there to say?"
The Dharma heir of Chan Master Langya Yongqi was one person:
Laywoman Yu Dao, a native of Jinling. She made her living selling sesame cakes and regularly followed the assembly to consult Langya.
He instructed her with the koan of Linji’s "True Person of No Rank. One day, she heard a beggar singing a Lotus Song that said: "Not..."
Because of the story of Liu Yi delivering a letter, how could she have reached Mount Dongting? Suddenly she attained great enlightenment and threw her rice-cake tray to the ground.
Her husband looked on askance and said, "Are you mad? His wife struck him with her palm and said, "This is not within your realm.
She went to see Langya; Langya gazed at her and recognized the depth of her realization. He asked, "Who is that person of no rank? The nun replied immediately, "There is one."
The person of no station has six arms and three heads, exerting effort in wrath. With one strike, Mount Hua is split into two paths;
the flowing waters of ten thousand years know nothing of spring. Because of this, her reputation became widely renowned. Whenever a monk arrived, she would say, "Child! Child!
If the monk hesitated, she would immediately close the door. Chan Master Fodeng Xun went to test her. Upon seeing him, the old woman questioned him as she had before. Xun said:
"Where is my father? The old woman turned around and bowed to a pillar. Xun immediately kicked it over and said, "I thought there was something truly extraordinary here.
He then went out. The old woman called out, "Son! Son! Come here! I cherish you! But Xun paid him no heed.
When Head Seat An arrived, he asked, "Where have you come from? Xun replied, "From De Shan. An said, "De Shan Tai is the son of an old woman. Xun said, [He is].
“Who is the son of this old woman? [The monk] said, “Upon being questioned by the Venerable One, I was so struck that I stood there urinating; let me go in peace.
He once composed a verse on the occasion of Mazu’s illness, saying: “The face of the sun, the face of the moon, A flash of spiritual light like lightning.
Though it cuts off the tongues of all the monks under heaven, It clearly says only half the truth.”
*Jiatai Pudeng Lu*, Scroll Eleven. Phonetic Explanations: Chù (閦):
initial *chū*, final *-u*. Guàn (丱): phonetic *guàn*. Xiè (爕): initial *sū*, final *-xié*. Qīn (嶔): phonetic *qīn*.
Shuā (shuǎ) sāwá (sà) qiè; niè (niè) wǔ jié (jiē) qiè; luò (luò); tóu (tóu);
chuāng (chuāng) yīn chuāng; jué (jué) jū jué (jué) qiè; wò (wò) yú jué (jué) qiè;
xiè (xiè) yīn xiè; téng (téng) yīn téng; xún (xún) yīn xún; xī (xī) yīn shè; làng (làng) yīn làng.
*Āo*: five-lao (qiè) cut; *Bēng*: fāng-dèng (qiè) cut; *Yì*: yī-lì (qiè) cut.
Compiled by the Monk (Subject) Zhengshou, from the *Jiatai Pǔdēng Lù*, Volume Twelve, Bào'ēn Guāngxì Chán Monastery, Píngjiāng Prefecture.
The Fourteenth Patriarch of Nanyue (the Tenth Patriarch of Linji and the Third Patriarch of Cuiyan),
Chan Master Zhikai Puyong Daoping’s Dharma heir was Chan Master Jingyin Foci Pan’an Jicheng of Dongjing. He was a native of Yichun in Yuan, belonging to the Liu clan.

Guān was renowned for his extensive learning. During the Chóngníng era, he entered the imperial examination system as a tribute student, but did not pass under the Minister of Rites. Disheartened, he conceived a resolute aspiration to transcend the mundane world.
He took refuge with Chan Master Pǔ of Yǎngshān to receive full ordination, and subsequently relied upon the elder Zhì of Yúngài, from whom he grasped the general principles of the Dharma.

He went to visit Puyong, who thoroughly clarified the essential points for him. Puyong personally recommended him with great force, and he was soon invited to share the teaching seat at Yüquan, where his fame resounded throughout the old capital.
In the spring of the sixth year of the Xuanhua era, an imperial decree appointed him to reside at Xianzhong Temple in the Right Ward; after a long period there, he was transferred to Jingyin Temple.

During the time when Emperor Gaozong was still in his private residence, he bestowed twenty-one imperial calligraphies upon the fan-screens and granted funds to provide meals for monks, commanding him to ascend the seat.
At the beginning of the Jianyan era, he resided at Huading Peak on Mount Tiantai; during the Shaoxing era, he moved to Xiufeng in Min.
Entering the hall, he held up his staff and said: "The fundamental nature is pure and still; how is it that suddenly mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise?"
"Look! Look! Pūrṇa has passed through the nostrils of Old Śākyamuni; Old Śākyamuni has pierced the belly of empty space.
Tell me, where are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth now? He threw down his staff, called to the assembly, and said:
"Empty space has performed a somersault and gone off to the kingdom of Silla. You all must take care not to—"

Clinging to leaves to stop a child’s crying; marking the boat to seek a lost sword. Ascending the hall: Beneath the Gate of the Great Sun, every day is like the third autumn month; from east to west it passes.
Before the Hall of the Bright Moon, every moment is like the ninth summer month; pointing to a deer and calling it a horse. Do you understand?
Coral branches reach out, supporting the moon. Ascending the hall: Vast and boundless, all are people searching for the Buddha; throughout the world, it is hard to find one who is at ease on the Way.
People: "The mutual exchange of staff and shouts forms a medicinal taboo; having realized there is no medicinal taboo, one is not yet the true original man.
[He] ascended the hall: "A servant from Kunlun wears iron trousers; he takes one step for every blow he receives. How can this compare to fishing for turtles in fire or hiding water in the sun?"
Shadows and echoes are but *wangliang* spirits; empty space is bound by hemp rope. Ascending the hall, he sat cross-legged and said: "To seize tigers and rhinoceroses and crush the *caotu*;
to sit and cut off the path of the thousand sages; to shatter the realm of the hordes of demons—does there exist any such monk? At that time, a monk asked:
"When one seeks not the various sages and honors not one's own spiritual essence, what then? He replied: "One."
The Master went up the steps and said, "I understand, student. The monk replied, "Do not take a bamboo pole that brushes the ground and attempt to compare it to a pine tree that sweeps the clouds.

The Master asked, "What can be done? Above, there is nothing to grasp or look up to; below, one's own self is cut off. The monk said, "Let it be as it may: it shall support the heavens and pillar the earth. The monk bowed.

The Master struck the meditation seat and descended from it. One day, he went together with the ten Dharma masters Fazhen, Cishou, and Yuanwu, as well as monks from the four Chan temples and various lecture halls—totaling one thousand monks—to attend a vegetarian feast at the residence of the Grand Marshal, Chen Gong Liangbi.
Emperor Huizong went there in private to view it; the Grand Preceptor, Duke of Lu, was among those present.

There was a man skilled in the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, a "tiger" of the Xianshou school, who addressed the assembly and questioned the Chan masters, saying: "Our Buddha established his teachings ranging from the Small Vehicle up to the Perfect and Sudden.
Only after sweeping away both emptiness and existence to realize the true and eternal can one then be adorned with the myriad virtues. Only then...
He was named Fo (Buddha). I have heard it said that a single shout of the Chan school can transform an ordinary person into a sage; this seems to contradict the various sutras and treatises.
Now, if a single shout can enter the five teachings of our school, it is a correct teaching;

if it cannot so enter, it is a false teaching. The various Chan masters looked toward the Master [Zongmi]. The Master said: "As for what the Dharma Master has asked, it does not suffice to fill three great volumes."
"What the Chan Master has replied will allow the Junior Elder of Jingyin to dispel the Dharma Master's doubts. The Master summoned Shan;
Shan responded with an assent. The Master said, "What the Dharma Master calls the 'teachings of the foolish Small Vehicle' possess meaning.
What is called the 'Initial Teaching of the Mahayana' possesses no meaning. What is called the 'Final Teaching of the Mahayana' possesses the meaning of neither being nor non-being."
The Sudden Teaching of the Mahāyāna is the principle that existence is itself emptiness.

The Perfect Teaching of the One Vehicle is the principle that there is existence without being existent, and emptiness without being empty (alternatively, "emptiness yet not non-existent, existence yet not existent").

Just as my single shout can penetrate not only these five teachings, but even enter into the fields of craftsmanship, arts, and all the various schools of thought and the hundred philosophers—Master [Linji] roared with a thunderous voice.
[The Master] let out a shout. He asked Shan, "Did you hear it? Shan replied, "I heard it. [The Master] said, "Since you heard it, this shout is 'existent';
it can enter the teachings of the Hīnayāna. A moment later, he asked Shan again, "Did you hear it? Shan replied, "I did not hear it. [The Master] said, "Since you did not hear it..."
"The previous shout was 'non-existence,' which allows one to enter the Initial Teaching (Shijiao). He then looked at Shenhui and said: 'When I first shouted, you said it existed;
now that the sound has long faded away, you say it does not exist. To say it does not exist implies that it originally did exist; to say it exists implies that it currently does not exist.
That it is neither existent nor non-existent allows one to enter the Final Teaching (Zhongjiao). At the moment I uttered the shout, it was not existent.'"

This is existence. Because of non-existence, there is existence. There is no time when this shout is not present; yet this non-existence is not a mere absence. Because of existence, there is non-existence.
Thus, existence and non-existence are simultaneous. One can thereby enter the Sudden Teaching. You must know that this single shout of mine does not function as a mere shout;

it transcends both existence and non-existence, and all intellectual interpretations are forgotten. When the Way is manifest as existence, not even a speck of dust can stand; when the Way is manifest as non-existence, it extends horizontally throughout all space.
"Empty space—this single shout enters into hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts, and those hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts enter into this single shout.
Therefore, one can enter the Perfect Teaching. Shan then rose and bowed twice. The Master spoke again, saying: "It is not only this single shout that is thus;
it extends even to speech and silence, movement and stillness—in all times, all places, all matters, and all things."
His teachings accorded perfectly with both principle and capacity, being exhaustive and leaving nothing unaddressed; those who heard him could not help but express their admiration and reverence.
The Emperor turned to his attendants and remarked, "The Zen school is so profound and mysterious, reaching such depths; yet the talent and eloquence of Jingyin are also rare indeed.
An attendant reported, "These are merely the remnants of this Master’s legacy. In the autumn of the Guihai year, he passed away at Xiufeng, accompanied by many auspicious and extraordinary signs.
Chan Master Falun Dazong Yanzi of Nan’an, Tanzhou, was the son of the Chen family of Longquan.
He ascended the hall and said: "If one is a person of true realization, their entire being is free from obstruction; their every movement is beyond the slightest discrepancy.

With a wave of the hand, they emerge from the red dust; they pry open the upward-opening aperture. They settle decisively at the head [of the matter], never violating its sharp edge; they take hold of it and turn it back toward themselves."
The application is perfectly fitting; not a single hair’s breadth is missed. The container and the lid correspond exactly.
Were any Buddha or Patriarch to gaze upon this, their hairs would stand on end. Do you understand? “Go drink tea. A monk asked, “What is the phrase that does not involve the waves and mists?
He replied, “The bright moon on the cold pine; the drifting wind at the valley mouth. [The monk] said, “All errors are swept away. One phrase—”
The "Stream-Cutting Machine" (Jueliu Ji). [The Master] said, "A point. A monk said, "Arrived. The Master said, "Borrowing someone else’s mask to dance the Three Platforms.
[The Master] asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "A white-browed tiger. [The monk] asked, "As for Dongshan saying 'three pounds of flax,' what about that?
He replied, "A venomous snake boring into a pillar. [The monk] said, "I do not understand. He replied, "Only when you step on it will you be startled."
Chan Master Kaifu Chongzhe of Hengzhou was a native of Shaoshan. His clan name was Liu. He received full ordination at Guangfu Monastery in Xinhua.

Having visited various monastic assemblies, he later met Puyong and attained a profound realization of the Dharma-patience (*dharmakṣānti*). He subsequently went forth to reside at Kaifu. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The wondrous body is majestic and manifest everywhere; one must quickly turn back and take it up. This morning, before the assembly..."
"I give it all away. Do not say that my house has anything hidden. He threw down his whisk. Calling to the attendant, he said, "Why did you strike down the old monk's whisk?
He ascended the hall and said, "This mountain monk has three seals; there is nothing added, subtracted, or left over.
I present them directly to your face, capable of transforming the ordinary into the holy. Do you all know them? If you do not yet know, I cannot help but speak further."
A heavy commentary shatters it; one seal stamps the sky, where sun, moon, and stars are arrayed beneath the wind. One seal stamps the mud, where every head and every thing reveals the true mechanism.
One seal stamps the water, twisting the fish’s head and making the dragon’s tail its end. The three seals are distinct, yet their substance is one and the same;
look closely, they are neither crimson nor red. If you do not realize how high and low are exchanged, the green mountains remain as they are.
At Old Baiyun, a monk asked: "A single stream swallows the void and stretches afar; three peaks rise with steep cliffs and precipices. The lion throne has been swept and wiped clean once more;

we all rejoice that the Master has returned. But how will you provide for us upon arriving home? He replied: "Empty-handed, I clench my two fists. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of this? He said:
"It bursts forth so suddenly it is difficult to discern."
Chan Master Fude Sheng of Hongfu Temple in Taizhou was a successor of Chan Master Ledu Jingxiang.
A native of Hengyang, he received the tonsure after selecting the scriptures as a youth and immediately relied upon Ledu to receive the transmission of the Dharma seal.
He ascended the hall and said: "If you all come up here in this manner, you fall into seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing."
To proceed in such a manner is to fall into the realm of movement and stillness, of action and exertion. If you neither go nor come, this is precisely the livelihood of a ghost cave.
How can you utter a phrase that allows for transcendence? If you can utter it, then I shall entrust you with this staff.
"If you cannot attain it through the Way, practice in accordance with it. [The Master] struck his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Huaisu of Wanshou Monastery in Jianning Prefecture was a native of Pucheng County. His clan name was Huang.
At the age of twenty-seven, he received the tonsure under Chan Master Jun of Nanfeng and observed the dhūta ascetic practices for three years. He then took leave to visit Yuanwu.
The various masters of the various schools from Caotang went to visit Baofeng, where they attained sudden enlightenment regarding the Dharma of the Mind.

After serving him diligently for a long time, when the Lord of the Prefecture, Zu Xiushi of the Longtu, heard that the Master could not refuse the earnest invitation from Wanshou, he [Zu Xiushi] ascended the hall. A monk asked:

"The kalpa-fire blazes fiercely; the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed. I wonder, will this [Dharma-nature] also be destroyed? Da-sui said, "It is destroyed. Xiu Shan-zhu said, "It is not destroyed.
"I do not know who is right and who is wrong," [the student] said. The Master said, "One is destroyed, one is not destroyed. This would make Guanshiyin laugh to death.
A lion suddenly bites a person; mad dogs all chase after clods of earth. He spoke again, "Do you understand? The student said, "No."

The assembly gathered. The Master said, "A lacquer bucket is not yet satisfied," and then descended from his seat. One day, a monk came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "You, Reverend, ought to know where I have come from. The Master said, "A man carrying dung from Hunan; a guest harvesting rice in Jiangxi.
The monk said, "Reverend, you truly possess the divine eye. I served as the head gardener at Daguai and as a laborer at Donglin."

"Keeper of the Storehouse," the Master struck him three times with his staff and shouted, "Get out! On the first day of the sixth month in the twenty-third year of the Xiangxing era, he bathed, sat in the lotus position, and wrote this verse:
"Last night wind and thunder suddenly arose; The pillar sprouted two fingers. At dawn, the lantern laughed itself to tears;
The staff, as before, supports it up. The whisk leaps across the shifting sands; It snatches back the one-eyed barbarian monk."
He took his single sandal and, with a solemn countenance, passed away. He was seventy-nine years old and had fifty-three years of ordination.
Chan Master Daoyuan of Xiangshan in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of that same prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "In the wine shops and fish markets..."

Every single thing is a treasure-trove. When the crows cry and the magpies screech, each sound is a wondrous melody. [The Master] planted his staff upright and said, "Tell me, what kind of Buddha-work is this?
There is no small amount of mess here. Ascending the hall, he said: "Xiangshan has a 'head-word' (hua-tou) that fills the four great continents.
If you attempt to critique it using the teachings of the Buddha-dharma, it is like mistaking a horse for an ox. Since none of you have done so..."
A critique of the Buddha-dharma: What, after all, is its underlying principle? [The Master] struck his whisk and said:
"One who has no padlock does not weary of movement. At midnight, one must reach for one's pillow. Take care!"
Chan Master Ledu Weizu of Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "A rushing torrent crossing a blade;
a swift flame passing through the wind—this is already like a hawk flying over Silla. Grasping the tail of a scorpion upside down; stroking a tiger’s whiskers against the grain;

practicing the 'dead-horse cure. Shifting stars and changing constellations; overturning mountains and emptying lakes—it is still somewhat lacking. Heh! Elder Zu’s previous words were not [in accord with]..."
[The Master] delivered these supplementary remarks and then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Qixia Dehong of Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of Hengyang. He traveled extensively among the seats of various masters and later attained awakening at Letan.
He emerged from seclusion to reside at Wuhui, and subsequently moved to Qixia. Entering the hall, he said: "When those of superior capacity meet, they strike the stone."
Fire! A shooting star bursts forth, passing by in the blink of an eye. This fellow has already attained Buddhahood long ago;
it is truly laughable that this deluded Chan practitioner sits in the dark. A-he-he! When will this dream in the murky depths ever end? Guarding his rice basket until it is empty, he endures hunger.
The Head Seat Daoqiong of Mukan at Kainsen in Jianning Prefecture was a native of Shangrao. The monastic communities honored him as a man of venerable virtue;

Lestan also remarked that he had undergone extensive training. On the day he sat upon the teaching seat, he once raised the saying regarding the "single shoe returning to the West" and said to the assembly:

"To pass away while seated or standing, or to manifest a 'reverse transformation' (death), is certainly possible; however, there has yet been no instance of one who has departed and then emerged again."
Regarding the one who left behind his sandals: was it that the descendants of later generations were unable to equal the Patriarch? Or was it that the Patriarch had this one "extra turn" remaining?

He then laughed loudly and said, "Old wild fox. In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Xiangshou era, the Governor Xin changed Chao-hua Temple from the Vinaya school to the Chan school and invited him to be its first patriarch.
Qiong said to the special envoy, "I originally had no intention of being among men."
I wish to be a son of this mountain, merely to rectify its lineage. However, I fear that many will be unable to go there.

Having accepted the invitation, I took the painted image of Bao Feng that I had preserved and the two characters "Mu'an" (Wood Hermitage). I then wrote a verse and entrusted it to the elder Qingquan Heng, to be sent to my dharma-heir Huishan.
The verse says: "The mouth and beak are not those of a sage; He loves to beat the drum amidst the forest groves."
"No," [he replied]. He entrusted the matter to the Head Seat of Xuefeng Mountain, saying, "Scold him for me severely; do not let him off.

Turning to the messenger, he said, "Convey my words to the Minister: my departure is so urgent that I have no time to compose a formal reply. His voice ceased and he passed away on the sixteenth day of the tenth month.
Jingchun, the Librarian (Zhizang), was a native of Meizhou. He received ordination at Huadu Monastery and subsequently went to rely upon Baofeng.
During one of his private interviews, Baofeng asked, "How much does the iron ox of Shanfu weigh? Jingchun stepped forward with his hands joined and said, "But tell me, how much does it weigh?"
Feng said, "The tail is north of the Yellow River; the head rests south of the Yellow River. Shancai has no nostrils; he continues to travel south in search of teachers.

When Chun hesitated, Feng struck him. Suddenly, he attained sudden enlightenment. Having served as an attendant for many years, he eventually retired to live in seclusion among the forests and ravines.
I once composed a verse that says: Afraid of the cold, I am too lazy to shave my tangled hair; Loving the warmth, I frequently add more firewood to the hearth.
My tattered *kāṣāya* robe is draped on in a disheveled manner; Who could trouble themselves to arrange it with such effort?
Xinzhou Huaiyu Yongxuan, the Head Seat, was a native of Siming. His clan name was Peng. He became a monk in his youth and proceeded directly to a monastic community. He attended Litan at Huangbo.
One day, while returning from Linchuan with his alms bowl, he encountered Litan’s evening discourse, which included the words:
"A single leaf drifting through the air reveals autumn; the Dharma-body must penetrate the bustling clamor. Upon hearing this, Yongxuan grasped the essential meaning. Litan...

This serves as evidence. Later, he relied upon Daohui; Daohui also considered him to be of that same caliber. For this reason, high officials and eminent personages welcomed him with the honors due to a high-ranking monk, yet he did not accept.
He once composed a verse on the story of Dayu’s response to the Buddha, which draws from the poetry of Old Du: "The saw has split the scale-weight;
the red rice, pecked at until exhausted, remains as parrot-sized grains; the green paulownia tree, where the phoenix has grown old, remains its branch."
Chan Master Wuxiang Fazhen of Lushan in Qingyuan Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Huilan of Guangxiao Biluo. He was a descendant of the Later Liang Emperor of the South.

Having received full ordination at Guǎngshèng Monastery in Dōngchéng, Wúhé, he traveled extensively among monastic communities and eventually entered the quarters of Guangxiao, where he was subsequently promoted to the position of Linji.
He went to inquire about the circumstances of Huangbo’s encounter with Mazu. As the Master was about to offer a reply, Xiaozhen let out a single, piercing shout.

Upon hearing it, the Master’s lingering "thieving mind" was utterly extinguished, and he received a formal transmission of dharma. He stayed for one night and then departed; from this point on, his reputation became preeminent in his time, and he went forth to reside at Xingjiao Temple.
He moved to Jianfu and then to Lushan. Entering the hall, he said: "In the depths of Lufeng, no one arrives; before the gate, snow weighs down the withered pines.
The sound of the board startles those dreaming within; a single ancient road is swept clear by the pure breeze. Entering the hall again, he said:

"If you wish to clarify that which transcends [the ordinary], you must possess the eye atop the crown of your head. Only when you possess this eye will you truly accord with the purpose of leaving the household life."
Mind. Having already attained accord with the mind of renunciation, one constantly possesses the eye of the crown of the head. Do you wish to understand this eye of the crown?

The people of the four capitals wear their robes and eat their meals; the people of the two provinces of Zhe and Xi are content and well-fed as they please. At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, the fragrant breeze is pure; three or four peach trees grow there, bearing blossoms.
Chan Master Lingyan Dezong of Wenzhou, the fourteenth-generation successor of Qingyuan (the eighth generation of Yunmen), was a native of Kuaiji.
His clan name was Li. He received full ordination at Dashi Monastery.
He served as the presiding priest for the capital temple and proceeded to the seat of Bao-yin. He was dedicated to asceticism, taking only one meal per day.

After a long time, he attained awakening. Not long after, he heard that Huian’s transformation through teaching was flourishing in the region of Guanzhong; he went there to pay his respects. Upon meeting him, Huian praised him highly.
When Yin heard of him, he welcomed him back to serve as his head seat (*dìyī zuò*). His reputation spread far and wide.

When the Governor of Wenzhou sent an imperial envoy to appoint him as the abbot of Lingyan, he lay stubbornly refusing to respond. He closed his door and cut off all food for several days before finally complying.
Disciples gathered like clouds. On the day he entered the monastery, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Lingyan? He replied, "The ground is divided from within the Three Isles; the gate faces..."

The opening was situated between two peaks. When Fang La gathered his forces in a revolt and the masses fled in terror, the Master sat upright and composed. When the rebels arrived, they bowed in reverence and departed.
On the twenty-third day of the sixth month in the Xinhai year of the Xuanhua era, while partaking in a meal offering, he happened to suffer from poisoning from oil;

his illness became critical. His disciples requested that he take medicine with wine, but the Master rebuked them, saying: "Where there is birth, there must be death. This can be understood. He passed away.
"Shall I violate the precepts to escape death? He then recited a verse: "I have dwelt here for twenty-four years, establishing causes and conditions as circumstances required.
Now I depart; what need is there for a specific time? The wind remains in the green pines, and the moon is in the sky. Having drunk from his own eyes, he passed away.
Chan Master Xiang of Jingci Temple in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall. The ancients said, "A single film over the eye causes empty flowers to fall in confusion.
Holding up his staff, he said, "When Jingci raises this staff, is it not 'a single film over the eye'?
Within this staff, the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas all manifest bodies sixteen feet tall, with the purple-golden hue of refined gold, riding upon their lands."
Traveling through the ten directions, preaching all dharmas, and delivering all sentient beings—is this not like empty flowers falling in confusion?
Is there anyone here right now who can sit and cut it off before the staff has even been raised? Come forth and meet with Jingci.
If there is no one, you must by all means avoid settling for the notion that "space originally has no flowers" or that "the eye originally has no cataracts. Now then—
He threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
Zen Master Haeyul Yong of Xuefeng in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "One is not; two is not. The mouth eats rice; the nose breathes air.
Cease speaking of the Northern Dipper concealing its body; what need is there to speak of the South Mountain turtle-nose? Bring forth your family wealth."
He went out to engage in relations with others. I urge you not to compete for the profit of a needle’s point.
Chan Master Dazhu Dahe of Ganlu Monastery in Zhenjiang Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Daohe of Changlu.
Fuzhi, his native place, was Changle. Having received the tonsure at a youthful age, he carried a single almsbowl.
Youfang was a man of lofty conduct that set him apart from his peers; he was revered by the monastic communities. He went forth to reside at Ganlu Temple, where he ascended the hall and said:
"The sages and worthies are not divided; past and present are one. It may be said that fire seeks dryness and water flows to moisture.
Dig the well and drink; plow the field and eat. O Great Assembly! The Old King of the Eastern Village has departed and does not return; the yellow leaves fall in profusion, scattered in vain."
A monk asked Zen Master Ming of Tiantong in Yizhou, "Did Lingyun truly awaken to the Way upon seeing the peach blossoms?
The Master said, "Every depth has its source. The monk asked, "As for Xuansha’s words, 'It is perfectly accurate, most perfectly accurate;
I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate,' what was his meaning? The Master said, "He would leave the whole world in doubt."
Chan Master Yuanzhi Fachun of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "My mind is like the autumn moon, clear and bright in the azure depths.
The Master then gave a shout and said: "Hanshan has fallen into error! "O practitioners of Zen, this clarity and purity is free from dust;
how could it be compared to the moon on the Mid-Autumn Festival? This spiritual brilliance is beyond all dependence; it cannot be equaled by the world-illuminating pearl."
Standalone, it reveals heaven and earth; its light swallows the myriad phenomena. Pervading all under heaven and across the earth, it shines through antiquity and soars through the present.

But tell me, what is this? After a long silence, he said: "On this night, the single orb is full; where is its clear light not present? [The Master] ascended the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month.
Case: Master Zu Zhao said: "At midnight he leaped over the city wall, calling out but unable to turn him back; deep within the Snow Mountains, not even a speck of dust remains.
That the reed sprouts pierce his knees is but an ordinary matter; upon seeing the morning star, his eyes opened wide. The former master spoke thus.
It is perfect and complete; yet, for now, there is no path for one to emerge from it. Where this mountain monk sees it, I wish for all of you to know it together:
the scene of leaping over the city walls at midnight is empty; deep within the Snowy Mountains is "tsui lu du.
Even if one were to awaken upon seeing the morning star, that would already have been a failure of spirit at that time. Let clear-eyed monks do as they please with their critical scrutiny.
Chan Master Daichang of Yuedang at Jingci Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Miaozhan Sihui of Xuefeng. He was a native of Baixi in Xiadu and belonged to the Wu clan.
His mother gave birth to him after experiencing a miraculous dream. At the age of six, he followed Dezheng of Luyuan; at thirteen, he received the tonsure. After this...
In his second year, he visited Miaozhan at Daochang Monastery. Upon hearing the master raise the "Mount Sumeru" koan, he realized his true home beneath the words.
Miaozhan cautioned him to conceal his talents within himself and further showed him Xuedou’s verse on "Daily Diminution for the Path," instructing him to investigate it thoroughly. One day—

Having finally realized the profound and subtle depths, he immediately went to inform Zhàn, who expressed his joy for him. Thereupon, he resolved to travel extensively to seek instruction from various masters.
Leading a group of outstanding contemporaries, such as Wén-ān Zōng and Zhèngtáng Biàn, they traveled together through the regions of Huái, Chǔ, Hú, and Xiāng.
They relied upon several great masters, including Chánglíng Zhuó, Bǎoníng Jí, and Yuánwù Qín, all of whom held him in high esteem. He was particularly [favored] by Yuán...
In the meditation hall, his responses to questions were unhindered; the Master specially invited him to sit at the front and appointed him as scribe.

Zhenxing brushed aside his robes and departed without looking back, returning to visit Zhàn at Jìngcí Temple, where he was tasked with managing the library and preaching the Dharma for the assembly. His reputation for the Way resounded widely (at the age of twenty-three). After a long time had passed...
Hu Shou appointed Miaozhan Gouyou as the abbot of a monastery; the Master accepted the summons.
Before long, he was appointed to Qionglong and Ruiguang, and subsequently transferred to Yuyang. During the Jianyan era, he retired from his seat and rode a yellow ox while traveling to Tiantai.

At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, he resided at Daji in Min, and later moved to Guishan on Xiufeng. When his followers numbered in the tens of thousands, an imperial decree ordered him to move to Jinshan.

He ascended Mount Jiang. Mount Jiang had recently been ravaged by war; when the Master arrived, he renovated it entirely. Furthermore, by imperial decree, he was appointed to Jing Mountain and Lingyin.

In the winter of the Gengchen year, he submitted a memorial requesting the issuance of ordination certificates (*duji*). In the spring of the Xinsi year, permission was granted. That same year, he withdrew to seclusion at Lingquan.
In the autumn of the Bingxu year of the Qiandao era, as the position of Abbot at Jingci Temple was vacant, the monks presented their petitions with earnest sincerity.

The Master was seated. He requested the Master to rouse him [from his hesitation]. Wang Gongyan entered the mountain to pay his respects and make his request; consequently, the Master could not decline. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The Way does not belong to knowing, nor does it belong to not-knowing. Knowing is deluded awareness; not-knowing is indeterminate (avyākṛta).
If one truly reaches the Way that is free from doubt, one will not let a copper basin obstruct him while he strikes a rat. Therefore, he withdrew his body and entered Qian. From...

Coming from within the hall, the teaching platform and bench are set steady; let us briefly raise three cups. In the earnestness of calling one another "elder brother" and "younger brother," we ensure that descendants remain to discern the ashes of the kalpa.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you have not yet penetrated the Patriarch’s Barrier, there are a thousand difficulties and high obstacles."

Once you have passed through the patriarch’s barrier, there are a thousand difficulties and ten thousand hardships. Setting aside for a moment the difficulty of not yet having passed through, why is it difficult once you have already passed through?
Though you may gain the price by setting down the strainer, moving the handle of the ladle is quite groundless.
Ascending the hall, he said: "One who resembles me has no affinity with you. I overturn the medicinal cauldron and pour out the furnace smoke;
yet that single grain of elixir remains clearly visible—how many years has it wandered through the human world? *Du!* Ascending the hall, he said: "A wild goose flies across the vast sky."
The reflection sinks into the cold water; the wild geese have no intention of leaving a trace, and the water has no thought of retaining the reflection.
If one can be thus, it is precisely the right time to buy straw sandals and travel the path. Therefore it is said: "If there is movement, the shadow appears; if there is awakening, ice forms.
To be neither moving nor awakening is to be right within dead water. Setting aside for a moment the question of whether the Elder of Jianfu could emerge from it, as for Yuyang:
"What is it today? [The Master replied: "I told you not to travel the path beneath the mountain; indeed, one hears the cry of a monkey that breaks the heart.
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and held up his whisk, saying: "At the start of the year, when one grasps the brush, all matters are auspicious.
Suddenly, a man came forward and said: "Master, this is what a village headman uses to write on the gates of a common hamlet. Why [do you use it]?"
Mozang treated this as the *zong* (essence) of the teaching while seated upon the Flower-King Throne. He simply said to him: "A thousand head of oxen are presented;
a hundred horses are brought in. A monk asked: "When the Great Function manifests before one, and no rules or regulations remain—what then?
He replied: "The brothers of the Zhang family are far too unkind. The monk said: "In that case, is it so that all places are [the Way]? He replied: "Do not be so impulsive."
"Excellent. Question: "When the mind arises, phenomena arise; when the mind ceases, phenomena cease. But at the moment when both mind and phenomena are forgotten, where do arising and ceasing reside?
He said: "What you receive with your left hand, use with your right. Question: "What is the matter of the ancestral school from above?
He said: "An acre of land. [The questioner] said: "If one understands it in this way, what then? He said: "Buried."
"Not a few. A monk asked, "What is it like when one comes with head held high and horns upon it? The Master said, "I, the old monk, simply watch. The monk said, "After watching, what then?
The Master said, "Rising by oneself and falling by oneself. The monk said, "Can you, Reverend, get out of this? The Master said, "Bring me a blade of grass.
As the monk hesitated, the Master said, "Why such a desperate hurry? A monk asked, "What is the fundamental nature of all Buddhas?"
Yuan said, "Asking for directions at one’s own door. He asked, "Is there anything further above? Yuan said, "Throwing a brick under the moon. He asked, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer?
Yuan said, "Discussing a choking while drinking water. The Master’s realization through wisdom was profound and penetrating; his conduct was lofty and remote.
When he lowered his hand [to teach], he did not grant even the slightest concession. Many who sought to pass through his barrier retreated in despair upon seeing the precipice. This was Shao.
When the [Buddhist] Revival arrived, the monastic communities were nearly on the verge of collapsing to the ground. The Master exerted his strength to support them with the Orthodox Teaching.
For over fifty years, whenever princes, dukes, or high ministers passed by his gate, he would go out to welcome them; yet he never once descended from his hall. He once said to the assembly:

I wish to find a man of true sincerity who aspires to the Way, so that he may achieve great penetration and great awakening, thereby establishing the Yunmen school and ensuring that all those throughout the world who turn toward my teaching know of this lineage.
Then, people will naturally flow toward it like water rushing into a ravine; why should they laboriously traverse the monastic forests by taking a circuitous path?
On the twentieth day of the first month of the Xinmao year, he beat the drum and took leave of the assembly; far and near, all [were moved].

As the assembly gathered, there was not one who did not weep as they begged him to remain. When the attendants requested a verse for a second time, the Master rebuked them, saying, "Canyuan Zhao and Daotong, as well as my late teacher, none of them acted in this manner.
He then closed his eyes and passed away. Seven days later, his entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the eastern ridge of the monastery;
it was named Changle (Eternal Bliss). He was eighty-three years of age and had been a monk for sixty-nine years.
Chan Master Liaotang of Jing Mountain in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall and said:

"When practitioners who investigate the profound encounter circumstances and conditions, their inability to penetrate through directly and attain liberation is due to the depth of their karmic consciousness and the stubborn adherence of their deluded emotions."
The six gates have not yet ceased; one place remains unpenetrated. Utterly pure and devoid of a single speck, it is difficult for sentient beings to reach.
You must enter the forest without stirring a blade of grass and enter the water without disturbing a ripple; only then can you follow the current of birth and death and enter the world of humans.
Do you all understand? (He strikes once with his staff and says: "Receive this right here!"
Chan Master Daji Fayuan of Fuzhou ascended the hall. Holding up his whisk, he said: "It cannot be traced; it cannot be painted.
Swallowing a hot iron ball, one opens wide the great mouth. At Mount Ji, the retribution is such as this; I laugh at myself that it is rarely seen in the human world."
Chan Master Liaoxin of Mount Jinshan in Zhenjiang Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Who would say that the single word 'Buddha' does not exist?
Wooden horses and clay oxen fill the roads. Leaning against the balustrade, the spring colors fade; the sea breeze blows through the azure coral.
Are there any here who respond with the same sound or seek one another through the same breath? When the hundred birds do not come, the pavilions remain closed.
"I hear only the night rain dripping on the banana leaves.
Chan Master Shisong Zu Tian of Fuzhou was asked by a monk, "What is 'the non-arising of the single mind'?
He replied, "Seven strides, eight bounds. The monk asked, "What is 'the faultlessness of all dharmas'? He replied, "A complete exposure."
Chan Master Zisheng Yuanzu of Jiaxing Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Ba'en Baoyue Jueyan, was asked by a monk: "The purple-gold lotus supports feet with the thousand-spoked wheel;

the white jade hair-tuft illuminates the body of myriad virtues. What is the Buddha? He replied, "Dragging a spear and wearing armor. [The monk] said, "The *Guanhua* (Flower-Piercing) contains a thousand verses."
Although their categories differ, when pointing to the moon, they both return to the same principle. What is the Dharma? He said: "The Yuanfeng statutes and the Shaoshing ordinances state:
'In the groves below, one is a refined guest beyond the mundane world; in the human realm, one is fit to be a lotus amidst the fire. What is the Sangha?"
It is said: Unfolding his mat and grasping his bowl, [he was] Chan Master Jishi Huiguang of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Cishou Huishen of Huelin.
He was the son of the Xia family of Qiántáng. As a person, he was diligent...
Suffering. He sat at the site of enlightenment four times and three times received imperial edicts. Entering the hall, he said: "There is no need to seek the Truth; why must one cease seeing?
Riding a cow backward into the Buddha Hall, a single sound of the barbarian flute makes heaven and earth empty.
Who knows who can recognize the face of Gautama? A monk asked: "At the peak of Feilai Peak, the mountain colors manifest the Pure Dharma Body. [How does it] merge with the valley stream?"
By the bridge, the sound of the stream performs the mark of the broad and long tongue. At this very moment, what is the "One Song of Yunmen"? He said:
"The rain at the third watch upon the leaves of the banana tree. [The Master] said: "A single phrase fully presented transcends Buddhas and patriarchs;
all those in purple and crimson at the banquet are connoisseurs of the sound. He added: "When meeting people, do not err in its presentation."
Chan Master Miaoyin Yugou of Guoqing Temple in Taizhou ascended the hall and said:
"Why is it that those who can speak with their whole mouths do not know 'that which exists'? Why is it that those who know 'that which exists' to the full cannot speak with their whole mouths?
Tell me, where does this confusion lie? If you can understand this, I grant you that illumination and function are simultaneous, and clarity and darkness are both resolved."
If this were not yet so—whether one has attained the Way or not, whether one knows it exists or not—the Great Tiger of the Southern Mountain can let out a lion’s roar.
Master Chuchi Puzhao of Guoqing Temple in Taizhou ascended the hall and said: "Lingyun awakened through the peach blossoms; Xian..."
Śāṇavāsa was unwilling; how many deluded practitioners of Chan there are! They carry snow away to fill the well. Now the spring flowers bloom again—who can grasp this meaning?
Truly, few know it: when the flowers fall, the spring breeze is still.
Chan Master Jiuzuo Huisui of Quanzhou ascended the hall and said:

"Today, Jiuzuo shall launch a single iron boat upon the solitary peak at the very summit, cutting off the vital passages for all people under heaven, so that they cannot raise their oars or move their paddles.
There is a silken prize; tell me, in whose hands does it lie? Raising his staff, he said: "Look! Look!"
"Those who face the Way are dragons; they do not easily believe. Only when they have casually snatched it away do they startle others.

This was Zen Master Shoujian of Wanshan on Mount Lu, a successor of Zen Master Huihai of Huilin, whose native place was Xiangzhou. On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said: "There is one..."
This person does not bow to the New Year; they do not welcome the coming year. Cold and heat cannot invade their body;
sages and ordinary folk cannot confuse their traces. From the beginning, their nostrils have pointed toward the heavens—who cares for the many years on the calendar?
"Assembly, tell me: where is this person now? He planted his staff and said: "Hah! Hah! Hah! Nowhere to go."
Chan Master Shoulong of Wanshan on Mount Lu succeeded his elder brother, Chan Master Jian, upon the latter’s seat. Students flocked to him from all directions.
One night, after concluding his informal discourse (*xiaocan*), he said, "I cannot help but cite a public case (*gongan*) to bid farewell to the assembly.

After a long silence, he said, "The green mountains are boundlessly fine; yet people still say it is not as good as returning home. As these words fell, his voice ceased and he passed away. The assembly stared in astonishment. At that time—
It was the height of midsummer, as if scorched by fire. He remained there for seven days, his countenance showing not the slightest change. After the fire, *śarīra* (relics) fell like rain.
Chan Master Weichu of Huangbo in Junzhou was a successor of Chan Master Kaixian Zong;
he was a native of Jinxia in Piling, surnamed Cai. Having renounced his home at a tender age, he entered the monastic life.
Having passed the scriptural examinations and received ordination, he went to Kaixian. Kaixian asked, "The wise ones of the ten directions all enter this school;
as for this very school, how does one enter it? As the Master was about to respond, Kaixian shouted, "The moment you open your mouth, what is there to be done?"
The Master [Zhaozhou] was struck with awe and said, "I pray that you, Master, will instruct me. Xuanzhe replied, "It is like practicing archery: every thought must remain fixed on the red center;

the eyes do not glance elsewhere, and the hand does not grasp the bowstring in vain. Once the arrow is released from the string, it is certain to hit the mark. Thereupon, Zhaozhou attained sudden enlightenment.
He went to reside at Huangbo, where he ascended the hall and said, "I have seen Elder Brother Zong for my whole life; he has remained silent and steadfast."
He sat. This so-called decaying wooden frame has never clamored with its lips, yet it takes the teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs as its own gateway.
It simply requires that one rest completely; then, naturally, one will not become attached to this leaking shell.
At that time, a monk asked: "If one does not become attached to this leaking shell, I wonder how one preserves [the Dharma]?"

Ren said, "There is no place for you to apply your mind. [The monk] asked, "Does the Master have no skillful means? Ren said, "If there is no sauce for the pan-cakes, how can pressing sand yield oil?"
A monk asked Chan Master Hai of Mount Lu in Tanzhou, "What is it like when one steps forward three paces?
He replied, "One bumps one's head and strikes one's forehead. The monk asked, "What is it like when one steps back three paces? He replied, "One falls into a pit or a ditch.
The monk asked, "If one reaches the point where there is neither advancing nor retreating, what then? He replied, "A corpse standing upright."

Chan Master Daozhao of Fengshan in Fuzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Zongyan of Xuefeng Yuanjue, ascended the hall and said: "The true eye of the Tathāgata; the authentic rule of the successive patriarchs."
Transcending both the holy and the mundane, surpassing all manifestations of existence—this is not a dharma before one's eyes; do not give rise to various thoughts.

Arising and ceasing do not know one another; within this, there is no facing toward or turning away. Since there is neither facing nor turning away, how can one thoroughly penetrate and settle therein?
If you can see without seeing, only then, upon lifting your head, will you realize the non-empty emptiness.
Chan Master Huishun of Xichan Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of Zhending Prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "Every five days there is a formal assembly;

every three or eight days there is a general discourse. To speak a thousand times or ten thousand times—speaking horizontally or vertically—if suddenly a monk comes forward and says, 'There is no lack of speaking, but what can be done about the two who refuse to consent at the entrance of the mountain gate?
I would simply say to him: [The two at the gate are the Buddhas of the past and present; if you do not recognize them, you will surely be reborn as a beast.]'"
"Blind fellow! Had you not encountered those two, Xichan would have been like one who failed to meet a true知音 (zhīyīn—a person of like mind).
Ascending the hall, he said: "This clear morning, all matters are settled. Even if you were to simply rest as you are, that would already be to produce branches and entangle vines.
Tell me, how do you say the single phrase that cuts off the tangles? A water-dwelling iron ox returns to the northern ridge; its two hooves [rest upon the earth]."
A single pillow; the wild geese fly south. Entering the hall: Where words cannot reach, how can you bring it forth?
Where it cannot be brought forth, how can you understand it? Where it cannot be understood, how can you clarify it? Where it cannot be clarified, how can you penetrate it?

After a long silence, he said: "Begging fire, one receives it with the smoke; carrying spring water, one returns with the moon. If you have not yet understood this point, the red sun will shine forth at dawn.
[This was] Master Xiangyan Haiyin Zhiyue, a successor in the Dharma lineage.
Chan Master Yisong Ruyi of Xiangyan in Dengzhou was a native of Linchuan. His clan name was Rao and his original given name was Jie, with the style name Decao.
He began his career as a Confucian scholar; from his youth, he was well-versed in learning, preeminent in talent, skilled at literary investigation, and distinguished for his integrity.
Consequently, he was widely known among people. However, he met with repeated failures in the civil service examinations. Later, he traveled to the capital...
The Master was renowned for his poetry and prose at the Imperial Academy; thus, the famous scholars of the time all associated with him.

When Prime Minister Zeng Gongbu heard of his reputation, he invited him as a guest of honor. One day, the Master submitted a memorial outlining matters of benefit and harm, but Zeng would not accept it.

He then departed for Dengzhou to rely on Master Yu Yanming. After staying there for several months, Master Yu noticed that the Master’s responses during private audiences were extraordinary, and he privately marveled at this, saying: [...the rest of the passage...]
I said, "You must have something to tell me. He replied slowly, "When I was previously guarding the quarters, I had no particular focus.

Hearing that the Elder Haiyin of the neighboring temple possessed a reputation for the Way, I went to request from him a turning phrase (*yǎnyǔ*) to investigate through meditation. Suddenly, I attained awakening;
my body and mind became serene and at ease, with nothing else remaining. He looked back at me and said, "If you were able to do this, I would not be as I am now. Why is that?"

"Ah! He went straight to strike the seal. After more than ten days, he suddenly pulled the lock and attained enlightenment. The Seal (Yin) sealed him with a verse. The Master wrote a letter to inform his friend, Mr.
Lü Gong Benzhong, the Gentleman of the Secretariat, saying:

'I requested a discourse for inquiry and resolution from the Elder Haiyin on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month last year. From then on, I went to attend his teachings every day. On the fifteenth day of the first month...'"

In an instant, there was a sudden moment of realization. How marvelous! How marvelous! The world has always contained these ineffable, ineffable, ineffable, immeasurable, and boundless supreme matters.
The Buddha’s words regarding the "One Great Matter" (Ekakṛtya-hetu)—how could they deceive me? Thus, it is found within the mountains, rivers, and great earth;
the grasses, trees, and thickets; the walls, tiles, and rubble; and even in the crowing of the rooster and the barking of the dog.
"Vai! Whether putting on clothes, eating a meal, raising a hand, or moving a foot—in every such instance, one sees one's original face.

Only then does one realize that since time immemorial, one has been subject to the delusions of birth and death, turning according to external objects. Upon reaching this point, it is like a lamp dispelling darkness;
[all delusions] are suddenly lost. Is this not a matter of immeasurable significance? Thereupon, he abandoned his marriage and official career, emptied his treasury to purchase [the scriptures].

He shaved his head together with me; my name is Rulin, and I honored him as my elder brother. Subsequently, he and Rulin traveled together to consult various renowned masters, receiving their approval wherever they went.
Upon returning, he built a thatched hut at Hubei in Xiangyan.

When the eminent scholar-officials first heard that the Master’s head was shaven, they sighed deeply, saying, "Our community has lost a man of national caliber; we mourn for him on behalf of the four seas."—Xiang.
Shou Zhao Gong Qian invited the Master to open a Dharma center at Tianning Monastery. Monks vied to gather there, and donors made offerings every day without fail.

Just as his influence was flourishing, he abandoned it and departed. Wang Gong Zhongchi of Dengzhou requested that he reside at Xiangyan Monastery; however, after a short time, he again abandoned it and left.
Both monastics and laypeople tried to detain him, but he would not comply, and so he withdrew to his former cottage. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Transformation shifts secretly."
Why such haste? In a single moment, a single thought, a single breath—there are eighty-four thousand gates of expedient means.

Tell me, which gate is there that cannot be entered? Whether you enter or do not enter, when dawn comes and the rain falls upon the banana tree, making it wet, one must respectfully inquire further of those within:
they stand facing each other, grandly and openly, outside the gate. Hearing the woodpecker cry, he spoke this verse: *Peck, peck, peck!* The interior...
Worms on the face peck from without; how many are these people, drifting in a daze! A shove from behind the crown of the head, yet they still do not wake.
If you do not wake, listen further to this mountain monk’s *pop, pop, pop*. Other words have not been seen; it is regrettable that the record was not compiled by a patch-robed monk (bhikṣu).
Now, only his collected works circulate in the world. On the first day of the fourth month in the third year of the Jianyan era, he wrote a verse to leave to the assembly.
He passed away without illness. Gentry and commoners offered sacrifices without ceasing. On the first day of the fifth month, his entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the foot of Mount Ruyi.
His secular age was sixty-five, and his years of monastic seniority were twenty-seven.
