Chan Master Wengan Sizong of Xuedou in Qingyuan Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Hongzhi Zhengjue of Tiantong (the tenth generation of Dongshan).
He was a native of Huicheng and belonged to the Chen clan. In his youth, he studied the sutras.

Upon receiving full ordination, he relied upon Chan Master Miaozhanhui. During a session of interrogation, he attained sudden and profound enlightenment. Miaozhanhui entrusted him with his fly-whisk (*zhuchi*).

Later, he visited Hongzhi and received his seal of approval; his Way became increasingly honored. He went forth to reside at Puzhao, then moved to Shanguan and Cuishan, and subsequently transferred to Xuedou.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Every person has a nostril, yet only Shanguan has none."
The nostrils. Why are they not there? Twenty years ago, they were pulled off by someone.
Everyone has two eyes, yet only Shanquan has no eyes. Why are they not there? They were exchanged for *muhanyu* (wooden prayer beads) by someone.
Everyone has a skull, yet only Shanquan has no skull. Why is it not there?
"I have already lent him out to serve as a dung-scoop. He called to the assembly, saying, "He has no nostrils, he has no eyes, and he has no skull.
Do you all recognize this skillful means (*upāya*)? If you do not recognize it, you are burying this skillful means.
If this is still not so, listen further to this verse: 'The mud ox at the bottom of the ravine has its face gilded with gold; the stone woman atop the mountain...'"
Clad in true crimson, a fungus grows upon the tethering stake; this is not the misty haze of Mount Xianglu. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:
"The field of the empty kalpa is vividly distinct; the scenery beyond the realm is majestically unrevealed.

Relying on the ancestral land-deeds of former years, we entrust them to our descendants for plowing and weeding today. Within this, the seeds of the Way do not wither; directly beneath, the numinous sprouts flourish."

Xiushi: "Within function, one attains the wondrous; the natural livelihood flourishes spontaneously. When there is no self-interest beneath one's feet, only then can one believe that, fundamentally, there is no leakage.
Those who have gained strength must know its source; those who have thoroughly investigated must avoid being muddled and superficial.
If you can remain undeluded at every step, you are a member of my family. Ascending the hall, he said: "Cuiyan is not one who does not speak; it is simply because there is none [to be spoken to]."
At this very moment, a favorable opportunity such as this is difficult to encounter today. I shall expound a single phrase for you: the pillar is originally but wood;
the scale-weight is nothing but cast iron. If you all travel to other places, do not say that this mountain monk is a talkative fellow.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Sitting at Shaolin, walking on Mount Yuyang; composing a verse and transmitting the robe turned it into a war. Walking on Mount Yuyang, sitting at Shaolin;
attaining the marrow and finding peace of mind turned it into a fallacy. The public cases of these two houses have never been resolved;
descendants of later generations have created calamity and disaster. This calamity and disaster is truly immense; the monks of the world cannot penetrate through it. A monk asked: "If the eye..."
"Not sleeping. "All dreams are naturally eliminated. "What is the eye of one who does not sleep? He said, "It has never been opened for kalpas.
"Why has it never been opened for kalpas? He said, "Because it disregards all things. Question: "What is the Way? He said: [The rest of the response follows].
"When the rain is heavy, the roots and feet rot; when the sun is fierce, the hair on the temples withers. He asked, "What is it to be a person on the Way?

He replied, "The icy skin is as clear as jade; the snowy body is as brilliant as a pearl. He asked, "What is the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū? He replied, "At midnight, the crimson wheel shines upon the great earth;
the myriad phenomena of the forest and the heavens are all at once illuminated. He asked, "What is sitting for ten kalpas? He replied, "..."
At the site of enlightenment (daochang), he said: "The red dust of the great earth rises; empty space does not show its face. He asked:
"What is it that the Buddha-dharma does not manifest before one? He replied: "Tao Qian’s Stone of Intoxication remains even now; within the shade of the five willows, spring never changes.
He asked: "Who is the person who is always present? He replied: "There is no spark within the stone; when pressed, light is produced. He asked: "How so?"
"This is one who does not dwell at the bottom. He said, "Turning over, he passes straight through beyond the thousand peaks;
he no longer looks back at the old pass. [The Master] asked, "How should one approach such a person? He replied, "The path of white clouds is cut off and there is no news;
from of old, Buddhas and Patriarchs have found no name for him. Question: "What is it like when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water? He replied, "It has blocked your nostrils."
[The Master] said, "After emerging from the water, what is it like? He replied, "It pierces through your eyes. He asked, "What is the matter of returning to the root and restoring the source?
He replied, "A clay ox enters the earth. He asked, "What is Chan? He replied, "Using forceful words to seize the correct principle.
He asked, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? He replied, "Black beans. On the first day of the tenth month in the twenty-third year, he manifested a slight illness. On the third day...
Having taken leave of his dharma-heir, Cuiyan Zongjing, he passed away in serene stillness.
On the thirteenth day of this month, his entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the southwest corner of the temple.
The Master said: "The bright moon hangs high, yet has not yet shone before; a man with snow-white brows leans against the jade balustrade. The night deepens, rain passes, and wind and thunder cease;
guests disperse, and the wine cups on the cloud-palace stand dry. Ascending the hall, he said: "In the Three Realms there is no dharma;

where can one seek the mind? A startled snake enters the grass; a flying bird leaves the forest. After the rain, the mountain hall is still in the autumn night; the clamor of the marketplace never reaches here."
At Guchen. Chan Master Fahui of Dahuang in Suizhou was the son of the Bao family of Tiantai. He ascended the hall and said: "The Dharmakāya is without form;
it cannot be sought through sound or voice. The wondrous Way transcends words; how could it be understood through written characters? Even if one were to transcend..."

Even the Buddhas and Patriarchs would still fall short of the steps; even if one were to speak of the wondrous and discourse on the profound, it would ultimately remain caught between the lips and teeth.

One must have merit that is unassailable and traces that leave no shadow. Like withered wood and cold rocks, there is no longer any moisture; like illusory men and wooden horses, all emotional consciousness is empty.
Only then can one lower the hand to enter the marketplace and turn the body into other forms. It is said: "In the realm of no-outflows..."
Unable to remain, he returns instead to lie amidst the cold sands in a misty grove. Ascending the hall, he raised the story of Xiangyan climbing the tree and said:
"A slender lady with crimson hairpins and a red skirt gathers mulberry leaves in a garden of a hundred flowers.
In groups of threes and twos, they shy away from being seen, casting sidelong glances as they flirt with young men."
Chan Master Lin of Changlu in Zhenzhou ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said: "As for its essence, it is beyond mind, intellect, and consciousness;

as for its purport, it transcends the past, present, and future. Because it is beyond mind, intellect, and consciousness, it encompasses the myriad categories of existence without perceiving any distinction."
Because it transcends the past, present, and future, throughout the ten directions there is no further leakage; it does not offend at the very head, and it is utterly without dependence.
Awakening occurs prior to the arising of any signs or omens, functioning in a state where merit and achievement are not transgressed. This is the ordinary livelihood.
Do not hesitate; in the mere interval of a thought, you will lose the connection.
Chan Master Zide Huihui of Jingci Temple in Lin’an was a native of Shangyu in Kuaiji. His clan name was Zhang.

In his youth, he relied upon Dao-ning at Chengzhao Temple. At the age of twelve, he donned the saffron robes and received full ordination. Just upon reaching twenty, he went to seek instruction from Zhenxie at Changlu.
Lü attained a slight realization. Upon returning home, he went to visit Hongzhi. Hongzhi asked him: "When there is light within darkness, do not meet it with darkness;
when there is darkness within light, do not look upon it with light. Lü’s words did not accord with the Master's intent.

During the first watch of the night, as he returned from his meditation before the sacred statue to burn incense, Hongzhi happened to arrive. Upon seeing him, the Master suddenly understood the previous dialogue. Next...
One day, Zhi entered the room and remarked with admiration, "Your countenance when you left was like jade; yet I lament that your hair is now like frost upon your return.

He questioned him further, and the Master replied, "When he enters, he departs; when he leaves, he is subtle. From then on, their questions and answers were unhindered. Zhi recognized him as a true son within his lineage.
In the Ding-si year of the Xiang-sheng era, the Imperial Commissioner Qiu Gou invited him to propagate the Dharma at Putuo, and later he moved to Wan-shou.

Auspiciousness! Xuedou. In the third year of the Chunxi era, by imperial decree he was appointed to Jingci Temple. He ascended the hall and said: "The piercing north wind sweeps through the cold forest;
leaves fall back to their root, revealing the bare heart. Myriad streams flow toward the source as the boat reaches the shore;

the six windows reflect in emptiness as a mustard seed meets the needle. It is originally manifest—do not seek it elsewhere. The nature-ground is tranquil, shining through ancient and modern times. Outside the door..."
The frost melts and the spring colors stir; the four mountains resound as one with the dragon’s cry of the wood. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:

"Śākyamuni Buddha exhausted all principles and realized the full nature of reality. With his golden mouth, he proclaimed the timely teachings of a lifetime, turning the pearl and revolving the jade. Yet people call this 'wiping away dirty paper.
Bodhidharma, the Patriarch, directly pointed to the Single Vehicle Dharma for direct transmission. He sat facing the wall for nine years."
He did not rely on words or letters, yet people called him the "Wall-Gazing Brahmin. Tell me, how should one conduct oneself so as to avoid being pointed out by bystanders?
"The patched robe covers the head, and all matters cease; at this time, even I, the mountain monk, do not understand.
Ascending the hall, he raised the dialogue concerning the wind and the banner. The Master said: "If you can set up an eye where the wind and banner move, that is it."

"Venerable Elder, you have lost your eye at the very place where the wind and the banner move; that is precisely the wind and the banner. If this is not yet so, then it is neither wind nor banner, nor is it mind.
Monks merely exert themselves like driving a needle through a cone. After the rain has passed over the mountain retreat, the murky smoke clears;
lying down, one listens as the cool breeze arises from the bamboo grove. In the autumn of the seventh year, he retired to Xuedou, where he remained hidden for ten years at the Mingjue Pagoda.
On the twenty-ninth day of the middle winter month, at midnight, he bathed, wrote a verse, and passed away. His entire body was interred at Mount Zhongfeng, where it is known as the "Double Pagoda.
He was eighty-seven years of age in secular life and seventy-five years in the monastic order.
Chan Master Fagong of Rui’an Shichuang in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of Fenghua in the commandery. His clan name was Lin.
He received the tonsure and full ordination at Qizhen Monastery. Later, while attending the lectures of Yanqing Monastery, one night as he was reciting the Lotus Sūtra, he reached the passage:
"The eyes born of one’s parents can see the three thousandfold world-system. At that moment, hearing the sound of wind rustling through the leaves of a *tāla* tree, he suddenly attained realization.
He abandoned his reliance on Tiantong and began to clarify the Great Matter. All those who propagated the Dharma in the world at that time went to him to seek his counsel and resolution.

He left [Tiantong] to reside at Nengren, and subsequently succeeded to Guangxiao and Ruiyan. Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring wind and willow brows; The spring birds warble their hundred-tongued songs.
A single piece of the Patriarch’s mind— In both places, it has been leaked. Without moving a step, one returns home; [Yet] habitual outflows..."
Suddenly extinguished. At that moment, cast the jade thread’s tip; at dawn, pierce the golden needle’s eye. Deeply firm and truly profound, remote and far-reaching—who is there to discern it?
How pitiable are those who feel shame! Head after head follows the same track. Do not think of Amitābha; *Namu* to the dry dung-stick.
Before those of no wisdom and deluded minds, one must never speak of this. Ascending the hall: When the First Patriarch had just begun...
Ascending the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat and departed; it was neither Shide nor Hanshan. Even if one has reason, there is no place for it to be cleared away. Ascending the hall:
If you see through to the bottom, your application will be intimate. Wherever you meet, all are people of this same caliber. Raining down jewels from the void—do not boast of wealth.
Having no ground to hold even a single awl—this is not yet poverty. Treading upon the scale-pan, as hard as iron: eight *liang* is originally...

"Coming here is half a catty. Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient precedent: "When the World-Honored One was born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, saying, 'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
The Master said: 'A single arrow of thistle and mugwort from the Five Indias stirs up a million troops in China.
Had it not been for Yunmen executing the true command, one would have nearly mistaken the zero point on the scale.'"
Chan Master Fazhen of Qingliang in Shimen, Xiangyang Prefecture, was a native of Jianmen.
Later, he resided at Wanshou Monastery. Entering the hall, he said: "The willow colors hold mist; the spring light is brilliantly exquisite. A single peak rises solitary and steep;

ten thousand plants vie for their fragrance. The white clouds are limpid and already without intent; the green mountains before one’s eyes are fundamentally unmoving. The fisherman lowers his hook by a stream of cold."
The snow has not yet melted; the wild crossing is deserted. For ten thousand ages, the azure pool is as clear as a mirror.
Within the guest is the host: one carries a staff across the wheel of sun and moon. Within the host is the guest: one tramples through straw sandals and runs barefoot.

Thus, guest and host manifest each other; killing and giving life are free. Principle and phenomena are blended; the orthodox and the deviant are unimpeded. Entering a desolate field, one makes no selection.

"Plucking a blade of grass as it comes to hand. But tell me, how can this be fully understood? "Though there may be the art of invisibility within the dust, how does it compare to entering the Imperial Capital with one's whole body?
Master Liantang Sicheng of Guangxiao Temple in Qingyuan Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "A sheep-headed cart is being pushed..."
The bright moon; a bottomless boat carrying the morning breeze. A single phrase instantly transcends the realm of conceptual thought; there is no south, north, east, or west.
Thus, the news from before the kalpas cannot be transmitted by mouth or ear; the true rule beyond the categories cannot be understood through deliberation.
You must know that the Buddhas and the Patriarchs have not bestowed a single dharma upon others. From generation to generation...
Grandson! To bear the whole body directly beneath [the source], once the myriad functions have been stilled and eliminated, naturally not even a grain of dust remains.
The profound waves reflect the cool clarity of azure waters amidst the autumn colors; the numinous illumination washes the clear sky like a pure moon in the frost.
Winding and interlacing, harmonizing and encompassing all: with dream-like hands one pushes open the jade doors, and with a single turn of the body, one sets the pivot in motion.

The Wheel. As soon as the mandate is set in motion, one sees the first yang-line sprouting; the transformative function operates in secret, and suddenly one is startled by the shifting of the three periods of time.
Although it is silent and wordless, how can one help but speak of it when it blazes forth? Without shifting, without changing—set this aside for now.
There is the old and there is the new; tell me, how will you explain this? Do you all understand? The multitude...
The dark forces have been exhausted and stripped away; tomorrow will be a day of brilliant clouds.
Zen Master Miaojue Hewu of Changlu in Zhenzhou, a successor of Zen Master Zhenxie Qingliao of Changlu, ascended the hall and said: "The entire earth is this single interpretation."
[The Master] stepped out of the gate and grabbed him by the hand, pulling him back, but [the monk] refused to enter. "Old man Xuefeng, why do you force others so?
Since he has arrived here, why is his nose in another's hand? After a long silence, he said: "Gazing greedily at the moon in the sky, one loses the oar in one's hand. A monk asked:
"A wild goose flies across the vast sky, its shadow sinking into the cold water; yet the goose leaves no trace behind."
The Master said, "Water has no intention of reflecting shadows; there is not even a trace of them at the far end.

The monk asked, "When the reeds and flowers on both banks are snow, and the river water is the autumn of the heavens—what then when one proceeds in this very way? The Master said, "A wild goose flies across the vast sky, does it not? The monk hesitated.
The Master said: "A keen and talented patch-robed monk.
Zen Master Yichu of Guishan in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "I have long kept this essential matter silent; I did not strive to speak of it hastily."
"What is this old Śākyamuni prattling in his sleep? I now guarantee this matter for you; it shall never be in vain.
This is much like "forcing the honorable to become the lowly. Since it is not so, how is it ultimately? White clouds shroud the mountain peaks;
their verdant hues grow ever more majestic.
Chan Master Xingyu of Baoning Temple in Jiankang Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Entering the Way-place, one’s shadow is reflected in the mirror of the school.

The stars are brilliantly arrayed like a net across a clear night; the flowers bloom vibrantly in springtime. The wooden man silently operates the mechanism of transformation, not missing even a hair’s breadth;
the stone woman fully raises the seal of emptiness, yet its patterns have not yet appeared. Now tell me: how is it that they are neither one nor different?"
"Going has no coming. How should one realize this? "Everywhere, vertically and horizontally, is wondrous function; you yourself have never come from anything other than this.
Zen Master Fātong of Beishan in Zhenzhou ascended the hall and said: "Why is it that he who has swallowed up the three periods of time..."
One cannot open one’s mouth. That which illuminates the four continents—why then can one not open one’s eyes?
How does one attain complete and unimpeded mastery? The golden needle and double lock are both prepared; the manifest and the hidden are fully encompassed. A monk asked:
"In the place where speech is severed and thought is extinguished, I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "Not a drop of water enters the stone."
Chan Master Zongjue of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Taking steps before the kalpas, one casts the body across the world beyond.
This wondrous accord cannot be reached through the intellect; this true realization cannot be transmitted by words.

It reaches the point where emptiness and stillness gather the mists, and white clouds sever against the cold crags; where numinous light pierces the darkness, and the bright moon follows the night boat as it comes. Precisely..."

At such a time, how does one tread upon it? The biased and the correct never depart from their original station; whether extending or crossing, how could they involve the causes and conditions of speech?
A monk asked, "What is the Way? He replied, "At the crossroads, do not crane your neck in expectation."
Chan Master Wulu of Huili Temple in Linjiang Commandery, a dharma successor of Chan Master Da Honghui Zhaoqing, ascended the hall and said: "All sounds are the Buddha’s voice;
the raindrops dripping before the eaves ring out with a clear, cold resonance. All forms are the Buddha’s form; presented face-to-face, they cannot be denied. Thus it is.
"How so? To clarify it: 'The moonlight is clear beyond the clouds in the azure sky.

once you have attained entry, you must bring it to thorough penetration. Although there is fundamentally nothing to attain upon entry, do not cling to this 'nothingness' without ceasing. [He] illuminated [this].
Upon hearing this, [Yunmen] said, "Brother Shen’s exposition of Chan is like this; it is only a pity that his karmic conditions for longevity were not sufficient.

One day, after concluding his general discourse, he composed a verse to bid farewell to the assembly. With a single stroke of his writing brush across his hand, he passed away without even gathering it back up.

Chan Master Tongli of Donglin in Jiangzhou, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Guishan Tianfengzi, ascended the hall and said: "To pilot an iron boat atop a mountain peak; at the third watch, the sun rises.
The mind is at ease, yet not self-evident; one knows whose fallen leaves have been swept away. Carelessly plucking a pear from Zhengzhou—" he left the sentence unfinished.
In his hand he held a date from Qingzhou.
Chan Master Fajian of Huiriji Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Tianyi Facong, was a native of that same prefecture. A monk asked: "What is harmony?"
He further offered a phrase for the people, saying: "When the dog runs, it shakes its mouth. A monk asked, "What is the meaning? He replied, "When the monkey worries, it scratches its head.
Chan Master Qin of Huguo in Wenzhou ascended the hall and said: "A phrase exists, yet no phrase exists; coming from light, going into darkness—alive!"

Seizing the living and capturing the captive; swift reports and public proclamations are like vines clinging to trees. Things gather according to their kind: ginseng from across the sea and aconite from within the rivers.
When the tree falls, the vine withers—strictly avoid following established patterns.
Where do these words return? *Sulū sulū*. A great laugh! The broken mirror does not reflect; the great earth is vast and boundless—let it leap and skip as it pleases.
Chan Master Ji-xiang Yuan-shi of Wuwei Army was a native of Gaoyou. Since arriving at Tianyi, he had applied himself with diligent effort day and night, never resting his side upon a mat.
One day, he happened to laugh out loud and disturb the assembly; Tianyi expelled him. That night, he stayed overnight in a village field.
Beholding the stars and moon shining brightly, he had an awakening. At dawn, he returned to the abbot’s quarters to see Yunyan.
Yunyan then asked, "How do you explain the Five Ranks of Master and Subject in Dongshan? He replied, "In my place, there is not even a single rank.

Yunyan ordered him to attend the hall and said to his attendant monks, "This fellow indeed has a point of view, yet he does not recognize the fundamental principle. Later, when [the monk] entered the room for instruction, Yunyan anticipated this.
He ordered the practitioners to stand in five groups, arranged in sequence. When the Master arrived, he called out to them all together: "Venerable Shishang!

Thereupon, they secretly attained the profound essence of the teaching, and he composed this verse: "The single rank has just been revealed, and the five ranks are distinguished; The ruler and his ministers dwell in harmony, as purple clouds gather."

The night-bright curtain rolls up, illuminating all without partiality; the layered golden halls manifest the Supreme Honored One. His robes were well-suited to him. Later he resided at Jixiang Monastery.
Daoxuan, who had long served Tianyi as a keeper of the Tripitaka, achieved no realization. Tianyi rebuked him, and Daoxuan forgot to sleep or eat for a month.
One night, he heard the sound of a patrol bell and suddenly had a profound realization, saying: "Stop! Stop! One sound pierces straight through the path to the azure heavens;
who knows of the bright moon in the cold pond? A clay ox butts a coral tree until it breaks.
Later, Wenyin was appointed to the Hall Administration and subsequently resided at Touzi. Whenever he was asked a question, he would make the gesture of shaking a bell with his whisk.
The Fifteenth Generation of Nanyue (the Eleventh Generation of Linji and the Fourth Generation of Huanglong):

It is exhausted. The spring breeze grows ever more frequent. If you understand it through the seasons, what then of the Buddha-dharma?
Tell me, are the conditions of the seasons and the principles of the Buddha-dharma the same or different? After a long silence, he said: "The shadowless tree is planted where no one sees;
yet when it blooms and bears fruit, its fragrance is naturally sweet. Ascending the hall, [he said]: "When Śūnyatā-jāti sat in meditation amidst the crags, the devas..."
Flowers rain from the void. As this mountain monk ascends this seat, how do you all understand it?

If you can grasp it thoroughly, the eight classes of beings will understand it spontaneously without a word being spoken. If this is not yet the case, what glory is there in seeking it through the sale of one's own mind?
Chan Master Xingdao of Meian at Huiji Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The gathering clouds are about to snow but have not yet snowed;
the beloved sun seems radiant but does not truly shine. Cold sparrows chirp noisily among the fences; the piercing north wind dances through the curtains.
If you wish to understand Yangshan’s intimate phrase, today I shall bring it forth face-to-face for you. He struck his staff, descended from the seat, and left.
Chan Master Guo Min of Guangxiao Temple in Guangde Commandery was a native of Taoyuan, De’an.
He ascended the hall and, citing the story of Nanquan’s “beheading of the cat,” said: “Nanquan raised it up and brought down the blade; even a six-armed asura could not have saved it.”
Even if both halls were to attain the Way, blood would surely flow to fill the streets and alleys.
Xuefeng Youxu, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Huizhong of Qutang at Xuefeng in Fuzhou, ascended the hall and said: "Zhenjue plays the 'Guangling San'."
Qinshan sang the *Pusa man* (Bodhisattva Man); he was entirely corrupted by Yantou. Today, this mountain monk takes the Mount Sumeru mallet and strikes the drum of empty space;
the sound is the music of ten-thousand-year sovereignty, singing the joy of ten-thousand-year longevity. But tell me, who corrupted him? At Shaolin, the nine tripods were clarified;

sù hóu qiè Yóu (pronounced like "yóu" in "yóuyōu") Cōu (chǔ yóu qiè) Měng (mò kǒng qiè)
Lì (pronounced like lì) Gǎn (hu zhǎn qiè) Quí (pronounced like quí) Gǔ (shǒu bǐ qiè) Xǔ (pronounced like yǔ) *Jiā Tài Pǔ Dēng Lù*, Volume 14.
Compiled by the Monk (Subject) Zhengshou of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture,
Fifteenth Generation of Mount Heng (Eleventh Generation of Linji, Fourth Generation of Yangqi),
Dharma Heir of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu Keqin of Tiantong Tianning, Eastern Capital (Volume One).
Chan Master Fóxìng Fǎtài of Dàméi in Tánzhōu was a native of Hànzhōu. His clan name was Jì. Having received the capping ceremony and become a monk, he studied the teachings of the Nánshān school.

After a long time, he traveled to various regions to seek instruction. His spiritual capacity accorded with that of the Fifth Patriarch; later, under the guidance of Yuánwù, he suddenly attained a thorough understanding of the Great Dharma.
He subsequently resided at Dèshān in Dǐng, Xīhú in Sháo, as well as Gùshān and Dàowū. By imperial decree, he was appointed to his current post.
Daming. He was bestowed the title Fuxing (Buddha-nature). He ascended the hall and said: "Pushing to the limit of the Real, the Real has no marks;
exhausting the delusory, the delusory has no form. When both Real and delusory are non-existent, the eyes are revealed in vast emptiness.
Now that the eyes are revealed, what do you see? The morning sun melts the snow upon the crags; the northern wind blows open the wax-plum blossoms. He ascended the hall again and said:
Nirvana has no divergent paths; the gates of skillful means are many. Holding up his staff, he said: "Look! Look!
This mountain monk’s staff swallows the waters of the West River in a single gulp. The carp of the Eastern Sea leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens."
Śakra, filled with wrath, seized Mount Sumeru and crushed it with a single blow. The Earth Goddess Sthāvarā joined her palms in praise and said, "Behold the Dharma of the Dharma King;
such is the Dharma of the Dharma King. Striking his meditation seat with his staff, he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: This morning, the first month has already reached its midpoint. Everywhere, lanterns and lamps flicker in confusion;

throughout the city, silks and brocades are gathered in dense crowds as people move back and forth to enjoy the festivities. Manjusri has run into the midst of the bustling crowd, while Samantabhadra sits upright atop a high tower watching.
Now tell me, where is Avalokiteśvara? Thundering drums resound through the heavens; flutes and songs fill the earth. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Vast and remote, encompassing the ten directions; level and expansive, beyond form and beyond appearance.
Eyes wish to see, yet the pupils wither; mouths wish to speak, yet words fail. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have no skill at all. Linji and Deshan..."
Mountains do not hinder the proclamation: the tortoise swallows the iron ox of Shanfu; the snake bites the Great Image of Jiazhou.
The carp of the Eastern Sea has been left gasping until this very day. Heh! Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The fire-clouds scorch the field crops;
the springs have ceased their flow. Where is the Great Dragon King Sāgara? [He] struck the meditation seat with his staff and said:"

"Look here! Clouds rise on the southern mountain; rain falls on the northern mountain. This old monk shall further add the sound of a thunderclap to help manifest his majestic radiance and spread it far and wide.
Then, he cried out in a loud voice: "Hōng-nòng! Hōng-nòng! Ascending the hall, he said:
"Whether thoughts are attained or lost, they are none other than liberation. What kind of talk is this? Whether dharmas are established or destroyed, they are all called Nirvana. Consider this..."

Agitation and submersion are interrelated; wisdom and folly are both equally *prajñā*. The vast and superficial Buddha-nature and the dharmas accomplished by bodhisattvas and non-Buddhists are all *bodhi*.
Yet, there is still a slight difference. Nevertheless, even so, it is like Emperor Yang losing his camel.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Under Deshan’s staff, the golden sand appears distinct; within Linji’s shout, host and guest are distinguished."

If you do not possess the true eye upon reaching this point, how lamentable that you would fail the person of your original nature! (He lets out a shout and strikes the meditation seat. He descends from the seat. Ascending the hall, he says:
"If you wish to know where the Buddha has gone, it is right here in this very sound of my voice. (He gives a shout: "Tut! Master Fu Daoshi does not recognize good from evil;
by teaching people to pursue a state of 'bright clarity' and 'vivid awareness,' he ruins the men and women of others' households! Master Zhigong said to him—
Heng said, "Great Being, do not speak thus; try saying it another way. The Great Being spoke another verse:
"Empty-handed, I grasp a hoe; On foot, I ride a water buffalo. A person passes over the bridge; The bridge flows, but the water does not flow.
Master Zhigong laughed heartily and said, "The first part was somewhat acceptable, but the last part is even more distressing. Ascending the hall, he said: "I recall the past..."
During my days of wandering, I obtained two things: first, a vajra-hammer; second, the bones of a thousand sages.
Carrying them throughout the universe, my spirit and bearing were lofty and towering. Thus it was for thirty years; I used them as my standard.
But now that I am old, what do I know of these two things? I cast down the vajra-hammer and smashed the bones of the thousand sages, throwing them away.
At the crossroads of the four paths, one can no longer hold on; let the fleeting life pass as it will. Pointing south, one treats it as north;
calling a tortoise a soft-shelled turtle; calling beans millet. Let those with clear eyes laugh at me for lacking the guiding line. A monk asked:

"When principle follows the transformations of phenomena, it encompasses all existence yet remains a single, empty stillness. When phenomena merge with principle, they equalize a thousand differences."

Yet all return to the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). [The questioner asks: "What is the dharma-realm of principle (*li-fajie*)? [The Master] says: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. [The questioner asks: "What is the dharma-realm of phenomena (*shi-fajie*)?

[The Master] says: "The myriad phenomena in their dense array. [The questioner asks: "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena (*li-shi wuai fajie*)? [The Master] says: "East, west, south, and north. [The questioner asks:
"What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between phenomena and phenomena (*shi-shi wuai fajie*)? [The Master] says: "Above, below, and the four intermediate directions. [The questioner] asks:
"What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. "I do not yet understand the meaning of this," [the questioner] said.
[Touzi] replied, "Under his heels, there are seven holes and eight perforations."
Chan Master Duan Yu of the Penglou Hermitage at Danxia Fozhi in Dengzhou was a descendant of the King of Wuyue.

His sixth-generation ancestor, An Shou, settled in Kuaiji, where the family resided. From birth, the Master was exceptionally distinguished; his features were profound and elegant. At fourteen, he drove away crows at Dasha Temple;
at eighteen, he received the tonsure and the full precepts. He then went to rely upon Chan Master Fazhenyi of Jingci Temple. Not long after...
Ji’ou was once with a monk who struck a pillar and asked, "Why do you not speak of Chan? Upon hearing this, the Master attained a slight realization.
He went to visit Longmen Yuan, Ganlu Zhuo, and Letan Xiang, all of whom recognized his exceptional brilliance and advanced understanding. Later, he met Yuanwu at Zhongfu.
One day, Wuzhuo asked, "Who knew that the Eye of the True Dharma would perish with this blind donkey?
Is it perishing right now, or not? Wuzu replied, "Please, Master, keep your mouth shut. Wuzu said, "This is still within the realm of ordinary sentiment.

As Wuzhuo was about to respond, Wuzu struck him. Wuzhuo was suddenly freed from his lingering attachments. He later composed a verse to express his realization. While serving Wuzu at Tianning Monastery, Wuzu commanded him— [The text ends here.]

He served as Director of the Secretariat. Soon after, he was invited to share the seat [of the abbot]. His reputation for the Way resounded widely. The Duke of Xian of Jingxi invited him to open a Dharma center at Danxia.
He subsequently moved to Huqiu and retired from Mount Jingshan. Responding to the requests of the clergy and laity of Pingjiang, he established a hermitage at Xihu.
After several years there, by imperial decree, he resided at Baoning in Jiankang. Later, he moved to Wanshou in Suzhou and then to Xiansha in Min.

Shoushan Xi was appointed to Lingyin by imperial decree. When Empress Dowager Cining visited the residence of Prince Wei, she summoned the Master to expound the Dharma and bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *saṃghāṭī* robe.
He requested to return to Xihu, but in the autumn of the Wuchen year of the Shaoxing era, the Yuyang Monastery in Siming dispatched an envoy to insistently invite him;
only after more than a month did he finally comply. Ascending the hall, he said: "Deshan..."
As soon as one enters the gate, he strikes with the staff; most people hide their tracks within the leather bag. As soon as Linji enters the gate, he shouts;
everyone appears and disappears within the realm of sound. If you are a truly heroic monk, you must have the wind blowing beneath your feet, transcending the paths of past and present.
[He] takes up his staff, strikes once, and lets out a shout, saying: "Just this—how is it? If you call it...
He struck with his staff and shouted. "If you are nodding off and have not yet realized it, do not call this a 'staff-shout. If you do not recognize Deshan and Linji, what is it ultimately like?
He struck once more and said, "In no way must you move. Ascending the hall, he said: "The entire earth is the eye of the śramaṇa; throughout the ten directions is one's own light.
Why is it that when the drum is beaten in Pūrvavideha in the east, [it is heard] in Aparagoyānī in the west?"
Yajñadatta did not hear it. While Jambudvīpa in the south lights its lamps, Uttarakuru in the north sits in darkness.

Even if you were to speak with complete mastery regarding this very point, it would still be nothing more than a livelihood within the realm of light and shadow. The Master struck his whisk and said, "It has been shattered into a hundred fragments.
What is the path for emerging? [He threw down the whisk and said: 'Study! Ascending the hall, he raised his whisk.

Once attached, even Buddhas and Patriarchs do not know it. If the profound mechanism remains concealed and its shadowy traces have not yet appeared, though you possess the eye that penetrates through the entire body, you still cannot perceive it.
If you come from this side over, I shall firmly press down the Vajra King and let loose a crouching lion;
I grant you a single step to investigate. Although your horns are already incomplete, do not [hesitate] right now.
"Is there anyone who can pass through the wind of the blazing flames? He gave a shout and said, "Where have you gone? Then he gave another shout and descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Movement brings forth shadows; awakening gives rise to ice. Even if one neither moves nor awakens, it is still nothing more than the axle-pin of a chariot from the Qin dynasty.
Reaching this point, one must employ subtle illumination amidst a thousand differences, so that all ten thousand doors open simultaneously, and the pivot is turned upon the tip of a hair."
The pivot of the mechanism: the life-vein does not sink into the sea of poison. At times awareness is like still water; at times movement is like flying stars;
at times both movement and awareness are forgotten; at times illumination and function are sovereign. But tell me: at such a time as this, is it movement or awareness?
Is it illumination or function? Is there anyone who can distinguish them? An iron ox lies across the ancient road—whom will it strike?
The marrow is pierced and the hair stands on end with cold. Entering the hall: It is easy to fill a vast chasm, but difficult to fill a leaking cup.
If one possesses firm resolve, there is neither difficulty nor ease. If you cast away the entire earth, there is ample room; if you let out even a single hair, there is no way through.
Suddenly, if you neither cast away nor let out, where will you tread? Sharing the same sincerity and common joys and sorrows, even when drinking water, one must [be mindful].
Fei. A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? He replied, "You are a common field laborer. The monk asked, "What is the host within the guest?

He replied, "Even meeting face-to-face, you are still coarse and reckless. The monk asked, "What is the guest within the host? He replied, "The radiance of the sword slashes through the clouds of sorrow.

The monk asked, "What is the host within the host? He replied, "Beating the bones and striking the marrow. Whenever the Master presided over the assembly, his countenance was invariably stern and awe-inspiring.

Nevertheless, he never turned his back on the community in matters of sleep or food, and he never grew weary in preaching the Way. In the tenth month of the Gengwu year of the Xiangshu era, he first manifested a slight illness.

On the night of the seventeenth, he wrote a verse and entrusted it to the administrator, saying: "I shall take a short rest. At the fifth watch, he rose from his seat. The head seat, Faquan, requested his final instructions.
The Master said, "Exhaust this mind and intention; support one another with the Way. Having spoken these words, he passed away. His body was cremated.

Afterwards, his eyeballs, teeth, and tongue did not decay. That ground emitted light throughout the entire night. The śarīras obtained were beyond counting and continued for over a month without ceasing.

Huang Guan Luo Zhao had been a lay disciple who regularly sought the Way from the Master. Once, having returned from outside, he alone had obtained nothing. His aspiration for the Way was earnest and intense;
while he was eating with a guest, as he was chewing, there seemed to be something in his mouth. When he spat it out, it was a śarīra.
They were as large as beans and the color of amber. A person fond of such things took them away, whereupon [the Master] prostrated twice at the site of the cremation.
Hearing a sound from the incense casket, he opened it immediately; what was obtained was as before, yet slightly reddish and lustrous.
His disciples enshrined the remains and erected stupas for them at Mount Mao and Xihu. He was sixty-six years old and had spent forty-eight summer retreats. His posthumous title was:
He attained great enlightenment. The name of his stupa was Baosheng.
Chan Master Huazang Miyin Anmin of Jiankang Prefecture was a native of Jiading. His clan was Zhu.

Initially, he lectured on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* in Chengdu and became a refuge for those studying the doctrinal teachings (*yixue*). At that time, Yuanwu resided at Zhaojue; the Master went there to seek instruction. Yuanwu ordered him—
Consider the National Teacher’s words when he called his attendant three times. Zhaozhou said, "It is like a person writing characters in the dark;

though the characters themselves do not take shape, the traces of the brushstrokes are already manifest. Where is it that the traces are already manifest? Just investigate in this way (some versions differ slightly).
Later, because of his realization during a general discourse, a monk came forward and asked about the *Ten Mysterious Gates*. [The Master] said, "As for what the ancients said: 'Question...'"
"What is the appearance of the seal upon your mind? What is its essential meaning? Wuzhuo said, "The patterns have already been revealed.

At these words, the Master attained a realization. However, Wuzhuo did not yet grant him approval. One day, the Master went to Wuzhuo’s quarters and said to him, "Master, please do not cite further words; let me speak for a moment. Wuzhuo consented.
The Master said, "When one ordinarily brandishes the mallet or raises the whisk, is this not what is taught in the sutras? Wuzhuo replied, "Yes. The Master continued, "'One'..."
"All the various phenomena in all worlds are, in their entirety, the wondrously luminous true mind of bodhi. Wuzhuo said with a smile, "So you have been making your living right here all along?
The Master further said, "When you let out a shout or strike the meditation seat, is this not 'returning the hearing to hear one's own nature,' whereby that nature accomplishes the unsurpassed Way?
Wuzhuo replied, "Have you not seen it stated in the sutras that the wondrous nature is perfect and complete?"

Ming said, "It is free from all names and characteristics; fundamentally, there have never been worlds or sentient beings. Master [Wu] was relieved and enlightened. He departed from Shu and resided at Jia Shan.

While the Master had ceased his lectures and was attending him on his travels, he encountered Wu giving a night discourse to the assembly, citing the karmic cause and condition of the ancient sail that had not yet been hoisted.

The Master heard this but did not yet understand, so he sought a definitive resolution. Huineng said, "Ask me. The Master repeated his previous question. Huineng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard.
At that moment, the Master attained clear and thorough enlightenment. He said to Huineng, "As the ancients said: 'It is like a single drop falling into a vast abyss.'"
Little did he know that the great ocean had been cast into a single drop. Wuzhuo laughed and said, "What can be done about this fellow?
Not long after, he ordered him to share his seat. Wuzhuo spoke a verse, saying: "I am too lazy to boast of the *Sifen* or the *Lengyan*; Press down the clouds and investigate minutely.
I do not follow Master Liang’s way of personally visiting Mazu; Rather, I am like Deqiao who visited Longtan. For seven years I have traveled back and forth to Zhaojue."
For three years he soared above the emerald cliffs; today, I trouble you to serve as the First Seat. Amidst a thicket of a hundred flowers, the udumbara flower appears.
Later, he visited Fojian at Jiangshan. Fojian asked, "Foguo has a phrase that he never spoke of to others indiscriminately;
has he ever spoken it to you? The Master said, "Shut that dog's mouth! Fojian roared and said, "It is not this!"
The Master said, "No one has snatched away your bag of salt and tea; why are you crying out in such confusion?
Guàn replied, "If Foguo had not spoken for you, I would have spoken for you. The Master said, "If you harbor doubts, O Monk, leave this monastery and seek instruction elsewhere."

Master Jian laughed heartily. After Master Jian entered nirvana, Yuanwu succeeded him on the seat. Not long after, the Master began teaching at Baoning, then moved to Huazang, and finally returned to his hometown to lead Zhongfeng.
He ascended the hall and said: "The multitude sell flowers, while I alone sell pines;
Their green hues do not match the red. In the end, they do not harmonize with the times; I shall return to the midst of the verdant mists. It may be said: "How fitting!"
I laugh at the ancients for speaking in such a manner; it is much like fleeing from a mountain peak only to rush into a ravine, or avoiding drowning only to throw oneself into fire.
How can this compare to accepting one’s lot and seeking out one or half a person at the edge of the eight-foot staff or the five-inch hoe?
Even so, Baoning does not want even half a person. Why? The wealthy loathe having even a thousand mouths; the poor lament having even a single body too many. Ascending the hall, he said: "Ha!"
The Buddha scolded the Patriarch; this required the skill of an adept like Deshan. Crossing horses and crossing donkeys—this was the technique of Zhaozhou.
"A blind donkey extinguishes the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye"—this moves the gentleman of keen faculties. For the deaf, two kinds of language are unnecessary.
Habituated to hooking the great whales, he administered four blows with a rattan staff beneath the Jiyun Peak. Both light and both dark—he struck the ribs of Dayu three times.
Below. Dying together and being born together. Before the patriarchs and Buddhas had yet appeared, those of superior capacity would call forth this matter;
after the "wild goat hung from its horns," the guest from Xiantuo seized the drum and pulled down the banner, baring his blade while concealing his point as he let out a lion’s roar.

Tearing asunder the seal of the patriarchs, sweeping away the traces of the patch-robed monks; hard as *tūla* cotton, yet soft as the iron of Nanbin. In the kingdom of Magadha, not even a drop of water could leak through;
before the peak of Shaoshi, this command was personally executed. Thus, Dingguang beckoned with his hand and Zhizhe nodded his head.
It may be said that a fine horse does not wait for the whip; it tilts its ear and knows the master’s intent. Do you understand?
Ma! A three-faced cat grasps the moon in its paws; a two-headed white ox treads upon the mist with its hooves.
A crowned blue hare stands atop the courtyard cypress; a shell-shedding turtle flies up into the heavens. Addressing the assembly on a winter night, he cited Master Yuyuan Huihao, who said:
"The snow, the snow—flakes beyond distinction. From the twelfth month down, continuing through the first, second, and third months of the coming year..."
In the first, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, and tenth months, he continued as before without ceasing.
He was frozen to death and starved to death, so that he might avoid making such wild and confused talk. The Master said: "This is not a curse, nor is it a praise.
It surpasses Linji and Deshan, yet it is not like Yunju or Luohan. Tell me, what is the essential meaning of Yuyuan?"
After a long silence, he said: "As soon as the snow has melted away, spring will naturally arrive. Later, the Master entered nirvana at his home mountain.
During the cremation, a great many śarīras remained; even commoners digging the earth a foot deep obtained them, which were exceptionally radiant, clear, and pure.
His heart and tongue were likewise not destroyed.

Chan Master Yuanjue of Mount Xiang’er in Meizhou was a native of Meishan. His clan name was Yuan. In his youth, he underwent the examination on his studies at Chuandeng Monastery and received ordination;
his original name was Yuánjué. When the Prefectural Governor filled out the official silk document, he erroneously wrote "Yuan" (袁) instead of "Yuán" (圓). The Governor—
Mian playfully said to his teacher, "Is it permissible to have only a single word as one's name? The teacher smiled and replied, "Even a single word is already too much.
The Prefect, marveling at this, provided him with full ordination. Thereafter, he left Sichuan and visited Wuzu Zi, Haihui Zong, and Longmen Yuan;

yet he did not find the ultimate depths of their teachings. He then visited Chanti Zhao at Baofeng, where he stayed for a long time until Zhao entered nirvana, after which he went to serve [the successor].

Shimen Zheng served as an attendant for several autumns and personally received the transmission of the seal of enlightenment. At that time, Yuanwu’s reputation for the Way eclipsed all others of his era.

The Master [Zhaozhou] took up his staff, intending to go and see him. Shimen’s disciples looked at the Master and said, "Brother, since you have already attained realization, you ought to sew your own cooking cloth;
why do you trouble yourself to travel so far? The Master replied, "It is not so. As for me, wherever I go, there is no obstruction. He did not stop.
"You should wait here like one guarding a stump. When the Master arrived at Jiangshan, Xuedou Wuzhuo had just received an imperial decree to reside at Tianning Temple;

the Master thereupon went to Dayue to rely upon Foxing. After some time, he entered the inner quarters to present his insights. Foxing said, "You are still far from it," yet recognizing him as a vessel for the Dharma, he appointed him as an attendant to manage guests.
Whenever the Master attended upon Foxing, Foxing would invariably cite passages from the *Lotus Sūtra*.
He was instructed to recite the four characters "kai-shi-wu-ru" (open, reveal, awaken, enter). Furthermore, he was told: "Only when I nod my head vertically will you be correct.
By chance, he did not recognize [the signal] and was rebuked; having no one to rely upon during his period of retreat, he stayed in the home of a layman. One day, he was reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*.
When he arrived, he still did not know what was fire and what was the house; then, suddenly, it became clear to him. When Xingjian saw that he had attained realization, he nodded in approval.

Yuanwu subsequently received an imperial decree to reside at Yunju. When the Master arrived there, he reported his realization to Yuanwu, who scolded him, saying, "This is originally a place of purity;
why are you defecating here? At these words, the Master’s doubts were instantly resolved. (The year was) Shaoxing.
In the year Ding-si, the seat at Mei was vacant. The Prefect remarked, "This monastery has long been a den for vermin;
were it not for a man of renown and superior character, one could not restore its former glory. The various Chan masters proposed the Master to accept this invitation.
He once said to a guest: "Suduan Dongpo said, 'I carry this stone back home; within my sleeves lies the Eastern Sea. Huang Tingjian (Shan谷) said, 'Hui-chong’s misty rain and reeds...'"
"Wild geese! Sitting here on the Xiao and Xiang rivers and Lake Dongting, wishing to call my small boat back home, passersby say I am a painting.
This is the very marrow of Chan. He also said: "When I strike the meditation seat and raise the whisk, Śākyamuni and Confucius are both standing in the lee.
When someone recounted these words to Chan Master Fohai Yuan, Yuan said: "These are the words of Old Jue."
It is so. Here in our place, it is not like that.
Zen Master Ché’ān Dàyuán of Zhāojié Monastery in Chengdū Prefecture was a man from Bā County in Mián. His clan name was Dèng.
In his youth, he received full ordination at Jiàngjí Monastery. He traveled east to visit Zen Master Xīndào of Dàbié, whereupon he began contemplating the phrase, "Vast emptiness, nothing holy."
The Sage’s words caused him to suddenly burst into laughter, saying, "Dharma originally resided right here. Daoyu then went to study under Fojian and Foyan, receiving their recognition.
Later, he relied upon Yuanwu at Jinsan Mountain and reported his insights to him, but Yuanwu did not approve.
When Emperor Gaozong visited Yangzhou, he summoned Yuanwu to preach the Dharma and bestowed upon him the title "Yuanwu."
Furthermore, ten attendant monks were granted purple robes; the Master was among them. Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Yunju, and the Master followed him there.
Although he had attained a degree of conviction, he remained suspicious because a sense of obstruction had not yet been removed from his chest.

On one occasion, Yuanwu asked the assembly of practitioners, "When the time of birth and death arrives, what then? A monk replied, "The incense altar laughs at the Master. Yuanwu then asked the Master, "As for you—"
"How is it? he asked. [Wuzu] said, "The grass-thief is utterly defeated. Wuzhuo said, "What would you say if someone were to ask you this?

As the Master was about to answer, Wuzhuo pressed him, saying, "The grass-thief is utterly defeated! At that moment, the Master attained complete realization. Wuzhuo struck him with his fist, and the Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly.
Wuzhuo asked, "What did you see to be so? He replied, "The poisonous fist has not yet been repaid; for eternal kalpas, I shall never forget it."

Wangwu returned to the teachings of Zhaoguo, who personally appointed him as the head of the assembly. As Wangwu was about to pass away, he designated his teacher to succeed him to the seat (the recorded *jigu* has not been seen).
Chan Master Shaolong of Huqiu in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of Heshan. He renounced worldly life at the age of nine and resided at Fohui Monastery.
After more than six years, he received the tonsure and the full precepts. Five years later, he traveled to Changlu to pay his respects to Jingzhao.
Chan Master Xin grasped its general outlines. When someone brought him a record of Yuanwu’s teachings, the Master read it and sighed, saying, "It is like imagining the flavor of fermented vinegar;
though it has not yet moistened my intestines or washed my stomach, it nonetheless brings one a sense of joy and liberation. My only regret is that I have not yet heard his voice.
He subsequently followed Zantang at Baofeng, stayed as a guest at Huanglong, and questioned Sishin, from whom he attained wondrous and extraordinary expressions of enlightened insight.
At one time, he arrived at Jia Shan. Hearing that Huairang had moved to Daolin, the Master followed him there. One day, upon entering the inner room for instruction, Huairang asked:
"When seeing the very act of seeing, that seeing is not [ordinary] seeing; even seeing is already beyond seeing, such that seeing cannot reach it. He then raised his fist and said:

"Did you see it? He replied, "I saw it. Baizhang said, "Placing a head on top of a head. Upon hearing this, the Master attained a sudden realization of the truth. Yuanwu scolded him, saying, "What have you seen?
He replied, "The dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing water from passing through. Yuanwu approved him; from that time on, he never forgot this.
Having fully realized the subtle essence of complete enlightenment over twenty years, he returned to his native district. He subsequently resided at Kaisheng Temple west of the city.

During the disturbances of the Jianyan era, he built a thatched hut at the foot of Mount Tongfeng. There, the Prefectural Governor and Minister Li Guang invited him to reside at Zhangjiao Temple for four years.

He moved to Huqiu, where his spiritual transformation of others flourished even more. Entering the hall, he said: "Whenever there is anything displayed or entrusted, it all falls into the realm of the present moment.

[The Master] said, "I have tested you until your very bones are exposed. [The monk] asked, "What is 'one shout not used as one shout'?

[The Master] said, "You must recognize the person holding the needle; do not merely praise the fine plumage of the mandarin ducks. [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of Jingnan? [The Master] said, "A thousand li."

"The clouds and waves are perilous in the Three Gorges; a single sail finds the wind and waves vast upon the Five Lakes. [The student] asked: "What is it like to be a person within this realm? He replied:
"How could there be no 'Solitary Seat' of the Tang dynasty for one who offers direct remonstrance? A hero ought to have the patronage of the 'Bearded Old Man. [The student] said:

"I have already received your instruction regarding the person and the realm; how is it to uphold the Patriarchal Seal so loftily? He replied: "The sea-roaming yakṣa has horns upon his head; lightning strikes the flint stone."
"Fire, do not hesitate. The monks prostrated. The Master said, "You must further penetrate that which exists prior to birth. A monk asked, "What is 'the partial within the central'?
He replied, "The night-bright curtain is lowered deeper into the night. The monk asked, "What is 'the central within the partial'? He replied, [as above].
At dawn, the thief threw himself into an ancient well. [The Master] asked: "What is it like to come from the very center? He replied:
"A hundred plants, riding the spring, bloom everywhere. He asked: "What is it like to arrive at the convergence? He replied: "Snow and rain intermingle; there is nowhere to hide. He asked:
"What is it like to reach the ultimate convergence? He replied: "Both ends are cut off; there is no reliance. When mind and dharmas are both forgotten, only then is the mystery attained. — Shao.
In the first month of summer in the Gengwu year, he manifested slight illness. On the first day of the fifth month, rising at dawn, the assembly of monks gathered around him, seeking his final words.
The Master gestured them away, saying, "Throughout my life, my verbal transgressions have not been few; what more is there for me to say now? Depart, depart! I shall rest for a while.
Thereupon, he closed his eyes and passed away. For three days, his countenance remained as if alive. After the cremation, [relics] were obtained.
There were pearls as large as clam shells; those of five colors were beyond counting. He enshrined them in the eastern part of the monastery.

Because the Master’s conduct was without blemish and he was strict regarding the transmission of the Dharma, the Governor-General Shao Gong Pu and the Court Gentleman Feng Gong Jie, along with dozens of eminent practitioners, all served him as their teacher.
He lived for sixty-four years and spent thirty-five summer retreats in meditation.
Chan Master Fuyan Wenyuan of Tanzhou was a native of Xinfan in Chengdu. His clan name was Yang. At the age of eighteen, he became a monk under Zian, a disciple of Guangxiao.
He ascended the platform to receive full ordination and resided there to study the sutras and śāstras. After some time, he visited Chan Master Zhengfaming.
Upon hearing the story of Yunmen’s “moldy cake,” he attained a realization. Later, when he met Yuanwu, he finally reached the ultimate source of the Dharma.
He first resided at Zhidu and later moved to Foyan. Entering the hall, he said: "When one sits firmly facing the sun, the traces of both ordinary beings and sages are cut off.

When one lets go with the hand, heaven revolves and earth turns. It reaches the point where the sun and moon intersect, tigers roar and dragons吟 (sing). In every instance and every object, [the sound] reaches the ear."
"Listen! Look! What is this that is firmly established upon the Truths? Do you understand thoroughly? *Asiṣṭha!* (It is not so! *Tut!* Entering the hall:
It is spontaneously clear and naturally present without being conceptualized. The Buddhas of the past and future have been unable to point it out;
the monks of the world cannot calculate it, nor can they restrain it. It is utterly detached from the dust of emotion; it is only for oneself."

When one is willing, one is intimate; when the total mechanism is let go, one proceeds by relying solely upon it. Above, there are no Buddhas or patriarchs to rely on; below, there is no self to take as a basis.
Like the great void, there is no further attachment or obstruction. It is truly blazing forth, never failing to perceive anything.
Once you have grasped this "little nose," its application will be inexhaustible; yet, you must also press down upon it with your hand as the occasion arises.
Only when it is shattered can it be attained. Why? Because a great furnace of red-hot metal does not tolerate a single speck of snow.

A monk asked, "What is the true master of Dinglin? He replied, "He sits, cutting off the tongues of all people under heaven. The monk said, "I do not know how one should approach him. He replied, "If you look at him, you will go blind.
The monk asked, "A student has come here; I pray that the Master will grant me an audience. He replied, "The seal of the Three Essentials is opened. The monk said, "This is merit."

He did not give away his possessions recklessly. Someone asked, "What have you seen? He replied, "Guest and host are both present and solemn. The questioner said, "You are addressing your prayers to empty space.
On the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month of the *bingzi* year of the Xiangxing era, while sitting upright, he suddenly gathered his elders and entrusted them with his final affairs.

Having finished writing his verse of farewell, he let out a shout, cast aside his brush, and passed away. He was sixty-five years old and had been a monk for forty-eight years. During his cremation, [relics] were obtained.
His five-colored *śarīra* relics were enshrined together with his sacred bones in the Three Lives Pagoda (*Sengsheng Ta*) of the monastery.
Chan Master Tanyuan of Mingyin Monastery on West Mountain in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of Leqing in Wenzhou; his clan name was Huang.

Having donned the monastic robes at a tender age, he traveled extensively to visit various monastic communities. In the *gengzi* year of the Xuande era (1120), he returned to Zhongfu (Mount Zhong). At that time, the Imperial Court had recently...
The monk was a man of virtue. Together with several like-minded companions, he entered the Dhūta Cave, where he dwelt, subsisting on pine nuts.
After some time, Yuanwu received an imperial decree to reside on this mountain; he personally went to the cave and ordered [the master] to shave his hair and beard.

When Yuanwu was subsequently summoned by imperial edict to take up the position at Tianning Monastery in the capital, he went there together with the master, who was appointed to oversee the Xiangshuihai (Perfumed Sea) Hall. Not long after, because [Yuanwu] raised a drumstick and struck...

When the drum was beaten, he suddenly clarified the Great Dharma; those who attained awakening recognized it through silent understanding. Whenever anyone asked a question within his quarters, he would invariably reply, "Do not try to understand.
Consequently, his contemporaries all referred to him as "Mo-li-hui" (Do Not Try to Understand).

Imperial Uncle Prince Qi'an requested an imperial decree to invite him to open the Dharma and clarify its causes. He subsequently moved to Baohua Temple. Entering the hall, he said: "You have a pair of eyes; I..."
There is also a pair of eyes. If you deceive me, you deceive yourself. If you become a Buddha or a Patriarch, I, this old monk, shall have no share in your merit.
If you become a donkey or a horse, I, this old monk, shall not be able to save you.

One day, when several donors entered the mountain to invite the Master to ascend the hall, he spoke a verse, saying: "I have no special excellence; my name is a hollow claim. I thank you for your earnest [invitation]."
"You have come from afar with great diligence; I see that you lack the Dharma to be entrusted. In vain do I open the mountain gate for you.
A monk asked, "What was it like before the Master had seen Yuanwu? He replied, "Do not concern yourself with it. The monk said, "And what was it like after seeing him? He replied, [as before].
"Do not concern yourself. He asked, "What is it like when one sees and when one has not yet seen? He replied, "Do not concern yourself. Do not concern yourself.
In the twenty-third year of the Xianghe era, he retired from his post and resided at the stupa of Mingjue on Mount Xuedou in Siming.

When his Imperial Cousin wished to petition for the return of the imperial carriage, he ultimately declined on the grounds of illness. The following year, he passed away; his manifestations of spiritual excellence were exceptionally remarkable, so they are not detailed here.
Record.
Chan Master Xueting Yuanjing of Pingjiang Fu’s Huqiu [Monastery] was a native of Shuangxi. He ascended the hall and said:
"If you wish to walk, then walk; if you wish to sit, then sit. What is this sixfold supernatural power? When it is firmly grasped, not a single thing exists."

He did not do it. When he was letting things go—whether killing people or setting fires—if a monk were suddenly to come forth and say, "This faceless fellow, do not act recklessly," Xueting would simply say to him, "I thought there was no one to witness this. Ascending the hall, he said:

"For those who know there is [the fundamental reality], ten thousand years pass as if they were a single day; for those who do not know there is, a single day passes as if it were ten thousand years."
"May you live for ten thousand years. This does not reflect the way of Master Sītacitta (Dead Heart), who said:
"I have been traveling as a mendicant for over thirty years, spending ninety days each summer retreat. I cannot add a single day, nor can I subtract a single day; it cannot be grasped."
One cannot abandon it; within that which is unobtainable, one simply attains it. Yet, as for the place where Cuiyun sees it, it is not so.
This mountain monk has been traveling on pilgrimage for over thirty years; who cares about a single day or ninety days? There is neither attainment nor non-attainment.
"Everywhere one shall meet Maitreya in the future"—but tell me, where is Maitreya? The golden wind blows everywhere.
Water. Fallen leaves fill Chang’an. Entering the hall, he said: "To speak, one must see; to see, one must also be able to speak.
If you can see but cannot speak, you fall into the realm of shadows and your understanding becomes biased and withered.
If you can speak but cannot see, you fall into the trap of timing and descend into a sea of poison. But if you are under the gate of Cuiyun, even if you can both speak and see—it is well."
"Thirty blows! You cannot speak of it, you cannot see it—yet he too deserves thirty blows. Cuíyún speaks thus—yet he too deserves thirty blows.
He then called out loudly to the assembly, "How perilous! Ascending the hall for a discourse, he said: "Day after day the sun rises in the east;
day after day the sun sets in the west. This is something everyone knows. From antiquity until now, it has been as common as hemp and flax."
Suddenly, he twisted the pivot of the dialogue; it did not emerge from the east, nor did it subside in the west. Tell me, from where did it emerge and subside?
If one who has penetrated the barrier hears such a statement, they will certainly know that the five-li milestone stands outside the city gate.
As for those who cannot penetrate it, they often say, "Halfway up the mountain," deceiving people. The monk said: [This is the end of the recorded exchange.]

"Where does a deceased monk go when he passes away? He replied, "To the head of a dung heap. [The questioner] asked, "What is the meaning of this?
He replied, "Striking it, bumping into it."
Chan Master Zongzheng of Yunding Hermitage in Huai’an Army, a native of Qi County in Tongchuan, ascended the hall.
Holding up his staff, he struck it once and said, "Where there is hearing, hearing is extinguished. Raising it upright, he said, "Where there is seeing, seeing is extinguished.
"The wind moves and the dust rises; the target is set and the arrow is drawn. Before things have reached this point, they are clearly split in two. Deshan holds [the staff] crosswise and cuts it off.
A deliberation. Huangbo’s deployment of the opportune moment was like a flash of lightning; within a single hair-tip, the entire dharma-realm of the great thousand-millionfold world is contained.
His hands and eyes pervade his whole body, with no front or back. *Du!* (A shout).
Chan Master Netang Fansi of Tianting Monastery in Quzhou was a native of Soutai. His clan was Zhu. He was twenty-one years old [when he entered the path].
He shaved his head and received full ordination, serving as an attendant to Master You. He spent many years coming and going among the assemblies of Fojian and Foyan, and later relied upon Yuanwu.
After attaining thorough realization, he presided over seven monasteries. Entering the hall for a formal discourse, he said:

"Kicking over the sea of birth and death, trampling down the shore of nirvana—there are no living people in the world, and no dead men in the Yellow Springs. He then held up his staff and said: "Now, Nuetang..."
"Every day this staff has a place where it is entrusted. Is there anyone who can take responsibility for it?

Come forward and carry it; is there anyone? Is there anyone? After a long silence, he threw down the staff and descended from his seat. He ascended the hall and said: "Those who know have their breakfast and dinner;
those who do not know also have their breakfast and dinner. How can one directly verify this?"
Whether it be existence or non-existence, right or wrong, or the deviant and the correct—if these cannot be verified through experience, the matter of studying under a teacher remains far off.
*He lets out a shout and descends from his seat.* Ascending the hall, the mountain monk says: I am a fourth-generation descendant of Yangqi.
This old fellow had a public case regarding a three-legged donkey that walks by prancing its hooves. Although everyone can cite this case, they simply do not...
To know where it lands: the mountain monk, not begrudging his eyebrows, provides this annotation for you all:
"An octagonal grindstone rolls in empty space."
Chan Master Fozhao Jue of Mount Yu’s Junshan Monastery ascended the hall and said: "If it is, it is thoroughly so;
from the beginning, it has been a complete manifestation prior to heaven and earth. If it is not, it is thoroughly not; ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences share a single mechanism.

To say 'it is' is to fail to touch upon it; to say 'it is not' is to fall short of it. At this moment, from where could Buddhas and Patriarchs be established? The heavy frost of the clear sky reveals the truth."
The Pivot: A single sphere, luminous and bright, neither form nor non-form. Since it is neither form, tell me, what is it?
When its wondrous essence is fully manifested, it is clearly known only by oneself. Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient saying: "The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems;
the more one drills into it, the harder it becomes. One gazes for it to be before one, yet suddenly it is behind. Do you all recognize this? If you do not recognize it, [you have missed it].

I provide a commentary for you: "The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems; not even a hair’s breadth separates us. At the vital ford, the passage is cut off, and even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot escape.

"The more one drills into it, the firmer it becomes; the true essence is spontaneous. When the birds sing and the flowers smile before the emerald cliff, looking toward it, it is right here in front of you.
Neither correct nor biased, he sits squarely throughout the ten directions, his majesty subduing the great chiliocosm. Suddenly appearing behind one’s back, he lets slip a single flaw.
How laughable is Yunmen, hiding himself within the Big Dipper! *Duḥ!* (A sharp rebuke)
Chan Master Xian of Baohua in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of that same province. He ascended the hall and said:
"The rice gruel has been eaten; to place a head atop a head. 'Go wash the alms bowl'; to draw legs upon a snake. If you ask further how it is, you will only bring about your own defeat."
After a long silence, he called out loudly to the assembly. When the assembly raised their heads, the Master said, "Return to the hall for tea.
He ascended the hall and said: "Do not practice Zen; cease studying the Way. Rest the mind and let go of artifice, and it will always be vast and open.

The ready-made case is already too much complication; this very 'no-mind' is already a fabrication. Even if you were to cut off all movement before birth, it would still be difficult to penetrate my errors—error, error, error!"
Chan Master Jue of Mount Dongshan in Shaoxing later resided at Yingsheng. He ascended the hall and said: "The three beats of the drum have ceased;
everyone has come forward, intending to investigate the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. Do you know that the sword has long since departed?
Even if you were to attain sudden enlightenment right now, it would still be like cutting off one's own head and seeking life therein. Dongshan has no choice but to act."
Furthermore, let us examine the second head with thorough scrutiny. [The Master] struck the meditation seat with his hand and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The flowers are in full bloom; the scenery is warm and bright. There is no need to speak of another heaven within a flask.

If you can recognize it at the tips of the hundred grasses—east three feet high, west eight inches wide. Ascending the hall, he said: "Pūrvavideha in the east and Aparagoyānī in the west are clashing forehead to forehead."
"Do you understand? All of you still do not know that the mouth of the alms bowl is turned toward the sky.
Ascending the hall, he said, "I cannot say it with my whole mouth; it is formed by chance. After a long silence, he asked, "Have you received the staff yet?

Ascending the hall, he said, "The venerable Master Yan said, 'To speak of mind and to speak of nature—here in this old monk's place, this is foul-mouthed. I, this mountain monk, say: if it were the Teachings..."

The Outer Separate Transmission. This is the authentic imperial capital lineage. Entering the hall, he raised [the following] as an example: "In the past, there was a butcher named Wide Forehead who slaughtered a thousand sheep daily.
One day, he went to where the Buddha was, cast down his butcher’s knife, and said, 'I am counted among the number of the thousand Buddhas.
The World-Honored One said, 'So it is; so it is. Nowadays, those in the monastic groves mistakenly believe that Wide Forehead was a Buddha in a past life. This is merely a provisional [teaching]."
He appeared as a butcher, slaughtering a thousand sheep each day. When he saw Guang'e (Wide Forehead) in this way, [the Master] said, "I am glad there is no connection here.
He further said, "Guang'e is precisely a man who would not blink when killing people; yet, having cast down his butcher's blade, he stands there and becomes a Buddha.
I am glad there is no connection here. He also said, "Guang'e cast down his butcher's blade and said, 'I am counted among the thousand Buddhas. This..."
One Buddha—how clear and distinct! For now, rejoice that there is no further connection to be made. Do you wish to recognize Guang'e?
