Chan Master Dahui Pu-jue Zonggao of Jing Mountain in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Xuancheng. His clan name was Xi. From his youth, he possessed a brilliant spirit.
At the age of thirteen, he enrolled in a local school. One day, while there, he was mocked by a fellow student;

the Master grew angry and threw his inkstone at him, accidentally striking the hat of the *guangwen* (the head teacher). He paid the gold for the damage and returned home, saying: "A man of great character studies the world..."
[He] wrote: "Why not investigate the supramundane Dharma? Thereupon, he went to Huíyún Monastery on Mount Dōngshān to serve under Huìqí.

The following year, he shaved his head and received full ordination (*vinaya*). While casually perusing the *Record of the Ancient Yúnmén*, he felt as if it were something he had practiced in a former life.

He subsequently relied upon Chán Master Lǐ of Guǎngjiào, before departing to travel through the four quarters and following various elder masters of the Cáo-dòng lineage. Having mastered their teachings, he went to Mount Bǎofēng to pay his respects.
Chan Master Zhantang Zhun saw [the young] Zhun and marveled at him; he had him attend to his robes and sash, pointing him toward the shortcut for entering the Way.

The Master [Zhun] took up the scriptures without yielding anything. Zhun rebuked him, saying, "You have not yet attained awakening; your illness lies in understanding through consciousness, which constitutes the cognitive obscuration (*jñeyāvaraṇa*).
When Zhun was gravely ill, he instructed the Master, saying, "After I am gone, you will surely see Master Chuanqin, who will certainly be able to bring it all to completion."
When Zizhi (Qin, i.e., Yuanwu) passed away, the Master hurried to pay his respects to the Layman Wujin, seeking a stele inscription for Zhun’s tomb.

Wujin received him and named his hermitage "Miaoxi" (Wondrous Joy), while also earnestly urging him to go see Yuanwu. Upon arriving at Tianning Monastery, the Master encountered Yuanwu ascending the hall, where Yuanwu raised the following case:
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the place from which all Buddhas emerge? Yunmen replied, "The water of the East Mountain flows..."
"Upward movement! If it were a celestial being, it would not be like this. What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? "A fragrant breeze blows from the south;
within the halls and pavilions, a subtle coolness arises. Upon hearing this, the Master attained sudden spiritual enlightenment.
Over a month later, Wuzu said to him, "It was no easy matter for you to reach this state. It is simply a pity that once you die, you cannot come back to life; yet, you do not doubt it."
Words and phrases are a great illness. It is said that one does not see the Way until one lets go at the edge of a precipice and takes responsibility for oneself;

only after death can one return to life, and this cannot be faked before the Master. One must believe that such a principle exists. Yan was appointed as the attendant of Zhemu Hall (Zhemu being a place where court officials rest).
Daily, he entered the room with the Master several times. Each time, Wuzu would raise the question: "The phrase that has it, and the phrase that lacks it."
Wu asked, "It is like a rattan vine leaning against a tree. As the Master was about to respond, Wuzhu said, "That is not it.

After half a year had passed, he asked again, "I heard that when you were with the Fifth Patriarch, you once asked this same question. I do not know how the Fifth Patriarch answered. Wuzhu lowered his head.
The Master said, "The Abbot questioned you before the great assembly of humans and devas at that time; what harm is there in saying it now?
Being unable to refuse, Wuxue said, "I asked: 'As for the phrase with no-phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree—what then? The Patriarch replied:
"It cannot be depicted; it cannot be painted. When [the Master] suddenly encountered the moment when the tree fell and the vines withered, he asked, "What then?
The Patriarch said, "I have come along with you. Upon these words, the Master cast away all his intellectual views and insights. He exclaimed, "Only now do I know that I was not deceived by you.
He then appointed him to oversee the brush and ink, entrusting him with the *Record of the True Lineage of Linji*. Not long after, he ordered him to share the seat in the meditation hall.
He held a bamboo comb in his hand while teaching to test his disciples; thus, the monastic communities universally accorded him great respect, and his fame resounded throughout the capital.
Minister Lü Shuntú memorialized the Emperor, requesting that he be granted the purple robe and the title "Buddha-Sun" (Fórì).

During the Jurchen upheaval, the chieftain intended to take ten or so Chan monks as captives; the Master was among those selected but managed to escape. He then proceeded to Mount Húqiū in Wúmén to spend the summer retreat. Consequently—
While reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he reached the point where the Bodhisattva ascends to the seventh stage and realizes the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).

At that moment, the circumstances regarding his previous inquiry to Master Zhantang about Aṅgulimāla carrying an alms bowl to the house of a woman in childbirth became perfectly clear and transparent to him.

When he heard that Yuanwu had been summoned by imperial decree to reside at Yunju, he went to visit him and again served as the First Seat (*prathama-āsana*), teaching the Way to the assembly; his reputation and esteem increased further.
The Master remained later at the ancient Yunmen Hermitage, where students gathered like clouds. After some time, he entered Min Province and built a thatched hut at Yangyu in Changle;
thirteen people followed him there and attained the Dharma. He subsequently moved his residence to Xiaoxi Hermitage. At that time, Yuanwu was in Sichuan.
He entrusted the Right Vice President, Zhang Weigong Jun, saying, "The Head Seat Gaofeng has truly attained the marrow of the Dharma.
If he does not emerge [from seclusion], there will be no one to uphold the Linji lineage. When Vice President Zhang returned to court, he welcomed him to Mount Jing;

the flourishing of his Way and Dharma was preeminent in his time, with over two thousand followers, all of whom were eminent talents from various quarters. Minister Zhang Jiucheng also followed him as a disciple.
He attained a clear and sudden realization. One day, while discussing state affairs, he incurred trouble along with the Master. The Master remained serene.
In the fifth month of the *xinyou* year of the Xiangshu era, he discarded his monastic certificates and retired to live in seclusion at Hengyang.

There, he compiled the recorded sayings of former virtuous masters, interspersing them with his own comments and critiques, arranging them into three volumes titled *The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye*. After ten years, he moved to Meiyang. Another five...
In the [X] year, Emperor Gaozong granted him special imperial favor and released him from his vows. In the spring of the following year, he resumed wearing the *saṃghāṭī* robe.

Monasteries in all directions offered him vacant seats to entice him, yet he generally declined them. Later, he received an imperial decree to reside at Yuyang Monastery; after more than a year, he was ordered by imperial edict to move to Jingshan.
Monastics and laypeople revered and admired him just as they had in the beginning.
When Emperor Xiaozong was the Prince of Puan, he dispatched an inner palace supervisor into the mountains to pay his respects to the Master.

The Master composed a verse to present to him. Later, while residing at the Jianfu Palace, the Emperor again sent an inner guest master to the mountains to provide offerings for the five hundred arhats.
"I request the Master to preach the Dharma. [The Master] personally inscribed the three characters "Miaoxi Hermitage" (Wondrous Joy Hermitage) and composed a eulogy to honor and send it to him.

Entering the hall, he said: "The Patriarch said: 'When the one mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault. When there is no fault, there are no dharmas; when there is no arising, there is no mind.

The capacity can follow along with the extinction of objects, and objects follow along with the sinking of the capacity. Objects are objects because of the capacity; the capacity is the capacity because of objects. Great or small..."

The Patriarch, however, held the views of a mere lecturer. Jingshan is not like this. The eye cannot see itself; a blade cannot cut itself. Eating food relieves hunger; drinking water quenches thirst.

Linji and Deshan caused themselves to be needlessly deluded, wasting their spirit on the bestowing of blows and shouts. Set aside the blows; cast away the shouts. How can you stop this fellow Meng? Case: A monk asked Lishan, “When all forms return to emptiness, where does emptiness return? He replied, “The tongue does not leave the mouth. The monk asked, “Why is it so?
He replied, “Because inner and outer are one as such. The Master said, “In matters, the box and its lid must fit;
in principle, the arrowheads must meet point-to-point. One must be like Lishan to achieve this. If it were Jingshan, it would not be so. Or, if someone were to ask about all forms...”
They return to emptiness. Where does emptiness return? The peony flower blooms upon the Bodhisattva’s face; the palm leaves scatter upon the Yakṣa’s head. Why is it thus?
Simply discern the heart of resolve, and you shall certainly not be deceived.
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff, struck it once, and let out a shout, saying: "Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout—today I shall pick them up again for your sake. Heaven...
How high? How wide is the earth? Cease adding more dung to the refuse heap! Change the bones; wash away the entrails.
Jing Shan steps back three paces and permits you all to deliberate. But tell me, how will you deliberate?
He cast down his staff, gave a shout, and said: "A beautiful woman is easily made from rouge and powder; without money, it is difficult to be a fine young man. Ascending the hall, he said:
"On the fourteenth and fifteenth of the first month, at Shuangjing, gongs are struck and drums are beaten.

If you wish to recognize the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, look at the village songs and communal dances. Ascending the hall, he raised an example: A monk asked Fengxue, "The ancient melody has no..."
"Melody. How can one harmonize it? He said: "The wooden cock crows at midnight; the straw dog barks as dawn breaks.
Even this answer from the Yellow-Faced One (the Buddha) does not yet qualify him as a true descendant of Linji.
Today, if someone were to ask Jingshan: "The ancient melody has no sound—how can one harmonize it? I would simply say to him: "The wooden..."
The rooster crows at midnight; the straw dog barks as dawn breaks. [He] ascends the hall and says: A monk asked Linji, "What is the realm of the three eyes?
Linji replied, "I shall enter the Pure and Wondrous Realm with you, donning the garment of purity to preach the Dharma-body Buddha.
Again, we enter the Realm of Non-differentiation, donning the garment of non-differentiation to preach the Reward-body Buddha. Again, we enter the Realm of Understanding..."
He has shed his physical realm and dons the robe of radiant light; he speaks of the *nirmāṇakāya* Buddha. The Master looked at the great assembly and said:
"Do you see this old fellow Linji? If you still do not see him, I, Jingshan, shall point out for you the *dharmakāya*, the *saṃbhogakāya*, and the *nirmāṇakāya*."
"Alas! You wretched goblins and sprites! To encounter you in the Land of Three Eyes is to make the Unranked True Person laugh to death.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The long rains have not cleared; suddenly, heaven and earth are bright and clear. As for the matter within the Gate of the Patriarchs, what need is there to present it further?
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: A monk asked the Fifth Patriarch, "When Oxhead had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, why was it that [he possessed] a hundred..."
A bird offered a flower in its beak and said, "Wealth and honor are what people desire.

Later, when asked why it did not offer a flower in its beak, it replied, "Poverty and low status are what people loathe. The Master said, "When the Elder answered in this way, he spoke as one who has attained the Way."
Although you have skillfully responded to the immediate occasion, how can you avoid startling the ears of those present?
Jingshan also has two turning words with which he wishes to meet his venerable teacher: "Before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds carry flowers to offer him?"
A thatched hut has a cauldron placed upon it. Seeing this later, why does it not take up flowers to offer?
To dig a latrine inside the Buddha Hall. Ascending the hall, he raised an example: A monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, "Who can attain the essential meaning of Huangmei?
He replied, "One who understands the Dharma attains it. The monk said, "Does the Master attain it? He replied, "I do not attain it. The monk asked, "Why does the Master not [attain it]?"
[The Master] said, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma. He asked, "Does the great assembly still see the Patriarch?
If you do not see him, I, Jing-shan, shall point him out for you: *jiao-ba jiao-ba* (plantain). It has leaves but no fruit.
Suddenly, a gale arises—just like at the northern corner of the east corridor in the thirty-six courtyards of the Great Imperial Temple in the Eastern Capital. Wang-he... [the sentence trails off].
"Even so, it tears the *kāṣāya*. In the end, what is to be done? Return to the hall for tea. He ascended the hall and said:
"Master Yuantong Xiu addressed the assembly, saying: 'At Shaolin, nine years of cold sitting were ultimately seen through by Shen Guang.
Now, jade and stone are difficult to distinguish; one can only wrap hemp around paper. This one, that one, and yet another—if one is truly enlightened...'"
O people of the eye! Why must I laboriously explain this further? Today at Jing Mountain, I cannot help but continue the "dog's tail" after the "badger's fur.
There is indeed something to be said. The Old Barbarian’s talk fell into a trap for nine years;

it is a pity he let it pass then, which allowed those followers of silent illumination to sit in meditation within ghost caves for years on end—one person here, another there, yet another more. Although I have spoken with bitter, earnest warnings.
It is like the wind passing through the tops of trees. Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat: Mañjuśrī’s three-year retreat; Master Zhìgōng was no ordinary monk.
Kāśyapa wished to exercise the true command, yet he could not avoid seeing ghosts before his eyes.
But tell me, what is the business today under the gate of Jìngshān? After descending from the seat, everyone should perform three prostrations with full bodies. Ascending the hall:
A monk asked, "Is there? Is there? The Hermitage Master held up his fist. "Is this truly definitive? The Master immediately descended from his seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters.

Ascending the hall, he brought up the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl and said, "The masters of all quarters have commented on this many times, and those who have provided footnotes are also numerous.
Yet, not one person has ever clearly explained it through and through. Now, Miaoxi [will speak]..."
Rujing spoke clearly and thoroughly for the sake of all people: "Having finished eating the congee, he immediately washed his bowl.
Tell me, did he ever give any instruction? Black beans have always been good for making sauce; a bhikṣuṇī is certainly a *shigū* (nun). Ascending the hall, he said:
"It has only just been the Mid-Autumn Festival of the eighth month, and already it is the fifteenth of the ninth month. He took up his staff, struck the ground, and said: "There is only this."
[He] did not move. Throwing [the staff] down, he said: "The entire assembly has heard it with their ears and seen it with their eyes. Ascending the hall, he raised [this case]:

Wuzu cited a monk who asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. To understand it in this way is already to be mistaken.
What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The cypress tree in the courtyard. To understand it in this way—[is also to be mistaken].
Only then is it so. Do you wish to recognize the Fifth Patriarch? Look at his cheek from behind his head; do not associate with him.

When the Emperor Xiaozong was still a prince in the imperial residence, he dispatched an inner attendant to enter the mountains to make offerings to the Arhats and pray for the longevity of the Sovereign.

He invited [the Master] to ascend the hall, whereupon [the Master] said: "If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season. If the time and season..."
The principle is naturally manifest. I venture to ask the great assembly: what is this self-manifesting principle? Raising his whisk, he asked, "Do you see it?
Striking the meditation seat, he asked, "Do you hear it? Hearing and seeing are distinct and clear—what is this?
If you can grasp it here, the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace will both be fully repaid at once. If not yet so, [you must strive further].
Jingshan has gone to entangle himself in complications. Again, he raised his whisk and said: "Look, look!

The World-Honored One Amitāyus, atop Jingshan’s whisk, emits a great radiance that illuminates worlds as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably, unspeakably, and yet again unspeakably many Buddha-fields, turning the Great Dharma Wheel and performing immeasurable, boundless, and vast [deeds]."

This is a great Buddha-activity. Within it, whether ordinary or holy, correct or deviant, grass or wood, sentient or insentient—whosoever encounters this light shall all attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
It is for this reason that the Buddhas attain it here and become endowed with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*);
and it is for this reason that the great Bodhisattvas attain it here and accomplish the various perfections (*pāramitā*).
Pratyekabuddhas attain it here; appearing in worlds devoid of Buddhas, they manifest supernatural powers and radiance.
The assembly of Śrāvakas, including those who came by night to invite five hundred Arhats, attain it here; they obtain the eight liberations and are endowed with the six supernormal knowledges.
Devas and humans attain it here, increasing the ten wholesome actions. Asuras attain it here, [and] eliminate...
Those who possess pride shall attain it here in hell; they shall suddenly transcend the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*).
Hungry ghosts, animals, and all sentient beings of the four modes of birth and nine categories shall likewise attain it here, each receiving its benefit according to their own faculties and natures.
After the World-Honored One Amitāyus has finished performing his buddha-works by emitting great rays of light, he then [takes] the waters of the four great oceans...
He poured water over the crown of the World-Honored One Maitreya’s head and conferred upon him the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
He shall perform great Buddha-work as the Regent. The World-Honored One Amitāyus possesses such supernatural powers, such mastery, and such majestic spiritual authority.
Having arrived at this point, is there anyone here who recognizes this kindness and seeks to repay it? If there is, please come forward.
I have come to meet you at Jingshan to bear witness for you. If there is none [to do so], listen to this verse: "The Dharma-realm reaches the mouths of all beings;
All that exists within the Dharma-realm is their tongue. Relying solely upon these mouths and tongues, May we pray for the long life of our Sovereign without ceasing.
For ten million years and more, may the source of blessings flow, Like the surging ocean, never to be exhausted. The Master [concluded].
Within the den of the father, the *śarabha* is born; the *juezuo* phoenix will surely emerge from the cave of Mount Dan.

As an auspicious omen, it brings blessings throughout the nine realms; plants, trees, and even insects all rejoice. I bow my head to this inconceivable event, which is like the myriad stars surrounding the bright moon.
Therefore, I now proclaim these wondrous verses, spoken with truth within the ultimate reality (*paramārtha*). — Chan Master Yuanwu (Wumen)
[The Master] paused. Holding up the incense, he said: "This venerable one was in his lifetime stubborn and upright, his spirit suppressing all quarters.

He indulged in an over-the-top, reckless bluntness and employed an extra-ordinary, unbridled simplicity. He claimed of himself: 'I would trade my wooden prayer beads for the eyes of everyone under heaven.
Little did he know that his unfilial son has taken this broken string and threaded it through his nostrils—the end of the cord..."
"Since he is already in the hands of Jingshan, if Jingshan wishes to make him live, it is Jingshan; if Jingshan wishes to make him die, it is also Jingshan.
Tell me, what is the proof? He then burned incense and said, "This is the proof. A monk asked, "When Bodhidharma came from the West, what did he transmit?
He replied, "One must not take everything as the view of a wild fox spirit. The monk asked, "How so?"
"Coarse enters the subtle. [The Master] said: "A single pore within the ocean of fragrant water. "How is it that the subtle enters the coarse? He said:
"The ocean of fragrant water within a single pore. Question: "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? He said: "Fire does not wait for the sun to be hot.
"How is it after it has been polished? He said: "Wind does not wait for the moon to be cool. "What about polishing and not polishing? He said: [The same as before].
"How is it at that time? [He] said, "Intersecting. [The Master] asked, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion?
[The Master] said, "When you have sucked the waters of the West River dry in a single gulp, I will tell you. What is the meaning of this? [The Master] said, "Nailing it down and gluing it on."
Question: "If there is a single dharma, Vairocana falls among the ordinary; if the myriad dharmas are non-existent, Samantabhadra loses his realm.
Departing from these two paths, I pray that you, Master, will speak swiftly. He said: "A shelled turtle flies up into the sky. Question:
"When one bows high to Śākyamuni and does not prostrate to Maitreya, what is it like? He said: "Awake within a dream. Question: "Great cultivation..."
"Does this person still fall within cause and effect, or not? The former Baizhang said, "It does not fall within cause and effect. Why did he fall into the body of a wild fox?
[Dongshan] said, "Whenever you meet someone, simply present it thus. Baizhang the Later said, "It is not that cause and effect are obscured.
Why was he released from the body of a wild fox? [Dongshan] said, "Whenever you meet someone, simply present it thus. [Dongshan] said, "Suppose someone were to ask..."
Jingshan asked, "Does a person of great cultivation still fall within the realm of cause and effect? I wonder, what did you say to him, Master?
Jingshan replied, "I told him: 'Whenever you encounter someone, simply speak thus. A monk asked, "What is it like when the light comes from the front?"
[The Master] said: "The head is large, yet the tail is thin at the tip. [The monk] asked: "What is it like when one comes with a darkened mind? [The Master] said:

"A wild horse neighs in the wind, its hooves clattering. [The monk] asked: "Tomorrow there is a communal meal at Beichuan Monastery; what then? [The Master] said: "Xuefeng has already spoken on this."
Question: "The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended. How is this so? He said:
"The words of a parent come from the parent’s own mouth. Question: "I do not yet understand how one should receive and uphold them. He said: "Simply receive and uphold them in this very way."

"I certainly will not deceive you. Question: "In our school there are no words or phrases; truly, there is not a single dharma to give to others. What then? He said: "Five flavors stuffed into a weight. Question:
"When both mind and Buddha are forgotten, what then? He said: "The old woman selling fans shields her eyes with her hand from the sun. Question:
"The scriptures say that it is preached in every atom and preached in every world without interruption. I wonder, by what means..."
"What is the tongue? The Master struck the right corner of the meditation seat once. The monk said, "The World-Honored One spoke what is not spoken;
Kāśyapa heard what is not heard. The Master struck the left corner of the meditation seat once. The monk said, "I know that today’s command has not been issued in vain.
The Master said, "What do you understand of good and evil? In his quarters, the Master asked a monk, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha..."
"This is an object. How do you understand it? The monk said, "I have received it. The Master said, "You have received your seven generations of ancestors in your own home.
The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "Just now you said 'received,' and now you shout. This has nothing to do with what is not the mind, not the Buddha, or not an object.
What is this matter? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him out. A monk requested instruction on the story regarding Jia Shan’s "realm" (jing). [The Master] raised his voice.

Before he had finished speaking, the Master gave a shout. The monk was left bewildered. The Master asked, "What were you asking? The monk tried to raise the question again, but the Master struck him repeatedly and shouted him out.
As soon as another monk entered, the Master said, "Not so! Get out! The monk immediately left.
The Master said, "A man of immeasurable capacity has been turned around by the flow of words. Then another monk entered, and the Master likewise said, "Not so! Get out!"
A monk stepped forward. The Master said, "I told you it was not so; what more do you seek by coming closer? He struck him out.
Another monk entered and said, "Just now, those two monks did not understand the Master's meaning. The Master lowered his head and let out a sigh. The monk was at a loss.
The Master struck him, saying, "In fact, it is you who have understood my meaning. He asked a monk, "The other day..."
"There is a question for you. You answered it to me the other day; why are you dozing off now? The monk said, "Just so, just so.
The Master said, "What did you say? The monk said, "Not so, not so. The Master struck him twice with his staff and said, "One blow strikes you for saying 'just so';
one blow strikes you for saying 'not so. [He] raised his bamboo pointer.
The Master asked a monk, "If you call it a bamboo stick, you commit an offense; if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you turn your back on the truth.
You may not utter a word, nor may you remain silent. Speak! Speak quickly! The monk said, "Please, Reverend, set down the bamboo stick, and I will speak with you.
The Master set down the bamboo stick. The monk brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "Attendant, recognize this monk."

[The Master] laughed. He then raised the question to the monk, who said, "I was afraid the turtle would escape from the jar. The Master stepped down from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Whose words were those?
Speak quickly! The monk said, "Truly, I did not dare deceive you, Master. This is what Venerable Zhuan’an instructed me to say.
The Master struck him several times with his staff and said, "Clearly report this to all the quarters [of the monastic community]. The Master...
In his advanced years, he sought to retire from public life. In the spring of the *Xinsi* year, he received imperial permission. He withdrew to reside at the Mingyue Hall.
In the first year of the *Lungxing* era, one night, a star fell to the west of the temple; its radiance was brilliant and intense. Shortly thereafter, he manifested a slight ailment.

On the ninth day of the eighth month, when his disciples came to inquire after his health, the Master exhorted them to propagate the Way. He then said slowly, "I shall set out tomorrow. At the fifth watch of the night, he personally wrote his final testament.
He submitted this memorial. He also sent a letter declining the invitation of the Layman Ziyuan. When his attendant monk Liaoxian requested a verse, he wrote it out in large characters and said:
"Living is just like this; dying is just like this. Whether there is a verse or no verse—what a fuss! He then threw down his brush and passed away peacefully.
At dawn, a snake about one chi long with a white waist and head was found coiled at the Longwang Well.
[The] railing. As for the one who was like a righteous monk, he was the manifestation of Zhaoji of the mountain.
The fourfold assembly wailed in grief; when the Emperor heard of this, he sighed with regret. The Chancellor and others came in succession to offer sacrifices.
His disciples enshrined his remains in a stupa beside the Bright Moon Hall. He was seventy-five years old, having lived fifty-eight summers. [The Emperor] issued an edict...
The Mingyue Hall was converted into Miaoxi Hermitage. He was posthumously granted the title Pujue (Universally Awakened), and his stupa was named Baoguang (Jewel Light).
At the beginning of the Chunxi era, his complete recorded sayings in eighty fascicles were bestowed upon him, to circulate alongside the Tripitaka.
Chan Master Cihu Guo Chian Jingyuan of Taizhou was a native of Nanxi in Yongjia. His clan name was Zhang.

At the age of eighteen, he took refuge with Higan Xigong at Lingshan to become a monk and studied the Tiantai teachings for three years. During the summer, he changed his robes and traveled to Jingci Temple to visit Yuanwu on Mount Zhongfu.
Not long after, he saw two monks reading the records of Sijun’s *xiaocan* (informal sermon), which said: "Since you are deluded, you must..."

He attained an awakening. Having awakened, he had to recognize delusion within awakening and awakening within delusion; then, with both delusion and awakening forgotten, he established all dharmas from the state where there is neither delusion nor awakening.
The Master brushed his sleeves and walked to the corridor of the hall, whereupon he attained clear and thorough realization.

He immediately reported what he had realized to Huineng, but Huineng did not grant him approval. The Master followed him upstream against the current, without wearying himself in the service of grooming and polishing, and he attended Huineng constantly.
He entered the capital to attend court in Yangzhou and was granted a purple robe. Upon his realization and return to Shu, he entrusted his Dharma robes to him.
When the Layman Taixiu, the Dragon-Scholar Geng Tingxi, governed Kuacang, he honored the Master’s Way and requested that he open a Dharma assembly at Nanming.
He remained there for two years before retiring to Huguo Monastery in Yongjia. There, the Provincial Commissioner Ming Gong Tao and the Prefect Lü Gong Piwen [invited him].
Lianyun invited him, and after three requests, he finally arrived. The Dharma community flourished greatly, and it was truly due to this Master that the monastic centers of Kuacang were revitalized.
He subsequently moved to Zhenru and Huguo Monasteries. Entering the hall, he said: "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, this group of fellows went wrong seven times and eight times;

In the winter of the Yichou year of the Xiangshu era, he manifested a slight illness. In the first month of the Bingyin year—

On the ninth day, he invited Chan Master Tanhua of Xitang to serve as the Seat-Head (Zuoyuan). He subsequently gathered the administrative affairs (Shizhu) and gave his final instructions almost entirely.
His exhortations remained as usual until, suddenly, he clenched his fists and passed away. His disciples mourned him with deep longing. Upon cremation, five-colored *śarīra* relics were obtained.
His teeth and tongue remained intact, and his right fist was undamaged. On the second day of the second month, he was interred in front of Liúruàn Cave to the east of the monastery.
He was fifty-three years old in secular age and thirty-five years in the monastic order.
Chan Master Hongfu Ziwen of Taizhou ascended the hall and said: "How do you understand that which is neither obscured nor falling?

Even if you understand it, you will still fall as before into the state of a wild fox. One night, a cool wind arises from the painted horn; the bright moon fills the boat as it drifts upon the rivers and lakes."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Where the hook and the awl do not reach, the thousand eyes open at once; when the arrowhead has no time to strike, ten thousand functions converge simultaneously.
The wisdom of boundless differentiation and the gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī—when one lets out a shout, the sun shines upon heaven;
when one strikes a blow with the staff, clouds move and rain falls. Cast aside the mountain before you, turn your tongue back, and try it for me!"
"Try saying a single word for me. If you cannot say it, do not claim to have seen Hongfu after thirty years.

After a long silence, he said: "When walking at night, do not step on white; otherwise, you will not avoid a broken leg."
Water is stone. [The Master] ascends the hall: "Shifting the pivot, one penetrates beyond the dust of emotion; cutting off past and present, one reveals one's true face.
Principle and phenomena reach their consummation; striking and singing proceed together. It reaches the point where the clay ox bellows and the pillar is startled into haste;
the Buddha Hall runs out through the triple gate, and the Vajra Guardian opens his mouth and laughs loudly. But tell me, what is he laughing at? He then...
He said, "Matters within one's own house are difficult to explain to others. Striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he descended from the seat.

Rui Feng Zhang Chanshi returned to his hometown with a shaven head and went to visit Qionglong Yuan Chanshi.

He laughed. From this, his name became known. He returned to reside at Sīyì (Siyi) to the west of the city, then moved to Guānyīn (Guanyin) on Small Lake, and later lived on South Peak.

The dragon roars and mist rises; the tiger howls and wind is born. He asked, "Is there anything further beyond this?
The monk replied, "Right before one's face, you have missed it. The monk said, "Truly a master craftsman! The Master said, "A ghost deludes people in broad daylight.

At the age of thirteen, because his elder brother had entered the monastic order, the master asked him, "What is the purpose of leaving the household life? His brother replied, "To seek liberation."
[The Master] spoke of the Dharma of liberation. The teacher said, "In this way, I too may do so. He then informed his mother, Lady Song, saying, "I wish to go together with you.
His mother was delighted. He subsequently served Zongbian of the Yaoshi Monastery as a monk. For four years, he went to Daci to study the sutras and treatises.
Afterward, he went to rely on Chan Master Hui of Lingyan. After a long time, he attained a slight realization. When Yuanwu took charge of Zhaojue, the Master went to him. There he heard...
Wu (Wuqin) preached extensively. Suddenly, [Foyan] attained sudden enlightenment and collapsed among the assembly. The assembly helped him up, whereupon he said, "I have awakened from my dream.
By evening, his dialogue with Wu was unhindered. Wu was greatly pleased and presented him with a verse. From then on, his spiritual acumen emerged with sharp brilliance.
In the spring of the Yimao year of the Shaoxing era, the Governor of Mei appointed the Master to open a Dharma center at Xiang'er; he did not accept. In that same year, Yuanwu passed away.
Master Shi traveled eastward to the Huainan region, where he went forth to reside at Panlong. He subsequently moved to Langya, and later transferred to Pujie in Wuzhou and Dingye in Quzhou.
Prince Zhao Lingjin of Guangxiao and Minister Zeng Gongke both sought instruction in the Way from him.
Later he resided at Nantai. Not long after, he traveled to Tiantai, visiting the three monasteries of Huguo, Guoqing, and Hongfu. At that time, Minister Shen Jie was the governor of Pingjiang;
because the Tiger Hill Monastery had been abandoned for a long time, he invited the Master to restore it. This was the year of Gengchen in the Qiandao era.
By imperial decree, he was appointed to the Chongxian Monastery. The following year, he received an edict appointing him to Lingyin.
Emperor Xiaozong summoned him into the inner palace for discourse; his Way thus became even more honored. In the spring of the Gui-si year, [he departed].
A special imperial bestowal upon Chan Master Fohai. He ascended the hall and said: "The Way transcends names and words; the Dharma is beyond hearing and seeing.
To shatter empty space into seven or eight fragments—even if one’s armor and helmet were perfectly intact, it would still be like Byung Ki’s secondary arrow."
Ascending the hall: Last night the announcement for the fifth session arrived; it happened that the old monk was washing his feet.
Rising up, he shook out his spirit, yet in the end, he lost the move to him. Ascending the hall: The Way of Heaven diminishes the full; the Way of Earth transforms the full;
ghosts and spirits harm the full; the way of man loathes the full. The old monk’s original registration is from Meishan County, Meizhou Prefecture. His age is the Guiwei year.
Born at the hour of the Snake on the sixteenth day of the twelfth month, I left home from childhood. I do not pluck the horizontal grass, nor do I grasp the vertical blade;
let the mountain turns and the path winds be seen by you yourself. To the south there is no turtle-head, and to the north there is no gabled roof.

Ascending the hall, he said: "A drop of water freezes into ice, its coldness beyond measure. Frozen clouds close in, locking the peaks and ridges. Roots and dust are not obscured; the jewel of the mind is revealed."
Blink your eyebrows and look closely. Ascending the hall for discourse: There is a reason for the new year;

tea is brewed and we ascend the wine tower. A pair of feet with no legs; half a head with three faces. Penetrating through, it is difficult for spirits to discern; meeting it, even ghosts are filled with sorrow.
Blowing a holeless flute upside down, dancing the Liangzhou with rapid beats. *Du!* Ascending the hall: How pleasant it is that mid-spring is gradually warming;

how much more so on the days of Han-shi and Qing-ming! Ten thousand layers of cloud-covered mountains tower in emerald green; the wind and moon of the vast sky serve as neighbors. Everywhere flowers are red and willows are green;
the lake and heavens have calm waves and gentle breezes. Mountain birds on the branches warble repeatedly and earnestly. [Repeated three times. *Suo.*

the serpent’s head falls, and ghosts and spirits are struck with alarm. A monk asked: "Throughout the twelve hours of the day, how should a student apply their mind? He replied: "Dip."

Question: "What is it like when 'this very mind is Buddha'? He said: "A topknot with three points. Question: "What is it like when 'neither this mind nor Buddha'?

why was he unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi? He said: "No needle is hanging from his shoulder. Question: "In the past, there was a scholar who composed..."
The Discourse on the Absence of Ghosts. When the discourse was completed, a ghost scolded him, saying, "What can you do about me?

Indeed, on the day after the end of the *xin* hexagram in the *bingshen* year, he contracted a slight illness. Upon reaching the *shangyuan* festival, he composed a verse and sat peacefully.

Those who escorted him numbered nearly ten thousand. His secular age was seventy-four, and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇera-vaṣa) was fifty-nine.

Beyond the breadth of a hair, beyond the width of a fine down, it is like mountains and like peaks. Upon the point of a needle, a lion turns somersaults; within the hollow of a lotus root, a great garuḍa spreads its wings.

The Guest within the Host asked, "When we meet, there is no need to inquire about one's future. [The Master] said, "What is the Host within the Host?
He replied, "Once the ancestral decree is issued, who is the one who dares to emerge? [The Guest] said, "I have already received the Master’s instruction regarding guest and host;

as for the matter of the supreme vehicle (*zongcheng*), what is it like? He replied, "Ask about the supreme [vehicle]. [The Guest] asked, "What is the matter of the supreme [vehicle]? He replied, "The great ocean."
"If one were content with what they have attained, the hundred rivers would flow backward. When the monks prostrated, the Master said, "This is what Elder Xun has learned over thirty years.
On the day the Master entered the monastery, he said to the assembly, "Brothers, if there is a place of realization, it is not bound by time or occasion."
"Please let me have some news. On a snowy night, a monk knocked on the door of the abbot's quarters. The Master rose, took up a candle, and with a majestic shout, said:
"It is a snowy night at midnight; you have come to resolve your doubts. Why is it that you do not possess the proper decorum? The monk looked down at his robes and satchel.
The Master expelled him from the monastery. He would often say: "The former master lived only to the age of fifty-nine; I am now fifty-six."

"Indeed. There are not many days remaining. In the year Jia-yin of the Xiang-ning era, after concluding the retreat and retiring from my seat at Tian-ning Monastery, I said to the Double槐 (Shuanghuai) Layman Zheng Ji:
'The eighth day of the tenth month is the anniversary of the passing of Fo-jian; that is when my time has come. I beg to return to the south of Zhang.
On the fourth day of the tenth month, Master Zheng sent his younger brother, the monk Dao-ru, to inquire after me. The Master said: 'Your coming is exactly what it should be.'"
"It is time. One day before, it was not yet convenient; one day after, it has been missed.
Although I was born of the same lineage as Fojian, in the end we shall not die of the same lineage. Tomorrow morning, you may seek out a pair of small boats for me.
When [the attendant] said, "Do you want a long one? Do you want a high one? he replied, "About five feet high. Three days later, at the crowing of the cock, he sat upright as usual.
During his lifetime, when an attendant requested that he compose a verse for his passing, the Master said, "I have never been able to compose one. Having said this, he passed away.
On the fourth day of the eleventh month, his body was cremated; his tongue remained unburnt. The local official Chen Shiyen enshrined it in a precious casket and kept it in his home.
The disciples enshrined the remains in a stupa beside Puying Monastery.
Master Ming of Lestam in Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and spoke, citing the karmic conditions of Zhaozhou’s visit to Zhunyu to test the water.
The Master said: "Old Zhao, clouds withdrawn and the mountains revealed; Zhunyu, rain passed and the bamboo breeze clear. Whose family [is this]?"
"In the pond within the villa, a pair of mandarin ducks cannot be fully captured in painting. He then raised the story of Deshan’s alms-bowl, saying:
"From of old, when a family is wealthy, the young children are spoiled; they head toward the riverbank to dangle their painted oars, drawing forth the old master who cannot hold himself back."
They also came aboard the boat to join in the singing and chanting.
Master Baozangben of Taizhou ascended the hall and said: "More than ten days have passed since Qingming;
the rain of blossoms has thinned, yet the depths of my heart remain profound. Spring colors vex the spirit, making sleep impossible; a yellow oriole flies past the green willow shade. Thereupon—
He laughed loudly and descended from his seat. While he was residing at Shousheng Monastery in Wuzhen, Chan Master Dahui arrived while on a tour of propagation.
After the Master had finished his formal expressions of thanks upon ascending the hall, he said: "In years past, Old Bao laughed at Guo Lang; Guo Lang’s dancing sleeves were far too grand."
When it came to the old man Bao performing his dance on stage, Bao Lao’s carefree mastery surpassed that of Guo Lang. He descended from the seat.
Da Hui lit incense and bowed to him.
When Chan Master Qinghai of Zhongxing Xiangfu Temple in Jizhou first met Fojian, Jian asked: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time..."
"He swallowed it all in one gulp. Where else could there be sentient beings to be taught? What is the meaning of this?

Before the Master could offer a word in response, Guanding shouted at him. The Master suddenly realized the essential point and composed a verse, saying: "The ultimate reality has never been defiled by dust; Within it, there is neither old nor new.
The green mountains are, after all, my own family property; There is no need to seek another home or ask for a different path. Guanding—
He said, "Put it down. The Master bowed and departed.
Chan Master Jingzhong Fuzhen Liaocan of Zangzhou was the son of the Luo family of Quannan. He ascended the hall and, looking at the fourfold assembly, said:
"Last night I prepared two segments of Chan; even the final phrase is not required today."
The drum was struck and the hall ascended; not a single word had been prepared. Seeing everyone crowding forward, this mountain monk could not help but speak at random:
"Hú Zhāngsān! Hē Lìsì! Every one of you knows how to sing 'Lálālī'."
"Even so, upon entering the gate of Guangxiao, one cannot avoid piercing through the skull and changing one's eyes. *Chan!* Entering the hall:
On the ninth day of the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums are fresh; this single phrase is luminously manifest throughout ancient and modern times.
Yang Guang’s camel is nowhere to be found; last night its tracks were left in the shade of the pines."
Chan Master Gushan Hai of Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "To speak once and not again is already to fall into the second or third [level].
To meet face-to-face without raising an eyebrow turns into mere fabrication.

Even if one could change the tune upon the movement of a single string, knowing the future by what has passed, or act at the mere sight of the whip's shadow, yet turn back upon seeing the flagpole—such a person deserves thirty blows beneath the heels. How much more so for that stagnant [delusion]!"
"Here, he grinds sparks from stone and seizes flashes of lightning. All his diligent effort is but a trivial matter;
it makes the blue-eyed barbarian from the West fall over with laughter. He struck his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Zhuan’an Shigui of Longxiang in Wenzhou was a successor of Chan Master Qingyuan Fuyan of Longmen.
He was a native of Chengdu and belonged to the Shi clan; his family had for generations followed the Confucian tradition.
He was of marvelous age and keen intelligence. At thirteen, he sought to become a monk; his parents opposed him, and he would refuse to eat.
His paternal uncle allowed him to follow his own will, so he took the tonsure under Zongya of Daci Temple at the foot of the city wall. There, his mind became intoxicated by the *Śūraṃgama Sūtra*.

After more than five autumns, he traveled south to visit Yiqin of Yuquan, Zhixian of Yungai, Xingsu of Baiyang, and Lingyuan Qing. He remained with them for many years before finally ascending to Longmen.

He immediately presented what he had attained during his ordinary practice to Byakugyō (White-Eyed). Byakugyō said, "Your understanding of the mind is already ultimate; you simply lack the exertion required to open your eyes.
He was subsequently appointed to the position of Hall Attendant (*dōshi*). One day, while standing in attendance, [Gensha] asked, "What is it like when all dualistic dependencies are transcended?"
[Daowei] said, "It was just like when you struck the gavel in the Sangha Hall. Yunyan was at a loss for words. Later that evening, he went to the Hall Office (Tangsi).
Daowei again questioned him with the previous remark. Yunyan said, "Idle talk. At these words, Daowei attained great enlightenment.

Yunyan said, "Now there is no more to say. At the end of the Zhenghe era, the Magistrate of Hezhou, Mr. Qian Jingshu, invited him to open a Dharma seat at Tianning Temple; subsequently, he moved to Baoshou.
He served at Chan, Donglin, and Xishan. Subsequently, he moved to Shengquan and Gushan. Later, by imperial decree, he was transferred to Nengren on Mount Yandang.
In the year of Yichou during the Shaoxing era, he received the grace of being appointed to Longxiang on Jiangxin. Entering the hall, he said: "Ten thousand years in a single thought;
a single thought for ten thousand years. Rolling in the mud with one's robes on; washing one's feet and going up to bed to sleep. As for matters spanning kalpas..."
In these present times, the great ocean surges with waves, yet the square inch of the petty man’s mind remains deep and unfathomable. [The Master] picks up his staff and says:
"All of you, if you have not yet attained a point of entry, you must attain a point of entry.
Once you have attained a point of entry, you must have a path for emerging; only then will it suffice. "Great assembly, what is this path for emerging? After a long silence, he says: "Snow."
The pine at the bottom of the ravine is difficult to crush; the moon at the edge of the sky is unmoved by the wind. Holding up his staff, he descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Beyond the reach of ten thousand functions—eyes see forms, ears hear sounds. One phrase presides in the hall: the head wears the heavens, the feet tread upon the earth.
You all know only that today is the first day of the fifth month, yet you do not realize that the golden bird [the sun] is already at midnight."
Hurrying away, the Jade Hare ascends the eastern sea at the break of dawn. (With his whisk, he strikes the meditation seat and descends.
Ascending the hall for discourse: "Clearly there is no awakening; to have a dharma is delusion. You people cannot stand here; you people cannot dwell here.
If you stand, you are precarious; if you dwell, you are blind. You must ensure that the mind does not rest in the mysterious, nor linger in phrases."
Do not let the mind cease; do not let the mechanism cease. Once these three are clarified, there is no need to manage or obstruct anything in any place;

it will naturally manifest before you. There is no need to look after anything in any place; it will naturally become clear. Nevertheless, one must further know that there is a matter beyond this. "The long rain does not stop.
*Du!* [He struck the floor with his staff. Ascending the hall, he said: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to the world. He wished—
Exhausting the vision across a thousand li, one ascends yet another story. When a single speck of dust arises, the entire earth is gathered within it.
When Jiazhou struck the Great Image, and when Shanfu doused the Iron Ox—how should a man of clear eyes respond? After a long silence, he said: "A phrase from the eaves during a long drought."
“The bridge flows, but the water does not flow. [Zhaozhou] struck his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
“Today is the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. Old Chan asks you all: tell me, is it the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, or is it not?
If you say it is not, what words are these? If you say it is, you may deceive the Abbot, but how can you deceive the others?”
"What is the noble eye? He then struck the meditation seat and descended from it. Ascending the hall, he said: "When seeing is seen, that seeing is not seeing.
Seeing is already detached from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. When petals fall, they have intent to follow the flowing water; the flowing water has no sentiment to cherish the fallen petals.
All things that can be returned to their source are naturally not you. That which does not return to its source—what else could it be but you? Long have I harbored this regret."
"Spring has returned, yet there is no place to find it; one knows not that it has turned and entered herein. (He lets out a shout. He says:
"Thirty years from now, do not say that Nengren has ruined the men and women of the family. Ascending the hall, a monk asks: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
He replies: "The eastern neighbor lights the lamp; the western neighbor sits in the dark. The monk says: "I do not know what the purport of this is. He replies: [He remains silent].
The horse immediately has its saddle girthed; the donkey immediately pushes the millstone. The monk bows, and the Master says, "A sharp-witted patch-robed monk requires only one.
He then says, "The horse has its saddle girthed; the donkey pushes the millstone. A sharp-witted patch-robed monk requires only one.
Even if the neighbor to the east lights a lamp clearly, it is not certain that the neighbor to the west sits in the dark. How is the meaning of the West's coming? [To speak] much is superfluous.
"Why does the Master bring calamity upon himself? Question: "What is the primary meaning (paramārtha)? He said: "That which you ask about is the third meaning.
Question: "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? Zhaozhou said 'no. What is the intent of this? He said: [The same as above.]
Once bitten by a snake, one fears even seeing a broken well-rope. Question: "The swallow speaks deeply of the true mark (*dharmatā*) and skillfully explains the essential teachings.
How is this principle? Answer: "It does not compare to the wild goose carrying reeds. Question: "What is the Buddha? Answer:
"A stone tortoise at the mouth of the Huayang Cave. Question: "Luzu faced the wall; what was his intent? Answer: "Metal, wood, and water."
Fire and Earth. The planets Rāhu and Ketu. Question: "When there is neither the phrase nor the absence of the phrase, it is like a vine leaning against a tree;
what then? Answer: "The heart of a thief is always afraid. Question: "What about when the National Teacher called his attendant three times?

Answer: "Beating the drum to play with the monkey; the drum breaks and the monkey runs away. On the eighteenth day of the seventh month of the Bingyin year, he summoned the Elder of his Dharma lineage.
Zongfan entrusted his final affairs to his disciples. His parting verse said: "Thirty-one in the first period, nine in the middle, and seven in the last.
Where the old man’s words end, Guige’s eyes turn red. The following day, he bathed and changed his robes, then ordered the sounding of the great bell with a loud voice.

At the hour of Hai (9–11 p.m.), when the assembly had gathered, he sat upon his seat and entered nirvana with serene composure. After cremation, those who escorted him all obtained *śarīra* relics, which were enshrined in a stupa.
At Mount Gu, his life span was sixty-four years and his *dharma*-age fifty-one.
Chan Master Shayuan Wenshu of Yunju Gao’an in Nankang Commandery was the lay disciple Xiangzhidao; his clan name was Li.
At the age of eleven, he left home, studied the sutras, and received ordination. Possessing innate wisdom, he heard Chan Master Chong cite Emperor Wu’s question to Bodhidharma.
Regarding the causes and conditions of his polishing [his practice]: it was like recovering an old possession. He suddenly said, "Since I have become vast and empty, what 'saint' could there be?

Fayan Chong found these words extraordinary and urged him to travel south to seek instruction. There, he received a prediction of enlightenment from Longmen. One day, a monk had his foot bitten by a snake.
Foyan asked, "Since this is the Dragon Gate (Longmen), why has he been bitten by a snake? The Master immediately replied, "Indeed."
He manifested the marks of a great man. His eyes benefited those who were vessels for the Dharma. He first resided at Jitian Temple in Jiyuan for seven years, then moved to Yunju.

After seven years there, he was ordered by imperial decree to move to Jinshan; he declined on the grounds of illness and was granted exemption. Ascending the hall, he said: "The wall-gazing at Shaolin harbors within it the lands of the East and the West.
The ascent of the hall at Mount Ou fills the four quarters and the zenith and nadir. Thus, the mountains stand majestic and firm."
The palms are level; the water is murky yet remains ever clear. The flowers lack brilliance yet bear fruits in the void.
The wind does not stir, yet a single leaf falls. People have no dharma, yet they may seek instruction; the Buddha has no mind, yet he can further achieve realization.

With wild greens and plain rice, one passes the days and months; moving according to conditions as they arise, the Way is spontaneously efficacious. In the end, what is it? At midday, strike the third watch.
Chan Master Wenlian of Xichan Monastery in Suining Prefecture was a native of Changjiang in that commandery. His clan name was Zhang. By nature, he was exceptionally brilliant and outstanding.
In his youth, he followed the local scholar Zhao Suye and became quite proficient in Confucian learning; Zhao expected great things of him in the future.

However, the Master possessed a soaring aspiration to transcend the mundane world and went directly to rely upon Xicheng at Chongfu Monastery. At the age of twenty-three, he shaved his head and went to Cheng... [text continues]
Du Biao stated that while at the lecture hall, he had deeply grasped the essential meaning of the *Awakening of Faith* and the *Perfect Enlightenment Sutra*.

When Yuanwu returned to Zhaojue, Du went there to rely upon him; however, after a long time, he made no progress. He then traveled east to visit Xian of Guyin and Yuan of Dongshan, yet again he attained no realization.
Later, he arrived at Longmen, where he sat in meditation so intently that he forgot both sleep and food. Foyan, pitying his single-minded devotion to the Way, one night—
Taking Master [Foyan] along, he walked at a leisurely pace down to the foot of Puxian Slope. Looking back at the Master, he said, "I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion;
I have already met you at Wushilong. At these words, the Master realized the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).

The next day, Foyan ascended the hall and certified him before the assembly. His reputation for the Way spread widely. After three years, he requested leave to return home because his mother was elderly.
Yanjue presented him with a verse: At Wushan Ridge, at Wangzhou Pavilion, Before the thought had even arisen, the Way was already complete.

Ten years of bitter toil wandering the rivers and seas— On this day of returning home, he asks not for the distance. The road to one’s native roots is no different; Whether in action or concealment, let there be guarding.
When the fruit ripens, it naturally emits fragrance; Remember the steps you took when you came. He further wrote in a letter: "The Chan practitioner, the Venerable Liau, has..."

The Heart-Jewel entered the Dragon’s Grotto; having recovered it, he returned to his old retreat, never forgetting his origin. He then led several dozen retired monks and long-time companions to see him off.

Thereupon, he traveled upstream to return to his place of study and built a hall for secluded practice. In the first year of the Jingkang era, the Prefectural Governor converted the Xichan Vinaya Monastery and invited the Master to open the Dharma there.
Entering the hall, he said: "If one proceeds exclusively in this manner, one will directly attain..."
The paths of the ordinary and the sage are severed; it is as impenetrable as water cannot leak through. An iron snake cannot bore its way in, and an iron hammer cannot break it open.
Even for thousands and tens of thousands of miles, birds cannot fly across.

To come directly in this manner is inevitably to have one’s head covered in dust and face smeared with mud, to sing nine as ten, and to point to a deer as a horse. Not only does this betray the former masters, but it also buries [the truth].
Having extinguished his own spirit, he dared to ask the great assembly: "Tell me, is it the one who goes thus that is right? Or is it the one who comes thus that is right?
When the peony blooms, it is the face of a Bodhisattva; when the palm leaves scatter, they are the head of a yakṣa. Ascending the hall, he said:

"In all quarters, they discourse on the profound with great clamor, striking the bells and beating the drums every day. At Xichan, there is no dharma to be preached; we have already scrutinized and seen through the lanterns and the pillars."
Do not place a mounting platform at the entrance, lest passersby come to ask for the way. If you must lend them the way, you must look after their feet;
if they stumble, it is like learning the gait of Tang from Handan. Ascending the hall, he said: "When the mind arises, all manner of phenomena arise;

the myriad phenomena of the universe spread out in all directions. Pick up whatever comes to hand and use it immediately. When the sun has passed its zenith, it is already the third watch. When the mind ceases, all phenomena cease."
The various dharmas are extinguished; the paths of the four propositions and the hundred negations are cut off. Even if Bodhidharma were to appear here, he would still be like dust in the eye.

"When the mind arises and the mind ceases, who is it? A wooden man joins hands and returns together. Having returned to the fields of one's native village, one still meets a blow upon the crown of the head.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the first month of spring, the cold still lingers. Directly beneath this, every word and phrase is to the point."
He grasps the nostrils of the monks and pierces through the very heart and liver of the Buddhas and patriarchs.

For those who know this, Bodhidharma did not come to the Eastern Land and the Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven. For those who do not know this, who realizes they have missed it right before their own faces?
Ten thousand eight thousand miles away—this mountain monk shall recite a verse for you once more. Great assembly, do not let it be in vain. Early spring still...
Cold. He ascended the hall and raised this case: A non-Buddhist asked the Buddha, "What Dharma do you teach today? He replied, "I teach the Dharma of certainty.
The next day he asked again, "What Dharma do you teach today? He replied, "The Dharma of uncertainty. The non-Buddhist said, "Why was it certain yesterday?"
"Why is it not fixed today? [The Master] said, "Yesterday it was fixed; today it is not fixed. The Master said:
"Regarding what was said yesterday and what is said today about being fixed or not fixed: 'The Emperor’s decree within the realm; the General’s command beyond the frontier.
The outsider entered the land of dreams that year, and even until now he has still not awakened. A monk asked: "Before the lion has emerged from its cave..."

"How is it? he asked. [The Master] replied, "The claws and fangs have already been bared. [The Questioner] asked, "After emerging from the cave, how is it? He replied, "A dragon's head with a snake's tail.

[The Questioner] asked, "How is it when one has emerged and when one has not yet emerged? He replied, "Just right for a beating. [The Questioner] asked, "I do not ask about going through one layer after another;
but what is it like when one does not go through one layer after another? He replied, "The Acharya has quite a lot of work on hand."
In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year of the Xiangxing era, he suddenly manifested illness. On the twenty-eighth day, sitting upright, he instructed his disciples.
With his own hand, he wrote a testament appointing the monastery’s secretary, Xi Xiu, to succeed him in the Dharma and serve as abbot.

He donated his personal funds to increase the temple lands and, having finished his final exhortations to the assembly, someone requested a verse from him. The Master said: "The late Master of Longmen, in his final instructions, once said: 'No...'"
"The world may take its leave. There is no Dharma to be preached, and no verse to be left behind. How could I betray the intention of my former teacher? Having finished speaking, he passed away.
He was seventy-two years of age and fifty-one years since his ordination.
Chan Master Huanglong Muchuan Fazhong of Longxing Prefecture was a native of Siming. His clan name was Yao. At the age of seven, he took the precepts under Daoying of Guoning Temple in Ning County.

At nineteen, he underwent the examination on the scriptures and received full ordination. He studied the teachings of the Tiantai school and attained insight into the principle of the three contemplations within one mind, yet he had not yet been able to efface his traces.
He traveled to consult various eminent monks until he reached Longmen, where, upon seeing a water mill turning, he experienced a sudden awakening.
He clarified the essential point of the mind and spoke in verse: "The Great Dharma Wheel turns; it is encompassed right before one's eyes.
If you ask further how this is so, it is like water pushing a stone mill. He presented this to Foyan, who asked, "What is the matter within it?

He replied, "The water flows ever longer in the mountain stream. Foyan said, "I have a final phrase to entrust to you. The Master immediately covered his ears and left, subsequently going to Mount Lu.
On Mount Tong’an, he sat in meditation for a long time without food amidst withered trees. During the Xuánhuáng era, there was a great drought in Xiāngtán;
when prayers were offered but no rain came, the Master leapt into the Dragon Abyss and cried out, "You wretched beast! It shall rain one chi! and the rain arrived immediately.

Later, while dwelling at the Rear Cave of Nanyue, he sustained himself on wood and stream water, keeping company with tigers, leopards, monkeys, and gibbons for twenty years. He authored the *Zhèngxīnlùn* (Treatise on Rectifying the Mind) in ten fascicles.

Whenever he rode out on his tiger, Confucians and Buddhists alike would prostrate themselves upon seeing the dust of his approach. In the autumn of the Jia-yin year of the Xiang-er era, the State Councilor Zhēng Yànzhì sent a formal letter of invitation;
through the power of his meritorious deeds, he urged the Master to open the Dharma gate. Praising his earnest devotion, the Master finally consented to go.
Before long, he moved to Nanmu and Yungai, where he retired from his duties. He subsequently accepted invitations to Ersheng, Yuejiang, and Daming, and later resided at Huanglong.
Entering the hall for a formal discourse, he said: “Lord Zhang drinks the wine, yet Lord Li gets drunk. Reflect on this carefully—it is inconceivable!
When Lord Li awakens from his drunkenness and asks Lord Zhang about it, it leaves Lord Zhang with no good mood. No good mood? No!”
It is like returning home and simply falling asleep. Ascending the hall: Today is the fifteenth day of the first month. I have a matter to settle for you.
Be most careful not to let your two eyes be changed by the lamps and fires. Ascending the hall: I have a single phrase that does not borrow the mouths of the various sages;
it does not move one's own tongue; it is neither sound, breath, nor respiration; it is neither emotional consciousness nor conceptual discrimination. Even if one were pure...
This is what is called "closing one's mouth at Vaiśālī," or "Śākyamuni closing his room at Magadha. It is very much like covering one's ears while stealing a bell;
one cannot avoid the leakage of the celestial mechanism (*tianji*).

Even if it were Deshan’s "staff upon entering the gate" or Linji’s "shout upon entering the gate," if examined under the jurisdiction of Mu’an, they would only receive a single blow. A thousand kinds of words and ten thousand ways of speaking—none of them suffice.
"I must teach you to rest within your own house; let the great earth and empty space be as they are—seven hollows and eight protrusions.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? He said, "Do not seek it outwardly. The monk asked, "What is the mind? He said, "Do not search for it outwardly."
[The Master] asked, "What is the Way? [The monk] said, "Do not seek it outwardly. [The Master] asked, "What is Chan? [The monk] said, "Do not transmit it outwardly.
[The Master] asked, "Ultimately, what is it? [The monk] said, "Svāhā in a quiet place. A monk asked, "The assembly is gathered before you;
please, Master, proclaim the Dharma. The Master held up his whisk. The monk said, "I beg the Master to further grant us a skillful means. The Master struck the meditation seat.
In the year Jia-si (1753), in the eleventh month, he showed signs of slight illness. On the day of Wang (the fifteenth), two trails of white vapor drifted out from behind his meditation hall.
The Master suddenly said, "My time has come. He ordered the assembly to gather and gave instructions until they were exhausted.

Then, taking up his brush, he wrote a verse and passed away. His remains were enshrined in a stupa at Hyangwon-dong. Upon the completion of the burial, a great snowfall fell, covering only that specific area. He was sixty years of age.
10. At forty-seven years of age, Chan Master Xuedang Daowen of Wugu in Quzhou, a native of Kuocang, was born into the Ye clan.
His father, Zhongchen, held the rank of two-thousand-shi and devoted his heart to the ancestral Way, styling himself the Layman Jiandu. His mother, née Tao, dreamed that a *bhikṣu* struck her [womb].
She conceived while still in her chamber. Once born, she was dignified, alert, and quick-witted. Upon reaching the age for study, she developed a resolve to transcend the mundane world.

Although she frequently ranked first in the examinations of the classics, she occasionally followed the Chan Master Wei of Tianning, through whom she realized her ultimate destination beneath his words. When she requested to leave the household life, her parents granted their permission.
At the age of nineteen, she paid homage to the Chan Master Jueyin Ying of Puzhao and received the *saṃghāṭī* robe. She then went first to visit...
[The Master] pointed to Chan Master Yuanrun, who had nowhere to enter [the path]. He went directly to Longmen to verify what he had attained.

Foyan admonished him, saying, "Only when you have reached the truth without doubt will you have a share in the discourse. The Master had no reply. One day, [Foyan] raised the case of Xian Sha’s stubbing his toe;
the Master attained awakening. He immediately rushed to the abbot’s quarters. Foyan said, "Awakening is not non-existent, but it is surely like traveling a thousand li..."
He rose from his seat. "If one were to support and uplift [the Dharma] here, what kind of sequential order would there be?

He then had him attend to the right. After more than eight years, he took leave to visit his parents. The District Magistrate and Palace Attendant, Mr. Huang Baoguang, built a hermitage in the rear garden of the Yellow Hall and earnestly invited him to reside there.
In the second year of the Jianyan era, Mr. Xu Kangguo, a Minister of the Household (Zhongsan), came to govern this prefecture and firmly requested that he open the Dharma gates.

At Shouning, he subsequently moved to Fahai, Tianning, and Wugu, where he widely disseminated the profound wind of the Dharma. how deep is the water in the pool of eight virtues at the site of enlightenment? How many red-striped carp are there?"

Only then will you understand that on the path of the Way (dōjō), one swallows three or four things every day and spits out seven or eight. Have you not seen how Master Bailin asked Layman Pang:
'Layman, have you ever shared your phrase of realization with anyone? He replied, 'I have. Bailin asked, 'To whom did you share it? Pang [replied]..."
Baizhang pointed to his chest and said, "Pang. Pang then asked, "Master Bailin, have you ever shared your 'sentence of attaining power' with anyone?
He replied, "I have shared it. Baizhang asked, "To whom did you share it? Bailin donned his bamboo hat and walked away. Baizhang said, "May you fare well on your journey. The Master said:
"Master Pang was much like one who opens a tavern in front of his hall; he was a man of business within the house. Bailin..."
Spirit is like two wrestlers grappling before a horse; at every step, there is no deficiency. Today, if someone were to ask about the site of practice:
"What is the phrase by which Chan Master Jianfeng gained power? simply say: "The superior man follows the mountains and waters;
the man of middle virtue sits within the bamboo grove. If they should ask, "Have you ever shown this to others? simply say: "Standing and walking, he turns back; his literary talent is vast."
Comparing this to Zhongren: Ascending the hall, the Master raised the story of Guishan asking Yangshan, "Is it cold for you?
He said, "One question and one answer; jade threads interlace, and the brocade of clouds is completed. There is no leakage whatsoever.

If you can see this, you will know that Guishan and Yangshan, father and son, sang and clapped in perfect harmony. If you have not yet realized this, I shall further provide a verse for all of you. (He blew his flute.)
Exhausting the elegance of the *Dàshí* (Great Stone) mode, he sings forth the wealth and honor of the *Huángzhōng Gōng* (Yellow Bell Palace) key.
