Question: "Before the lotus has emerged from the water, how is it? He said: "Seven feet, eight feet. Question:

"After it has emerged from the water, how is it? He said: "Three feet, four feet. Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He said: "A venomous snake without horns is most ferocious.
Question: "If one understands it in this way, what then? He said: "The head of the Liangshan office. Question: "As for the teachings..."
"What about your own intention? He replied, "The long river rolls on without ceasing. Question: "What is the Cao-Dong school? Answer:
"A crane roosts in the branches of the wu tree. Question: "What is the Yunmen school? Answer: "A wooden horse ascends a golden ladder.
Question: "What is the Guiyang school? Answer: "Before one's eyes, there is no other grass. Question: "What is the Linji school? Answer: "I shall never..."
"I will not tell you. [The student] asked: "In that case, what kind of Buddha is this? The Master then snapped his fingers three times. [The student] asked:

"The words touch upon both transcendence and subtlety; how can one pass through this without transgression? He said: "Transversely situated beyond the triple world, alone liberated before the myriad functions. [The student] said: "Understood."
"Just as it is said, 'The wind is busy and the road is long; I remember the third month in Jiangnan, where the partridges cry and the hundred flowers are fragrant.
What do you say to this? He replied, "Why speak of this lackluster fellow? The other said, "Tender bamboo sways in the fine golden breeze."
"Hundreds of flowers carpet the ground as the sun lingers. [The Master] said, "Where do you see the 'wind-cavity'? He replied, "Within my eyes and ears, all is serene and elegant.
[The Master] said, "That is merely a flimsy fabrication; it has nothing to do with it. He asked, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?"
He said, "Do not speak of cold until the winter solstice has passed. [The monk] asked, "What about after emerging from the water? He said, "Do not speak of heat until the summer solstice has passed.
[The monk] asked, "What about at the time of emerging and before emerging? He said, "Thirty years from now, do not misrepresent this."
Question: "What is the Buddha? He said: "A fierce fire burning without fuel. Question: "What is the Dharma? He said: "A poor man dressing up as a wealthy person.
Question: "What is the Sangha? He said: "An old woman selling fans shielding her eyes from the sun with her hand.
Question: "What is the master’s 'thorn-bush' (liji pong)? He said: "I will not answer this question. Question: "Why do you not answer? The Master laughed loudly and said: "Swallow it!"
He could not advance, nor could he spit it out. [The student] asked: "What is the meaning of 'one shout like the precious sword of the Vajra King'?
[The Master] said: "A venomous snake in an ancient tomb with horns upon its head. [The student] asked: "What is the meaning of 'one shout like a crouching lion'?

[The Master] said: "The void laughs and nods its head. [The student] asked: "What is the meaning of 'one shout like a probe-stick and shadow-grass'? [The Master] said: "The stone man claps his hands and laughs."
"Haha," he said. "What is 'one shout that does not function as one shout'? [The Master] said: "A pig's head in a cloth bag. He asked: "I have already received your instruction on the four shouts.
Is there anything further above this? [The Master] said: "There is. He asked: "What is this matter that lies above? [The Master] said: "Sawing apart a weightstone.
As soon as these words were spoken, he let out a shout. This was the occasion for the memorial service of Chan Master Foyan. The Master [Zhaozhou] took up the case.
Xiang said, "Master Longmen, you are a decadent icchantika who does not believe in the Buddha-dharma and seeks to extinguish the path of Chan.
You have forced open the gate beyond Vairocana; a cat washing its face thinks it looks fine. A stick of incense burns upon the censer—changing hands and beating one’s breast is but empty vexation.
He then shook his hand and said, "Stop this vexation," and placed his sitting cloth over his shoulder, making a gesture.
The woman bowed and said, "Please do not take offense that this junior daughter-in-law has disturbed you, Great Master.
From within the room, he asked, "Why does a cat love to catch mice? He asked again, "When the wooden board sounds, why does the dog bark?

On the upper ten days of the second month in the twenty-seventh year of the Xiangshi era, while traveling to the western plain of the temple, he pointed to the ground and instructed his attendant monk.

While laborers were repairing a small stupa, on the first day of the third month, the Master showed signs of slight indisposition. On the following day, the Marquis of Wei sent a physician to see him.

The Master smiled and said, "If medicine could truly cure people, there would be no such thing as death in this world. Send word to the Marquis of Wei: he has served the state generously; let him take care of himself.
On the sixth day, an attendant monk reported that the stupa was nearing completion. The Master ordered the drum to be beaten to assemble the assembly. He ascended the seat and took up his staff.
He tapped once on the left side and said, "The thirty-two marks lack this mark. He tapped once on the right side and said, "The eighty minor characteristics lack this characteristic.
With a single stroke, Master Yao finished his portrait of Zhigong, revealing the draft.
He tapped once more, looked at the assembly, and said, "Do not be distressed; accept it directly and cease further seeking. He descended from his seat and returned.
In the abbot’s quarters, he sat upright in meditation and passed away. He was seventy-three years old and had spent fifty-four summer retreats.
After the cremation, his remains and *śarīra* relics were collected and enshrined in a stupa built at Mount Xianren (Immortal Mountain).
A monk asked Chan Master Fangguang Shen of Tanzhou: "If there is even a single dharma, Vairocana falls into the state of an ordinary person;
if there are no myriad dharmas, Samantabhadra loses his realm. I do not yet understand the meaning of this—what is its intent? The Master said: "The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few;
the poor regret that a single body is too many."
Shiqi, the Head Seat, was a native of Chengdu. He studied under various masters and later joined the assembly at Longmen.
One day, while seeking further instruction, his doubts were completely dispelled. When Yan [Yunwen] ordered him to share the seat with him, Qi firmly declined, saying, "This is no small matter."
It is like using a golden needle to pierce the eye; were there even a hair’s breadth of error, the pupil would be destroyed.

I wish that in every lifetime I may dwell on the stages of learning to refine myself, for the eye is what I hold most dear. In my later years, when students earnestly requested [instruction], I could not refuse them. Thereupon, he spoke this verse:
Because all dharmas are empty, my mind is empty; because my mind is empty, all dharmas are the same. All dharmas and my mind have no separate essence;
they exist only within this present single thought-moment. But tell me, which thought-moment is this? The assembly was at a loss.
[The Master] gave a wondrous shout and ended the session.
The nun Huizhen of Jingju Monastery in Wenzhou addressed the assembly, citing Fayan’s ascent to the hall:
“When the three beats of the drum have ceased, they come crowding up; the Buddha-dharma and human affairs are all settled at once. Huizhen said, “I, this mountain monk, say:
when the three beats of the drum have ceased and they come crowding up, my staff is not here, so I shall give them thirty blows with the handle of a broom for now.”

Chan Master Daopei Yue’an Shanguo of Tanzhou (15th generation of Nanyue; 11th generation of Linji;
4th generation of Yangqi), whose dharma heir was Chan Master Kaifu Daoning, was surnamed Yu and native of Lianzhou. He lost his father when he was young.
Relying on the seven treasures, he first shaved his hair at Yuanjia. Traveling to Ehu, he heard two children playing and had an awakening.
He then went to Yunju. One day, a monk came from Huanglong and asked, "How do you instruct people in the room of Sishi (Dead Heart)?
He replied, "Whenever I cite the karmic conditions of Yunmen’s 'falling into a word' to question my students, I ask them: 'Where is the falling into the word?'"

Upon hearing this, the Master was filled with great joy. He immediately went to Huanglong, where he received the seal of approval (*anujñā*). When Sīxīn retired from his post, the Master went to Kāifú;

their conversations were even more harmonious, and Kāifú appointed him to share the seat [of the abbot]. As Kāifú was about to enter *parinirvāṇa*, he presented his fly-whisk (*cāmara*) to the Master, but the Master declined it with all his might.
Fufu said, "In the final age of the Great Dharma, we rely upon you for its revival; do not refuse. After Fufu passed away, the Master stayed at Xiangxi.

He encountered Chan Master Foguo, who was residing at Daolin Temple, and appointed him as Librarian. The Master then presided over the *bifu* (the striking of the whisk) for the assembly. Having concluded his summary of the essential principles, he cited:
"Qianfeng addressed the assembly, saying: 'If you raise one, you must not raise two. To let pass one point is to fall into the second. Yunmen then stepped forward..."
The assembly said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went back to Jingshan. Feng said, "The head cook must not be called for general labor tomorrow.
The Master said, "Gan Peak creates mounds on level ground; Shao Shi stirs up waves with the wind.
Although it is like mixing water and mud, it has been a model for the monastic community for a thousand ages. Since it is a model for the monastic community, why [is this so]?"
"Mixing water with mud—do you understand? If one does not enter the great waves, how can one see the one who plays amidst the tide? Foguo (Foguo Yuanwu) struck his palm in approval;
from that time on, he became widely renowned. The District Magistrate, Mr. Zeng Xiaoxu, submitted an official memorial requesting that the Master take up residence in a monastery.
He subsequently served as abbot at Daowu and Foyan, moved to Huangbo in Min Province and to both East and West Chan monasteries, and finally resided at Dayue (having twice held the abbacy at Foyan).
Ascending the hall, he said: "When Xi Zhong constructed a carriage, there were one hundred spokes. Take away both ends and remove the axle.
He struck a circular mark with his staff and said, "Do not mistake this for the zero point on the scale. He tapped the floor once and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall again, he said:

"In the autumn of the eighth month, where is there heat? As for the matter that transcends [the ordinary], it is spoken of at all times. Turning back the pivot of heaven and letting the earth revolve."
[The Master] did not even ask about the axis. But tell me: when the ground is of gold and the houses are of white silver, what kind of person dwells there?

After a long silence, he said: "Majestic and lofty is his sacred virtue, meeting the Three August Ones; distinct and clear is his pure radiance, swallowing the two luminaries. He then ascended the hall.
The path of language is cut off; things and self are both thus. The road of meaning does not arise; wind and clouds meet in harmony.
Thus, the profound gate is fully opened and the true eye flows forth. Radiance shines throughout the earth, manifesting auspiciousness and portents.

Even though it is so, how shall one speak the single phrase of responding to things without partiality? He lets out a shout and says: "In every instance there is neither grasping nor rejecting; in every place..."
Severing intimacy and distance. Entering the hall: This Dharma cannot be shown; words and signs are quiescent. Striking through the vast void—ten thousand miles of a single bar of iron.
All you practitioners of Chan: what was the pivot of the teaching just now? If you can see it, [you have attained it].
Merit is not bestowed in vain. If this were not so, one would only know that committing grave offenses obstructs Bodhi, while failing to perceive the Tathāgata’s true secret instruction.

[The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended from it. [The Record of the Master] thanking the *gòngtóu* (offering supervisor) for the assembly’s meal: "I untie the golden bell from beneath the tiger's chin."
Stirring the multitudes and moving the masses, he took the bright pearl from within the scales of the Azure Dragon; its light illuminates heaven and earth.
Today, even this mountain monk has arrived here and cannot praise it enough. How should you all proceed? Raising his whisk, he said:
"Blinking your eyebrows, you must quickly realize it! He threw down the whisk and descended from his seat. A monk asked: "Dharma sat facing the wall for nine years."

[The Master] asked, “What about at that time? [Dongshan] said, “When the fish swims, the water becomes turbid. [The Master] asked, “When the Second Patriarch prostrated three times, why did he instead obtain the marrow?
[Dongshan] said, “The earth is fertile, so the eggplants are large. [The Master] asked, “It is just like the saying: ‘One flower opens into five petals; the fruiting occurs naturally.’”
"What matter does this clarify? He replied, "A thief uses his loot as proof. [The questioner] said, "Sometimes riding upon a fine moon, one does not realize one has passed the Azure Isle.
He replied, "The Acharya has no share in it. [The questioner] asked, "What is the Moon Hermitage? He replied, "It cannot be painted in colors."
[The Master] asked: "What is the house style of Yue-an? He replied: "Cast from raw iron. [The Master] asked: "When there is a phrase and no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree—what then?
He replied: "Exhaustively tested by those of the same lineage. [The Master] said: "When the tree falls and the vine withers, where do the phrases return?
And how about that? He replied: "Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun. [The Master] said: "Why did Muzhou laugh 'he-he'? He replied: "Waves."
[The student] read the Sanskrit characters, which said: "Daowu pushed him into the mud, and Guishan did not care. [The teacher] asked, "What is the meaning of this?
[The student] said, "Reason does not depend on a loud voice. [The teacher] asked, "Luoshan said, 'Daowu is a fellow who picks up horse dung.
What about that? [The student] said, "That talkative master. [The teacher] said, "Today I see the Master is thoroughly proficient in every way. [The student] said, "Indeed."
He looked up and cried out to the blue heavens. The monk prostrated himself, and the Master said, "A mistake. A monk asked, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?
The Master said, "Heaven and earth have no different colors. The monk said, "And what is it like after it has emerged? The Master said, "Its fragrant scent pervades the entire world.

On the thirteenth day of the first month of the Ren-shen year of the Xiang-er era, he fell ill. On the nineteenth, he wrote a parting letter to his acquaintances and gathered the assembly to exhort them.

He advanced toward the path. Having finished writing the verse, he passed away with a smile. On the eighth day of the second month, his entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the western peak of the monastery.
He was seventy-four years of age and fifty-eight years since his ordination.
The Fifth Patriarch Baizhang, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Zhi, recorded that Chan Master Gao of Longhua in Qizhou ascended the hall and said: "The Elephant King walks; the Lion King dwells.
The barefooted Kunlun has eyebrows standing upright. Hanshan and Shide laugh heartily, pointing at the old pine tree before the gate. Now tell me," he said, "what is it?"
What was he pointing out? Suddenly, when the wind blows it down, it is a fine pile of firewood.
Chan Master Sheng of Nan’an, of Jianzhou, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Nantang Yuanjing of Dasui, ascended the hall and held up his whisk to show the assembly, saying: "Recognize the hook-tip."
My friend, do not mistake the scale for the stars. Do you understand? "This very mind is Buddha"—how few know this! Standing in the snow with waist-deep drifts, one gains but the skin.
When the waves of the four seas are stilled, the dragon plays with his treasure; let the ants shake Mount Sumeru as they please.

Neither Buddha nor mind, beyond all description or sentiment—this is the bird-path of the profound way; hasten back on your journey. With the *śakrāloka* eye, preserve your skillful adaptability; do not cling to the cold.

"It is like a person cutting down a tree: if one strike is delivered at the root, the life-force is severed. You have been striking at the branches; how could that sever the life-force?
Today, those who discourse on Chan in all directions are for the most part like this—what benefit is there for the matter at hand?
As for the direct transmission of the authentic lineage, there are only three or four people. The Master departed in indignation. The following day, Huì asked him: "You..."
"Are you still in doubt? he asked. [The Master] replied, "There is nothing to be doubted. [Fayan] said, "It is just like when the ancients met one another:

before a word was spoken, they already knew whether the other was substantial or hollow; or upon hearing their speech, they immediately recognized its depth or shallowness. How is this principle to be understood? The Master was struck with awe, and his sweat poured down.
He did not know where to go. Huì commanded him to investigate the phrase "having" and the phrase "not having. As Huì passed by Yunmen’s hermitage, the Master accompanied him on the journey.
One night, he asked: "I have reached this point, yet I cannot attain thorough penetration. Where does my illness lie? Huì said: "Your illness is most peculiar;
even the world's physicians fold their hands in helplessness. Why is that? Others die and cannot be revived, but you are now alive and have never been dead."
"One must die in order to reach the ground of great peace and bliss; it is only by dying once that one can attain it. The Master’s doubts grew even deeper. Later, he entered the room for instruction.
Huì asked, "The porridge has been eaten, the bowl has been washed, and the medicinal taboos have been removed.

Now, bring forth a single phrase! The Master said, "It is split asunder. Huì let out a thunderous shout and said, "Are you talking about Zen again? At this, the Master attained great enlightenment. Huì—
He beat the drum and addressed the assembly, saying: "To grasp the hair of a tortoise and laugh with joy—strike once and the myriad layers of gates and locks are opened.
What a celebration for my entire life today! Who would say that a thousand miles have deceived me here? The Master also presented a verse, saying:
A single pressure strikes the disciple like a thunderclap; it startles the North Star from within Mount Sumeru.
The vast waves surge, flooding the heavens; he grasps his nostrils but loses his mouth. Huang Duānfú of Shǎowǔ established a hermitage and requested the Master to serve as its abbot.

He stayed for two years, then returned east to occupy a seat at Gǔshān. When the Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Li Gōngbǐng, invited him with the title "Teaching Loyalty," he opened the Dharma there.
Ten years later, he moved to Guishan. Entering the hall, he said: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. Why act so foolishly?
When the tree falls and the vine withers, where do the phrases go? I know that you all will ultimately fail to find their heads and noses.
Why is this so? It is simply because when clarity reaches its peak, it conversely causes what is attained to be delayed."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Dreams, illusions, and empty flowers—what need is there to grasp at them? Gain and loss, right and wrong—let them all go at once.
He threw down his whisk and said, "I, this mountain monk, have already let go today. As for you all, what will you do?"
He spoke again: "Attendant, take up the whisk. He ascended the hall, struck the meditation staff, gave a shout, and said:
"It is not that I sit here frequently urging you to drink wine; it is simply that since we parted, I have rarely seen you. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he said:
"If you bring nothing forth, you cannot bear the weight upon your two shoulders. To directly accept this is to sit within a pit of excrement. Is there anyone [who can do so]?"
"One who has emerged alone and free? Even if there were such a person, they would still be a spirit of Huanglong.
A monk asked, "Why was Mañjuśrī unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi? The Master said, "I am tired today. The monk said, "Why was Wangming, however, able to emerge?

The Master said, "It leaves people in a state of doubt. The monk said, "If that is so, then the thousand peaks of Mount Hua are split open, revealing their exquisite beauty. [The Master] let out [a shout].
"Yellow River, one stream of clarity. He said, "Leave it to your own conjecture. Question: "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]? He said: "Seventy-three, eighty-four.
The Master resided at Mount Gui for over a year, then returned to Yunmen Hermitage due to illness.

On the eighth day of the second month of the Yihai year of the Shaoxing era, he shaved his head, bathed, changed his robes, and informed the assembly before passing away in the right-side reclining posture. On the fifteenth day, his body was cremated.

He obtained five-colored śarīra relics. His disciple Huikong (慧空) brought them back to Guizhao Jiaozhong (歸教忠). On the eighth day of the sixth month, a stupa was erected on the southern slope of the mountain.
Chan Master Tanyi of Yuyuan in Fuzhou had long relied upon Yuanwu; he considered himself free from doubt. At the beginning of the Shaoxing era...

Chuzhu resided at Xinghua Xiangyun, where his Dharma assembly was quite flourishing. When Dahui entered Min, he realized that Chuzhu’s realization was not yet authentic, so he sent a letter summoning him to come.
Chuzhu delayed for some time. Dahui then gave a small lecture (xiaocan), severely rebuking him, and posted a public notice to the fourfold assembly.
Having no choice, Chuzhu broke the summer retreat to go and visit him. Dahui interrogated him regarding his realization; after a while, he said: "With such a view as yours, how dare you..."
"Is he the successor to the Elder Yuanwu? The Master withdrew from the monastery and went to visit him.

One day, upon entering the room for instruction, Dahui asked, "I want someone who does not understand Chan to serve as National Teacher. The Master replied, "I am fit to go and serve as National Teacher. Dahui shouted him out.
Not long after, Dahui said to him, "Xiangyan’s place of awakening was not in the striking of the bamboo; Jushi’s attainment was not in..."
[The Master] pointed to his finger. The Teacher (Zhaozhou) thereupon attained sudden enlightenment. Later, while residing at Yuyuan, he offered incense for Huì.
He subsequently visited Huì at Xiaoxi. When Huì ascended the seat, he raised [the following]: "One day Yunmen held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying:

'Ordinary people truly say it exists; those of the Two Vehicles analyze it and say it does not exist; Pratyekabuddhas call it illusory existence; Bodhisattvas realize its emptiness in its very substance. The patch-robed monk...
When the monk saw the staff, he simply called it a "staff. When walking, he simply walked; when sitting, he simply sat; he was not permitted to touch it at all.
Huì said, "I am not like the old man Yunmen, who carves out a hollow in empty space," and then suddenly picked up the staff and said:
The staff does not belong to existence; it does not belong to illusion; it does not belong to emptiness. *He strikes once.* He says:
"Ordinary people, those of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—all turn toward this very place. Each, according to their own capacity, fully obtains its utility.
Yet, within the domain of the patch-robed monk, it acts as a harm and a grievance: when one wishes to walk, one cannot walk; when one wishes to sit, one cannot sit. To take even one step further—"
Having been led astray from the path by this staff, if you take a step back, you will have your nostrils pierced by it.
Is there anyone here now who is not dissatisfied? Come forth and meet this staff!
If there is none, next year there shall be new branches; the spring wind that causes such disturbance will never cease. At this very moment, what should be done?
"How so? [The Master] descended from his seat and said, "I trouble Yuyuan to bring this forth for the sake of the assembly. The Master ascended the seat;

having finished his expressions of gratitude, he then raised the previous dialogue and said: "Just now, the Abbot’s critique was much like a weary fish resting in a pond, or a sick bird perching on reeds.
If it were Yuyuan, it would not be so. He picked up his staff and said: "This staff—can it exist? Can it not exist?"

"Able to manifest illusions, able to be empty. Ordinary people, those of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—*claps once*. He says: 'Here, everything is shattered into a hundred fragments.
Only within the domain of the patch-robed monk is it like a dragon finding water, like a tiger relying on a mountain; wherever he wishes to go, he goes."
When it is time to sit, he sits. To take one step forward, heaven and earth tremble; to take one step back, the grass bows and the wind blows.
But tell me, how do you speak that phrase of neither advancing nor retreating? After a long silence, he said:

"Holding a scripture in hand, leaning against a pine tree, he smiles and asks the guest from where they come. He descended from his seat, and the assembly bowed to him (or, according to some versions, this occurred after Yuanwu had left).
Chan Master Wuben of Jianfu Temple in Raozhou was a native of Hukou on the Yangtze River. He first resided at Boshan. Entering the hall, he said:
"To those who bow high to Śākyamuni but do not prostrate to Maitreya, I grant thirty blows of the staff.
Why? Because they only know how to ascend step by step; they do not know how to let go from the void. They plow for the eastern neighbor and pull the harrow for the western neighbor."
"I give you thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because you only know how to let go from the void; you do not know how to ascend step by step.
When the Mountain Monk speaks thus, is there any fault in it? Is there anyone among the assembly who can examine this and find it wanting?
If you can examine it and find it wanting, I shall walk hand-in-hand with you to the southern side of Mount Sumeru. If you cannot examine it and find it wanting, [I shall] spread my robe.
An old crow in a sack; though alive, it is as if dead. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Śākyamuni shut his room in Magadha;
Vimalakīrti sealed his mouth in Vaiśālī; Subhūti manifested the Way by shouting 'No-speech';
Śakra and Brahmā ceased their sight and hearing and rained down flowers. O Great Assembly! This crew of incompetent fellows has, for no reason, privatized the ancestral fields and gardens."

The covenant was sealed; at once, the flower was split asunder. This has caused the descendants of later generations, even after a thousand years, to have not a single tile above their heads to shelter them, nor a spot the size of a needle’s point below them to plant it.
Had Boshan seen this at that time, he would have dug a pit in the middle of a crossroads and buried them all at once, sparing them from this mutual neglect. Why is this so?
This is not seeing the Way. "A family prospers through filial sons; a state achieves hegemony through strategic ministers.
Chan Master Cigan Shoujing of Xichan in Fuzhou (the introductory remarks are not detailed) ascended the hall and said: "To discuss the profound and explain the subtle..."
To discharge excrement and urine; to wield the staff and shout; to use salt to quench thirst; to establish host and guest;

to analyze the patriarchal teachings in detail—should one instead do none of these things, that too is merely sitting in a ghost cave. At this point, I, this mountain monk, have already beaten the retreat drum.
But tell me, when you people are usually frustrated in heart and stifled in speech, what should you do? Do not take it...
Studying idly for understanding buries the mind of the Patriarchs. Ascending the hall, he said: "To sit squarely upon the crown of Vairocana, one must be a person of immeasurable capacity.
If one is a person of immeasurable capacity, one does not sit upon the crown of Vairocana. Ascending the hall, he said:
"If you clarify only the self and do not awaken to what is before your eyes, this person has eyes but no feet. If you only awaken to what is before your eyes..."

Not understanding oneself—this person has feet but no eyes. Only when the eyes and feet assist one another, like the two wheels of a cart or the two wings of a bird, is it right to examine them thoroughly before striking.
Ascending the hall: Today is the ninth day of the twelfth month. The destitute man wanders abroad.
Although he does not return home, he is nonetheless a skilled hand. Since he does not return home, for what reason?
Moyu then said, "He is a master of his craft. In the narrow alleys he does not ride a golden horse; on his return journey, he wears a tattered robe. He ascended the hall and said:

"In the midst of the scorching heat of the nine summer months, the wooden man sweats without ceasing. Now that one or two nights have passed and it has become cool, do not say that this mountain monk does not speak.
He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall again and said: "If you wish..."
This is the correct grasp of the essential. One must simply let the great earth become desolate. If you wish to come forward to meet the snow-blade, you cannot avoid exposing its sharp edge.
At such a time, setting aside the question of whether Śākyamuni could have shown his head, how would you all explain it when you are hiding your body inside a stirrup?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Way is the constant Way; the mind is the constant mind."

When you people hear this old mountain monk speak in such a manner, you immediately say, "I understand. You think it is simply that the large month has thirty days and the small month has twenty-nine;
that there is heaven above your head and earth beneath your feet; that you hear sounds with your ears and breathe through your nose.
But what if the four great oceans were suddenly upon your heads, and venomous snakes pierced your eyes, while frogs entered [your nostrils]?
“Your nostrils—how about that? Ascending the hall, he said: “Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra discuss principle and phenomena;
Linji and Deshan employ the staff and the shout. Dongchan takes one great sleep until dawn; he simply loves the wind blowing from the cool places. *Du!*”

Ascending the hall: Upon the crown of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, there is a great road that pierces the heavens. If one has not yet penetrated the barrier of birth and death, how can they dare to take a step forward?
Whether they advance or do not advance, the great thousandfold world-system offers no obstruction. A single phrase cuts off all verbal explanation; Nanda holds up an iron pillar.
On the day of opening the hall, after the incense has been offered, the Master takes his seat. National Teacher Nantang strikes the mallet and says: "The Dharma assembly..."
"O assembly of dragon-elephants, you should contemplate the primary meaning. As the Master uttered these words, he immediately shouted, "This is the 'seventh' meaning!

Those who had long studied under former masters already discerned the underlying intent; for those among the later students who harbored doubts, what harm was there in their asking questions? A monk asked:
"When Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, 'Aside from the transmission of the golden robe, what else did the World-Honored One transmit? Kāśyapa called out, 'Ānanda! and Ānanda responded."
[The student] said, “Yes. I do not yet understand what this means. [The Master] said, “By all means, do not touch it.
[The student] asked, “What about when Kāśyapa said, ‘Throw down the banner-pole before the gate’? How is that? [The Master] said, “A stone ox lies across the ancient road.
[The student] asked, “As for you, Master, did you have this very message while you were with Furi? [The Master] said, “I had no such message. [The student] asked, “How so?”
“Dingguang beckoned from afar at Golden Ground; Zhizhe nodded his head in the dark at Jiangling.
He said, “Do not take the cypress by the courtyard and lightly compare it to the mugwort by the roadside. The monk bowed. The Master then said, “Dingguang beckoned from afar at Golden Ground;
Zhizhe nodded his head in the dark at Jiangling. This is already ten thousand miles away amidst white clouds; how much more so when one does not know to stop right here?”
If one were to stop right here, the mess would be considerable. Is there anyone who can examine this thoroughly?
If not, I, this mountain monk, suffer a defeat today. Question: "The Buddhas hand it down to one another; the Patriarchs transmit it from one to the next. I wonder what it is they transmit?
Answer: "Quickly, prostrate three times. Question: Yongjia said, "Not seeing a single dharma..."
"Only then can one be called Avalokiteśvara. What is the meaning of this? It is said: "A monkey playing with sticky glue. It is also said:
"Wherever there is water in a thousand rivers, there is the moon; where there are no clouds for ten thousand miles, there is the sky. It is further said: "A monkey tied to a pillar."
[The Guest] asked: "Without brandishing even an inch of blade, I request that you, Master, meet me. [Dongshan] said: "When meeting the strong, one becomes weak. [The Guest] asked:

"How can one bury the weapons and engage in combat? [Dongshan] said: "It is precisely because you, Dharma brother, do not brandish even an inch of blade. [The Guest] asked: "I wonder, is there still something further above this?"
[The Master] said, "There is. [A monk] asked, "What is the matter that transcends this? He said, "A defeated general is not executed.

[A monk] asked, "Before the hall of the ancient Buddha, who arrives first? He said, "An eyeless village elder. [The monk] said, "I do not understand how one should proceed. He said, "Carrying a knotted staff slung across the shoulder."
Chan Master Miaokuan Daoxian of Kaishan in Jianning Prefecture was a native of that province (his clan name is lost).

Having received full ordination, he traveled to the Eastern Capital, where he served under Dahui within the assembly of Yuanwu. When Dahui was appointed to Mount Jing, the Master accompanied him as an attendant; not long after, however—
He was sent to Lingling to deliver greetings to the Layman Ziyuan. On the way, he suddenly attained sudden enlightenment. Upon his return, Huì specifically granted him formal certification (*inka*).
He retired to seclusion at Mount Xianzhou, where the fourfold assembly gathered like clouds and the Dharma seat flourished in great prosperity.
Master Liu Yanxiu of Baoxue invited him to reside at Kaishan. Entering the hall, he said: "Last year, there was also a June fifteenth."
This year, too, there is a June fifteenth; last year, there was a June fifteenth. This year’s June fifteenth lacks that of last year’s;
this year’s June fifteenth exceeds that of last year’s. Where there is excess, there is no need to subtract;
where there is deficiency, there is no need to add. Since there is neither addition nor subtraction, then let that which is in excess be used extensively.
Using very few words, he let out a shout and said, "Is this much? Is this little? After a long silence, he said, "Among those who know this message, how many can there be?
He ascended the hall and said, "Dongshan’s 'three pounds of hemp'—take it and weigh it on a scale with no markings.
Every pound weighs exactly one hundred and sixty taels and two hundred cash; not even a single coin less."
"Li! This is exactly the same as that which was inside Zhaozhou’s hall. It simply was not right for Daoyu to saw apart the iron weight;
consequently, it leaves people unable to understand it. If you wish to understand it now, simply ask Yunmen about the 'dry dung pellet.
[He] ascended the hall [and said]: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. The lantern is knocked over, the moonlight is shattered."
Leaning on [the staff], he rushes through the Buddha Hall and looks back toward the Sangha Hall. Look closely: what kind of furniture is this?

*Du!* It is fit only for beating rats. Ascending the hall, he said: "All of you come up from the Sangha Hall in such a manner, and shortly thereafter go down from the head of the Dharma Hall in such a manner;
you have never missed a single step. Why, then, do you not understand? Liang...
Jiuzhou said: "It is precisely because it is so utterly clear that what is attained is made all the more delayed.
He ascended the hall and raised the following cases: Master Mazu said, "This very mind is Buddha. The Master said, "Wrong. He also said, "Neither mind nor Buddha.
The Master said, "Wrong. Nanquan said, "Not mind, not Buddha, not a thing. The Master said, "Wrong. If a person can break through these three stubborn obstructions...
I grant that he has gained an eye within his study of the Way; yet, if this were not so, a sudden Vairambha wind would arise and startle the sleep of the Brahma King.
Chan Master Danyuan Zunpao of Yushan in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of Changxi. In his youth, he studied together with Yuyuan Yiwen.
Dao Yuanwu practiced for several years until, at the beginning of the Jianyan era, he returned to his hometown to assist Zongyi at Xiangyun in Putian.

In the spring of the Jia-yin year of the Shaoxing era, Dahui was residing at Yangyu; the Master went there to visit him. During the "entering the room" session, Dahui asked about the dialogue concerning whether San-sheng and Xing-hua had emerged or not, and whether they were acting as persons or not acting as persons:
"Tell me, do these two old fellows have a way of emerging?"
There was no place for it. The Master struck Hui once on the knee.
Hui said, "Was this single punch of yours to avenge San-sheng, or to avenge Xing-hua? Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
As the Master hesitated, Hui struck him again and said, "You must never forget this blow. Later, while in his quarters, Hui asked a monk, "De..."

The official document was issued. As the monk hesitated to deliberate upon it, Huì gave a shout. Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly grasped the subtle meaning. Dàhuì joyfully granted him permission [to teach] (his words regarding his emergence in the world have not yet been seen).
Chan Master Nengren Kumu Zuyuan of Yanshan in Wenzhou was a native of Changle in the Seven Min regions. His clan was the Lin family.
Initially, he visited Xuefeng Yu and subsequently relied upon Foxin Cai; he had already attained realization through their respective methods.

Later, when he was staying at Yunmen Hermitage in the presence of Dahui, he saw a monk trim a lamp while sitting in meditation at night, and only then did he abandon his previous realizations. He composed a verse which says: "Trim the lamp up!"
This fire has, throughout kalpas, illuminated and shattered ignorance. Upon returning to the hall, one bumps into the Holy Monk;

He visited Gushan Gui and Jingzhong Yue, both of whom granted him their seal of approval. Later, he arrived at Jiaozhong.

One day, while entering the inner quarters, he heard the master cite the story of the woman emerging from meditative concentration (*samādhi*). As he was about to step through the door, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and said:
"Carrying my own flask, I went to buy village wine; putting on my robe, I have come back to be the host. Jiaozhong asked, "Who is it that stands in the middle? The Master bowed and departed.
Chong laughed at him. In the Jisi year of the Xiangshu era, when Chong moved to reside at Guishan, the Master succeeded him on the seat.
Later, he transferred to Dajian and Chongfu. In the Dinghai year of the Qiandao era, he retired from his duties and resided at Xuefeng, Dong’an, Yangyu, and Yunmen.

In the spring of the Gengshen year, Lord Wang Shipeng, Governor of Quanzhou and Dragon-Scholar, invited [the Master] to reside at Fashi. On the day he accepted the invitation, he ascended the hall and said:
"In the mountains of Yunmen, a hard fortress has been established for years already; yet at the head of the Yangyu River, not even a single star of the first magnitude has appeared.
Raising a hand to grasp the Southern Dipper, turning the body to lean upon the Northern Pole—casually cast out the East."
The Mountain’s Secret Code: Having scrutinized all the wild foxes under heaven, when the opportunity arises and we face one another, there is no room for leniency.
Under a single shout, the lame donkeys flee in a pack. Therefore, Yaoshan said: "There has never been one who travels far without staying, nor one who stays long without traveling.

"Alas! The ancients were much like those who used a pearl from the River Sui to shoot at a sparrow, or traded the Jade Disc of Zhao for a crow.

when the Abbot of Yunmen goes today to the invitation of Fashi, what words does he have to benefit people? An eighty-year-old old man rolls a brocade ball—straight from the Yangtze."

I ask those with the eye of study to examine this for themselves. On the full moon of the twelfth month in the year Wushen, he wrote this verse and entered nirvana.

Chan Master Mian Xianjie of Tiantong, of the lineage of Chan Master Ying'an Tanhua of Tiantong, was a native of Fucheng in Fujian.
He presided over the assembly at Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture. One day he ascended the hall and said:

Dog meat. Zhaozhou examines the abbot. Buying high and selling low; not worth a single coin. It is just like this:

when the wind is faint among the oak leaves, the dust nurtures the young antlers. Ascending the hall, he struck his staff and said: "When deluded, one is deluded only by this very thing. Then...

"If you cannot say it, Huazang will speak for himself. He threw down his staff and said, "Thirty years hence.
He ascended the hall and raised a case, citing Master Sishin’s instruction to the assembly: "One must reach the place where one person is; one must also reach the place where half a person is;

Once the arrow has been withdrawn, who would worry that the four seas are not at peace?

Suddenly he attained awakening. He spoke a verse which said: "The dog has no Buddha-nature; Rāhu enters its destiny. It is not that it kills people;

At the Dharma Hall of Huazang Yian Youquan, Chan Master in the lineage of Chan Master Fajian of Wuan, it was said in a formal address: "Today the mouth of the sack has been tied shut;
O clear-eyed monks, do not wander aimlessly. Where the activities of the mind cease, one turns the body around; even a sneeze becomes the Teacher."
The Lion’s Roar. A sandalwood grove; let it run wild. Raising the eyebrows, they grow upon the crown of the head. Carving flesh to form a sore reveals the family’s disgrace.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Chan! Chan! Without faction, without partiality. When lost, one is separated by a thousand miles; when awakened, it is right at the edge of the lips."
Chan Master Deshan Juan of Dechang Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Dayang Xuanjue of Daming, was a native of Tongchuan. He ascended the hall, held his staff horizontally, and said:
"One, two, three, four, five, six, seven; seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. Count them forward and backward in succession."
Counting on until the endless days of the future: because of the seven, one is seen; when one is seen, the seven vanish.
Treading through the great void, even the iron ox breaks into a sweat; breath ceases, and no trace remains. Throwing down his staff, he said:
"You must let go of this as well, and only then will the work of study be complete. Ascending the hall, he said: "When seeing the seeing, that which sees is not the seeing; seeing is still..."
He transcends seeing; seeing cannot reach him. He then shouted, "The whale swallows the sea until it is empty, revealing the coral branches.
Suddenly, a monk from among the assembly came forward and said, "Elder, stop your delirious talk! For this, he was granted the gift of a pair of eyes.

Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Sometimes the person is taken away but the environment is not; the staff wanders freely in all directions. Sometimes the environment is taken away but the person is not;
this mountain monk acts in a topsy-turvy fashion. Sometimes both person and environment are taken away;
the staff and this mountain monk leave no trace and swallow their voices. Sometimes neither person nor environment is taken away. He struck the ground with the staff.
Zhàng said, "I have traveled a thousand li with my companion; I have led you across ten thousand mountains. What would it be like if we suddenly encountered Master Linji?
The Master shouted, "If you have not yet clarified the Seal of the Mind-Ground, it will be difficult to pass through the Barrier of the Patriarchs."

The Sagely Sovereign, Emperor Taizong, by means of the ultimate truth of his sagacity, extensively opened wide the gates of deliverance.

He occasionally revealed the primordial mechanism [of the Dharma], yet few were able to respond to him. For instance, when he visited the Prime Minister’s residence and saw a monk reading a sutra, the Emperor asked, "What are you reading?"

(Later, Chan Master Xuedou Mingjue Chongxian offered this response on his behalf: "The August Heaven has no partiality; it assists only virtue.

"Why have you come here? The monk had no reply. (Mingjue replied on his behalf: "It is difficult to escape Your Majesty’s transformative influence. When the monk entered for his audience, he reported:
"Does Your Majesty still remember? The Emperor said: "Where did we meet? He replied: "Since our parting at Vulture Peak, it has been until this very moment.
The Emperor said: "What proof do you have? The monk had no reply. (Mingjue replied on his behalf: "I, a poor monk, have come specifically for this purpose.")
